HPC KernelBench — benchmark specifications

One specification per kernel track, derived from how that track's own papers actually evaluate (arXiv fulltext + artifact benchmark scripts). Each variant fixes the input suite, the timing protocol (warmup, repetitions, statistic, timer), what the timing window includes (preprocessing / format conversion / tuning search), the correctness gate, and the reported metric. Where the literature's common practice is unfair or unreproducible, the spec diverges and says so under Fairness notes.

310papers with artifacts surveyed

spmm36 papers4 variants

Sparse matrix times dense matrix (SpMM), the dominant kernel behind GNN message passing, pruned/quantized DNN inference, and iterative sparse solvers; measured as steady-state throughput with preprocessing reported separately, across GPU tensor-core, GPU CUDA-core, CPU, and quantized variants that the surveyed literature treats as genuinely different claims.

C[M,N] = A[M,K](sparse) * B[K,N](dense row-major)

spmm-gpu-kernel-f32steady-state GPU kernel throughput, sparse format given (no runtime conversion), fp32. The common denominator most GPU SpMM papers (RoDe, GE-SpMM, SMaT, DTC-SpMM's inner kernel) actually report.

Excludes matrices used by only one paper's abstract with no code confirmation (avoids silent cherry-picking).

Fairness notes
  • IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (added while building bench/, 2026-08-06): the phrase "max relative error" used by this track's papers and by the variants above is under-specified, and taken literally it fails correct kernels. An output element here is a sum of many signed products; cancellation regularly leaves a true value near zero, and |out-ref|/|ref| then blows up to O(1e-2..1e0) for a perfectly good fp32 kernel (measured: 3.9e-2 on SuiteSparse/cant at N=128 with scipy's own fp32 CSR product). The reference harness therefore gates on |out-ref| / (|A|*|B|) elementwise — the standard componentwise backward-error denominator — and records the naive pointwise-relative, absolute and L2-relative values alongside so the choice stays auditable. Any implementation of this spec must state which denominator it used; "relative error" alone is not a gate.
  • GE-SpMM ships a correctness-check macro that is commented out by default, and SMaT's sweep script runs with -enable_check=false: both artifacts' OWN reported numbers come from unverified runs. This spec makes the correctness gate mandatory, not opt-in.
  • RoDe, GE-SpMM, and SMaT all time a batch of N iterations with a single CUDA-event pair and report only the resulting mean, which cannot expose run-to-run variance or thermal throttling. This spec requires per-iteration timestamps (Magicube's pattern) and mandates reporting median + min/max, not just mean.
  • RoDe cleanly separates preprocessing into its own CSV; DTC-SpMM's driver structurally excludes reordering from the per-call timing loop. Neither, however, states an explicit amortization count k. This spec fixes k=100 explicitly (spmm-gpu-e2e-preproc-f32) instead of leaving preprocessing either silently excluded or silently amortized over an unstated number of calls.
  • SparseLNR reports a 1.23-1997x speedup range against baseline TACO, which likely reflects pathological worst-case baselines rather than typical performance; this spec requires reporting the median speedup and IQR across the fixed recommended_subset, not a single headline max.
  • Distributed-memory SpMM (Arrow Matrix Decomposition, CAGNET) optimizes communication volume at 100+ node scale, a fundamentally different bottleneck and metric (words moved, not GFLOP/s) than the single-node variants here; folding it into one of the four variants above would compare incomparable things, so it is excluded (see open_questions).
  • Precision families (fp32, fp64, fp16-mixed, int4-int16 quantized) are not pooled into one GFLOP/s ranking: fp64 halves cuSPARSE's fp32 peak, fp16 changes arithmetic intensity, and quantized ops are integer MACs, not FMAs at all. Each stays in its own variant/metric.
Open questions
  • Whether Phase 2 wants a 5th distributed-scaling variant (communication volume + weak/strong scaling vs. node count) to cover Arrow Matrix Decomposition and CAGNET, given the project's Phase 2 machine is not fixed to a single-node target. Left out of this spec since it needs a fundamentally different metric and multi-node access, which most of the track's artifacts (GPU/CPU single-node kernels) don't require.
  • Exact warmup/repeat count used INSIDE DTC-SpMM's compiled kernel binding (DTCSpMM.run_DTCSpMM) was not visible from the Python driver script alone — only the fact that preprocessing happens once outside the per-N loop was confirmed from code.
  • FusedMM, SparseLNR, and CAGNET fulltext was only available via ar5iv's HTML rendering; some evaluation-section detail (e.g. exact CAGNET dataset list beyond Reddit/protein) was truncated in the fetched content and not independently re-verified against the PDF.
  • The 8-graph GNN suite (YeastH, OVCAR-8H, Yeast, DD, web-BerkStan, reddit, ddi, protein) is confirmed code-side only for DTC-SpMM; its reuse by Voltrix/FlashSparse/GeneralSparse/MP-SpMM (all citing RoDe/DTC-SpMM as baselines) is inferred from convention, not independently verified since those 4 papers were only read via abstract for this survey.
spmv20 papers4 variants

Sparse matrix times dense vector (SpMV), the core kernel behind iterative solvers (CG/GMRES/AMG), graph algorithms (GraphBLAS BFS/PageRank), and similarity search; measured as steady-state throughput with format construction reported separately, plus dedicated variants for the conversion-amortized, sequence-of-calls, and symmetric-storage claims that this track's literature treats as genuinely different from a single isolated y=Ax call.

y[M] = A[M,K](sparse) * x[K](dense)

spmv-csr-kernelsteady-state kernel throughput, sparse format given/constructed once (construction excluded from the per-call number but measured and reported), single isolated y=Ax call. The common denominator every surveyed paper except FBMPK and AmgT actually reports; run at both fp64 (primary) and fp32 (secondary) since the track splits roughly evenly (fp64: TileSpMV, DCS-SpMV, CB-SpMV; fp32: AlphaSparse, Bit-GraphBLAS, Serpens).
inputs
suiteSuiteSparse Matrix Collection
selectionreal (non-complex), square or rectangular matrices, 1e4 <= nnz <= 2e8; excludes matrices used by only one paper's abstract with no code confirmation (avoids cherry-picking). Explicitly binary/ pattern-only matrices (Bit-GraphBLAS's 521-matrix domain) are kept out of this general variant, since 1-bit storage changes the byte-accounting model (see open_questions).
recommended_subsetaudikw_1, ldoor, Serena, StocF-1465, Bump_2911, Flan_1565, Hook_1498, Geo_1438, dielFilterV3real, Long_Coup_dt6, Cube_Coup_dt6, crankseg_2, cage15, delaunay_n24, roadNet-CA, hugetrace-00020, wiki-Talk, soc-LiveJournal1, com-Orkut, webbase-1M, in-2004, nlpkkt240, Queen_4147, mip1, pwtk
vector_operandx: dense, initialized U(-1,1) with fixed seed=42; y: initialized to zero (beta=0, no accumulate into y) unless the technique's kernel signature requires accumulate, in which case beta and the initial y contents must be documented alongside the result.
protocol
formatmatrix given as CSR (or COO, converted to CSR by a reference loader). If the technique requires a different internal layout (BSR, tiled, ELL, bit-packed, mixed-precision blocks, etc.), the ONE-TIME conversion is performed once before the timing loop; its wall-clock cost is measured and reported (see preprocessing_reported) but is NOT counted in the per-call throughput number. This matches TileSpMV/CB-SpMV/AlphaSparse's actual runtime structure (conversion happens once, outside the loop) but requires the conversion time to actually be surfaced, which TileSpMV and CB-SpMV's own artifacts do not do.
warmup20
reps100
statisticmedian (report min/max/stdev alongside)
timerplatform-specific, one timestamp pair PER ITERATION (not a single pair around a batched loop, which is what all 9 surveyed SpMV-implementing artifacts do): GPU = CUDA/HIP event pair per call; CPU = std::chrono::steady_clock or omp_get_wtime per call; FPGA = vendor runtime/on-board kernel-invocation counter per call (matching Serpens's explicit "Kernel time" label).
timing_scopekernel only. GPU: H2D/D2H excluded, operands device-resident before timing starts. FPGA: host<->accelerator DMA excluded from this number and measured/reported separately, once (this fixes Top-K SpMV's ambiguity about whether PCIe/HBM transfer is inside its reported time, by requiring the Serpens-style split explicitly).
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: format-conversion wall time reported alongside the kernel throughput number, never silently folded in and never silently dropped (fixes TileSpMV/CB-SpMV, whose artifacts don't surface this number at all). If the technique's construction step is an open-ended autotuning/design SEARCH rather than mechanical conversion (e.g. AlphaSparse's per-matrix format+kernel search, up to 8h), that search cost is EXCLUDED from this variant's "preprocessing" line item entirely and reported only in spmv-e2e-preproc, since blending a millisecond-scale conversion and an hours-scale search into the same field would understate how different in kind they are.
precisionfp64 (primary): reference computed in fp64. fp32 (secondary): reference is the same fp64 computation, error measured against it.
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (2*nnz flops per call; no beta*y term, since beta=0 by default)
secondaryGB/s = bytes_moved/time, where bytes_moved = nnz*(sizeof(value)+ sizeof(index)) + (num_rows+1)*sizeof(index) [row pointer] + num_rows*sizeof(value) [x, read once per row, compulsory-traffic lower bound] + num_rows*sizeof(value) [y, write once] — the standard roofline-style minimum-traffic formula, not each paper's own ad hoc accounting (DCS-SpMV's dataSize formula was the closest match found and is generalized here).
correctnessfp64: max relative error vs. an independently-computed fp64 reference (cuSPARSE fp64 CSR on GPU, Intel MKL fp64 CSR on CPU, same computation re-run on host for FPGA) < 1e-9. fp32: max relative error vs. the fp64 reference < 1e-4. Both are tighter than 3 of the 9 surveyed papers' own tolerances (TileSpMV's 1%, Serpens's <2%-of-elements-mismatch, CB-SpMV's 1e-4/1e-3) and are gated BEFORE timing counts, unlike FBMPK's and CB-SpMV-style artifacts where correctness checking exists in code but is off by default or unautomated.
spmv-e2e-preprocend-to-end throughput including one-shot format construction (mechanical conversion), amortized over k=100 repeated calls on the SAME matrix — the realistic reuse pattern for iterative solvers/AMG/graph algorithms that call SpMV many times per matrix factorization (AmgT: 31 SpMV calls per V-cycle x up to 50 iterations = up to 1,551 calls, so k=100 is conservative relative to real solver usage; DCS-SpMV's own reported numbers already average over 100 calls, just without folding in construction cost).
inputs
suitesame as spmv-csr-kernel
selectionsame as spmv-csr-kernel
recommended_subsetsame as spmv-csr-kernel
vector_operandsame as spmv-csr-kernel
protocol
formatinput is raw CSR/COO; conversion to the kernel's native format IS timed, once
warmup20
repsk=100 post-conversion calls; report BOTH the amortized number and the pure post-conversion kernel time
statisticmedian
timersame per-platform per-iteration timers as spmv-csr-kernel, plus one std::chrono/CUDA-event bracket around the one-shot conversion
timing_scopeconversion + k kernel calls; H2D/D2H of the ORIGINAL matrix included once, D2H of y excluded (matches AmgT/Bit-GraphBLAS's separate-preprocessing-report intent but forces an explicit stated k instead of an implicit or absent one)
preprocessing_reportedboth standalone (ms, once) AND amortized-per-call (construction_ms/k added to each call's time). If construction_time > 10*k*kernel_time (i.e. no realistic k choice would amortize it away — AlphaSparse's regime, where an 8h search dwarfs a microsecond-scale kernel call even at k=100), report the amortized-at-k=100 number AS-IS (which will honestly show construction dominating) plus the raw uncapped construction time, rather than silently choosing a larger k to make the amortized number look favorable. This is the explicit fix for AlphaSparse's own practice of reporting zero amortization argument for its multi-hour search.
precisionsame fp64/fp32 split as spmv-csr-kernel
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (amortized: k*2*nnz / (construction_time + k*kernel_time))
secondaryms (construction, standalone, once); ms (per-call, pure post-conversion kernel, median)
correctnesssame tolerance as spmv-csr-kernel, checked post-conversion
spmv-sequence-krylovthroughput on a bounded SEQUENCE of SpMV calls on the same matrix A with related vectors (Ax, A^2 x, ..., A^k x, or linear combinations), the Krylov-subspace / multigrid usage pattern that FBMPK targets directly and AmgT exhibits inside its V-cycle — distinct from a single isolated call because cache/reuse effects across the sequence and reordering that only pays off over multiple calls change what "fast" means.
inputs
suitesame as spmv-csr-kernel
selectionsame as spmv-csr-kernel, restricted to matrices where a k-step Krylov sequence is numerically meaningful (i.e. exclude structurally singular / non-square matrices)
recommended_subsetsame as spmv-csr-kernel
vector_operandx_0: dense U(-1,1) seed=42; x_{i+1} = A x_i for the sequence (or the paper's own linear-combination scheme if applicable, documented explicitly)
protocol
formatsame as spmv-csr-kernel
warmup20
repsk in {2, 4, 8}; report each k separately (not just the largest)
statisticmedian per-call time within the sequence, across 100 repeated sequences

timing_scopeper-call amortized reporting (average across the k calls in one sequence, then median across 100 repeated sequences) — REQUIRED even though FBMPK's own artifact only reports total-sequence time; this closes the fairness gap where a slower solve that's simply "not divided by k" would look incomparable against papers reporting a single-call metric.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: any sequence-specific preprocessing (matrix reordering/partitioning done to reduce cache pressure across the k calls, e.g. FBMPK's ABMC reordering) is measured and reported — NOT silently excluded from the total the way FBMPK's own public artifact does (it ships a pre-reordered matrix so this cost never appears in the timing loop at all).
precisionfp64 primary (matches FBMPK); fp32 optional secondary
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (per-call, averaged across k calls in a sequence: k*2*nnz / sequence_time)
secondaryms (total sequence time, once per k); ms (sequence-preprocessing, standalone, once)
correctnesssame tolerance as spmv-csr-kernel, checked on the final x_k (or each intermediate x_i if the technique claims per-step accuracy)
spmv-symmetric-kernelsteady-state throughput exploiting matrix symmetry (half-storage, lower- or upper-triangular CSR), for the numerically-symmetric subset of the standard suite — kept as its OWN variant rather than a data filter on spmv-csr-kernel because the computational kernel itself differs: a symmetric SpMV writes to both y[i] and y[j] per stored nonzero (requiring conflict-free or atomic accumulation across threads), a correctness dimension the general kernel never faces, and because GFLOP/s must be counted against the FULL unfolded nnz, not stored nnz, to stay comparable to spmv-csr-kernel at all.

reps100
statisticmedian (report min/max/stdev alongside)
timersame per-platform per-iteration timers as spmv-csr-kernel
timing_scopekernel only, same H2D/D2H exclusion as spmv-csr-kernel
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once, same discipline as spmv-csr-kernel
precisionfp64 primary (matches DCS-SpMV); fp32 optional secondary
metric
primaryGFLOP/s using the FULL (unfolded) flop count: 2*(2*nnz_stored - diag_nnz), explicitly NOT the stored-nnz count — this is a deliberate anti-gaming fix: a symmetric kernel reporting GFLOP/s off stored nnz alone would show an inflated number for doing LESS arithmetic, not more.
secondaryms; GB/s using the half-storage byte count (the actual memory-traffic reduction symmetry buys)
correctnesssame relative-error tolerance as spmv-csr-kernel, PLUS a mandatory race-freedom check: the same input run twice with different thread counts/scheduling must produce bit-identical or tolerance-identical output (catches unsynchronized write-write conflicts on y[i]/y[j], the failure mode this variant's technique family is specifically built to avoid).
Fairness notes
  • IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (added while building bench/, 2026-08-06): the phrase "max relative error" used by this track's papers and by the variants above is under-specified, and taken literally it fails correct kernels. An output element here is a sum of many signed products; cancellation regularly leaves a true value near zero, and |out-ref|/|ref| then blows up to O(1e-2..1e0) for a perfectly good fp32 kernel (measured: 3.9e-2 on SuiteSparse/cant at N=128 with scipy's own fp32 CSR product). The reference harness therefore gates on |out-ref| / (|A|*|B|) elementwise — the standard componentwise backward-error denominator — and records the naive pointwise-relative, absolute and L2-relative values alongside so the choice stays auditable. Any implementation of this spec must state which denominator it used; "relative error" alone is not a gate.
  • TileSpMV and CB-SpMV never measure or surface their format-conversion cost anywhere in the released artifact (not even "reported separately, excluded" — it's simply absent). This spec makes measuring and reporting construction time mandatory for spmv-csr-kernel, not optional.
  • AlphaSparse's per-matrix format+kernel search can take up to 8 hours (vs. a microsecond-scale single SpMV call) and the paper offers no amortization argument. Rather than picking an arbitrarily large k to paper over this, spmv-e2e-preproc requires reporting the amortized number honestly AT k=100 (which will show construction dominating for AlphaSparse-style techniques) plus the raw uncapped construction time, so the spec doesn't quietly launder an 8-hour one-off cost the way an unstated-k "amortization" claim would.
  • CB-SpMV's released code (`ITER=10`) contradicts its own paper text ("executed 1000 times") — an artifact-vs-paper mismatch caught only by reading the benchmark script directly. This spec fixes reps=100 as the single number to use regardless of what any individual paper's text or code claims, and requires per-iteration timestamps so the 100 reps yield a real median+range, not just a mean.
  • FBMPK's public artifact drops its ABMC reordering preprocessing cost entirely (ships a pre-reordered matrix, no line item for the cost at all) — stronger exclusion than any format-conversion paper's practice. spmv-sequence-krylov requires this cost be measured and reported, not silently absent.
  • Correctness tolerances across the surveyed papers range from FBMPK's 1e-6 (but gated behind a compile flag that's OFF by default) to TileSpMV's 1% and Serpens's "<2% of elements may mismatch." This spec fixes one tolerance per precision (1e-9 fp64, 1e-4 fp32) and makes the gate mandatory before any timing counts, tighter than the majority of surveyed artifacts' actual shipped behavior.
  • No surveyed paper reports median+min/max; all 9 SpMV-implementing papers report only a mean (sometimes an amortized/on-device mean, as in Serpens). This spec requires per-iteration timestamps specifically so a real distribution (median, min, max, stdev) can be reported, catching the kind of jitter/throttling a batched-mean timer structurally hides.
  • DCS-SpMV's symmetric-SpMV technique writes to both y[i] and y[j] per stored nonzero from concurrent threads; the paper's own artifact does not describe an explicit race-freedom test. spmv-symmetric-kernel adds one as a mandatory correctness check, since a data race that happens to not manifest in a single test run is not the same as a proven-correct parallel accumulation scheme.
Open questions
  • Mixed/cascade precision (AmgT's fp64/fp32/fp16-per-multigrid-level scheme; Top-K SpMV's 20/25/32-bit fixed-point sweep) doesn't fit the single-precision-per-call model used by spmv-csr-kernel/ spmv-e2e-preproc/spmv-sequence-krylov. A dedicated "spmv-mixed-precision" variant was considered but not added — the 4-variant budget went to the shape-level divergences (kernel-only vs. amortized vs. sequence vs. symmetric) that recur across more of the surveyed papers; AmgT and Top-K SpMV's precision-cascade claims are left as a follow-up extension.
  • Top-K SpMV computes an approximate top-K index subset, not a full y vector — its correctness model (Kendall's tau, NDCG vs. an exact reference) is fundamentally different from elementwise numeric tolerance and doesn't fit any of the 4 variants above. It is treated as a related-but-distinct benchmark (top-k sparse similarity search), out of scope for this general SpMV spec.
  • Bit-GraphBLAS's 1-bit matrix representation (B2SR format, 521-matrix binary-square-matrix domain) has a fundamentally different byte-accounting model (1 bit/nonzero vs. sizeof(value)+sizeof(index)) that the GB/s formula in spmv-csr-kernel doesn't capture correctly. Excluded from the general suite's selection criterion; a bit-packed format extension is a candidate future variant if more binary-matrix papers appear in this track.
  • FBMPK's exact matrix suite, ARM hardware claim, and k-sequence-length choices could not be verified (both available PDF sources had unreadable font encodings); the `recommended_subset` entry for this track's sequence variant is inferred from the one confirmed example (audikw_1) plus the general suite's large symmetric matrices, not independently confirmed against the paper's own evaluation table.
  • Whether the FPGA-specific host<->accelerator DMA number (spmv-csr-kernel's "reported separately" requirement) should itself become a first-class secondary metric (e.g. "effective end-to-end GFLOP/s including DMA") is left open — Top-K SpMV's ambiguity about whether DMA is in-scope suggests this matters in practice, but neither FPGA paper's artifact gave enough detail to fix a specific DMA-inclusion protocol with confidence.
sddmm13 papers4 variants

Measure Sampled Dense-Dense Matrix Multiplication throughput — computing dot products between rows of two dense matrices only at the nonzero positions of a given sparsity pattern — across the three input traditions (general SuiteSparse, sparse-DNN/DLMC, real GNN graphs) and two precision regimes (fp32/fp16 unstructured Tensor-Core, sub-fp32 quantized) the track's papers actually use, plus an end-to-end fused-attention variant for papers that only report SDDMM embedded in a bigger pipeline.

P[i,j] = S[i,j] * dot(A[i,:], B[j,:]) for (i,j) in nnz(S); A: M x K dense, B: N x K dense (row-major), S/P: M x N sparse with identical sparsity pattern

sddmm-csr-kernel-f32steady-state SDDMM kernel throughput on general (non-DNN) sparse matrices given in CSR, fp32, preprocessing excluded from the timed loop. This is the common denominator most GPU papers in the track report (RoDe, and implicitly the Sputnik/Gale-2020 kernels every later paper baselines against).

(Not recoverable from the excerpted Magicube artifact files — this threshold is a spec design choice, not a reproduction of a stated paper tolerance; flag for follow-up against the paper's Table if a tighter number is published.)
sddmm-attention-e2eend-to-end fused SDDMM + softmax + SpMM ("3S" sparse-attention) pipeline cost, one-shot preprocessing (block partition / row-window layout) amortized over k=100 repeated forward passes — the context most track papers actually deploy SDDMM in (GNN attention / graph embedding), and the only number several papers (Fused3S headline figures, FusedMM's end-to-end Force2Vec runs, FlashSparse's GCN/AGNN tables) report at all. Isolated SDDMM-stage cost is additionally reported via kernel-name profiling so this variant stays comparable to sddmm-tensorcore-blocked-fp16.
inputs

statisticmedian per-pass wall time (report min/max/std) across the 100 passes; preprocessing cost amortized in (one-shot cost / k added to each pass's reported time)

metric
primaryms/pass, fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM, preprocessing amortized
secondaryGFLOP/s, FLOPs = nnz*K*2 (SDDMM) + nnz*5 (softmax) + nnz*K*2 (SpMM) — Fused3S's own three-term formula
tertiaryisolated SDDMM-stage GFLOP/s (2*nnz*K), from kernel-name-filtered profiling, directly comparable to sddmm-tensorcore-blocked-fp16
correctnessfused-pipeline output within 1e-2 relative error of an unfused fp32-CSR SDDMM -> softmax -> SpMM reference chain computed independently; the SDDMM sub-stage additionally held to the same 1e-2 relative-error bar as sddmm-tensorcore-blocked-fp16. Gated before timing counts — none of the source papers (Fused3S's accuracy test is a separate script; FusedMM validates only via downstream F1 score) actually gate correctness this way today.
Fairness notes
  • IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (added while building bench/, 2026-08-06): the phrase "max relative error" used by this track's papers and by the variants above is under-specified, and taken literally it fails correct kernels. An output element here is a sum of many signed products; cancellation regularly leaves a true value near zero, and |out-ref|/|ref| then blows up to O(1e-2..1e0) for a perfectly good fp32 kernel (measured: 3.9e-2 on SuiteSparse/cant at N=128 with scipy's own fp32 CSR product). The reference harness therefore gates on |out-ref| / (|A|*|B|) elementwise — the standard componentwise backward-error denominator — and records the naive pointwise-relative, absolute and L2-relative values alongside so the choice stays auditable. Any implementation of this spec must state which denominator it used; "relative error" alone is not a gate.
  • No two of the 8 papers with recovered protocols share an input suite (DLMC vs. general SuiteSparse vs. real GNN graphs) — the spec resolves this with per-suite variants rather than an artificial forced union that would silently favor whichever tradition has more matrices.
  • RoDe's shipped correctness check (#ifdef VALIDATE) is off by default in the artifact's own AE binary; every variant here makes the equivalent check mandatory before a run counts.
  • FusedMM validates SDDMM output only indirectly, via downstream classification F1-score equivalence, not a per-element numerical tolerance on the SDDMM output itself; all variants here require a direct numerical tolerance instead.
  • Magicube reports the mean of 512 timed reps; RoDe reports the (effectively) mean of 10; only Fused3S reports median. All variants here standardize on median + reported min/max/std, per the track-wide instructions, which is a deliberate change from 3 of the 4 GPU papers' own practice.
  • RoDe and FlashSparse both correctly separate and report preprocessing/format-conversion cost rather than silently folding it into steady-state throughput; this practice is generalized to all variants here, including the DLMC quantized-packing cost, which was not visibly separated in the excerpted Magicube files.
  • Fused3S's headline numbers are for the fused 3-stage pipeline, not isolated SDDMM; sddmm-attention-e2e reproduces that framing explicitly (with a stated amortization count, which the source papers do not always give) while sddmm-tensorcore-blocked-fp16 keeps an isolated-kernel number so both kinds of paper claim are comparable on their own terms rather than conflated.
  • distributed_sddmm/HnH's min-wall-time dynamic-repetition protocol (run until elapsed >= min_time, variable trial count) is structurally different from every fixed-rep GPU protocol surveyed and is NOT folded into any variant above; a distributed/CPU-cluster SDDMM variant would need its own protocol definition, left as an open question below rather than forced into the fixed-rep template.
Open questions
  • Gale et al. SC'20's exact DLMC matrix count and sparsity-bucket boundaries were only recovered via an AI-summarized ar5iv extract, not a verbatim table quote; cross-check against the paper's actual Table 1 (or against Magicube's eval_matrices/s*.txt file contents, a faithful machine-readable proxy) before the harness locks in matrix counts.
  • Gale et al. SC'20's own timing protocol (warmup/rep count/statistic) could not be recovered from the arXiv extract at all; needs a PDF-level re-read or inspection of the separately maintained Sputnik/google-research repo (the track input's artifact_url, luckylsk34/Sparse-Kernels, appears to be a third-party mirror, not the original google-research/sputnik repo — flag for the artifact-verification pipeline too).
  • RASSM's SDDMM-specific timing protocol (warmup/rep/statistic) was not fully recovered; code/src/main.cpp confirms the --kernel sddmm path and data_movement_experiment_sddmm entry point exist, but the actual measurement loop (likely in global.cpp/common.cpp, not read in this pass) needs a follow-up read before RASSM numbers back the CPU reference point in sddmm-csr-kernel-f32-style comparisons. Also unclear whether RASSM treats SDDMM as a first-class contribution or an SpMM-adjacent add-on -- its own abstract frames the headline speedup entirely in SpMM terms.
  • HP-SpMM-SDDMM's currently hosted artifact contains no SDDMM benchmark code despite the paper and repo name (only spmm/ and test/ are present); unresolved whether an SDDMM path exists in a different branch/commit or was simply never open-sourced -- needs a `gh api repos/fan1997/HP-SpMM-SDDMM/branches` and commit-history check before concluding the gap is permanent.
  • Insum (ASPLOS'26): the artifact repo (nullplay/IndirectEinsum) is a single unrelated SpMM-COO Triton-codegen demo with no benchmark/dataset/run scripts; ASPLOS'26 has not yet occurred as of this survey, so no methodology facts could be recovered at all. Re-survey once the conference proceedings/artifact are published.
  • distributed_sddmm/HnH's min_time threshold for its dynamic-repetition protocol is set by a caller not read in this pass (only the do-while loop structure and throughput formula were recovered); a concrete value is needed before this protocol family could become its own spec variant for a future distributed-SDDMM track.
  • sddmm-quantized-dlmc's correctness thresholds (4b/8b/16b relative-error bars) are a spec design choice, not a reproduction of a number stated in the Magicube paper/artifact -- the excerpted sddmm_benchmark.cpp did not expose a validation/tolerance check. Revisit if the paper's own accuracy table is located.
  • Whether FlashSparse's and Fused3S's TC-block padding overhead (nnz_padded vs. nnz_raw) is large enough to materially change variant rankings was not quantified in this survey -- both dual-FLOP-count metric fields in sddmm-tensorcore-blocked-fp16 are a hedge, not a resolved answer.
spgemm13 papers4 variants

Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication throughput and scaling, covering the single-device steady-state kernel (symbolic+numeric, format-conversion excluded), the amortized end-to-end cost including one-shot format conversion / row reordering, a tensor-core / mixed- precision variant, and distributed multi-GPU strong scaling.

C = A[M,K](sparse, CSR) * A[K,M](sparse, CSR) — self-product (A x A); A x A^T and general A x B as noted secondary modes

spgemm-square-kernel-f64steady-state device-side SpGEMM kernel throughput for C = A^2 in fp64, one-time A/B format conversion excluded (reported separately, once); symbolic (size-determination) phase and the result matrix's device memory allocation are INCLUDED, since they are unavoidable, data-dependent per-call costs, not amortizable preprocessing.

dnf_handling30s per-run timeout (per Ocean's config/bench.json); a method that fails/OOMs/times out on a matrix is recorded as DNF for that matrix, EXCLUDED from that matrix's geomean contribution (not penalty-filled with another tool's time, unlike Ocean's own convention, since penalty-filling silently rewards fragile methods with an artificial ceiling)
metric
primaryGFLOP/s = 2*flops_naive / (time_ms * 1e6); flops_naive = the naive/symbolic count of scalar multiply-accumulate operations needed to form C from A and B BEFORE duplicate-index compression (i.e. sum over i,k of nnz(A row i)*nnz(B row k) for each A[i,k]!=0) — NOT 2*nnz(C). This matches the Ocean/TileSpGEMM convention and must be used uniformly since compression rates (intermediate products / nnz(C)) range 1.1x-136x across the recommended_subset, so a nnz(C)-based FLOP count would make heavy-cancellation matrices look implausibly fast.
secondaryms (total, plus symbolic_ms/numeric_ms breakdown)

correctnesssame relative-error gate as spgemm-square-kernel-f64, checked once per (matrix, GPU-count) configuration against a single-device or small-scale reference run of the same method (not necessarily cuSPARSE, which cannot run at this scale)
Fairness notes
  • A x A dominates the surveyed literature (4/6 papers primary mode) purely because it needs only one input file; the spec keeps it as the default but this is a convenience convention, not evidence that A x A is representative of general SpGEMM workloads — see survey.md Divergences #1.
  • The spec deliberately INCLUDES symbolic-phase and result-allocation time inside the kernel-only variant's measured window, diverging from TileSpGEMM's own headline number (which excludes both, per its README's line-17/Fig.6-7 vs. line 8-14/Fig.10 split). Excluding allocation lets allocation-heavy matrices (e.g. TileSpGEMM's own 'gupta3' example) look artificially fast; the spec fixes this.
  • TileSpGEMM's public artifact ships with REPEAT_NUM=1 (single run, no warmup, despite computing a time_min variable that implies a multi-rep design was intended). The spec does not adopt this — it mandates warmup=10/reps=20/median regardless of what the artifact's default build does.
  • Ocean's own convention of penalty-filling a DNF baseline with the slowest valid time observed (rather than excluding it) inflates the apparent competitiveness of fragile baselines under a geomean; the spec excludes DNFs from that matrix's aggregate instead.
  • clusterwise-spgemm's amortization-break-even reporting (Fig. 10) is the only surveyed paper that treats one-shot preprocessing rigorously as an amortization question; the spec generalizes that methodology (k=100, report both raw preprocess cost and break-even k) to the GPU papers, none of which do this formally themselves.
  • AmgT cannot supply a clean 'kernel-only' SpGEMM number from its own artifact (time_spgemm is a level-aggregated sum across one AMG setup, not a per-call measurement); the spec's variants therefore treat AmgT as an evidence source for the tensor-core/mixed-precision and 'real embedded usage pattern' motivation, not as a source of directly reusable timing numbers.
Open questions
  • Exact matrix names/sizes used by AmgT and Hussain-CA-SpGEMM's full test set were not recoverable from the sources checked (AmgT: IEEE-only paper, no arXiv/OA link, so only the artifact code was inspected, not a workload table; Hussain: only the 7 headline matrices from Table V were retrievable via the ar5iv fulltext render, not any larger appendix table).
  • No surveyed paper publishes a numeric correctness tolerance for a tensor-core/mixed-precision SpGEMM result; the spgemm-tensorcore-mixed-precision variant's 1e-2 relative-error gate is this spec's own choice (loose enough for fp16, tight enough to catch gross errors) and should be revisited once real data exists.
  • Trident's precision (fp32 vs fp64) was not confirmed from the fetched arXiv HTML sections; spec assumes fp64 by analogy with the rest of the distributed-SpGEMM literature (Hussain/CombBLAS) but this is unverified for Trident specifically.
  • Whether TileSpGEMM's paper-reported numbers (Fig. 6/7) actually came from a REPEAT_NUM>1 build is inferred from the code structure (a time_min-over-array pattern) but not confirmed textually anywhere in the paper or README; the public artifact's default (REPEAT_NUM=1) is the only reproducible ground truth available.
  • No surveyed paper reports a general A x B benchmark on two independently-sized/structured operands (as opposed to A x A, A x A^T, or an application-forced A x B like AMG's R.A.P); the spec's variants therefore cannot cite literature precedent for a pure 'mismatched-operand' A x B mode, only synthesize one by analogy — flagged here rather than silently added as a 5th variant.
sparse-factorization5 papers4 variants

Sparse direct factorization of a matrix stored in a sparse format — nonsymmetric LU (partial pivoting or threshold pivoting), SPD Cholesky, or (possibly rectangular) QR — via a fill-reducing-ordering + symbolic-analysis + numeric-factorization pipeline, measured so that ordering cost, symbolic cost, and numeric cost are never silently merged into one number unless the variant says so explicitly.

LU family: P*A*Q = L*U (A[N,N] sparse nonsymmetric, P/Q permutations from pivoting/ordering, L unit-lower-triangular, U upper-triangular, both sparse with fill-in beyond A's nonzero pattern). Cholesky family: P*A*P^T = L*L^T (A[N,N] sparse SPD, P a fill-reducing symmetric permutation, L sparse lower-triangular). QR family: A*Q_col = Q*R (A[M,N] sparse, M>=N typical; Q_col a column-fill-reducing permutation, Q orthogonal (implicit, Householder/ multifrontal), R sparse upper-triangular).

sparse-factor-symbolic-kernelsteady-state SYMBOLIC factorization time only (fill-in pattern / elimination-tree or supernode-partition computation), with the fill-reducing ordering computed once beforehand and given as a fixed, pre-permuted input matrix — NOT counted in this variant's timed region. This mirrors gSoFa's own methodology exactly (its README states the reordered matrix is dumped once from SuperLU_DIST and fed to gSoFa "for fair comparison"), generalized here to all three factorization families so LU/Cholesky/QR symbolic phases are comparable on the same protocol. This is the track's common-denominator variant: it is the only phase gSoFa's paper reports at all, and it isolates the graph/combinatorial cost from the floating-point cost.
familyLU | Cholesky | QR (harness run separately per family; do not average across families)
inputs
suiteSuiteSparse Matrix Collection
selectionLU: the 13 real nonsymmetric matrices gSoFa evaluates (order 11,948-943,695; nnz ~149K-77.6M; circuit/structural/CFD/thermal/ economic/chemical/EM/bioengineering domains) — chosen because this is the only fulltext-verified matrix list in this track's survey. Cholesky: real SPD matrices; swCholesky's own "FloridaSparse0" list is unpublished (open question below), so this spec fixes a named standard substitute set instead of inheriting an unknown one. QR: STM-multifrontal-QR's public 16-matrix smoke-test set (any shape/symmetry; QR tolerates rectangular and non-SPD inputs).

Tile/block size (PanguLU's `-nb`, or the analogous supernode-merge parameter in Cholesky/QR) MUST be disclosed per run as a required CLI argument, not a silent default — this is PanguLU's own interface convention (`pangulu_example.elf -nb <block_size> -f <matrix>`) and matches this benchmark suite's sibling `cholesky` track's fairness rule.

Where a solve is more natural than a factor-residual (e.g. reusing PanguLU's own pangulu_gstrs), ||Ax-b||/||b|| under the same tolerances is an acceptable substitute — disclose which check was used.
sparse-factor-ordering-sensitivityhow much the CHOICE of fill-reducing ordering algorithm affects downstream numeric-factorization time, fill-in ratio, and memory, on a fixed matrix suite — makes explicit what STM-multifrontal-QR's paper studies directly (its entire contribution is picking AMD vs. COLAMD vs. METIS vs. NESDIS per-matrix via a learned classifier) and what GPTuneCrowd instead folds invisibly into one bundled runtime number by treating ordering (`COLPERM`) as just another autotuned knob. This variant is this spec's answer to "fill-reducing ordering in or out of scope": it is IN scope, but as an independent, disclosed, swept axis — never silently fixed to one method and never silently hidden inside an end-to-end number.

Fairness notes
  • gSoFa's own protocol ("average of three runs", no explicit warmup/min/max reporting) is weaker than this spec's median+min/max convention; this spec upgrades it rather than copying it verbatim, per the track instructions' engineer-not-diplomat principle.
  • PanguLU's `-nb` block-size parameter and GPTuneCrowd's tuned `NSUP`/ `NREL`/`nprows` SuperLU_DIST parameters both demonstrate that this family of kernels has significant, easy-to-hide-behind-a-"best config" tunable knobs; every numeric variant in this spec requires the knob value(s) used to be disclosed per reported number, never silently hand-picked-best-of-N and reported without the value.
  • STM-multifrontal-QR's own README admits its released artifact does NOT actually combine its two headline contributions (GCN ordering-selection + STM numeric scheduling) — "not really combined... due to lack of accuracy of GCN automatic classifier". Any reproduction against this repo will reproduce the STM numeric-phase speedup only, not the paper's full claimed 20.78% symbolic-time reduction; this is flagged here so a future Phase-2 harness builder doesn't discover the gap the hard way.
  • gSoFa and swCholesky both exclude ordering from their timed kernel by feeding a precomputed permutation as input — this is a legitimate experimental design (isolating the FLOP-bound phase from the graph/combinatorial phase) but becomes an unfair comparison if its numbers are ever placed side-by-side with PanguLU's or STM-QR's ordering-inclusive numbers without noting the difference. This spec's 4-variant split exists specifically to prevent that silent mixing.
  • GPTuneCrowd is not a factorization-kernel paper at all — it is included in this track's input list because two of its case studies happen to tune sparse-solver parameters, but its own "speedup" numbers measure tuning-quality-per-function-evaluation-budget, not kernel throughput. Its numbers should NOT be cited as a sparse-LU-factorization performance baseline; it is used here only as motivation for the e2e-amortized variant's k=30 realistic-usage argument and for the disclosed-tunable- parameters fairness principle above.
Open questions
  • PanguLU's exact SuiteSparse matrix list/count for its SC23 headline numbers (11.70x/17.97x speedup) was not recovered — the SC23 paper fulltext is ACM-DL/IEEE-Xplore paywalled and the conference proceedings page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. The "1.50x/3.32x geometric mean" figure surfaced in web-search snippets is ambiguous (possibly from a later citing paper, e.g. arXiv:2512.04389's comparison, rather than PanguLU's own text) and should be re-verified against the primary PDF before being used as a spec target number.
  • swCholesky's actual matrix suite (`FloridaSparse0`), its timing/ repetition protocol, and its baseline comparison are all unrecoverable from the public repo (job-launcher script only, no paper text fetched — TPDS is IEEE-Xplore paywalled). The Cholesky recommended_subset above is this spec's own standard-substitute curation, NOT swCholesky's actual set — flagged explicitly rather than presented as verified.
  • Neither PanguLU's nor swCholesky's correctness-checking methodology (residual formula, tolerance) was confirmed from any available source; both projects' interfaces (`pangulu_gstrs`/`pangulu_gssv`; a presumed solve step in `sw_cholesky`) suggest a residual check would be natural, but this spec's residual gate for those two families is this spec's own requirement, not a reproduction of the original papers' practice.
  • STM-multifrontal-QR's "error verification" field (written to `Results/QR_time.txt`) has an unknown exact formula/tolerance — the README documents that the field exists but not its definition.
  • Sunway SW26010 (swCholesky) is realistically inaccessible outside China; STM-multifrontal-QR's ARM NUMA "Taishan Server" is similarly non-standard. A Phase-2 harness targeting Perlmutter/any-x86-or-generic- ARM machine will need to either recompile these two artifacts for a different architecture (nontrivial — swCholesky's kernels are written against Sunway-specific scratchpad-memory intrinsics) or substitute a portable reference implementation (e.g. CHOLMOD for swCholesky's family, SuiteSparseQR-on-x86 for STM-QR's family) and treat the original paper's numbers as reference-only, not reproducible targets.
sptrsv5 papers4 variants

Sparse triangular solve (SpTRSV), L*x=b for x with L sparse lower- triangular, the core kernel behind sparse-direct-solver back-substitution and ILU/IC-preconditioned Krylov iterations; measured with the analysis/scheduling (level-set, DAG-partitioning, codelet-mining, warp-partitioning -- whatever the technique needs to prepare a parallel execution plan) split out as its OWN first-class variant rather than a footnote, because for several of this track's own papers that analysis step IS the contribution, plus a steady-state solve variant, a repeated-solve amortized variant, and a distributed-memory strong-scaling variant for the one surveyed paper (SC'23) whose claim is genuinely different in kind (multi-node/multi-GPU, real LU-factor input) from the other four single-device papers.

solve L[n,n](sparse triangular) * x[n] = b[n](dense) for x

sptrsv-solve-kernelsteady-state solve-phase wall time on a single CPU node or single GPU, single RHS (nrhs=1), analysis/scheduling done once beforehand and EXCLUDED from this number (see sptrsv-analysis-phase for that cost as its own first-class measurement, not silently dropped). This is the one denominator all 5 surveyed papers' code actually separates out, even though they disagree on how many times to repeat it and what statistic to report (survey.md Divergence #2).
inputs
suiteSuiteSparse Matrix Collection
selectionreal, square, structurally nonsingular matrices (any symmetry), 1e4 <= nnz(A) <= 5e7 -- the scale range actually exercised by the 4 single-device surveyed papers (YuenyeungSpTRSV: up to ~245 matrices at this scale; HDagg/partially-strided-codelet: per-matrix CLI runs at similar scale; Split_SpTRSV: UF-ID download, unbounded but demonstrated on FullChip-class matrices in this range). Matrices used ONLY by the distributed variant's 1e9-nnz-class LU factors (, dielFilterV3real) are deliberately excluded here even though small enough at the A-level, because this variant's derivation method (below) does not apply real fill-in and so does not need -- or benefit from -- SC'23-scale inputs.
recommended_subsetapache2, ecology2, thermal2, parabolic_fem, offshore, G3_circuit, StocF-1465, Serena, Hook_1498, Geo_1438, audikw_1, boneS10, af_shell8, cage14, torso3, crashbasis, Bump_2911, cant, pwtk, bcsstk36, ldoor
triangular_factor_derivationCANONICAL METHOD (fixes survey.md Divergence #1 -- 4 of 5 surveyed papers extract a "triangular factor" directly from an arbitrary matrix A rather than solving a real LU/Cholesky output, but do it three DIFFERENT ways: kept-values (YuenyeungSpTRSV), randomized values discarding A entirely (Split_SpTRSV), and an unconfirmed-from-code third variant for HDagg). This spec fixes ONE method for reproducibility: L = strict lower-triangular part of A (entries with col<row, values taken AS-IS from A, matching YuenyeungSpTRSV's convention since it is one of the surveyed methods (with partially-strided-codelet) that preserves the input matrix's actual numeric structure) PLUS an explicit unit diagonal (L[i,i]=1 for all i), never A's own diagonal entry -- unlike YuenyeungSpTRSV's code (which divides by whatever nonzero happens to sit last in the row, silently relying on A never having a zero/tiny diagonal, an unstated and unverified assumption). Unit diagonal guarantees solvability and numerical stability regardless of A's own diagonal, at zero reproducibility cost. This is a STRUCTURAL PROXY for a real triangular factor, not a real LU/Cholesky output -- it is used here because it is the majority (4/5) practice in this track and requires no factorization-library dependency, but its DAG-shape/parallelism characteristics differ from a real fill-in factor (see sptrsv-distributed-scaling, which uses real factors instead, and notes_on_fairness below).
rhs_and_referencex_ref: dense, U(0,1) with fixed seed=42, one fresh draw PER TIMED SOLVE CALL (never reused across repeated calls -- fixes the risk that a fixed b lets a race-prone synchronization-free kernel get "lucky" on the one input it's ever tested against, per survey.md YuenyeungSpTRSV correctness discussion). b = L @ x_ref, computed once per draw via a reference double-precision serial SpMV (never via the technique under test).
nrhs1
protocol
formatCSR (or whatever the technique's kernel signature natively needs); conversion from the reference CSR loader is a ONE-TIME cost folded into the analysis phase (see sptrsv-analysis-phase), never into the per-solve number.
analysisperformed once per (matrix, thread/GPU-config) before ANY timed solve call; whatever the technique needs (level-set construction, DAG partitioning, codelet mining, warp-partition table, split-point selection) happens here, once, and its cost is excluded from this variant entirely -- see sptrsv-analysis-phase for that number reported as its own first-class measurement, not a silent drop (fixes Split_SpTRSV's flaw of re-measuring and re-averaging analysis cost inside its own solve-timing loop, and YuenyeungSpTRSV /Sympiler-family's practice of measuring it but never surfacing it as a standalone benchmark result).
warmup10
reps50
statisticmedian (report min/max alongside)
timerGPU = CUDA/HIP event pair per solve call (fixes YuenyeungSpTRSV's gettimeofday-based host-side timer, which is unusual for a GPU-kernel paper in this track and adds host jitter); CPU = std::chrono::steady_clock or omp_get_wtime per solve call.
timing_scopesolve kernel only. Any per-call reset of algorithm-internal state (e.g. synchronization-free "ready" flag arrays, atomic counters) happens INSIDE the timed region only if the technique's own published design requires it as part of a genuine solve call (this matches YuenyeungSpTRSV's correct cudaMemset-before-timing practice), but H2D of L/b (done once before the loop) and D2H of the solution x (fixes YuenyeungSpTRSV's flaw of including the cudaMemcpy(x, d_x, ...) inside its timed region) are EXCLUDED, measured once, and reported alongside as a separate line item.
precisionfp64 (primary; matches 4 of 5 surveyed papers' default). fp32 (secondary, where the technique supports it).
metric
primaryms (wall time per solve call)
secondaryGFLOP/s = 2*nnz(L)/(time_ns) -- reported for comparability with the one surveyed paper (YuenyeungSpTRSV) that used this metric, but flagged as a WEAK metric for SpTRSV specifically: unlike GEMM/SpMM, SpTRSV's realizable performance is bounded by DAG critical-path length and per-level parallelism, not raw FLOP count, so two matrices with identical nnz(L) can have wildly different achievable GFLOP/s. Time (primary) and speedup-vs-baseline are the metrics this track's papers actually rely on for comparison (survey.md Divergence #6).
correctnessmax relative error vs. the x_ref used to generate b, < 1e-9 (fp64) / 1e-4 (fp32), gated BEFORE timing counts, checked on EVERY one of the reps=50 timed calls (not just once) -- tighter than all 5 surveyed papers (Sympiler family's 1e-6, YuenyeungSpTRSV's 1% relative, and SC'23's unconfirmed/never-gated berr) and explicitly checked per-call rather than once, since a technique that is only "correct on average" across repeated calls (a real risk for synchronization-free spin-wait designs, per survey.md) should fail this gate, not pass it on a lucky first try.
sptrsv-analysis-phasecost of the one-shot analysis/scheduling step itself, reported as a FIRST-CLASS benchmark result rather than folded silently into "preprocessing, mentioned once" or (worse) re-measured repeatedly inside a solve-timing loop the way Split_SpTRSV's own artifact does. This matters because for 2 of the 5 surveyed papers (HDagg, partially-strided-codelet) the analysis/scheduling ALGORITHM is the paper's actual contribution, not the solve kernel itself -- comparing only solve-phase numbers would erase exactly what those papers are claiming to improve.
inputs
suitesame as sptrsv-solve-kernel
selectionsame as sptrsv-solve-kernel
recommended_subsetsame as sptrsv-solve-kernel
triangular_factor_derivationsame as sptrsv-solve-kernel
protocol
warmup0
reps5
statisticmedian (matches the Sympiler family's own num_test_=5 convention, applied here specifically to the analysis phase rather than the solve, since analysis is itself a one-shot-per-matrix cost worth its own repeated measurement for variance)
timersame per-platform timers as sptrsv-solve-kernel
timing_scopethe full analysis/scheduling step, rebuilt from scratch on every one of the 5 repetitions (no caching across reps) -- level-set construction, DAG partitioning, codelet mining, warp-partition table construction, split-point selection, or whatever else the technique's own design requires before its first solve call can run. Includes any technique-specific format conversion.
metric
primaryms (median analysis time)
secondarybreak-even count = analysis_time_ms / single_solve_time_ms (from sptrsv-solve-kernel's median) -- the number of repeated solves needed before the analysis cost is amortized away, which is the number that actually determines whether a technique is worth using in a given application (feeds directly into the k choice discussion for sptrsv-e2e-amortized below).
correctnessstructural only: verify the produced schedule/partition is a valid topological decomposition of L's dependency DAG (every row's predecessors are scheduled in an earlier level/codelet/partition). No numeric output to gate at this phase.
sptrsv-e2e-amortizedend-to-end time = one-shot analysis + k repeated solve calls on the SAME matrix L with DIFFERENT right-hand sides, amortized -- the realistic ILU(0)/IC(0)-preconditioned-Krylov usage pattern (each preconditioned Krylov iteration issues one L-solve and one U-solve; HDagg's own paper targets exactly this via its ILU/IC evaluation) and the factorize-once-solve-many pattern SuperLU_DIST's own pddrive3d1.c driver exists to demonstrate ("we factorize A only once... and reuse... in the subsequent call"). k=50 is chosen as a conservative middle-of-the-road Krylov restart-cycle length (smaller than the SpMV track's k=100, since each SpTRSV "iteration" here already implies 2 kernel calls -- L-solve then U-solve -- for the same nominal iteration count, so 50 keeps total kernel-call count in the same order of magnitude as the SpMV variant's 100 single-matrix calls).

nrhs1
protocol
analysistimed once, exactly as in sptrsv-analysis-phase, folded into this variant's total
warmup0
repsk=50 post-analysis solve calls; report BOTH the amortized number and the pure steady-state solve time from sptrsv-solve-kernel side by side
statisticmedian
timersame per-platform per-call timers as sptrsv-solve-kernel, plus one bracket around the one-shot analysis
timing_scopeanalysis + k solve calls; H2D of L done once, D2H of x excluded from the per-call number (matches sptrsv-solve-kernel's scope) but reported once, standalone
precisionsame fp64/fp32 split as sptrsv-solve-kernel
metric
primaryms (amortized per-solve: (analysis_time + k*solve_time) / k)
secondaryms (total wall time for the k-solve batch, standalone); if analysis_time > 10*k*solve_time (i.e. no realistic k would amortize it away -- plausible for the more elaborate analysis passes in this track, e.g. codelet mining), report the amortized-at-k=50 number AS-IS, honestly showing analysis dominating, plus the raw uncapped analysis time -- never silently pick a larger k to make the amortized number look better (same principle as the SpMV track's spmv-e2e-preproc variant).
correctnesssame tolerance as sptrsv-solve-kernel, checked on EVERY one of the k solve calls; report the WORST-case (max) relative error observed across all k, not just the first or the mean -- the amortized-time claim is worthless if correctness silently degrades over repeated calls (e.g. accumulated floating-point drift in a reused schedule, or a race-prone synchronization-free design that is occasionally wrong).
sptrsv-distributed-scalingstrong-scaling wall time / speedup of a distributed-memory (MPI, multi-node, optionally multi-GPU) SpTRSV across a fixed sequence of process/GPU counts, on a matrix derived from a REAL numeric LU factorization with genuine fill-in -- not the structural-proxy triangular factor used by the other 3 variants. This is a genuinely different claim, not a stricter version of the single-node variants: only 1 of the 5 surveyed papers (SC'23) operates at this scale, and its own baseline comparison is against other distributed algorithms, not cuSPARSE/MKL.
inputs
suiteSuiteSparse Matrix Collection (subset used by the one surveyed distributed-SpTRSV paper)
selectionthe 4 SC'23 Table-1 matrices that are independently obtainable from SuiteSparse: nlpkkt80 (n=1,062,400, nnz(A)~=6.5e7, optimization), Ga19As19H42 (n=133,123, quantum chemistry), ldoor (n=952,203, structural) (n=1,102,824, electromagnetics). The paper's other 2 matrices (s1_mat_0_253872, a fusion-plasma matrix; s2D9pt2048, a synthetic 2D 9-point Poisson discretization) are NOT in SuiteSparse and are excluded here as non-reproducible inputs (see open_questions) rather than silently substituted.
recommended_subsetnlpkkt80, Ga19As19H42, ldoor, dielFilterV3real
triangular_factor_derivationREAL factorization, not the structural proxy used elsewhere in this spec: run one reference distributed sparse LU factorization (e.g. SuperLU_DIST) with METIS nested-dissection fill-reducing ordering on each matrix, ONCE, and reuse the resulting L/U factors (with their genuine fill-in) across every process-count configuration tested -- matching the surveyed paper's own description ("LU factors are generated by running the 3D numerical factorization algorithm... with METIS ordering"). Factorization cost is measured and reported once per matrix, standalone; never counted in the per-configuration SpTRSV numbers below.
nrhs1
protocol
process_grid_sweeptotal process count P = Px*Py*Pz swept over a fixed named list {128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048} (CPU, matching the surveyed paper's own Cori-Haswell sweep) or GPU count in {1, 2, 4, 8, ..., 256} (GPU, matching the surveyed paper's own Perlmutter sweep); for each P, Pz swept over {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32} (CPU) / {1, 2, 4, ..., 64} (GPU), Px approx= Py chosen to keep the 2D grid as square as possible for the remaining P/Pz processes -- reproducing the surveyed paper's own sweep design exactly, since it is the only precedent in this track.
reps>=3 independent job submissions per (matrix, P, Pz) configuration, report median with min/max -- this FIXES a gap in the surveyed paper itself: no confirmed in-code repeat/statistic was found for its reported figures (a single run per configuration is plausible given per-configuration LU-factorization cost of 10s-3000s), which cannot distinguish real algorithmic improvement from run-to-run network/scheduler jitter at this scale.
timerlibrary-internal solve-phase timer (e.g. SuperLU_DIST's SuperLU_timer_()/utime[SOLVE]), isolated from the one-shot factorization time
timing_scopesolve phase only (both L-solve and U-solve, single RHS); factorization/ordering excluded and reported once, standalone, per matrix (see triangular_factor_derivation above). Inter-grid and intra-grid communication breakdown reported as a secondary line-item where the technique under test exposes it (matches the surveyed paper's own Fig. 5/6/9 time-breakdown convention).
precisionfp64
metric
primarys (median solve-phase wall time per configuration)
secondarystrong-scaling speedup relative to the smallest tested P for the same matrix
correctnesscomponent-wise backward error (berr), computed per RHS and GATED against < 1e-10 (fp64) BEFORE a configuration's timing is accepted -- this explicitly FIXES the surveyed paper's own driver code, which computes berr and prints it but was never found to gate it against any threshold before reporting timing (a direct violation of the "correctness gate before timing counts" fairness principle).
Fairness notes
  • The single biggest fairness issue in this track is silent: 4 of 5 surveyed papers benchmark SpTRSV on a "triangular factor" that is simply an arbitrary SuiteSparse matrix's own triangular part (optionally with randomized values), not a real LU/Cholesky output -- and no paper's abstract discloses this. A "Nx over cuSPARSE" claim under this protocol is not testing the same DAG-shape distribution a real sparse-direct-solver back-substitution would present. This spec resolves it by (a) naming ONE canonical structural-proxy method for the 3 single-device variants, since that IS the field's majority practice and requires no factorization-library dependency, and (b) requiring genuine LU-factor inputs for the distributed variant, where a structural proxy would understate the fill-in-driven communication volume that variant exists to measure.
  • Split_SpTRSV's own artifact re-measures and re-averages its analysis phase inside a 10-iteration solve-timing loop -- undermining its own paper's amortization argument in its own benchmark code. This spec's sptrsv-analysis-phase / sptrsv-e2e-amortized split fixes that by forcing analysis to be measured exactly once and its cost surfaced explicitly, never re-paid on every timed solve.
  • Only YuenyeungSpTRSV among the 5 surveyed papers reports a throughput metric (GFLOP/s) at all; this spec keeps it as a secondary metric for comparability but explicitly flags it as weak for SpTRSV (DAG critical-path-bound, not FLOP-count-bound) and makes wall time primary, matching what the other 4 papers actually rely on.
  • No surveyed paper's driver code gates correctness against a threshold before accepting a timing result (SC'23 computes but never checks berr; the others check once, if at all, sometimes with a loose tolerance). Every variant in this spec makes the gate explicit and checks it on every timed call, not just once.
Open questions
  • Split_SpTRSV's ValidateResult() tolerance was not located in the fetched files (util.h's relevant section was not surfaced by search); the 1e-9/1e-4 gate this spec imposes may be tighter than what the original paper actually validated against -- worth confirming before treating a Split_SpTRSV-family technique's correctness pass/fail as directly comparable to the other 4 papers' numbers.
  • HDagg's SpTrSv_Final.sh script references a `matrix/*.mtx` directory whose contents are not checked into the repo, so the paper's actual evaluated matrix LIST (as opposed to the general SuiteSparse-matrix convention inferred from the README's apache2 example) could not be confirmed from the artifact alone.
  • SC'23's own reported figures could not be confirmed as single-run vs. multi-run-averaged from the extracted paper text or the reproducibility appendix -- the appendix states per-configuration wall time ("10s to 3000s") dominated by LU factorization, consistent with (but not proof of) a single run per configuration; this spec's >=3-reps requirement for sptrsv-distributed-scaling may therefore multiply the paper's own reported experimental cost several-fold if reproduced faithfully.
  • 2 of SC'23's 6 benchmark matrices (s1_mat_0_253872, s2D9pt2048) are not in SuiteSparse and were excluded from sptrsv-distributed-scaling's recommended_subset; if these become available (e.g. via the paper's Zenodo artifact DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8084212) they should be added back, since they are 2 of the paper's 4 headline result matrices.
  • Whether "unit diagonal" (this spec's canonical choice) vs. "A's own diagonal" (YuenyeungSpTRSV's actual, unstably-assumed practice) materially changes measured performance for any of the 4 surveyed single-device techniques was not tested -- flagged as a design decision made for reproducibility/stability, not verified as performance-neutral.
sparse-attention-kernel4 papers2 variants

Fused attention restricted to a 0/1 sparsity mask (softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d) + mask)V computed only over allowed positions), measured as steady-state kernel throughput with BOTH an effective (mask-nnz-based) and a dense-equivalent FLOP count reported side by side so speedup claims state which convention they use, split into a structured/swept-ratio variant (sequence-based, sparsity ratio as a first-class swept parameter) and a real-graph-adjacency variant (Fused3S's GNN-style sparse attention, where sparsity is a fixed dataset property, not a tunable knob) — plus a mandatory downstream quality-gate report that no surveyed paper currently provides.

O[B,H,S,d] = softmax( (Q[B,H,S,d] @ K[B,H,S,d]^T) / sqrt(d) + mask ) @ V[B,H,S,d], mask in {0,-inf}^{S x S} (or, for the graph-adjacency variant, O[N,d] = softmax_row(A ⊙ (Q K^T / sqrt(d))) V over N = graph node count and A = the graph's sparse adjacency matrix in CSR)

sparse-attn-structured-mask-kernel-fp16steady-state fused sparse-attention kernel throughput under a structured, parametrically-swept sparsity mask (sliding-window, block-local+global, dilated, or a model-defined dynamic/regional ViT mask), at a stated and measured sparsity ratio, with preprocessing (mask/adjacency construction, structural reordering, ILP-schedule solve, autotuning/operator-fusion search) excluded from per-iteration time and reported separately. This is the common denominator STOF's `benchmk_attn_unified.py` and TomczakK25's 6 kernel variants both measure, and what ipdps-26_vit's ILP-scheduled tile execution is a drop-in candidate for (its DynamicViT/RegionViT/VisionLongformer masks are treated as fixed sparsity patterns at their own native ratio, submitted at whatever Sf they produce).
inputs
suiteunion of STOF's 5 named mask types (causal, sliding, Longformer, BigBird, dilated) swept over sequence length, TomczakK25's swept sparsity-factor range applied to its Local/Local-1D-Dilated/ Local-2D-Dilated/Global/COO/CSR kernels, and ipdps-26_vit's 3 named ViT sparse-mask sources (DynamicViT, RegionViT, VisionLongformer) at their own native (unswept) sparsity ratio.
selectionfix a canonical sparsity-factor sweep since STOF (fixed band/global-width = sqrt(S)) and TomczakK25 (Sf swept 1e-4 to 1.0) disagree on how sparsity is parameterized: Sf in {0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}, applied at each of S in {1024, 4096, 16384} for the sliding/dilated/global-local kernel family (Longformer/BigBird-style constructions become memory-prohibitive to materialize explicitly above S=4096 per STOF's own extended-sweep cutoff, so those two mask types are capped at S<=4096). ipdps-26_vit's 3 ViT masks are submitted once each at their model's native resolution/sparsity (not swept), since sparsity there is a property of the trained model, not a benchmark parameter.

protocol
warmup10
reps100 minimum (raising both STOF's code-verified 20 and TomczakK25's 15 to this project's >=20-sample convention; see Divergences — STOF's own paper text claims 100 but its released script only runs 20, so this spec does not silently inherit either paper's own practice)
statisticmedian (report min/max) — not the average-only statistic both STOF's code and TomczakK25 actually use
timerdevice-side events (CUDA/HIP events), one pair per iteration
timing_scopekernel only; mask/adjacency construction, structural reordering (ipdps-26_vit's HC/IC/RCM), ILP-schedule solve, and any autotuning/operator-fusion search (STOF's Table-4 tuning cost) excluded and reported separately, once
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: mask-construction time, reorder+block-extraction+ILP-solve time (ipdps-26_vit), operator-fusion-template search time (STOF)
measured_sparsity_reportedmandatory: report the ACTUAL measured mask density (nnz/S^2) alongside the nominal Sf target, since BigBird's random component and ipdps-26_vit's model-defined masks do not land exactly on a requested ratio
metric
primaryeffective TFLOP/s: flops = 2 * 2 * B * H * nnz(mask) * d (QK^T + PV, 2 flops/MAC, nnz = actual number of unmasked (query,key) pairs — NOT S^2). This is the "useful work done" number.
secondarydense-equivalent TFLOP/s computed on the SAME wall time using the attn-prefill-kernel-fp16bf16 causal-aware dense formula (flops = (mask spans full S^2 ? 4 : 2) * B*H*S^2*d) — reported alongside the effective number specifically so the ratio (effective/dense = measured sparsity-derived speedup-vs-a-hypothetical-dense-kernel-at- the-same-wall-time) is visible. Neither number alone answers "is this fast because of sparsity or because of a fast dense kernel" — this spec requires BOTH, correcting the track's own practice where STOF/ipdps-26_vit report neither and TomczakK25/Fused3S report only one convention each without the other for comparison.
tertiaryms latency; measured sparsity ratio (nnz/S^2)
correctnessmax abs error < 1e-2 vs. a fp32-accumulate dense masked-softmax reference (PyTorch `scaled_dot_product_attention` with an explicit additive -inf mask, computed in fp32) — a single, mandatory, hard- gated pre-timing check for EVERY candidate, closing the gap where STOF's and Fused3S's own correctness scripts are disconnected from their perf benchmarks and ipdps-26_vit's timed path has no check at all. (TomczakK25's own `allclose(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5)` is tighter than this spec's 1e-2; candidates MAY additionally report against that tighter bound but 1e-2 is the pass/fail gate, matching this project's attn-prefill-kernel-fp16bf16 convention for fp16 arithmetic.)
quality_gateMANDATORY, once per named mask family (not per shape): for the 3 ipdps-26_vit ViT configs, report top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K val (or the model's own reported eval set) at the tested sparsity ratio vs. the model's dense-attention baseline; for the causal-LM-shaped STOF/TomczakK25/sf-sweep configs, report perplexity on a fixed small held-out LM eval set (e.g. WikiText-103 val) for a small causal LM (GPT-2-small scale) run with the candidate sparse-attention kernel substituted in vs. its dense baseline. NONE of the 4 surveyed papers implements this — see Divergences. This is a spec-mandated fix to a real gap, not a reproduction of current practice, and is why this variant is not simply "adopt whichever paper already does it best."
sparse-attn-graph-adjacency-kernel-fp16steady-state fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM graph-attention kernel throughput over a REAL graph's own sparse adjacency (not a synthetic or parametrically-swept mask), preprocessing (CSR to tensor-core-block conversion) excluded and reported separately. This is Fused3S's own claim and the only legitimate comparison point for it — its "sparsity ratio" is a fixed dataset property (typically <1% density for citation/social graphs), not a value any candidate chooses, so pooling it with the structured-mask variant above would force an artificial ratio framing onto data that does not have one.
