Not implemented by Fused3S's own release (see Divergences) — a spec-mandated fix, matching the structured-mask variant's quality_gate rationale.
Fairness notes
  • STOF's released benchmark script (warmup=10, running_iters=20, mean-only) contradicts its own paper text ('run 100 times... average performance') — this spec does not adopt either number from STOF as-is; it raises the floor to 100 reps with median+min/max, per this project's general convention (see benchspecs/attention-kernel/spec.yaml's identical treatment of PAT/MEATTEN).
  • No paper in this track reports both an effective (sparse/nnz-based) AND a dense-equivalent FLOP count for the same measurement: TomczakK25 states the two complexities analytically (O(SfL^2d) vs O(L^2d+SfL^2d)) but does not measure both; Fused3S measures only the effective number; STOF and ipdps-26_vit measure neither. Both variants in this spec require reporting both numbers side by side, directly implementing this track's key fairness axis (a speedup claim must state which FLOP convention it uses).
  • None of the 4 papers implements a downstream model-quality gate (perplexity or task accuracy) at the sparsity ratios they benchmark — all four only check numerical closeness of the attention OUTPUT TENSOR to a dense reference, never that the sparsity PATTERN preserves the model's actual task performance. Both variants' quality_gate sections are therefore spec additions, not adoptions of existing practice; flagged explicitly rather than silently invented, per the instruction to be an engineer and fix a literature gap rather than paper over it.
  • Fused3S's graph-attention kernel cannot share a variant with the other 3 papers' sequence-attention kernels: its 'sparsity ratio' is a fixed property of a real dataset (typically <1% density), not a value a candidate can choose or that a benchmark can sweep, and its 'sequence length' is a graph's node count. Pooling it into the swept-Sf variant would either force an artificial ratio framing onto real data or silently drop the ratio-sweep requirement for one candidate only — kept as a fully separate variant instead, matching this project's precedent of splitting variants along genuinely different input-suite axes (see attention-kernel's GPU-vs-CPU and prefill-vs-decode splits).
  • Correctness-check enforcement is disconnected from the performance benchmark in 3 of 4 papers (STOF, Fused3S, and — absent entirely — ipdps-26_vit); only TomczakK25 appears to genuinely gate on allclose. This spec makes the correctness gate mandatory and part of the SAME run as the timed measurement for every candidate in both variants.
Open questions
  • ipdps-26_vit: the aggregation from per-block mean_ms/p50_ms (run_bench.py's actual output) up to the paper's headline end-to-end '2.1x over FlashAttention' claim is not visible in the surveyed script — unclear whether it's a wall-time sum, a weighted average by block count, or a full-model forward-pass wrapper not included in the repo's src/ directory.
  • STOF: whether the arXiv text's stated '100 iterations' applies to a different script than benchmk_attn_unified.py (e.g. tuning_STOF_cost.py or the MCFuser/Bolt-specific paths) was not independently checked within this survey's time budget; the 20-iteration count is confirmed only for the MHA-comparison script behind fig9-10.sh.
  • TomczakK25: the exact dtype (fp16 vs fp32) used for the allclose(atol=1e-8, rtol=1e-5) correctness comparison was not confirmed from the fetched excerpt — those tolerances are unusually tight for fp16 arithmetic, suggesting the comparison may run in fp32, but this is not verified against source.
  • Fused3S: the default --embedding_dim (128, confirmed) and --batch_size (1024 for batched graphs, confirmed) in baseline_comp_kernel_only.py's own CLI were read, but the full sweep the paper's Figures 5/6/7 actually use (fixed at these defaults, or swept?) was not independently cross-checked against the plotting scripts (time_comp_figure.py was not read in depth).
  • Whether the quality_gate requirement (perplexity / ViT top-1 / node-classification accuracy) added by this spec is achievable within a reasonable Phase-2 benchmarking budget, given it requires running a full downstream model/task rather than just the isolated kernel, is left as a Phase-2 scoping question rather than resolved here.
spmspv2 papers3 variants

Sparse matrix times sparse vector (SpMSpV), where both the nonzero PATTERN and the resulting output density of the vector operand are first-class variables rather than fixed at "dense." Measured primarily as a function of swept input-vector density on a fixed matrix suite (the axis this track's own papers treat as central), with a second variant driven by a real, workload-generated non-uniform sparsity trace (BFS frontiers) since a synthetic sweep and a real trajectory are not interchangeable, plus a construction-cost variant for the bitmap/index structures several techniques in this track require.

y[M](sparse, nnz_y variable) = A[M,K](sparse, CSR/CSC/bitmap) * x[K](sparse, nnz_x swept); output nnz_y is NOT known a priori and must be produced (allocated/compacted) by the kernel, unlike SpMV where the output is always a fully-populated dense M-vector.

spmspv-density-sweep-kernelsteady-state kernel throughput as a function of INPUT VECTOR DENSITY, swept from near-empty to fully dense on a FIXED matrix — the controlled-sensitivity-curve variant LiAY21 runs directly and the one this track's whole point is to compare across implementations at matched density, not just at one arbitrarily chosen sparsity level.
inputs
suiteSuiteSparse Matrix Collection, same collection as benchspecs/spmv/spec.yaml
selectionthe spmv track's own recommended_subset (25 named matrices, 1e4 <= nnz <= 2e8), restricted to structurally non-trivial instances (drop pure diagonal/near-diagonal matrices where a sparse-vector multiply degenerates), reused here rather than re-deriving a new suite so SpMSpV-vs-SpMV throughput is directly comparable on the SAME matrices, per this track's stated goal of aligning with benchspecs/spmv/spec.yaml.
recommended_subsetaudikw_1, ldoor, Serena, StocF-1465, Bump_2911, Flan_1565, Hook_1498, Geo_1438, dielFilterV3real, Long_Coup_dt6, Cube_Coup_dt6, crankseg_2, cage15, delaunay_n24, roadNet-CA, hugetrace-00020, wiki-Talk, soc-LiveJournal1, com-Orkut, webbase-1M, in-2004, nlpkkt240, Queen_4147, mip1, pwtk
vector_operandx: sparse, nnz_x in {1, 0.001%, 0.01%, 0.1%, 1%, 10%, 50%, 100%} of K (LiAY21's "1 to n with a uniform interval" ramp, discretized into this explicit, reportable grid rather than an unstated continuous sweep), nonzero positions chosen uniform-random with fixed seed=42, nonzero values (where the semiring is arithmetic, not Boolean) initialized U(-1,1). At nnz_x=100% this variant's number MUST equal (within noise) the spmv-csr-kernel number for the same matrix at N=1 in benchspecs/spmv/spec.yaml — implementations failing this identity indicate the SpMSpV path is not a correct generalization of the dense case.
protocol
formatmatrix given as CSR (converted once if the technique needs a different layout, e.g. bitmap/CSC-with-value-index; conversion timed once and reported separately, never inside the per-call number — same discipline as spmv-csr-kernel).
warmup20
reps100 per (matrix, density) cell
statisticmedian (report min/max/stdev alongside)
timerdevice-side events (CUDA/HIP) or std::chrono per iteration, one timestamp pair per call, never a single pair around a batched loop
timing_scopekernel only (candidate-generation/filtering + accumulate + output-compaction), H2D/D2H excluded. If the technique performs runtime KERNEL SELECTION as part of every call (e.g. LiAY21's ML-based selector), that selection cost (feature computation + model inference) is INCLUDED in this per-call number and reported as its own line item (selection_overhead_ms) alongside the total — this fixes the common failure mode of amortizing away an adaptive framework's per-call decision cost, and matches LiAY21's own (better-than-average) practice of always including it.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: format/bitmap conversion time, plus (if used) any load-balancing preprocessing (LiAY21's "load-balanced" kernel family redistributes nonzeros before the main kernel runs).
output_allocationREQUIRED disclosure: how the implementation sizes/allocates the output buffer for y, since nnz_y is not known in advance. Three legitimate strategies exist in this track's literature and must be named explicitly: (a) dense M-length buffer, sparse-populate (BLEST's bitmap approach — implicitly "dense" allocation, O(M) memory regardless of nnz_y), (b) worst-case sparse buffer sized to an upper bound (e.g. sum of column nnz for touched columns) with a post-hoc compaction pass, (c) two-pass (count then allocate exact size then fill). The allocation strategy changes both peak memory and whether a compaction/atomic step appears in the timed kernel; this must be reported, not left implicit.
precisionfp32 (matches LiAY21); fp64 optional secondary. Boolean/bitwise semiring (BLEST's regime) is out of scope for THIS variant and covered by spmspv-bfs-frontier-trace instead.
metric
primaryGNZ/s = (nnz_x_effective_reads + output_nnz_writes) / time_seconds / 1e9 — nonzeros processed per second, a semiring- and precision-agnostic throughput unit chosen because neither surveyed paper's own metric (LiAY21's speedup-only; BLEST's ms/speedup-only) is directly comparable across the density range, and GFLOP/s is undefined for BLEST's Boolean kernels.
secondaryms (median); selection_overhead_ms (if the technique does runtime kernel selection, else 'n/a')
correctnessmax relative error vs. an independently computed fp64 dense reference (y = A*x computed with x's implicit zeros included, restricted to comparison at the positions the kernel actually returns as nonzero) < 1e-4 at fp32. In addition, the RETURNED SUPPORT (set of indices reported nonzero) must exactly match the reference's nonzero support — a value-only tolerance check without a support check would let an implementation silently drop or fabricate nonzeros and still "pass."
spmspv-bfs-frontier-tracethroughput across the REAL, non-uniform sparsity trajectory a level-synchronous BFS actually produces (frontier density rises then falls across levels, the "small-world bulge" BLEST's own numbers exhibit), as opposed to spmspv-density-sweep-kernel's synthetic uniform ramp — kept as its own variant because a technique tuned to do well on a smooth synthetic sweep is not guaranteed to do well on the bursty, workload-driven density sequence real graph algorithms generate, and this is the actual production use case for SpMSpV in this track (BLEST) and one of two real applications LiAY21 evaluates against.
inputs
suiteunion of benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml's bfs-kernel-real-graphs recommended_subset and BLEST's own custom SuiteSparse selection (|V|>=23M, |E|<=2^32-1)
selectiongraphs with a giant component and BFS diameter that produces >=8 distinct frontier levels, so the density trajectory has enough points to be meaningful
recommended_subsetcom-LiveJournal, com-Orkut, soc-LiveJournal1, GAP-road, GAP-web, GAP-twitter, uk-2005, it-2004, europe_osm, com-Friendster, webbase-2001, nlpkkt240
vector_operandx_0 = single source bit set (nnz_x=1); x_{i+1} = frontier of BFS level i+1, derived from x_i via the SpMSpV call itself (this variant is inherently sequential across levels, unlike spmspv-density-sweep-kernel's independent density cells) — same 64-fixed-seed-random-root protocol as benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml's bfs-kernel-real-graphs.
protocol
formatsame as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel; bitmap/BVSS-style layouts allowed and their construction timed once per graph, reported separately
warmup1 full BFS (discarded)
reps64 full BFS traversals (64 roots), matching benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml
statisticper-level nnz_x/nnz_y and per-level SpMSpV time recorded for EVERY level of EVERY traversal (not just a summary number) so the density trajectory itself is reportable, plus median end-to-end BFS time across the 64 roots for a single comparable headline number.
timerdevice-side events or std::chrono around each per-level SpMSpV call
timing_scopeper-level kernel calls only; graph load/format construction excluded and reported once (preprocessing_reported below); H2D/D2H of the output parent/level array excluded (matches benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml's bfs-kernel-real-graphs timing_scope).
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per graph: format/bitmap construction time, any reordering time, same discipline as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
output_allocationsame disclosure requirement as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
precisionBoolean/bitwise semiring is the PRIMARY mode here (matches BLEST); arithmetic fp32/fp64 semirings are optional secondary if the technique supports weighted BFS-like traversal
metric
primaryGTEPS (edges connecting frontier vertices to their parents / time_seconds / 1e9), matching benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml's definition so BFS-as-SpMSpV numbers are directly comparable to the bfs track's own numbers
secondaryper-level (nnz_x, nnz_y, GNZ/s) trace; end-to-end BFS time (ms, median of 64)
correctnesssame validation_level=2-equivalent gate as benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml (reached-vertex set and parent validity checked against an independent reference BFS), since the operation here IS a BFS; the per-level value-correctness check from spmspv-density-sweep-kernel does not apply (Boolean semiring has no numeric tolerance to check).
spmspv-e2e-preprocend-to-end throughput including one-shot structure construction (format conversion, bitmap/BVSS packing, or load-balancing preprocessing), amortized over k=100 calls at a FIXED representative density (10%, chosen as a realistic mid-sparsity operating point neither fully sparse nor fully dense) — the construction-cost analogue of benchspecs/spmv/spec.yaml's spmv-e2e-preproc, needed here because BLEST's BVSS structure and LiAY21's load-balancing preprocessing are both nontrivial one-shot costs neither paper's own artifact clearly amortizes with a stated k.
inputs
suitesame as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
selectionsame as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
recommended_subsetsame as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
vector_operandnnz_x = 10% of K, fixed across all k=100 calls (same support, resampled values per call)
protocol
formatinput is raw CSR/COO; conversion to the technique's native structure (bitmap/BVSS/load-balanced layout) IS timed, once
warmup20
repsk=100 post-construction calls; report both the amortized number and the pure post-construction kernel time
statisticmedian
timersame per-platform per-iteration timers as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel, plus one bracket around the one-shot construction
timing_scopeconstruction + k kernel calls; H2D/D2H of the original matrix included once
preprocessing_reportedboth standalone (ms, once) AND amortized-per-call (construction_ms/k added to each call's time), same discipline as benchspecs/spmv/spec.yaml's spmv-e2e-preproc
output_allocationsame disclosure requirement as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
precisionsame as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel
metric
primaryGNZ/s (amortized: k*(nnz_x + output_nnz) / (construction_time + k*kernel_time))
secondaryms (construction, standalone, once); ms (per-call, pure post-construction kernel, median)
correctnesssame tolerance and support-match check as spmspv-density-sweep-kernel, checked post-construction
Fairness notes
  • BLEST's own root-selection procedure (`constructGreatSourceVertices`) actively filters BFS source roots to those with near-average per-root runtime before reporting numbers, which is a stronger and less disclosed selection effect than any single-paper root-selection bias already documented in benchspecs/bfs/spec.yaml. spmspv-bfs-frontier-trace fixes this by mandating the SAME 64-fixed-seed-random-root protocol as the bfs track, with no post-hoc filtering of which roots' results count.
  • LiAY21 explicitly measures and includes its adaptive framework's per-call kernel-selection overhead (5.2-7.2% average, up to 14%) in every reported number — better practice than most of the SpMV track's papers, which never surface conversion/search cost at all. This spec requires the same disclosure (selection_overhead_ms) from every technique tested under spmspv-density-sweep-kernel, not just adaptive ones, so a non-adaptive fixed-kernel baseline's "free" selection cost (zero) is visibly comparable to an adaptive technique's non-zero cost.
  • Neither paper reports the OUTPUT nonzero-count/allocation strategy explicitly as a first-class experimental variable, even though it materially affects both peak memory and whether a compaction pass appears inside the timed region. All three variants above make output_allocation a mandatory disclosure field.
  • BLEST reports ms/speedup only (no GTEPS anywhere in the fetched text) and LiAY21 reports speedup/accuracy only (no absolute throughput number at all) — neither paper's own metric is usable as a cross-paper common denominator. GNZ/s is introduced here specifically because it is well-defined for both the Boolean (BLEST) and arithmetic (LiAY21) semirings this track spans, which GFLOP/s is not.
Open questions
  • Neither paper's exact correctness/validation method could be confirmed from the fetched sources (BLEST: an `OutputVerifier.cuh` exists but its check level is unconfirmed; LiAY21: no correctness/tolerance discussion was retrievable from the fulltext). The correctness clauses above are this spec's own fairness-driven default (value tolerance + exact support match), not derived from either paper's stated practice.
  • LiAY21's 2,010-matrix SuiteSparse set is used only to TRAIN its ML kernel selector, not as a reported-benchmark suite; whether a selector trained on that set generalizes to spmspv-density-sweep-kernel's recommended_subset (drawn from the spmv track's suite, not LiAY21's own 18-matrix test set) is an open question this spec cannot resolve without re-running LiAY21's training pipeline.
  • The exact semiring/output-format BLEST's BVSS structure supports beyond plain BFS reachability (e.g. whether it generalizes to weighted or multi-source SpMSpV) could not be confirmed from the fetched arXiv HTML; spmspv-bfs-frontier-trace assumes Boolean BFS only.
sparse-format-conversion1 papers2 variants

Converting a sparse matrix from a source storage format (CSR/COO as loaded) to a target format optimized for a downstream sparse kernel (here: SpMM), covering both the pure conversion throughput and the end-to-end, format-selection-amortized usage pattern this track's one surveyed paper (LiteForm) actually implements.

target_format = convert(source_format, A[M,K]); optionally target_format_selection = select(A) when the target format itself is chosen automatically per-matrix (LiteForm's CELL-vs-BCSR classifier + CELL partition-count regressor + bucket-config search).

sparse-format-conversion-kernelsteady-state, format-pair-specific conversion throughput (nnz/s), source format given/loaded, target format's construction timed in isolation from any downstream SpMM call — the "just the conversion" number this track's axis list asks for, which LiteForm's own artifact does not report as a standalone metric (it only reports conversion-stage wall time as part of a 3-stage preprocessing breakdown ahead of an SpMM run, never isolated on its own).
inputs
suitereal GNN adjacency matrices, reused verbatim from LiteForm's own artifact
selectionLiteForm's own NAMES list: cora, citeseer, pubmed, ppi, arxiv, proteins, reddit (7 named matrices; the artifact's SuiteSparse-scale download tooling exists but its own end-to-end driver does not exercise it, so this spec does not claim broader coverage than what was actually run)
recommended_subsetall 7 (small enough to run exhaustively)
format_pairs[CSR -> CELL (SparseTIR column_part_hyb, ELL-style partitioned hybrid)], [CSR -> BCSR]
protocol
warmup5
reps20
statisticmedian (report min/max) — no per-call repetition/statistic is defined for the conversion stage alone in LiteForm's own artifact (it is timed once via time.perf_counter per matrix); this is a deliberate strengthening
timerhost wall clock (time.perf_counter or equivalent), single-threaded host-side conversion
timing_scopeconversion only: source format assumed already resident/parsed; downstream SpMM kernel execution excluded
cache_statenot applicable (host-side conversion); GPU-side buffer allocation for the target format IS included in the timed region
format_selection_reportedif the target format is itself chosen automatically (as in LiteForm's own CELL-vs-BCSR classifier), the selection-model inference time and any partition/bucket-config search time are reported as two SEPARATE line items, never merged into the conversion-time number — directly matching LiteForm's own 3-stage timing breakdown (predict_format_selection / predict_num_partitions / search_bucket_config), generalized into a spec requirement rather than an artifact-specific detail.
metric
primarynnz/s = nnz(A) / conversion_time
secondaryms; construction memory footprint (bytes) of the target format relative to the source format's bytes, as a density/overhead ratio
correctnessroundtrip: convert source -> target -> back to source-equivalent (CSR), and require the recovered (row,col,val) multiset to match the original bit-exact for indices and within 1e-12 relative error for fp64-stored values / 1e-6 for fp32 (this roundtrip check is NOT present in LiteForm's own artifact — see notes_on_fairness — but is required by this track's own axis definition). Additionally, for formats whose only defined use is as an SpMM operand (e.g. CELL, which is not naturally invertible to CSR without extra bookkeeping), an equivalent check is required: SpMM(target_format, x) must match SpMM(source_format via a reference kernel, x) within the tolerance of sparse-format-conversion-e2e-amortized's correctness gate below.
sparse-format-conversion-e2e-amortizedend-to-end throughput: one-shot format selection + conversion + partition/bucket-config search, amortized over k repeated SpMM calls on the same matrix — this is what LiteForm's own released driver (drive05.spmm.end-to-end.sh -> proc05.spmm.end-to-end.py) actually measures, so k and the pipeline stages are reproduced from it rather than invented.
inputs
suitesame as sparse-format-conversion-kernel
selectionsame as sparse-format-conversion-kernel
recommended_subsetsame as sparse-format-conversion-kernel
dense_operandSpMM right-hand-side matrix width N reported per LiteForm's own artifact convention (feature-dimension sweep not fully recoverable from the files read — see open_questions); fp32, U(-1,1)
protocol
pipeline_stages_timed_separately(1) format selection (RandomForest classifier inference), (2) partition-count prediction (RandomForest regressor inference, CELL path only), (3) bucket-config search (CELL path only), (4) format construction/conversion, (5) k SpMM calls post-construction — matches LiteForm's own predict_format_selection/ predict_num_partitions/search_bucket_config/build_hyb_format/ bench_hyb_with_config split, generalized into an explicit 5-stage spec requirement.
cache_stateL2 cache flushed before every timed SpMM call (FLUSH_L2=ON, matches LiteForm's own driver env var) — a cold-cache discipline this spec keeps as the default rather than relaxing to warm-cache, since it is the only cache policy any file in this artifact states explicitly
warmup10
repsk=50 post-construction SpMM calls (this track's own choice; LiteForm's artifact delegates per-call timing/repetition internally to sparsetir_artifact.profile_tvm_ms, whose own warmup/rep convention was not confirmed from the files read — see open_questions)
statisticmedian (report min/max) over the k calls
timerdevice-side kernel time (CUDA events) for stage 5; host wall clock (time.perf_counter, matching LiteForm's own instrumentation) for stages 1-4
timing_scopetwo numbers reported: (a) amortized end-to-end (stages1-4_time + k*spmm_time)/k per call, and (b) pure post-construction SpMM time alone (median over k), so a reader can see both "what a cold-start user pays" and "steady-state kernel speed" without one number hiding the other.
preprocessing_reportedstages 1-4 each reported standalone (ms, once) AND folded into the amortized number per timing_scope above
metric
primaryamortized GFLOP/s (2*nnz*N / ((stages1-4_time + k*spmm_time)/k)) and pure-kernel GFLOP/s (2*nnz*N/spmm_time, stage 5 alone)
secondaryms per stage (1-4, standalone); ms per SpMM call (median, stage 5)
correctnessSpMM output vs. cuSPARSE fp32 CSR SpMM reference: max relative error < 1e-4 (LiteForm's own artifact does not state a numeric tolerance in the files read — this value is this spec's own choice, flagged in open_questions). Additionally requires the format-selection model's decision itself to be logged per matrix (CELL vs. BCSR), since a wrong selection that still passes numeric correctness would silently understate the technique's real-world reliability if only aggregate throughput were reported.
Fairness notes
  • LiteForm's own driver ships tooling to download the ~900GB full SuiteSparse collection but its actual released end-to-end benchmark only runs 7 named GNN graphs (cora/citeseer/pubmed/ppi/arxiv/proteins/ reddit). This spec's `selection` fields state that scope explicitly rather than let the presence of the download script imply a broader evaluated suite than what the paper's own pipeline actually exercises.
  • No roundtrip (target-format-back-to-source) correctness check exists anywhere in the reviewed artifact. sparse-format-conversion-kernel adds one as a mandatory gate (or an SpMM-equivalence check for non-invertible formats like CELL), since this track's own axis definition specifically calls for roundtrip correctness and the surveyed paper's artifact does not provide it.
  • LiteForm's own artifact already separates format-selection, partition-count-prediction, and bucket-config-search time from SpMM kernel time — a stronger preprocessing-disclosure practice than most other tracks' surveyed papers. This spec keeps that 3-way (extended to 4-way, folding in format construction) split rather than collapsing it into a single "preprocessing" number, to preserve that useful granularity.
  • No numeric correctness tolerance for the SpMM output is stated anywhere in the files read; the 1e-4 relative-error value in this spec is this spec's own choice, not derived from the paper.
Open questions
  • Exact warmup/repetition/statistic convention of sparsetir_artifact.profile_tvm_ms (the external timing helper LiteForm's own benchmark delegates SpMM-kernel timing to) was not confirmed — that package was not vendored in this repo and was not read directly; this spec's own k=50/median choice for the amortized variant should be reconciled against profile_tvm_ms's actual behavior before treating results as literally reproducing LiteForm's numbers.
  • The dense right-hand-side operand width N used in LiteForm's own end-to-end SpMM benchmark (a standard SpMM parameter, analogous to the "feature dimension" in GNN message passing) was not confirmed from the files read — `CostModelSettings.feat_size` exists in the code but its concrete swept values were not seen in the excerpt read.
  • Whether `bench_naive`'s baseline is cuSPARSE itself, a plain unpartitioned ELL/CSR SpMM, or something else was not confirmed from the files read; the paper's own "2.06x over cuSPARSE" headline claim (per this track's one-liner) could not be traced to a specific baseline function in the code excerpts reviewed.

dense LA

gemm35 papers4 variants

Dense general matrix-matrix multiplication (including uniform-shape batched GEMM and small-scale distributed GEMM); quantized/int8 GEMM is explicitly out of scope (see the quantized-gemm track).

C[M,N] = alpha*A[M,K]*B[K,N] + beta*C[M,N] (beta=0 unless noted); row-major storage by convention of this spec (papers surveyed used a mix of row-/column-major and NN/NT/TN/TT layouts — the harness must record which layout each measured run used, since LibShalom shows NT materially outperforms NN for some irregular shapes on the same hardware).

gemm-square-kernelsteady-state kernel throughput on large/near-square dense GEMM, preprocessing (allocation, JIT/codegen, autotuning search) excluded from the timed region but reported once, separately. This is the common-denominator "textbook HPC GEMM" variant most surveyed papers report in some form (WuZLHJWC23, CA3DMM's per-rank number, CL-DB-GEMM's "around 2048"/multiples-of-128 sweep, fBLAS, Tensile-FGPS/DGEMM).
inputs
suitesynthetic square and near-square dense GEMM
selectionunion of the surveyed papers' large/square sweeps: WuZLHJWC23's 1024-6144 (step 512) square set, CL-DB-GEMM's "multiples of 128" and "multiples of 129" (tile-boundary/padding stress) sets, plus two extra padding-stress points (+1 offset) at the 2048 and 4096 scale applying the same "multiples of N+1" idea CL-DB-GEMM already uses at smaller scale. Fixed list below, not sampled.
recommended_subsetM=N=K in {128, 256, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048, 2049, 2560, 3072, 3584, 4096, 4097, 4608, 5120, 5632, 6144} (16 sizes; the 2049/4097 points are the padding-boundary stress tests). On FPGA targets whose systolic/streaming design ties matrix size to on-chip tile size (fBLAS's convention: N = 5x tile size), substitute the platform's own tile-derived size for the 4 largest entries and record the substitution — do not silently reuse the CPU/GPU list where it doesn't fit the design.
dense_operandprecision in {fp64, fp32, fp16} (int8/quantized excluded — see quantized-gemm track); operands initialized U(-1,1) (this spec's choice; surveyed repos used U(0,1) (LibShalom) or 2*drand48() = U(0,2) (MPGEMM) with no stated rationale, so standardizing here does not contradict any paper's specific finding but is a genuine change from common practice — flagged in notes_on_fairness).
protocol
preprocessingone-shot: buffer allocation/H2D residency, any JIT/codegen compile (relevant for LIBXSMM-style JIT libraries and autoGEMM-style codegen baselines), and any autotuning search (Tensile, CL-DB-GEMM's BO tuner) happen once before the timed region and are reported separately, never amortized into per-call time. This directly follows autoGEMM's own practice of excluding LIBXSMM's JIT time "for fairness" and FastKron's separate "Autotuning Time" report.
warmup10
reps50 (min 20 if a single call exceeds 50ms wall time, to bound total harness time; max 500 if a single call is under 0.1ms, to keep the median statistically meaningful — this generalizes MPGEMM's manual per-size nreps scaling (500/100/20 reps for M=64/128/4096) into an explicit rule instead of an ad hoc per-shape choice)
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside)
timerper platform class: NVIDIA/AMD GPU - device-side kernel time (CUDA events, or the ROCm/Tensile KernelTime convention used by Tensile-FGPS) with the host synchronized before/after; CPU/ARM - host wall-clock via a monotonic clock (matches MPGEMM's dClock() pattern); FPGA/OpenCL - OpenCL profiling-event kernel time (the implied CLBlast convention CL-DB-GEMM inherits). Async-queue leakage into adjacent timed regions must be prevented by an explicit sync.
timing_scopekernel only; H2D/D2H and any data (re)distribution excluded (matches CA3DMM's own "matmul only" sub-metric, generalized to single-device variants here).
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once, before the steady-state loop
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (2*M*N*K / time)
secondaryms (median, min, max)
correctnessmax relative error vs. a same-precision-family vendor BLAS reference (cuBLAS/rocBLAS on GPU, MKL/OpenBLAS/ARMPL/Accelerate on CPU) computed at fp64: < 1e-6 for fp64 kernels (near machine epsilon, sanity check only), < 1e-3 for fp32, < 1e-2 for fp16. None of the 9 surveyed papers state a numeric tolerance (several only assert "compared against cuBLAS" with no number) — this spec fixes explicit values to close that gap; a run that fails this gate does not count toward the reported throughput.
gemm-small-irregular-kernelsteady-state kernel throughput on small and irregular (tall-skinny / long-rectangular) GEMM shapes sourced from real scientific and DNN/LLM workloads, with cache state as an explicit reported axis. This is the variant where the literature most disagrees on scope (hot vs. cold cache changes rankings by up to 2x per LibShalom), so both states are required, not one.
inputs
suiteunion of LibShalom (SeisSol/Nekbox-derived small cubic shapes), WuZLHJWC23's irregular sweep (K fixed, M/N swept), autoGEMM's small range plus ResNet-50-derived shapes, and MPGEMM's DeepSeek/LLaMA linear-layer shapes.
selectionM=N=K <= 128 (small/cubic class) OR (one of M,N <= 512 AND K >= 256) (irregular/skinny class) — matches the union of ranges the 4 source papers actually swept (LibShalom [8,120], autoGEMM [1,128], WuZLHJWC23 irregular M,N in [64,490] with K in {256,1024}, MPGEMM's M=64/128 with N,K up to 32768).
recommended_subsetsmall/cubic: (8,8,8), (16,16,16), (24,24,24), (32,32,32), (64,64,64), (96,96,96), (120,120,120), (128,128,128) (LibShalom/autoGEMM range, 8 points). irregular/skinny, K fixed at 256 and 1024 (WuZLHJWC23): (M,N) in {(64,64),(128,128),(256,256),(384,384),(490,490)} x {K=256, K=1024} (10 points). LLM-linear-layer shapes (MPGEMM, verbatim from the artifact's benchmark driver): (M,N,K) in {(64,2112,7168), (64,24576,1536), (64,32768,512), (64,7168,16384), (64,4096,7168), (64,7168,2048)} (6 points). 24 total named shapes.
dense_operandprecision in {fp64, fp32, fp16}; U(-1,1)
protocol
cache_stateboth reported, not one: "hot" (operands resident in the fastest cache level that fits them before the timed loop starts, i.e. repeated calls reuse the same buffers back-to-back — LibShalom's Fig. 7 setup) and "cold" (a companion buffer larger than LLC is touched between each timed call to evict the operands, or K is padded to a size that guarantees LLC eviction as in LibShalom's K=5000 trick — LibShalom's Fig. 8 setup). Report both numbers for every shape; do not average across cache states.

warmup10
reps100 (small kernels are fast and noisy — this is deliberately higher than the square-kernel default, closer to LibShalom's use of a min-max bar over reps, but larger than LibShalom's own 10 since 10 reps is too few for a stable median)
statisticmedian (report min and max)
timersame per-platform rule as gemm-square-kernel
timing_scopekernel only; explicit cache_state control is part of the timed region by construction (see cache_state above)
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once
metric
primaryGFLOP/s
secondaryms (median, min, max), reported per cache_state
correctnesssame tolerances as gemm-square-kernel
gemm-batched-kernelsteady-state throughput of uniform-shape batched GEMM (same M,N,K across the batch, independent problems, no data reuse across batch elements), preprocessing excluded. Thin in the literature (only 2 of 9 surveyed papers exercise it with real numbers) but explicitly in scope per this track's definition ("dense GEMM incl. batched").

recommended_subset(batch=8, M=N=K in {32,64,96,128,160,192,224,256,320,384,448,512, 576,640}); (batch=64, same M=N=K list); (M=N=K=128, batch in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096}).

gemm-distributed-e2eend-to-end distributed dense GEMM across multiple nodes/GPUs, including one-shot input/output data redistribution, amortized over k=10 runs (k chosen to match CA3DMM's own example CLI usage, `ntest=10`, which is the only concrete k found in this track's survey); the kernel-only "local matmul" component is also reported separately, since CA3DMM's own tool already computes this split internally.
inputs
suitedistributed dense GEMM, arbitrary M=N=K
selectionsquare problems large enough that per-rank local GEMM dominates redistribution cost at the smallest tested scale, matching CA3DMM's own example sizing rationale
recommended_subsetM=N=K in {4000, 8000, 16000}; process counts in {8, 24, 64} (single node through small multi-node, matching the 24-rank single-node example CA3DMM ships in its own README)
dense_operandprecision fp64 (DGEMM, matches CA3DMM's own MKL-backed default); fp32 optional if the artifact supports it
protocol
preprocessingone-shot process-grid setup and any static communication-plan construction; NOT the per-run data redistribution (that is inside the timed e2e region below, since it happens on every run in CA3DMM's own design, not once)
warmup1 full run (matches CA3DMM's own "Initialization" vs. "Number of executions" split, where the first call includes MPI warm-up costs the tool itself separates out)
reps10 (k=10, explicit and reported; matches CA3DMM's own example `ntest=10` — this is the amortization count called for by the design instructions whenever preprocessing is amortized)
statisticmean over the k=10 reps (this is CA3DMM's own built-in statistic — kept as-is here rather than forced to median, since the tool does not expose per-run raw samples in its default output; an open question for the harness implementation is whether to patch the tool to emit per-run samples so median/min/max can be reported like the other three variants)
timerMPI-synchronized wall clock (MPI_Wtime or equivalent), matching CA3DMM's own internal timers
timing_scopetwo numbers per run, both reported (CA3DMM computes both natively): "local matmul only" (kernel-only, excludes redistribution/comm) and "total execution" (end-to-end, includes A/B/C redistribution, allgather, and reduce-scatter communication phases)
preprocessing_reportedprocess-grid/plan setup reported separately, once; per-run redistribution is NOT preprocessing here and stays inside "total execution" every run (see claim above)
metric
primaryaggregate GFLOP/s (2*M*N*K / total_execution_time, summed across ranks) and per-rank GFLOP/s (matches CA3DMM's own reported unit, 64.40 GFlops/rank in its README example)
secondaryms, broken into the phase breakdown CA3DMM already prints (redistribute, allgather, local compute, reduce-scatter)
correctnessCA3DMM's own binary pass/fail validation flag (0 error(s) required); this spec additionally requires the numeric tolerance from gemm-square-kernel be checked wherever the harness can access raw output (the tool's built-in check does not surface a numeric error value, only a pass/fail count — open question whether to patch it)
Fairness notes
  • Every surveyed paper except CA3DMM and MPGEMM (via its separate correct.x/singlePerformance.x binaries) times correctness-checking code inside or right next to the performance loop, or doesn't state whether it does. This spec keeps correctness checking as a separate, un-timed gate before any run's throughput counts, following CA3DMM's and MPGEMM's own (better) practice rather than the track's modal practice.
  • Best-of-N ("min") is the most common statistic in this track's own artifacts (WuZLHJWC23's implied averaging aside, MPGEMM and FastKron both explicitly take a min). Min is optimistic — it reports the best run, not typical behavior, and is more exploitable by a paper's authors than by an independent reproducer. The spec uses median (reporting min/max alongside) for all three single-device variants; only the distributed e2e variant keeps CA3DMM's native mean because the tool doesn't expose raw per-run samples to compute a median from without patching it.
  • autoGEMM's own paper excludes competing baselines from platforms they don't support (LibShalom on M2/A64FX) rather than reporting a failure or a 0. This spec requires reporting "N/A (unsupported)" explicitly per (baseline, platform) cell rather than omitting the row, so a benchmark table can't be quietly pruned to hide baseline failures.
  • LibShalom's hot/cold cache-state distinction is the single most consequential methodological detail found in this survey for the small/irregular shape class (other papers in the track target exactly this shape class — autoGEMM, MPGEMM, WuZLHJWC23's irregular sweep — but none of them mention cache state at all, meaning their reported numbers are for whichever state their loop happened to produce, unstated and possibly inconsistent across their own baseline-vs-proposed comparisons). Making cache_state an explicit, both-reported axis in gemm-small-irregular-kernel is this spec's most significant fairness fix relative to track's own common practice.
  • Matrix initialization ranges (U(0,1) vs. U(0,2) vs. unspecified) differ across artifacts with no stated rationale in any of the 9 surveyed sources. Standardizing to U(-1,1) in this spec is a deliberate choice to avoid any accidental one-sided bias in accumulation, not a correction of a specific error found in any one paper.
Open questions
  • Exact statistic (mean/median/min) used by Tensile's library-client benchmark reporting (LiYTLZ22/Tensile-FGPS) is not visible in the surveyed repo README; would need Tensile's own documentation or source to confirm before treating its GFLOPS numbers as directly comparable to this spec's median-based numbers.
  • Whether Tensile-FGPS's final published numbers re-enable NumElementsToValidate (disabled, =0, in the sample auto-tuning-search config found in the repo) is unconfirmed from available sources.
  • CL-DB-GEMM/CLBlast's exact OpenCL timer mechanism (profiling-event kernel time vs. host-side wall clock around clFinish) was inferred from CLBlast conventions, not confirmed by reading the C++ client benchmark source in this survey pass.
  • autoGEMM's precision (fp32 assumed) and exact warmup/repetition counts were not recoverable from the extracted PDF sections available in this survey; would need the full paper body (tables/figures not captured by text extraction) to pin these down.
  • fBLAS's exact repetition count behind its "99% CI within 5% of mean" claim is not stated; would need the paper's appendix or the evaluation/ scripts in the repo (not read in this pass) to confirm.
  • No source surveyed gives a numeric correctness tolerance; the values in this spec (1e-6/1e-3/1e-2 by precision) are this spec's own choice, not derived from any paper, and should be revisited against actual reproduction runs once the harness exists.
  • fp64 batched GEMM has no evidence in this track's survey (both batched-GEMM sources, Tensile-FGPS and CL-DB-GEMM, use fp64/mixed and fp16/fp32/fp64-separate-sweeps respectively but neither shows a concrete fp64-batched number) — kept as optional in the spec rather than required.
  • CA3DMM's own tool does not expose raw per-run timing samples in its default output (only the mean over ntest runs), which is why the distributed e2e variant cannot use the median statistic the other three variants use without first patching the artifact.
quantized-gemm16 papers4 variants

Fused (or explicit) dequantize-then-multiply GEMM for LLM linear layers: a full/half-precision activation matrix times a low-precision weight matrix (INT4/W3/FP6/FP8/INT8, optionally per-group or MX-block scaled), measured across the batch-size axis from memory-bound decode to compute-bound batched/prefill regimes, with model-level accuracy (perplexity delta) reported as a mandatory companion to every speed number, never as an afterthought.

C[M,N] = A[M,K](fp16/bf16 activation, row-major) * B[K,N](quantized weight). B is stored packed at b in {3,4,6,8} bits per element (uniform or MX-microscaled), with per-group (default group=128 columns of K) or per-block scale factors s[K/group, N]. Dequantization of B to fp16/bf16 happens either FUSED inside the GEMM kernel (the dominant pattern: MARLIN, Tilus, FP6-LLM, QFactory, Quantix, ZipServ) or as a SEPARATE pre-pass producing a dense fp16 B' consumed by a standard dense GEMM (the naive/explicit baseline every fused kernel is compared against). variant qgemm-w8a8-mx additionally quantizes A (both operands in FP8 E4M3, MX block-scaled).

qgemm-w4a16-decode-kernelsteady-state fused-dequant kernel throughput in the memory-bound small-batch decode regime (batch=1..32), preprocessing (weight packing/quantization) excluded and reported separately once.

correctnessrecommended (not hard-enforced, see open_questions): flag any (format, group_size) combination with PPL delta > 0.5 points as "accuracy-compromised" in the report -- speed numbers for such configs must be reported alongside this flag, never presented alone.
Fairness notes
  • MixQ's headline throughput number is a full autoregressive decode loop through the whole model (tokenizer/attention/KV-cache/sampling included), not an isolated GEMM kernel time -- never compare it directly against MARLIN/Tilus/MXBLAS kernel-only numbers; the spec keeps qgemm-w4a16-* strictly kernel-only for this reason.
  • MARLIN's own benchmark script syncs the GPU only once before a 10-iteration timed loop (not per-iteration), explicitly to hide launch-overhead the way a real inference server's queued kernel launches would -- this is a deliberate design choice in MARLIN's own repo, but it produces a systematically lower/noisier per-call time than a properly CUDA-event-timed rep; the spec requires CUDA events with L2 flush per rep instead, at the cost of not reproducing MARLIN's literal README numbers exactly.
  • MXBLAS explicitly disables L2 cache flushing (flush_l2=False) in its benchmark utility -- repeatedly reusing the same weight tile across 100 iterations lets it stay L2-resident, overstating throughput relative to a real multi-tenant server; the spec mandates L2 flush before every timed rep across all three kernel variants.
  • No paper in this track publishes speedups across the full batch range with a stated crossover point; FP6-LLM's own numbers (1.06x at batch=8 down to 0.94x at batch=32 vs. one baseline) show speedup is batch-dependent and can invert. qgemm-w4a16-batched-kernel makes the crossover batch a required reported statistic, not an optional curve.
  • Only FP6-LLM and MixQ report model-level accuracy as a first-class artifact; the other 8 papers with retrievable protocol report only speed. qgemm-model-accuracy is mandatory in this spec specifically to close that gap, per the task's explicit accuracy-alongside-speed requirement.
  • Bit-serial arbitrary-precision kernels (APNN-TC, QGTC) use synthetic square/small-N shapes with no connection to any real LLM and quantize via INT1-primitive bit-decomposition, a fundamentally different implementation strategy from every group-scaled dequantization kernel above -- folding them into the LLM-shaped variants would force an apples-to-oranges shape suite onto them, so they are excluded from the mandatory variants (see open_questions for how to score them anyway).
  • Magicube (quantized SpMM/SDDMM on a sparse operand) and QIGen (CPU/AVX2, no GPU) are both real artifacts in this track but exercise a different operand shape (sparse) or hardware (CPU) than the dense-GPU GEMM variants above; they are out of scope for qgemm-* but should get their own track-crossing entries (sparse-quantized-gemm, cpu-quantized-gemm) if this benchmark suite grows.
Open questions
  • No surveyed paper states a field-consensus perplexity-delta threshold for 'still acceptable' quantization; 0.5 PPL points on WikiText2 is this spec's own judgment call (informally common in the GPTQ/AWQ literature) and should be revisited against a wider literature read before being enforced as a hard gate rather than a flag.
  • Quantix's (PPoPP'26) artifact repo has essentially no README content and its paper is paywalled (no arXiv preprint found); its exact GEMM shapes, timing protocol, and correctness tolerance could not be recovered. It is folded into the W3/W4 weight_formats set on the assumption its 3-bit non-uniform scheme fits the qgemm-w4a16-* variants' shape suite, but this has not been verified against the actual paper.
  • How to fairly score the bit-serial APNN-TC/QGTC family (arbitrary 1-8 bit BOTH operands via INT1 decomposition) against the group-scaled-dequant family (MARLIN/Tilus/FP6-LLM/MXBLAS) is unresolved -- they solve a related but not identical problem (uniform low-bit x low-bit vs. low-bit-weight x fp16-activation) and a shared shape suite may not be meaningful. Left as a candidate 5th variant for a future spec revision rather than forced in now.
  • ZipServ's lossless (bit-exact) compression sits structurally between qgemm-w4a16 (fused decompress+GEMM pattern) and a pure systems paper (no accuracy loss, so qgemm-model-accuracy is trivially a delta of exactly 0) -- included in qgemm-w4a16-decode-kernel's protocol shape but its correctness gate should really be exact bit-reconstruction, not the 1e-3 relative-L1 tolerance; this spec does not yet special-case it.
  • MXBLAS-scale (M,N,K up to 8192 square, Hopper-only WGMMA/TMA) shapes were only partially folded into qgemm-w8a8-mx's recommended_subset (as 3 square stress shapes) rather than the full 7-model-family list in MXBLAS's shapes_def.py, to keep the suite union tractable; a full merge is a reasonable extension.
cholesky8 papers4 variants

Dense/tile Cholesky factorization of a symmetric positive-definite (SPD) matrix (or covariance operator), spanning four claims this track's own literature treats as genuinely different: plain dense fp64 tile Cholesky (single-node and distributed/communication-optimal), tile low-rank (TLR) Cholesky for formally-dense but data-sparse operators, and mixed/adaptive- precision (FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8, plus INT8 for a non-Cholesky sub-kernel) tile Cholesky on CPU and GPU tensor cores.

A[N,N] (SPD) = L[N,N] * L[N,N]^T, tile-blocked (block size NB, tile count N/NB per dimension); TLR variants additionally compress off-diagonal tiles to rank <= r under an accuracy threshold before/while factoring; mixed- precision variants cast individual tiles or diagonal bands to a lower precision before the same tile-blocked factorization.

cholesky-dense-single-node-fp64-kernelsteady-state single-node (shared-memory) dense tile Cholesky factorization time, fp64, with tile size (NB) as a required, per-run-disclosed parameter rather than a silently fixed constant — the single clearest lesson from KwasniewskiKBZS21 (paper 1 in the survey), where 3 of 4 baselines only beat COnfLUX/COnfCHOX after the paper's authors hand-tuned NB. Matrix generation is preprocessing, excluded from the timed region but reported once. This is the entry point most reproducible without a multi-node allocation; it is smaller in scope than the distributed variant below because most of this track's own papers (paper 1-paper 5, paper 8) only report distributed-scale numbers even though the underlying binaries (hicma-x's testing_potrf_tlr, exageostat's dmle drivers) run on 1 node.
inputs
suitesynthetic random dense SPD matrices (matches KwasniewskiKBZS21's generation method; a covariance-generator alternative from STARS-H is used by the TLR/mixed-precision variants below, kept separate here since this variant targets the plain-dense baseline)
selectionsquare SPD, single-node-feasible sizes (fit in one node's RAM at fp64: N^2*8 bytes < ~80% of node memory); union of KwasniewskiKBZS21's lower sweep range and SalvanaAHLSGK21's largest shared-memory (univariate-equivalent) point.

protocol
tile_sizerequired, disclosed per run; sweep NB in {256, 512, 1024} plus one deliberately off-heuristic value (NB=128) to demonstrate sensitivity, following KwasniewskiKBZS21's own artifact practice of sweeping four block sizes per (N,P) config and paper 2/paper 5's b=O(sqrt(N)) heuristic (report the heuristic-predicted NB alongside the swept values, do not silently pick only the heuristic point).
preprocessingone-shot: matrix generation/allocation, and any library-internal tile-layout setup, happen once before the timed region and are reported separately, never amortized into per-call time.
warmup1 full factorization (JIT/first-touch-page-fault effects, matches the general spec convention; no surveyed paper states a warmup count for this variant since paper 1's artifact does 5 runs with no separately-flagged warmup)
reps5 (matches KwasniewskiKBZS21's artifact-documented "five runs gathered for statistics" — the only concrete rep count found in this track for a single-node-adjacent sweep)
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside)
timerhost wall-clock (std::chrono or equivalent monotonic clock), matching KwasniewskiKBZS21's own timer choice
timing_scopekernel only; factorization time excludes matrix generation and any pre-factorization symmetrization/copy
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once, before the steady-state loop
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (N^3/3 flops, standard dense-Cholesky FLOP count)
secondaryms (median, min, max)
correctnessnormalized residual test ||A - L*L^T||_F / (||A||_F * N * eps_fp64) < 30 (the standard LAPACK/ScaLAPACK-testsuite normalized-residual threshold; none of the 8 surveyed papers state a numeric residual tolerance for the plain-dense case, so this spec adopts the field- standard test rather than inventing one). A run that fails this gate does not count toward reported throughput.
cholesky-dense-distributed-fp64distributed (multi-node) dense tile Cholesky at scale, reporting both time-to-solution and aggregate communication volume, with block size AND process grid (P x Q) as required disclosed parameters — this is the variant KwasniewskiKBZS21 (paper 1) is purpose-built for, and the one where the whole track's tile-size-tuning divergence (see notes_on_fairness) is most consequential, since 3 of 4 of paper 1's own baselines are only competitive after manual tuning.

primaryaggregate GFLOP/s (N^3/3 / time, summed across the run)
secondaryms; communication volume (elements/processor); theoretical I/O-cost-model comparison (% deviation from the N^3/(P*sqrt(M)) bound)
correctnesssame normalized-residual test as cholesky-dense-single-node-fp64-kernel (||A - L*L^T||_F / (||A||_F * N * eps_fp64) < 30), computed on a gathered or distributed-checked residual. This is a spec addition: paper 1's own paper validates only the I/O-cost *model*, not the numerical factorization result, so this gate is new relative to the track's own practice for this specific paper but consistent with paper 2/paper 5's residual- checking practice elsewhere in the track.
artifact_notetarget eth-cscs/conflux (the paper's maintained, BSD-3-Clause successor), not anonymousSC21/SC21 (an unmaintained, unlicensed anonymized-submission snapshot) — see survey.md's discussion of paper 1's artifact repos.
cholesky-tlr-lowrank-kerneltile low-rank (TLR) Cholesky factorization of a formally-dense, data-sparse SPD operator (covariance matrix or 3D RBF-interpolation operator), with TLR accuracy threshold AND tile size both required, swept, disclosed parameters. Compression (dense->TLR) time is measured and reported separately from factorization, following paper 2's own practice of showing compression can dominate once factorization itself is fast.
inputs
suiteSTARS-H-generated synthetic covariance matrices (2D/3D exponential/Matérn kernels), matching the CPU-side generator shared by CaoAPBLKD22 (paper 2), CaoPABLKD21 (paper 5), MondalAL0GK22 (paper 8), and SalvanaAHLSGK21 (paper 7); plus the real Middle-East wind-speed dataset (n=116,100, WRF-derived) shared by AbdulahCPBDGKLS22 (paper 3) and SalvanaAHLSGK21 (paper 7) as a real-data cross-check.
selectiontwo size tiers reflecting this track's own single-node-vs- distributed split: a small/medium tier (single-node feasible, matches paper 8's own shared-memory sweep) and a large tier (distributed, matches paper 2/paper 5's weak-scaling sweep). Accuracy threshold swept over the union of values this track's papers actually use: {1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5, 1e-7, 1e-8, 1e-9}.
recommended_subsetsmall/medium tier (single-node): N in {8100, 32400, 116100 (real Middle-East wind dataset)}. Large tier (distributed): N in {1080000, 2160000} (matches paper 2/paper 5's primary sweep points), with an optional stretch point at N=11880000 (paper 5's weak-scaling ceiling).
dense_operandfp64, RBF shape parameter or Matérn correlation length set to the generator's default mid-range value, disclosed per run
protocol
tile_sizerequired, disclosed per matrix size; use the b=O(sqrt(N)) heuristic from paper 2/paper 5 (report the concrete NB value derived, e.g. N=1.49M -> NB~4880 per paper 2's own worked example) plus one off-heuristic comparison point, matching cholesky-dense-single-node-fp64-kernel's tile-size-sensitivity requirement.
accuracy_thresholdrequired, swept over {1e-3, 1e-5, 1e-7, 1e-9} at minimum (matches paper 5 and paper 8, the two papers in this track that sweep it most rigorously), with 1e-8 as the headline/default point (matches paper 2's --check examples, paper 4's headline, paper 5's default).
preprocessingone-shot dense-matrix generation is preprocessing (excluded, reported separately). Dense->TLR compression is NOT folded into this preprocessing bucket — it is measured and reported as its own separate breakdown, following paper 2's Fig. 11 practice, since paper 2 shows it can dominate wall time once factorization is TLR-accelerated.
warmupnone beyond the single measured run per config (matches paper 2/paper 5's own "at least three times, minimum reported" practice structurally — this spec keeps 3 runs but changes the statistic, see below)
reps3 (matches paper 2's and paper 5's stated minimum rep count)
statisticmedian (report min and max) — deviates from paper 2/paper 5's own stated practice of reporting the minimum of 3 runs, per this spec's general fairness principle against best-of-N reporting.
timerhost wall-clock (matches paper 2/paper 5's std::chrono-based timers)
timing_scopepure factorization time-to-solution, excluding both matrix generation and dense->TLR compression (both reported separately, see preprocessing above)
preprocessing_reportedtwo separate one-shot numbers: matrix generation, and dense->TLR compression (the latter is the track-specific breakout paper 2 introduces and this spec preserves as mandatory, not optional)
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (effective, based on realized flop count after compression, not the formal dense N^3/3 count — matches paper 2's own roofline/critical-path-efficiency framing)
secondaryms; memory footprint (GB, vs. dense fp64 baseline); speedup vs. an Exact/dense-fp64 same-code-path reference
correctnessPRIMARY (required) gate: numerical backward error against the accuracy_threshold — paper 5 gives the concrete relationship found in this track (1e-8 threshold -> ~1e-9 absolute solution error); a run whose backward error exceeds its declared accuracy_threshold does not count. SECONDARY (reported, not gating): downstream statistical quality vs. a pure-dense-fp64 (Exact) reference — parameter-recovery boxplots and MSPE, following paper 3/paper 7/paper 8's practice — reported because for this track's geostatistics papers the inference result, not the factor's per-element error, is what ultimately matters (see survey.md's Divergences section; dropping this secondary check would hide a real methodological signal the track's own papers care about).
cholesky-mixed-precision-kernelmixed/adaptive-precision tile Cholesky (FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8, CPU or GPU tensor-core), with the precision-ASSIGNMENT STRATEGY itself (not just the resulting FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8 fractions) as a required, disclosed parameter, since paper 3/paper 4's band-percentage scheme and paper 6's tile-centric adaptive-decision scheme are structurally different rules that happen to produce comparable-looking fraction numbers — reporting only the fractions without the assignment rule would make cross-paper comparison meaningless (the same lesson as paper 1's tile-size finding, generalized to precision assignment).
inputs
suitesame STARS-H synthetic covariance generator as cholesky-tlr-lowrank-kernel; real datasets: Middle-East wind speed (n=116,100, paper 3/paper 7) and, for the GPU/tensor-core sub-case, the UK BioBank GWAS kernel-ridge-regression matrix from LtaiefACRSKDBAK24 (paper 6), N=305,880 (real) with a synthetic scaling series beyond it.
selectionunion of paper 3's real/synthetic sweep, paper 4's weak-scaling sizes up to the largest matrix that fits in pure FP64 given per-node HBM2, and paper 6's GWAS/KRR sizes; capped at a tier tractable without a full- machine Gordon-Bell allocation, with a stretch tier for sites with larger access.
recommended_subsetCPU/distributed tier: N in {116100 (real wind dataset), 1000000, 4000000}. GPU tensor-core tier: N in {305880 (real UK BioBank GWAS), 1000000}, with an optional stretch point at N=13000000 (paper 6's synthetic scaling ceiling).
dense_operandprecision configs, both required as named, disclosed strategies (do not report a bare fraction without naming which of these two produced it): (a) band-percentage vector "aD:bS:cH" (percent of matrix bands in Double/Single/Half), swept at {100D (fp64 reference), 10D:90S, 1D:99H} (paper 3/paper 4's own named points); (b) tile-centric adaptive decision (per-tile precision chosen at runtime by thresholding local numerical content against machine epsilon, paper 6's scheme), reported as "adaptive" with the resulting realized FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8 fractions logged per run, not fixed in advance. For the GPU/KRR sub-case only, INT8 tensor cores are used for the Euclidean-distance matrix-GENERATION step (paper 6) — kept segregated from the floating-point Cholesky/GEMM operands, not pooled into the same GFLOP/s number.
protocol
tile_sizerequired, disclosed per run, same b=O(sqrt(N)) heuristic convention as the TLR variant; paper 4's headline used a fixed NB=800 at N~=? without re-deriving the heuristic — this spec requires stating which of the two (heuristic-derived vs. fixed) was used.
band_sizefor the band-percentage strategy, BAND_SIZE per precision level is itself a disclosed, per-precision-tuned parameter (matches paper 3's own "tried several band sizes ... kept only the ones showing some difference"); report the swept range and the value used.
preprocessingone-shot matrix generation and any precision-assignment decision pass (the adaptive strategy's tile-classification step) are preprocessing, excluded from the timed factorization, reported separately once.
warmup1 full factorization (no surveyed paper in this cluster states a warmup count — this is a spec addition, flagged as an open question below for the actual protocol used at Gordon-Bell scale)
reps3 (this spec's own choice, since paper 3/paper 4/paper 6 do not state a rep count for their at-scale headline numbers — flagged as an open question; smaller, single-node-feasible points in this variant's recommended_subset SHOULD use 5 reps like the dense variants)
statisticmedian (report min and max); no surveyed paper in this cluster states a statistic for the at-scale numbers, so this is a spec default, not a track convention.
timerhost wall-clock for CPU/distributed runs; device-side kernel timers (synchronized) for the GPU tensor-core sub-case
timing_scopekernel-only factorization (and, for the GPU/KRR sub-case, the separately-reported matrix-generation "build" phase using INT8, following paper 6's own build-vs-factorize split)
preprocessing_reportedmatrix generation and the precision-assignment/classification pass, each separately, once
metric
primaryGFLOP/s (N^3/3 flops, uniform unit across this whole track despite papers reporting Tflop/s, PFlop/s, or ExaOp/s at their respective scales — a scale artifact, not a methodological disagreement, per survey.md's Divergences section)
secondaryms; speedup vs. a same-code-path pure-FP64 (100D) baseline run at the same N/tile size; memory footprint reduction vs. that baseline
correctnessPRIMARY (required) gate: numerical residual/backward error vs. a pure-FP64 same-code-path reference, computed at FP64 accumulation; tolerance scaled to the coarsest precision present in the run's assignment (1e-2 if any FP8/INT8 tile is present, 1e-3 if the coarsest is FP16, 1e-6 if FP32-only, 1e-12 if 100D). None of paper 3/paper 4/paper 6 state a raw per-element residual tolerance (see below) — these thresholds are this spec's own addition, needed to keep this variant's gate comparable to the residual-based gate used by every other variant in this track's spec, and should be revisited once real reproduction runs exist. SECONDARY (reported, not gating): downstream statistical quality vs. the 100D/Exact reference — parameter-recovery, MSPE, log-likelihood (paper 3/paper 4), or MSPE + Pearson correlation of KRR-predicted phenotypes vs. ground truth (paper 6) — the track's own primary validation practice for this precision family (see survey.md's Divergences section), kept as mandatory secondary reporting since it is the quantity these papers' own claims are actually built on.
Fairness notes
  • Tile/block size is treated as a required, disclosed, swept parameter in every variant, never a silently fixed constant. This directly follows paper 1's finding that 3 of 4 baseline libraries (MKL, SLATE, CANDMC/CAPITAL) only become competitive after hand-tuning block size, while only COnfLUX/COnfCHOX ship good out-of-the-box defaults — an undisclosed tile size would make any cross-implementation comparison in this track meaningless.
  • Timing statistic is fixed to median (with min/max also reported) across every variant. This diverges from the track's own modal practice: minimum-of->=3-runs is most common (paper 2, paper 5, and implicitly paper 1's I/O-cost validation), paper 7 uses mean-of-3, and paper 1's own artifact documents five runs with no stated statistic. Minimum is optimistic (reports the luckiest run); this spec's fairness principle prefers median.
  • TLR/HODLR accuracy threshold is a required, swept axis (not a single fixed value) in the TLR variant, mirroring paper 5 and paper 8's own practice — the two papers in this track that treat it most rigorously — rather than the single-fixed-value practice of paper 2's default (1e-4) or paper 4's headline (1e-8) taken in isolation.
  • Precision-ASSIGNMENT STRATEGY (band-percentage vs. tile-centric adaptive), not just the resulting FP64/FP32/FP16/FP8 fractions, must be disclosed per run in the mixed-precision variant, since paper 3/paper 4's scheme and paper 6's scheme are structurally different rules and reporting only a fraction number without the rule would make results look comparable when they are not.
  • Correctness is split into a required PRIMARY numerical residual/ backward-error gate (present in every variant, closer to paper 1/paper 2/paper 5's own practice and to this project's general fairness principles) plus, for the TLR and mixed-precision variants only, a SECONDARY downstream statistical-quality report (parameter recovery, MSPE, MLOE/MMOM, prediction correlation) matching what paper 3/paper 4/paper 6/paper 7/paper 8 actually validate against in their own papers. Neither is dropped: a residual-only report would hide the signal these application papers actually care about, and a statistical-quality-only report (the track's own majority practice for this family) would hide raw numerical error entirely.
  • Metric unit is normalized to GFLOP/s (via the standard N^3/3 dense-Cholesky FLOP count) across every variant, even though the surveyed papers report Gflop/s (paper 1, implicitly), Tflop/s/PFlop/s (paper 3, paper 4), and ExaOp/s (paper 6) at their respective problem scales. This is a scale artifact of the problem sizes involved, not a real methodological disagreement (see survey.md's Divergences section), so unifying the unit does not misrepresent any paper's finding.
  • hicma-x's `--check` correctness-validation flag is used in every example CLI invocation shown in its own TESTS.md alongside performance-relevant flags, suggesting it may run inside the same timed invocation in practice. This spec's protocol requires it be excluded from the timed region (validated separately, before the reported time), which is a disclosed DEVIATION from how the artifact's own example scripts appear to invoke it, not a confirmed match to the track's practice (see open_questions).
Open questions
  • Exact statistic (mean/median/min) computed over paper 1's artifact-documented "five runs" is not stated in the paper text or the artifact README — resolving this needs `eth-cscs/conflux`'s actual benchmark-driver source (not fetched during the survey pass).
  • Warmup/repetition/statistic protocol for the at-scale Tflop/PFlop/ExaOp headline numbers in paper 3, paper 4, paper 6 was not recoverable from the extracted text — these are Gordon-Bell-class full-machine-allocation runs where a repeated-timing-loop protocol may not be practical/affordable at all; this spec's reps=3/median default for cholesky-mixed-precision-kernel is therefore this spec's own choice, not evidence from the papers, and should be revisited once a harness exists to test whether repeated runs at that scale are even feasible on the measurement machine.
  • Whether hicma-x's `--check` flag (backward-error validation) is timed inside or excluded from the reported time-to-solution in the papers' OWN numbers was not confirmed from the source excerpts read; the testing_potrf_tlr.c driver source itself would need to be read to confirm before the harness can safely assume the papers' own reported numbers exclude it (see notes_on_fairness).
  • paper 6's exact pure-FP64-only ExaOp/s baseline figure (needed to compute the same "speedup vs. 100D" number paper 3/paper 4 report) was not captured during the extraction pass — the abstract states "1.8 mixed-precision ExaOp/s" but not the matching pure-FP64 number; needed before this variant's "secondary: speedup vs. baseline" metric can be cross-checked against paper 6's own headline claim.
  • `ecrc/hicma-x`'s license is a custom "Other"/NOASSERTION license (not a standard OSI license), unlike `ecrc/exageostat` (BSD-3-Clause, though archived in favor of `ecrc/ExaGeoStatCPP`, not fetched in this survey) — worth resolving before this spec's TLR and part of the mixed-precision variant (both hicma-x-dependent) are used as the basis for a redistribute -able Phase 2 harness.
  • No surveyed paper states a numeric per-element residual tolerance for the mixed-precision case; the tiered thresholds in cholesky-mixed-precision-kernel's correctness section (1e-2/1e-3/1e-6/ 1e-12 by coarsest precision present) are this spec's own choice, not derived from any paper, and should be revisited against real reproduction runs once the harness exists.
eigensolver5 papers3 variants

Symmetric eigenvalue decomposition spanning three claims this track's own literature treats as genuinely different: dense single-GPU full-spectrum 2-stage EVD (tridiagonalize + divide-and-conquer + back-transform, with tile size and back-transform panel width as required disclosed parameters); distributed structured divide-and-conquer for the symmetric TRIDIAGONAL full-spectrum sub-problem (with deflation threshold as a required disclosed parameter); and polynomial-filtered PARTIAL-spectrum solves (k eigenpairs inside a disclosed interval, generalized or standard eigenproblem), with the matrix-power-kernel degree and the search interval itself as required, disclosed, spec-level parameters. Every paper in this 5-paper track is symmetric or symmetric-definite-generalized; no genuinely nonsymmetric eigensolver appears in this track's literature — this spec covers the symmetric case only and flags the nonsymmetric gap explicitly (see notes_on_fairness and open_questions) rather than fabricating a variant unevidenced by any surveyed paper.

Standard form: A[N,N] (symmetric) = Q[N,N] * Lambda[N,N] * Q[N,N]^T, Q orthogonal (Q^T*Q=I), Lambda diagonal with eigenvalues as its diagonal entries. Generalized form: A[N,N]*x = lambda*B[N,N]*x, A,B symmetric, B positive (semi)definite. FULL-spectrum variants compute all N eigenpairs (optionally with eigenvectors); PARTIAL-spectrum variants compute only the k eigenpairs whose eigenvalues fall inside a disclosed interval [lambda_lo, lambda_hi], via polynomial-filtered Krylov iteration built on a matrix-power kernel A^d*x (or a shifted/scaled operator's power) as the dominant per-iteration cost.

eigensolver-dense-symmetric-full-spectrum-kernelsteady-state single-GPU dense symmetric EVD, full spectrum WITH eigenvectors, via the standard 2-stage pipeline (dense -> band -> tridiagonal -> tridiagonal-eigensolve -> back-transform), with BLOCK SIZE and BACK-TRANSFORM PANEL WIDTH as required, disclosed CLI parameters and a MANDATORY per-stage timing breakdown — matches WangDZWZLJZ25 (tridiagonalization) and WangHZSJWDZ25 (back- transformation)'s own combined pipeline exactly (their successor artifact, ASE, implements both papers' contributions together and is this variant's primary source). WangDZWZLJZ25's own headline finding motivates the mandatory per-stage breakdown: on cuSOLVER, FP64 tridiagonalization alone consumes "over 97%" of total EVD time — a single end-to-end number would hide exactly the bottleneck this track's own papers are about.
inputs
suitedeterministic (fixed-seed) synthetic dense symmetric matrices, matches the ASE/cuEV successor artifact's bench.cpp generator (entries in (-1,1), symmetrized by mirroring the lower triangle); ADDITIONALLY, matching the same artifact's own test suite, three adversarial eigenvalue-structure cases: identity, repeated eigenvalues (engineered maximal deflation), and clustered (near-equal) eigenvalues (forces the divide-and-conquer secular- equation path) — these are correctness-suite inputs, not performance inputs, but this spec requires at least one performance run per adversarial case too, since a D&C-based tridiagonal eigensolve's cost is NOT input-independent (deflation changes the actual work done).
selectionsingle-GPU-feasible sizes; matches the successor artifact's own default sweep exactly, since it is this track's largest single-GPU-dense evidence point.
recommended_subsetN in {512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768} (matches the ASE/cuEV bench.cpp default sweep verbatim); adversarial cases at N in {96 (identity), 120 (repeated), a clustered case} per the same artifact's own test sizes
dense_operandfp64, matches both source papers exactly.
protocol
tile_sizeREQUIRED, disclosed, positional (not a flag with a silent default): block size `b` (default 32 per WangHZSJWDZ25's own EVD4SC2025 driver) and back-transformation panel width `nb` (default `4*b`). This variant adopts WangHZSJWDZ25's OWN enforcement mechanism (the CLI refuses to run without both) as the spec's disclosure requirement, the strictest tile-size enforcement found across this project's three dense-factorization-track surveys.
preprocessingone-shot: matrix generation happens once before the timed region, reported separately, never amortized into per-call time.
warmup1 full EVD (a spec addition — neither WangHZSJWDZ25's EVD4SC2025 driver nor the ASE/cuEV successor's bench.cpp has an explicit warmup call).
reps3 (matches the ASE/cuEV successor artifact's bench.cpp default `iters=3` exactly — the one concrete rep count with clear provenance in this variant's literature).
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside) — DEVIATES from the ASE/cuEV successor's own stated practice (`best = std::min(best, ms)`, explicit best-of-3), per this project's general fairness principle preferring median over best-of-N.
timerdevice-side event timer (CUDA events), matches both source artifacts' own timer choice exactly.
timing_scopekernel-only EVD time (all pipeline stages combined), REPORTED alongside a MANDATORY per-stage breakdown (DBBR / bulge-chasing / divide-and-conquer / bulge-chasing-back / SBR-back, matching the ASE/cuEV successor's own `--timing` flag output exactly) — this breakdown is REQUIRED, not optional, per this variant's claim rationale above; matrix generation is excluded and reported separately.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once.
metric
primaryGFLOP/s ((22/3)*N^3 / time — the field-standard LAPACK JobZ='V' full-symmetric-EVD-with-eigenvectors FLOP count, matches the ASE/cuEV successor artifact's own formula exactly)
secondaryms (median, min, max), both end-to-end and per-stage; memory footprint (MB)
correctnessTWO required, GATING measurements, run ALWAYS (not compile-time- gated) — a deliberate spec addition responding directly to WangHZSJWDZ25's own EVD4SC2025 artifact, whose correctness check is gated behind a `#if CHECH_EVD_RESULT_ENABLE` compile flag not confirmed to default on (see survey.md open_questions); this variant instead adopts the ASE/cuEV successor artifact's OWN fix (a separate, always-run test suite) as the spec's required practice: (1) reconstruction residual, `max|A - Q*Lambda*Q^T| / scale < 1e-10` where `scale = max|A_ij|` (matches the ASE/cuEV successor's own `solve_test.cu` convention: max-entrywise difference, normalized by input scale, NOT a Frobenius or spectral-norm ratio — chosen as this variant's primary convention since it is this track's most recently published, most thoroughly tested artifact's own choice); (2) orthogonality, `max|Q^T*Q - I| < 1e-10` (same source, same normalization-free max-entrywise convention). Both thresholds are a spec default (the source artifact uses a size-and-scale-dependent `tol_evec(scale)` function whose exact formula was not extracted during this survey — flagged in open_questions); eigenvalues are ADDITIONALLY required to be sorted and within a size-dependent tolerance of a reference LAPACK `dsyevd` computation on the same input, matching the ASE/cuEV successor's own reference-comparison practice exactly. A run failing any of these does not count toward reported throughput.
eigensolver-symmetric-tridiagonal-dc-distributeddistributed (multi-node) structured divide-and-conquer eigensolver for the symmetric TRIDIAGONAL full-spectrum sub-problem, with DEFLATION THRESHOLD K as a required, disclosed, per-matrix-tuned parameter alongside tile size — matches LiaoLLR21 (PSDC) exactly, the one distributed paper in this track and the natural companion to variant 1's dense-to-tridiagonal reduction stage (this variant picks up exactly where variant 1's tridiagonalization stage leaves off).
inputs
suitethree synthetic structured tridiagonal families (Clement, Hermite, Toeplitz — matches LiaoLLR21's own generators exactly, standard closed-form NLA test matrices) PLUS real matrices reduced to tridiagonal form via a prior dense-symmetric-EVD reduction step (matches LiaoLLR21's own SiO/Si5H12-from-SuiteSparse practice, reusing this track's variant-1 pipeline as the upstream reduction step for a genuinely real-data entry point).
selectionsquare symmetric tridiagonal, N up to LiaoLLR21's own tested range; real matrices matched to LiaoLLR21's own two SuiteSparse-derived points.
recommended_subsetsynthetic: N in {8192, 16384, 32768} (matches LiaoLLR21's own strong-scaling sizes) for each of {Clement, Hermite, Toeplitz}; real: SiO (N=33401), Si5H12 (N=19896), both from SuiteSparse, matching LiaoLLR21's own real-data points exactly; process counts P in {64, 256, 1024, 4096} (matches LiaoLLR21's own Table 3 sweep).
dense_operandfp64, matches LiaoLLR21 exactly.
protocol
deflation_thresholdrequired, disclosed per matrix: K (the secular-equation-size threshold above which PSDC's rank-structured technique activates). Report both a literature-matched value (K=20000 for the N=30000 synthetic case, K=15000 for the real-matrix case, matching LiaoLLR21's own two examples exactly) and confirm K is BELOW the matrix's own largest realized secular-equation size at the chosen NB (LiaoLLR21 reports this concretely for Si5H12: "the largest K... is 15,489 when NB=64").
tile_sizerequired, disclosed: NB (block size). Report NB=64 (matches LiaoLLR21's own selected value, after its own NB in {64,128,256} ablation) alongside one off-default comparison point, per this track's general tile-size-sensitivity convention.
