A batch with any slice failing either gate does not count toward reported throughput. This spec REQUIRES these checks be run at least once per (m, n, tupe, batching_strategy) configuration to validate the harness, matching this project's general fairness principle, even though the source artifact's own correctness path is disabled by default.
Fairness notes
  • Orthogonality (||Q^T*Q - I||) is REQUIRED, GATING correctness in every dense/batched variant of this spec (relaxed to non-gating-on-a-subset only for the sparse multifrontal variant, where forming Q explicitly is itself atypical usage) — despite NO paper in this 4-paper track computing it anywhere in a performance-measurement path. This is the single largest gap this survey found relative to the task's own design brief for this track (orthogonality named as the QR-specific mandatory correctness check), and is treated as a required spec addition, not an optional refinement, matching this project's "be an engineer, not a diplomat" principle.
  • Pivoting/reordering/batching STRATEGY (not just the resulting performance number) is a required, disclosed parameter in every variant, following the same principle already established across this project's cholesky and lu specs: PAQR/QRCP/unpivoted-QR strategy for the dense variant, AMD/COLAMD/METIS/NESDIS/adaptive reordering for the sparse variant, based/batched/streamed for the tensor variant. An undisclosed strategy choice would make cross-run comparison meaningless, the same lesson generalized from this track's siblings.
  • Timing statistic is fixed to median (with min/max reported) across every variant, diverging MORE sharply from this track's own literature than either the cholesky or lu specs had to: every one of this track's 4 papers is either single-shot (no repetition at all: PAQR's LAPACK arm, STM-QR, cuTensor-tubal) or explicit best-of-N (GPTuneCrowd's minimum-of-2/10) — no paper in this track states an averaging or median statistic anywhere. This is the least repetition-disciplined literature found across this project's three dense-factorization-track surveys so far.
  • Correctness-check-present-but-disabled-by-default is a pattern found in this track too (cuTensor-tubal's `#if 0`-guarded diff), matching an identical pattern already documented in this project's lu track (OpenMxP's `--checksum`) and cholesky track (hicma-x's `--check`) — this spec's REQUIRED (not optional) correctness gates across every variant are a direct response to this now-3-track-wide pattern, not just a per-track fix.
  • TSQR/CAQR and an explicitly tall-skinny-only benchmark point are NOT covered by any paper in this track's input set. Rather than fabricate evidence for an algorithm none of the surveyed papers implement, this spec's dense variant sweeps a tall-skinny SHAPE using the algorithms this track's papers DO implement (Householder/QRCP/PAQR), and flags the TSQR/CAQR gap explicitly in open_questions as a known limitation of this track's current paper coverage, to be revisited if the track's input set is expanded.
Open questions
  • SidLakhdarCBALGTJWDDA23 (PAQR)'s own forward-error/accuracy measurement methodology (presumably `matlab/src/test.m`) was not fetched during this survey pass — needed to confirm whether ANY orthogonality or backward-error check exists anywhere in this paper's own artifact, even outside the LAPACK/ScaLAPACK performance-measurement path this spec otherwise bases its protocol on.
  • LinYWT021 (STM-QR)'s full "~80% of SuiteSparse" evaluation matrix set (its own abstract's stated scope) is not reproducible from the 15-matrix demo list shipped in its artifact — this spec's recommended_subset is therefore a small, fully-reproducible fraction of what the paper itself evaluated, not the paper's own full scope.
  • ZhangLWW20 (cuTensor-tubal) has no ready-to-run sweep script for t-QR specifically (unlike t-product/t-FFT in the same artifact) — the exact (m, n, tupe) sweep used to produce the paper's own reported t-QR figures was not recoverable; this spec's recommended_subset is adapted from the artifact's t-product/t-FFT sweep pattern, not confirmed against the paper's own t-QR numbers.
  • ChoDKLLL23 (GPTuneCrowd)'s ScaLAPACK PDQRDRIVER `THRESH` value used in its own reported PDGEQRF-tuning results was not confirmed from the extracted source — this spec's adoption of 30 (matching this project's other residual thresholds) is a spec default, not confirmed evidence.
  • Whether this track's assigned 4-paper input set omitting TSQR/CAQR entirely reflects a genuine gap in the underlying corpus (i.e. no TSQR/CAQR paper exists in the corpus this track's input was drawn from) or a narrower selection within a broader available set was not investigated during this survey pass.
lu3 papers3 variants

Dense tile LU factorization of a general (non-symmetric) matrix, spanning three claims this track's own literature treats as genuinely different: single-node/single-GPU blocked LU with the pivoting strategy itself (partial / tournament / none) as a required, disclosed parameter; distributed communication-optimal LU built on 2.5D tournament pivoting; and extreme-scale mixed-precision (FP16/FP32 factorization + FP64 iterative-refinement correction) no-pivoting LU in the HPL-AI benchmark family. Unlike Cholesky, LU's pivoting choice is not a minor implementation detail — it changes both asymptotic communication cost and the numerical safety argument, and none of this track's own papers report a growth factor despite pivoting strategy being exactly what growth factor is designed to diagnose.

A[N,N] (general, non-symmetric) = P[N,N] * L[N,N] * U[N,N], tile-blocked (block size NB, tile count N/NB per dimension), where P is a permutation determined by the run's pivoting strategy: partial pivoting (row-swap, LAPACK/ScaLAPACK-style, P re-derived at every column), tournament pivoting (block-recursive candidate-pivot selection via a butterfly/playoff reduction, P propagated as row-mask indices rather than physical swaps), or no pivoting (P = I, correctness relies on the input matrix being engineered well-conditioned and/or on post-hoc iterative-refinement correction rather than on P). Mixed-precision variants additionally cast the factorization to FP16/FP32 and correct the result to FP64 accuracy via iterative refinement (IR): r = b - A*x̃ (FP64), Ad̃ = r solved via the existing FP32/FP16 L,U factors, x̃ <- x̃ + d̃, repeated to convergence.

lu-dense-single-node-pivot-kernelsteady-state single-node (shared-memory or single-GPU) dense/blocked LU factorization time, with PIVOTING STRATEGY (partial / tournament / none) as a required, per-run-disclosed parameter alongside tile size — the central lesson of this track: KwasniewskiKBZS21's own baselines (MKL, SLATE) use partial pivoting while its own COnfLUX uses tournament pivoting, and MunksgaardHSO22's Rodinia-derived LUD case study uses no pivoting at all, relying instead on a specially-constructed well-conditioned input matrix. Reporting a bare GFLOP/s number without the pivoting strategy that produced it is the LU-specific analogue of Cholesky's undisclosed-tile-size problem (see cholesky/spec.yaml notes_on_fairness) and is treated with the same required-disclosure rule here.
inputs
suitetwo generators, matched to what this track's own no-pivot papers use, since a single arbitrary-random generator would make the no-pivot arm of this variant numerically meaningless: (a) a general random dense matrix U(-1,1) for the partial- and tournament-pivoting arms (pivoting makes this arm robust to an arbitrary matrix, so no special conditioning is required); (b) the Rodinia/Futhark well-conditioned generator (10*exp(-0.001*i) diagonal-decay construction, matches MunksgaardHSO22's lud-input.fut exactly) for the no-pivoting arm, since running no-pivot LU on an arbitrary random matrix would conflate "no pivoting is unsafe" with "this implementation is broken" rather than isolating the pivoting-choice comparison this variant is designed to make.
selectionsquare general (non-symmetric) matrices, single-node/single-GPU- feasible sizes (fit in one node's RAM or one GPU's HBM at the run's working precision); union of MunksgaardHSO22's three tested sizes and a size matched to KwasniewskiKBZS21's smallest reported point.
recommended_subsetN in {2048, 8192, 16384, 32768}
dense_operandfp64 for the partial-/tournament-pivoting arms (matches KwasniewskiKBZS21's precision); fp32 for the no-pivoting arm (matches MunksgaardHSO22's LUD case study exactly, so the no-pivot arm is directly comparable to its own literature source rather than to an invented fp64 no-pivot baseline this track's papers don't test)
protocol
pivoting_strategyrequired, disclosed per run: one of {partial, tournament, none}. Tile size (see below) MUST be reported alongside it, since tournament pivoting's cost is itself a function of the block size (see KwasniewskiKBZS21's Table 1: TournPivot communication cost v^2*ceil(log2(sqrt(P)+1)) is block-size-dependent even at P=1 conceptually, as v is the tunable reduction-block parameter).
tile_sizerequired, disclosed per run; sweep NB in {256, 512, 1024} for the partial-/tournament-pivoting arms (matches cholesky-dense-single-node-fp64-kernel's sweep for direct cross-track comparability); for the no-pivoting arm, additionally report the literature-matched block size NB=32 (MunksgaardHSO22's Futhark default) alongside the swept values, since the reference Rodinia implementation MunksgaardHSO22 itself compares against uses a DIFFERENT default (BLOCK_SIZE=16) — this spec requires the same NB be used for whatever two things are being compared in a given run, closing the block-size-mismatch gap documented in survey.md.
preprocessingone-shot: matrix generation/allocation, and any library-internal tile-layout setup, happen once before the timed region and are reported separately, never amortized into per-call time (matches this track's Cholesky-spec convention).
warmup1 full factorization (no surveyed paper in this arm states a warmup count; MunksgaardHSO22's own harness does not separate warmup from its 10 measured runs, so this is a spec addition to keep first-touch/JIT effects out of the measured statistic).
reps10 (matches MunksgaardHSO22's RUNS=10 default, the only rep count with a stated, concrete provenance found anywhere in this track).
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside) — deviates from MunksgaardHSO22's own stated practice (arithmetic mean of 10 runs), per this project's general fairness principle preferring median over mean/best-of-N (mean is less optimistic than best-of-N but still more sensitive to a single slow/fast outlier run than median).
timerdevice-side event timer on GPU runs (matches MunksgaardHSO22's Futhark/OpenCL-event-timer arm); host wall-clock (std::chrono or equivalent monotonic clock) on CPU runs (matches KwasniewskiKBZS21's timer choice). The two MUST NOT be mixed within a single reported comparison — this spec closes the device-timer-vs-host-timer mismatch documented in survey.md's Divergences section for MunksgaardHSO22's own Futhark-vs-reference comparison.
timing_scopekernel-only factorization time; excludes matrix generation and, for the no-pivoting arm, excludes any input-matrix well-conditioning setup (counted as preprocessing, not factorization).
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once, before the steady-state loop.
metric
primaryGFLOP/s ((2/3)*N^3 flops, standard dense-LU FLOP count, excluding the RHS solve — see notes_on_fairness for why this deviates from LuMOEJW22's own (2/3*N^3 + 3/2*N^2)-including-solve convention)
secondaryms (median, min, max)
correctnessTWO required, disclosed measurements, not one — this is a deliberate spec addition beyond what any of this track's 3 papers themselves report (none reports a numerical correctness signal for LU at all: see survey.md's Divergences section): (1) normalized backward-error residual ||PA - LU||_F / (||A||_F * N * eps) < 30 (same LAPACK/ScaLAPACK-testsuite-style threshold and normalization as this track's cholesky/spec.yaml, adapted to the PA=LU factorization residual since P is not always the identity here); (2) **growth factor** rho_N = max|u_ij| / max|a_ij|, REPORTED (not gating, since no surveyed paper states a numeric growth-factor threshold and the field-standard worst-case bound of 2^(N-1) for partial pivoting is almost never approached in practice, making a hard numeric gate uninformative) but MANDATORY to disclose per run, since growth factor is exactly the quantity that differentiates the risk profile of the three pivoting strategies this variant sweeps — a benchmark that reports only the residual (which will look fine on a well-conditioned test matrix regardless of pivoting strategy) would hide the entire point of this variant's pivoting-strategy axis. A run whose residual test fails does not count toward reported throughput; a run whose growth factor is anomalously large (rho_N > sqrt(N), a standard practical rule-of-thumb threshold, itself a spec addition not evidenced by any surveyed paper) is flagged in the report but not excluded, since growth factor alone does not certify or refute correctness.
lu-dense-distributed-tournament-pivotdistributed (multi-node) dense tile LU at scale using 2.5D communication-optimal tournament pivoting, reporting time-to-solution, aggregate communication volume, AND the extra communication/ computation cost pivoting itself imposes (separable from the rest of the factorization per KwasniewskiKBZS21's own Table 1 cost model) — this is the variant KwasniewskiKBZS21's COnfLUX is purpose-built for, directly paired with cholesky-dense-distributed-fp64 (same paper, same 2.5D decomposition, same artifact repo) but with pivoting as LU's one genuinely extra axis over Cholesky.
inputs
suitesame random-dense generator as lu-dense-single-node-pivot-kernel's partial-/tournament-pivoting arm
selectionsquare general matrices, weak-scaling sizes spanning single-node-infeasible up to a multi-node-but-not-full-machine range, matching cholesky-dense-distributed-fp64's own capped range for direct cross-track comparability (deliberately below KwasniewskiKBZS21's own N=524,288/P=512-node ceiling, since this project's Phase 2 does not require full-machine allocations).
recommended_subsetN in {16384, 65536, 131072, 262144}; process counts P in {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64} nodes, 2 MPI ranks/node (identical grid to cholesky-dense-distributed-fp64); a "large-scale" tier at N=524288, P up to 512 included as an optional stretch point matching KwasniewskiKBZS21's own headline sweep.
dense_operandsame as lu-dense-single-node-pivot-kernel's partial-/tournament-pivoting arm, fp64
protocol
pivoting_strategytournament (COnfLUX's own scheme); partial pivoting is reported as the baseline comparison point (MKL/SLATE's own scheme per KwasniewskiKBZS21's own text: "Both MKL and SLATE base on the standard partial pivoting algorithm using the 2D decomposition") — both arms are run so the pivoting-strategy comparison this track's own headline result is built on is reproduced, not just cited.
tile_sizerequired, disclosed per (N,P) combination; sweep 4 block sizes per combination (matches KwasniewskiKBZS21's own artifact protocol) and report which one is used for the headline number.
process_gridP x Q, P <= Q, as square as possible, matches cholesky-dense-distributed-fp64's convention; disclosed per run
preprocessingone-shot process-grid setup and matrix generation; excluded from the timed region, reported separately once.
warmup1 full factorization per (N, P, block-size) combination (matches eth-cscs/conflux's own "mandatory warm up round" documented in its README).
reps5 per combination (matches eth-cscs/conflux's README's "-r 5" flag, described there as "the number of repetitions").
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside) — deviates from this track's only stated-statistic evidence point (MunksgaardHSO22's mean-of-10), per this spec's general fairness principle; KwasniewskiKBZS21's own artifact states no statistic at all over its 5 runs (open question, matches the identical open question already flagged for this paper's Cholesky half).
timermax wall-clock time across all MPI ranks (matches KwasniewskiKBZS21's own reporting convention, identical to cholesky-dense-distributed-fp64)
timing_scopekernel-only factorization time; separately, aggregate communication volume (elements moved per processor) is measured via a profiler (Score-P or equivalent) and reported alongside a theoretical I/O-cost lower bound, following KwasniewskiKBZS21's own methodology for BOTH factorizations (validated to within +/-3% of measured for MKL/SLATE/COnfLUX/COnfCHOX in the paper's own results). ADDITIONALLY for this LU-specific variant: the pivoting step's own communication/computation cost is reported as a separate breakdown from the rest of the factorization (per-step cost model: TournPivot = v^2*ceil(log2(sqrt(P)+1)) communication, v^3/3*ceil(log2(sqrt(P)+1)) computation, from the paper's own Table 1), since this is the one cost component that has no Cholesky analogue and is otherwise invisible in an aggregate time-to-solution number.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once.
metric
primaryaggregate GFLOP/s ((2/3)*N^3 / time, summed across the run)
secondaryms; communication volume (elements/processor), split into pivoting and non-pivoting components; theoretical I/O-cost-model comparison (% deviation from the N^3/(P*sqrt(M)) bound, + the pivoting-specific O(N^2/P) term KwasniewskiKBZS21's own derivation adds on top of the shared Cholesky/LU leading term)
correctnesssame two-part residual + growth-factor test as lu-dense-single-node-pivot-kernel (||PA - LU||_F / (||A||_F * N * eps_fp64) < 30, gating; growth factor rho_N reported, non-gating), computed on a gathered or distributed-checked residual. This is a spec addition relative to the track's own practice for this paper: like its Cholesky half, KwasniewskiKBZS21's own paper validates only the I/O-cost *model*, not the numerical factorization result, for either factorization.
artifact_notetarget eth-cscs/conflux (maintained, BSD-3-Clause successor), not anonymousSC21/SC21 (unmaintained, unlicensed anonymized-submission snapshot) — identical artifact-targeting decision already made for this paper's Cholesky half; see cholesky/survey.md.
lu-mixed-precision-nopivot-ir-kernelextreme-scale mixed-precision (FP16 GEMM / FP32 panel-TRSM) no-pivot LU factorization, corrected to FP64 accuracy via iterative refinement (IR) rather than by pivoting — the HPL-AI benchmark family (LuMOEJW22's OpenMxP), a genuinely different claim from either pivoted-LU variant above: correctness here is a POST-HOC convergence property of the IR loop, not an a-priori pivoting-derived bound, and the metric convention (GFLOPS/GCD, EFLOPS at scale) and precision recipe (three distinct precisions, named per algorithmic stage) have no analogue in the other two variants.
inputs
suiteHigham-generator well-conditioned synthetic dense matrix (matches OpenMxP's higham_mat_impl.cpp exactly) — deliberately NOT the same generator as lu-dense-single-node-pivot-kernel's no-pivoting arm (which uses the simpler Rodinia diagonal-decay formula), since this variant's correctness mechanism additionally depends on IR convergence and should be evaluated against the literature's own matrix construction rather than a substituted one.
selectionmulti-node/multi-GPU sizes spanning what fits per-GCD memory up to a tier tractable without a full-machine allocation, with a stretch tier matching the paper's own near-full-machine points.
recommended_subsetN in {131072, 524288, 1368570 (LuMOEJW22's own headline Summit-partition size)}, with an optional stretch point matching the paper's Frontier-fraction scale.
dense_operandthree named precisions per algorithmic stage (not a bare fraction): diagonal-block factorization and panel TRSM in FP32; trailing-matrix GEMM in FP16 (accumulate FP32); residual computation and iterative-refinement correction in FP64 — matches OpenMxP's own recipe exactly (main.cpp's FHIGH=float/FLOW=__half convention).
protocol
pivoting_strategynone (by design; see operation and claim above).
tile_sizerequired, disclosed per run; report both the literature-matched default (B=2560, per OpenMxP's own README "Tuning Parameters" guidance: "the best B tends to be 2560") and one off-default comparison point, matching this track's general tile-size-sensitivity-disclosure requirement.
process_gridP x Q GPU grid, disclosed per run, PxQ = #GPUs (matches OpenMxP's own constraint documented in its README)
iterative_refinementrequired, disclosed per run: convergence threshold on the solution discrepancy (NOT confirmed from LuMOEJW22's own text — this spec provisionally adopts the standard HPL/HPL-AI residual-based stopping-test convention, flagged as unconfirmed in open_questions below) and the realized iteration count to convergence (a run-time outcome, not a fixed input, per the paper's own 3-step IR description).
preprocessingone-shot: matrix generation (via the Higham generator) and any precision-cast setup happen once before the timed region and are reported separately, never amortized into per-call time.
warmupone full application-scale warm-up run (matches LuMOEJW22's own documented practice: a dedicated warm-up mini-benchmark on Summit, or embedded small GEMM kernels at the start of the run on Frontier, per the paper's own "Warm up" subsection and Finding 10) — this is the one variant in this track's spec where warmup is a literature-evidenced, not spec-invented, requirement.
reps1 full-scale run (matches the paper's own practice: EFLOPS headline numbers are single full-machine-scale runs, not a repeated-timing- loop protocol, per survey.md; a repeated-timing-loop protocol is NOT required for reproduction at this variant's largest recommended_subset points, though it SHOULD be used at the smaller points where repetition is affordable — see reps convention for lu-dense-single-node-pivot-kernel).
statisticnot applicable at the largest scale (single run); median (report min/max) at smaller, repeatable scales, matching this track's general convention.
timerhost wall-clock around the full IR loop (not confirmed as the exact timer API from the extracted paper text; flagged in open_questions).
timing_scopethe reported EFLOPS/GFLOPS number covers factorization + IR correction together (per the paper's own metric definition, which already includes the RHS-solve term in its FLOP count); matrix generation and any warm-up runs are excluded and reported separately.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once.
metric
primaryGFLOPS/GCD = ((2/3)*N^3 + (3/2)*N^2)/time (matches LuMOEJW22's own formula exactly, INCLUDING the RHS-solve term - this is the one variant in this spec that keeps the paper's own FLOP convention rather than normalizing to the (2/3)*N^3-only convention used elsewhere in this track, since the RHS solve is not a separable optional step here but an integral part of what IR needs to run)
secondaryEFLOPS at full-system/partition scale; memory footprint per GCD
correctnessPRIMARY (required) gate: the IR loop's own convergence criterion — solution discrepancy below the run-declared threshold (see iterative_refinement above) — is itself the correctness gate for this variant, unlike the other two variants where residual is measured independently of how the factorization was computed. ADDITIONALLY, matching this track's general growth-factor-disclosure requirement: growth factor of the underlying (pre-IR-correction) no-pivot FP32/FP16 factorization is measured and REPORTED (not gating, since IR is the variant's actual safety net, not growth-factor control) — this isolates how much of the final accuracy is "the factorization was already fine" vs. "IR did the work," a distinction LuMOEJW22's own paper does not report but which this track's fairness principle (disclose the mechanism, not just the outcome) requires. NOTE: the artifact's own `panel_check.hpp` `--checksum` correctness path is construction-specific (only valid for the Higham generator) and is NOT enabled by default (see survey.md) — this spec requires it be run at least once per configuration to validate the harness itself, even though it is not part of the timed region.
Fairness notes
  • Pivoting strategy is treated as a required, disclosed, three-valued parameter (partial / tournament / none) in every variant, never a silently fixed implementation detail. This is the LU-specific analogue of this project's cholesky/spec.yaml tile-size-disclosure principle, directly motivated by KwasniewskiKBZS21's own text: its baselines (MKL, SLATE) use partial pivoting while its own COnfLUX uses tournament pivoting, and neither choice is a performance-neutral implementation detail — tournament pivoting has an explicit, non-zero, block-size- dependent extra communication/computation cost (Table 1 in the paper) that a bare GFLOP/s number would otherwise hide.
  • Growth factor is REQUIRED, DISCLOSED reporting (though not a hard gate) in every variant in this spec, despite NO surveyed paper in this track reporting it. This is a deliberate spec addition: the task's own design brief for this track calls out "residual+growth-factor correctness" as a key axis, and growth factor is precisely the quantity that would reveal whether a no-pivot run's apparent correctness (on a specially engineered, well-conditioned test matrix) would generalize to an arbitrary input — which none of this track's own 3 papers test, since both no-pivot papers (LuMOEJW22, MunksgaardHSO22) sidestep the question by construction rather than by measurement.
  • Timing statistic is fixed to median (with min/max also reported) in the two repeatable-scale variants, matching this track's Cholesky-spec convention and diverging from this track's only two stated-statistic evidence points: MunksgaardHSO22's explicit mean-of-10, and KwasniewskiKBZS21's stated-but-unspecified 5-run protocol. The extreme-scale mixed-precision variant is the one exception (single-run at its largest points), since LuMOEJW22's own paper documents that a repeated-timing-loop protocol is not what is measured at that scale.
  • Tile/block size must match between whatever two things are being compared in a single reported number, closing a specific gap found in MunksgaardHSO22's own artifact: its Futhark LUD implementation defaults to block size 32 while the Rodinia reference it is compared against defaults to block size 16, and the artifact runs each at its own default rather than a matched value.
  • Timer provenance (device-side event timer vs. host-side wall-clock) must be consistent within a single reported comparison, closing a second gap found in the same MunksgaardHSO22 artifact (OpenCL device-event timer for the Futhark arm, gettimeofday host timer for the Rodinia reference arm, feeding the same reported speedup ratio).
  • FLOP-count convention differs deliberately between variants: the plain-pivoted variants normalize to the RHS-solve-EXCLUDED (2/3)*N^3 convention (matches this track's cholesky/spec.yaml precedent and most LU-factorization-only literature), while the mixed-precision/IR variant keeps LuMOEJW22's own RHS-solve-INCLUDED convention, since the solve is an integral, non-optional part of what that variant's IR loop measures, not a separable add-on. Reported GFLOP/s numbers across variants are therefore NOT directly comparable without adjusting for this — flagged explicitly here rather than silently normalized away, since forcing a single convention would misrepresent what the mixed-precision variant's own metric is actually counting.
Open questions
  • CANDMC/CAPITAL's (KwasniewskiKBZS21's baseline libraries) pivoting strategy for LU is not stated in the extracted arXiv text - needed to complete this variant's pivoting-strategy comparison; the paper only gives author-supplied communication-cost models for these two libraries, not a described pivoting algorithm.
  • Exact statistic (mean/median/min) computed over KwasniewskiKBZS21's artifact-documented "5 runs" is not stated in the paper text or the eth-cscs/conflux README - identical open question already flagged in the cholesky spec for this paper's Cholesky half.
  • LuMOEJW22's iterative-refinement convergence threshold (the numeric value the solution discrepancy must fall below before IR stops) is not stated in the extracted OSTI PDF text. This spec provisionally assumes the standard HPL/HPL-AI residual-based stopping convention but this is NOT confirmed from the paper's own text or the OpenMxP source (iterative_refinement.hpp was not fetched during this survey pass) - should be resolved before lu-mixed-precision-nopivot-ir-kernel's correctness gate is used for real reproduction runs.
  • Whether LuMOEJW22's own reported EFLOPS headline numbers were measured with the `panel_check.hpp` `--checksum` correctness path enabled or disabled was not confirmed from the extracted text - the CLI flag exists and is construction-specific (only valid for the Higham generator), but the paper doesn't state whether it was active during the timed runs it reports.
  • MunksgaardHSO22's LUD case study has no correctness check anywhere in its shipped benchmark harness (Makefiles, .fut source, reference C++); whether the underlying Futhark/Rodinia implementations were separately validated (e.g. via `futhark test`) before the performance numbers in the paper were collected was not confirmed from the artifact alone.
  • The practical growth-factor stability threshold (rho_N > sqrt(N)) used as this spec's non-gating flag-for-review criterion is this spec's own choice, not derived from any of the 3 surveyed papers (none reports a growth factor at all) - should be revisited against real reproduction runs across all three pivoting strategies once the harness exists.
svd2 papers2 variants

Singular Value Decomposition, in this track's own form: t-SVD, the tensor generalization computed by applying an FFT along a tensor's 3rd (tube) mode and then computing k independent ordinary matrix SVDs of the resulting m x n frequency-domain frontal slices (k = batch/tube depth), followed by an inverse FFT. The track's two papers exercise the FULL (untruncated, one-shot, library-primitive) case and the TRUNCATED (low-tubal-rank, iteratively-called-inside-an-ALS-loop) case respectively — kept as separate variants below (see survey.md's Divergences).

T[m,n,k] = U[m,r,k] * S[r,r,k] * V[n,r,k]^T (per-frontal-slice, in the Fourier domain along the 3rd mode), where r=min(m,n) for the FULL case or r=target-tubal-rank < min(m,n) for the TRUNCATED case; computed as T_hat = fft(T, dim=3); for each of the k frontal slices, [U_hat(:,:,i), S_hat(:,:,i), V_hat(:,:,i)] = svd(T_hat(:,:,i)) (optionally truncated to rank r); U,S,V = ifft(U_hat,S_hat,V_hat, dim=3).

tsvd-full-batched-kernelsteady-state, one-shot FULL t-SVD (every singular value/vector of every frontal slice, no rank truncation) throughput on synthetic dense tensors, with the based/streamed/batched EXECUTION STRATEGY as a required, disclosed parameter (matching cuTensor-Tubal's own benchmark practice of sweeping all three), and BOTH square and tall-skinny frontal-slice shapes swept (the square-only practice both papers in this track actually use is called out explicitly as insufficient for this track's own "matrix shapes" key axis -- see notes_on_fairness).
inputs
suitesynthetic dense random tensors T(m,n,k), entries U(-1,1), matching both papers' own practice (no real/named dataset is used for the underlying t-SVD primitive by either paper in this track)
selectionSQUARE frontal slices m=n in {50, 100, ..., 500} (matches `CPU/testsvd.m`'s own confirmed sweep exactly) union {1000, 2000} (matches the GPU test.sh-confirmed upper range for the sibling t-FFT primitive, extended here to t-SVD); TALL-SKINNY frontal slices m:n in {4:1, 16:1} at m in {400, 1600} (a spec addition -- see notes_on_fairness, since neither paper's own fetched scripts exercise a non-square shape); batch depth k in {128, 256, 512, 1024} (matches `CPU/testsvd.m`'s own confirmed sweep)
recommended_subsetsquare: m=n=100, k=128, square: m=n=500, k=128, square: m=n=500, k=1024, square: m=n=2000, k=128, tall-skinny: m=1600,n=400 (4:1), k=128, tall-skinny: m=1600,n=100 (16:1), k=128
dense_operandfp64 (working assumption -- no fetched script confirms precision explicitly; flagged in open_questions)
protocol
formatdense tensor, row-major frontal slices; FFT along the 3rd mode is part of the timed t-SVD call (matching the library's own primitive boundary -- t-FFT is a SEPARATE primitive in this library and is not double-counted here, but the t-SVD call as exercised by this library's own test driver includes its own internal frequency-domain transform, not a pre-transformed input)
execution_strategyrequired, disclosed: one of {based, streamed, batched} (matches `GPU/test/test.sh`'s own literal CLI argument convention); "based" is the CUDA-stream-free reference GPU implementation (distinct from the CPU MATLAB reference), "streamed" parallelizes across frontal slices via CUDA streams, "batched" issues one batched-SVD-style call across all k slices at once -- report all three for every (m,n,k) point swept, not just the fastest, since this project's fairness principle disfavors reporting only a best-of-strategy number without disclosing which strategy produced it
warmup1 full t-SVD call before the timed sweep begins (spec addition -- see notes_on_fairness; the repo's own separate `GPU/test/warmup/` binary confirms a warmup concept exists in the codebase, but its placement relative to the per-config sweep in `test.sh` was not confirmed)
reps10 (spec default; the repo's own `test.cpp` drivers run each configuration exactly once with no loop, which this spec does not adopt -- see notes_on_fairness)
statisticmedian (report min/max)
timerdevice-side events (CUDA events) for the GPU path (a DEVIATION from the repo's own `clock()`-based timing -- see notes_on_fairness); host wall-clock (std::chrono) for the CPU MATLAB-equivalent reference path
timing_scopet-SVD kernel only (including its internal FFT/iFFT, per the library's own primitive boundary); host<->device transfer of the input tensor excluded
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once (device memory allocation)
metric
primaryGFLOP/s, using the standard batched-dense-SVD flop-count convention (per frontal slice: ~4*min(m,n)^2*max(m,n) + 8*min(m,n)^3 for a full SVD, summed over k slices, plus the FFT/iFFT flop count) -- a spec addition, since neither paper reports a GFLOP/s number; both report speedup only (see below)
secondaryms; speedup vs. the CPU MATLAB reference (dual 10-core Xeon, matching this paper's own baseline hardware/metric exactly, for direct reproduction of its 16.91-38.97x range across primitives); speedup vs. cuSOLVER/MAGMA batched-SVD as an ADDITIONAL required baseline this spec adds (see notes_on_fairness -- neither paper compares against a vendor batched-SVD library)
correctnessTWO required gates, since neither individually matches this track's "singular-value accuracy + orthogonality" pairing on its own: (1) orthogonality: max(||U^T U - I||_F, ||V^T V - I||_F) < 1e-10 per frontal slice (fp64); (2) singular-value accuracy: max relative error of the computed singular values vs. a reference batched-SVD call (cuSOLVER or MATLAB `svd`, computed independently of the based/streamed/batched execution-strategy code path under test) < 1e-10. This REPLACES cuTensor-Tubal's own practice of only cross-checking streamed-vs-based (its own two code paths against each other, with no external reference and no stated numeric tolerance) -- see notes_on_fairness for why an execution-strategy self-consistency check alone is not treated as sufficient evidence of correctness.
tsvd-truncated-completion-e2eend-to-end low-tubal-rank tensor completion via alternating minimization, where a TRUNCATED t-SVD (target tubal-rank r, a required, disclosed, swept parameter -- this track's accuracy/compression tolerance axis) is called once per iteration, amortized over the iterations needed to converge -- the variant the tensor-completion paper is purpose-built for.
inputs
suitesynthetic low-tubal-rank tensors with entries masked under BOTH a uniform (element-wise) sampling pattern and the paper's own motivating TUBAL-sampling pattern (whole tubes/fibers dropped together, not individual entries) -- both patterns included since the paper's own headline 7403x number is specifically a tubal-vs-uniform-sampling-algorithm comparison, not a general-sampling-pattern-agnostic number
selectionground-truth tensor T0(m,n,k) generated as a random low-tubal-rank product (rank r0 known exactly, so recovery error has a clean ground truth); m=n swept as in tsvd-full-batched-kernel's square case (a subset: 100, 500, 1000); sampling rate (fraction of observed tubes/entries) swept in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5}
recommended_subsetm=n=100, k=128, r0=10, sampling=0.3, tubal-sampling, m=n=500, k=128, r0=20, sampling=0.3, tubal-sampling, m=n=500, k=128, r0=20, sampling=0.3, uniform-sampling (ablation baseline), m=n=1000, k=128, r0=30, sampling=0.1, tubal-sampling
dense_operandtarget tubal-rank r for the truncated t-SVD sub-calls in {r0, 2*r0} (r0 = the exact planted rank, 2*r0 as an over-estimated-rank robustness point); fp64
protocol
formatdense tensor with a boolean observation mask; mask generation is preprocessing, excluded from the timed alternating-minimization loop, reported separately once
iteration_budgetk_iter=100 alternating-minimization sweeps as the default budget (spec addition -- neither paper states an iteration count or convergence criterion in the sources reached); report the break-even/convergence iteration count k* (smallest k_iter at which relative recovery error stops improving by more than 1e-4 between consecutive iterations) alongside the fixed-budget number
warmup1 full alternating-minimization run before the timed sweep (spec addition; not evidenced by either paper)
reps5 (spec default; not evidenced by either paper)
statisticmedian (report min/max) of the wall-clock time to reach convergence (k*) or, if not converged, of the k_iter=100 wall-clock time
timerdevice-side events (CUDA events) for the GPU path (a DEVIATION from the base library's `clock()`-based convention, for the same reason given in tsvd-full-batched-kernel's protocol)
timing_scopefull alternating-minimization loop (every truncated-t-SVD sub-call plus the surrounding update step); ground-truth/mask generation excluded and reported separately
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once (ground-truth tensor and sampling-mask generation)
metric
primarywall-clock time (s) to reach convergence (or the k_iter=100 budget); speedup vs. CPU MATLAB alternating minimization (matches the paper's own headline metric family: up to 248.18x reported), vs. GPU element-sampling (uniform- sampling-algorithm) tensor completion run on the SAME hardware (up to 7403.27x reported -- this is specifically an algorithm-vs-algorithm comparison under the SAME sampling pattern's data, not a hardware speedup, and must be reported as such, not conflated with the CPU-vs-GPU number), and vs. an external GPU matrix-completion (2D-only) system (up to 33.27x reported)
secondaryGFLOP/s (effective, using the truncated-rank r flop count, not the full-rank count -- a spec addition, neither paper reports this)
correctnessPRIMARY (required) gate: relative recovery error ||T_completed - T0||_F / ||T0||_F on the WITHHELD (non-observed) entries < 1e-2 (a spec addition -- the paper's own exact metric and tolerance were not recovered from the sources reached; 1e-2 matches this project's general convention for statistical/recovery-style gates on real-noisy-data-adjacent problems, as opposed to the 1e-10 tight numerical tolerance used in the full-t-SVD kernel variant above, because tensor completion from partial, possibly noisy observations is fundamentally an approximate-recovery problem, not an exact-numerical-identity one). A run whose recovery error exceeds this gate does not count toward reported speedup/timing.
Fairness notes
  • Both papers' own fetched scripts exercise SQUARE frontal slices only (m=n); this track's own key axes explicitly call for both square AND tall-skinny matrix shapes. The tsvd-full-batched-kernel variant adds tall-skinny shapes as a spec-level requirement rather than silently reproducing the square-only practice both papers actually use -- without this addition, this track's spec would inherit a real gap in the underlying papers' own evaluation coverage.
  • Neither paper compares its GPU t-SVD implementation against a vendor batched-SVD library (cuSOLVER's batched/strided-batched SVD APIs, MAGMA). cuTensor-Tubal's only baseline is its own CPU MATLAB reference; the tensor-completion paper's only external (non- ablation) baseline is an unnamed 2D matrix-completion system. This spec ADDS a cuSOLVER/MAGMA batched-SVD comparison as a required secondary metric in tsvd-full-batched-kernel, since a from-scratch hand-written batched-SVD implementation not compared against the vendor library it is nominally competing with is a real evaluation gap this project's fairness principle flags rather than reproduces.
  • cuTensor-Tubal's own correctness check (found directly in `GPU/test/tsvd/test.cpp`) only cross-validates its "streamed" output against its own "based" output -- two code paths of the SAME implementation, with no external ground truth and no numeric tolerance found in the fetched excerpt; the "batched" path has NO correctness check at all in the fetched code. This spec replaces that practice with an external reference (cuSOLVER/MATLAB `svd`) plus an explicit numeric tolerance for BOTH gates (orthogonality and singular-value accuracy) and for ALL THREE execution strategies, not just "streamed" -- an execution-strategy self-consistency check alone cannot catch a bug present identically in both "based" and "streamed" code paths, and provides no coverage at all for "batched".
  • The repo's own timing convention (`clock()`, single-shot, no warmup-per-config, no repetition loop) is replaced with this project's general convention (device-side events, explicit warmup, repeated + median-reported) in both variants -- a disclosed DEVIATION from the papers' own practice, not a claim that this matches how their headline numbers were actually produced (see open_questions in survey.md: `CPU/testsvd.m`'s fetched copy has its actual SVD call commented out, so even the paper's own script, AS FETCHED, would measure loop overhead rather than the algorithm -- reinforcing that this spec's own protocol, not a literal reproduction of the fetched script, is the right basis for a harness).
  • The tensor-completion paper's headline "7403.27x" figure is an algorithm-vs-algorithm (tubal-sampling-aware vs. naive element-sampling) comparison, not a hardware speedup number, and this spec's metric section requires it be reported and labeled as such -- conflating it with the CPU-vs-GPU hardware speedup number (248.18x) would misattribute an algorithmic improvement to a hardware one.
  • Full (untruncated) and truncated t-SVD are treated as separate variants rather than one variant with a rank parameter that happens to sometimes equal min(m,n), because the two papers in this track exercise them in genuinely different contexts (one-shot library primitive vs. iteratively-called ALS sub-kernel) with different correctness notions (numerical agreement vs. statistical recovery accuracy) -- collapsing them into one variant would obscure that difference (see survey.md Divergences).
Open questions
  • Neither paper's fulltext was reached (both closed-access; see survey.md) -- every protocol detail above not directly attributed to a fetched script is a spec addition, not evidence from the papers' own Methodology sections. This track's evidentiary base is thinner than every other track surveyed so far in this project.
  • The exact GPU model(s) used for either paper's headline numbers were not recovered.
  • Whether `CPU/testsvd.m`'s fetched copy (with its SVD call commented out) is a stale/debug artifact or reflects the actual script used for the paper's numbers is unresolved.
  • The tensor-completion paper's own concrete tensor sizes, sampling rates, target-tubal-rank values, and exact recovery-error metric/ tolerance were not recovered -- every concrete number in the tsvd-truncated-completion-e2e variant's `inputs`/`correctness` above is a spec-level default, not evidence-derived.
  • Whether cuTensor-Tubal's `test.sh`-confirmed t-FFT sweep pattern generalizes to its t-SVD-specific test driver was not independently re-confirmed (only `CPU/testsvd.m`'s MATLAB-side sweep was directly read for t-SVD specifically).
  • No public real (non-synthetic) dataset was found used by either paper for the core t-SVD/tensor-completion kernel itself; whether the papers' own headline application-level numbers (beyond the library-primitive micro-benchmarks) use any real tensor was not determined.
trsm2 papers2 variants

Triangular solve with multiple right-hand sides (TRSM), covering both a standalone single-call kernel across the full side/uplo/trans/diag layout matrix and a uniform-shape batched-CPU variant — the two claims this track's only TRSM microbenchmark (fBLAS) actually exercises. Distributed mixed-precision TRSM fused inside a Cholesky-based solver (this track's other paper, AbdulahCPBDGKLS22) is out of scope for a single-kernel benchmark spec; see notes_on_fairness and open_questions.

solve op(A)[N,N] * X = alpha*B[N,M] (side=Left) or X * op(A)[N,N] = alpha*B[N,M] (side=Right), A triangular (uplo in {Lower, Upper}), op(A) in {A, A^T} (trans in {NoTrans, Trans}), diag in {NonUnit, Unit}; result X overwrites B in place.

trsm-single-kernelsteady-state throughput of a single (non-batched) TRSM call, reported across the FULL side x uplo x trans layout matrix (diag=NonUnit) — not just the one Left/Lower/NoTrans configuration fBLAS's own paper publishes performance numbers for, even though fBLAS's own artifact already builds and functionally tests all 8 layout combinations per precision (`tests/host_api/trsm.json`). This closes the gap between fBLAS's functional test coverage (8 layouts x 2 precisions = 16 configs) and its performance-reporting coverage (1 config).
inputs
suitedense random triangular A + dense random B, no external matrix collection
selectionN=M square RHS problems; the two sizes with a directly-evidenced performance number in this track (fBLAS Table V: N=8192, N=32768), extended with 4 smaller doubling-sequence points by this spec to give a size-scaling curve (this spec's own addition — not evidenced by either paper — since a 2-point curve cannot show scaling behavior; flagged in notes_on_fairness)
recommended_subsetN=M in {1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768}
operand_initA: random triangular, diagonal entries offset by +N to guarantee well-conditioning (avoids a near-singular solve dominating error); B: dense U(-1,1), fixed seed=42
protocol
layout_matrixside in {Left, Right} x uplo in {Lower, Upper} x trans in {NoTrans, Trans}, diag=NonUnit fixed (8 combinations, matches fBLAS's own trsm.json coverage); diag=Unit as an optional 9th/10th pair, since fBLAS's own tests never exercise Unit diag (open question, not required)
precisionfp32, fp64 (both; matches fBLAS's own single/double sweep)
preprocessingA/B generation and any FPGA bitstream instantiation / on-chip module setup is one-shot, excluded from per-call timing, reported separately once

Neither surveyed paper states a numeric TRSM tolerance anywhere (confirmed by two independent searches of fBLAS's fulltext); these values are this spec's own choice, not derived from either paper.

Fairness notes
  • fBLAS's own README states host benchmark programs "report the lowest execution time" across a thread-count sweep — the single most optimistic statistic available (see the gemm-track spec's identical finding for fBLAS's GEMM harness). Both variants above fix this to median with min/max reported, and additionally require the FULL thread-count curve be disclosed, not just its minimum.
  • fBLAS validates TRSM correctness across all 8 side/uplo/trans layout combinations (per precision) via its unit-test JSON, but only ever publishes a performance number for 1 of those 8. trsm-single-kernel requires performance be reported for the full layout matrix a real user could invoke, closing this functional-vs-performance coverage gap.
  • Neither surveyed paper states a numeric correctness tolerance for TRSM anywhere in the available sources. This spec fixes a standard backward-error bound (not found in either paper) rather than leaving the gate unspecified, since an ungated throughput number is not a fair benchmark result per this project's general correctness-gate principle.
  • AbdulahCPBDGKLS22's TRSM usage (fused into tile-Cholesky + MLE, band-percentage mixed precision, statistical-quality correctness) is real and evidences an important usage pattern this spec's two variants do not cover, but building a faithful "embedded/mixed-precision TRSM" variant would require protocol details (band-size-to-precision mapping, per-band tolerance) that the paper does not disclose at the granularity a benchmark spec needs. Rather than fabricate those details, this usage pattern is left as an open question / future track extension, consistent with how the cholesky-track spec already treats AbdulahCPBDGKLS22's precision-vector axis as a first-class, separately-specified thing (see that spec's cholesky-mixed-precision-kernel variant) rather than folding it into a generic single-kernel spec.
Open questions
  • fBLAS's batched CPU harness (`batched_trsm.cpp`) exposes N, M, and `ntrsm` (batch count) as free CLI parameters with no example invocation or default values recoverable from the extracted paper/repo text; the N/M/batch_count values in trsm-batched-kernel's recommended_subset are this spec's own choice, not evidenced.
  • Whether fBLAS's FPGA TRSM templates (trsm_v1..v8.cl) differ in performance from each other (8 distinct implementation *versions*, not just 8 layout variants — the naming is ambiguous from the file listing alone) was not resolved from the sources read; if v1..v8 are competing implementations rather than one-per-layout, trsm-single-kernel's "report all 8 layouts" requirement may need to become "report all 8 layouts x all versions."
  • No source gives an FPGA-side H2D/D2H breakout number for TRSM specifically (only the general "memory-bound routines generate data on-chip" convention is stated); whether this convention actually applies to the TRSM templates specifically is unconfirmed.
  • Whether a dedicated "TRSM fused after Cholesky, mixed/banded precision" variant belongs in this spec or in the cholesky-track spec instead is left open; AbdulahCPBDGKLS22 is the only evidence for this usage pattern in either track's survey, and it is not independently benchmarked in that paper either way.
batched-gemm1 papers2 variants

Batched GEMM: many independent small-to-medium matrix multiplications launched as a single batched/grouped operation, covering both the uniform-shape case (every batch element is the same [M,K]x[K,N]) and the variable-shape/segmented ("grouped GEMM") case that this track's one surveyed paper (FASTEN) targets, where each of T segments has its own row-count M_i sharing a common K and per-segment weight [K,N].

uniform: C_b[M,N] = A_b[M,K] * B_b[K,N] for b in 0..batch-1 (independent, no cross-batch reuse). variable/segmented: given data[sum(M_i), K] and T per-type weights W_t[K,N], C[sum(M_i), N] where rows belonging to segment i are multiplied by W_{type(i)}; forward and backward (dC/dA, dC/dW) are both in scope, since FASTEN benchmarks both.

batched-gemm-uniform-kernelsteady-state kernel throughput of uniform-shape batched GEMM (same M,N,K across the whole batch), preprocessing excluded. Not directly evidenced by FASTEN's own artifact (which targets the variable-shape case) but included as the natural counterpart the track's axis list requires ("uniform vs variable batch"); shapes and K values below are taken from FASTEN's own benchmarked feature widths so the two variants stay comparable on K.

Fairness notes
  • FASTEN's own perf benchmark (test_perf, test_perf_random) times exactly one call per configuration via a single triton.profiler.scope, with no warmup-then-repeat-then-statistic structure of its own. This spec imposes warmup=10/reps=50/median on both variants, a strict strengthening rather than a value read out of the paper's practice.
  • FASTEN's shipped correctness tolerance (atol=1e-1, rtol=1e-2, loosened to atol=1.0 for large M/T) is loose enough to mask real numerical regressions, especially compounded by TF32 being enabled by default in the perf script. This spec tightens the gate for the TF32-off case and makes TF32-on/off an explicit reported axis instead of a silent default, so a batched-GEMM technique cannot look faster purely by trading away precision without that trade being visible in the result table.
  • batched-gemm-uniform-kernel has no direct evidence in this track's one surveyed paper (FASTEN only benchmarks the variable/segmented case) — it is included because the track's own axis definition ("uniform vs variable batch") requires it, using FASTEN's K values as the one point of continuity between the two variants.
Open questions
  • FASTEN's README headline speedups (13.65x vs CUTLASS, 4.72x vs cuBLAS) could not be traced to a specific aggregation formula (mean/geomean over which configs) from the files read; this spec's own median-based protocol should be treated as a redefinition, not a reproduction, of that headline number.
  • Whether Engine.AUTO's dispatch decision (Triton vs. torch/cutlass path) has a non-negligible one-time cost worth measuring as "preprocessing" was not confirmed from the source read; assumed cheap (dictionary/ heuristic lookup) but not verified.
  • No fp16/bf16 batched-GEMM evidence exists in this track's one paper (FASTEN's tests explicitly skip float16 on CPU and don't exercise it on GPU in the excerpts read) — left out of both variants rather than invented.
homotopy-continuation1 papers3 variants

Throughput of GPU homotopy-continuation path tracking for polynomial systems, separated into a fixed-work kernel measure (all paths tracked, so efficiency gains cannot be confused with work reduction) and an application-level RANSAC measure where solution quality gates the time.

Given a polynomial system F(x; p_target) = 0 with n unknowns and a start system G(x; p_start) = 0 with known solutions, track T homotopy paths H(x, t) = (1-t) G + t F from t=0 to t=1 by predictor-corrector stepping, yielding candidate solutions of F. For trifocal_2op1p_30x30: n = 30 variables, 33 parameters, T = 312 paths.
