Fairness notes
  • The track's four claimed speedup sources split into two incomparable kinds: direct parameter-homotopy evaluation and GPU-utilization work make the same work faster; path pruning and RANSAC early termination make the solver do less work. The headline 9-17x figures mix them. Variants 1 and 3 exist specifically to keep them apart — a kernel-level claim must move us-per- tracked-path, not just wall clock.
  • Success rate is a first-class gate, not a footnote. Homotopy path tracking fails by diverging or exhausting GPUHC_Max_Correction_Steps; a submission that prunes harder will be faster and worse, and nothing in the artifact currently makes that visible.
  • The public dataset is NOISELESS synthetic data. RANSAC and early termination are cheapest exactly there. Results on this data may not be presented as evidence about the noisy real-world regime, which is the regime RANSAC exists for and whose dataset is not yet released.
  • GPUHC_Max_Steps (80) and GPUHC_Max_Correction_Steps (3) are pinned by this spec. They trade time against success rate directly; letting each submission retune them turns the benchmark into a race to the loosest tolerance.
  • The artifact exposes no warmup/repetition/statistic constants, so this spec sets them rather than inheriting them, and says so.
Open questions
  • The paper's own timing protocol (warmup, repetitions, statistic) could not be recovered: IPDPS'25 is paywalled with no arXiv mirror, and the constants are not in gpuhc_settings.yaml or the README. Reading cmd/magmaHC-main.cpp in depth would settle it.
  • The real-world (noisy) RANSAC dataset is announced as "coming soon" in the README. Until it ships, the e2e variant covers only the clean regime.
  • Single-implementation track with a self-referential baseline (the authors' prior GPU-HC). Candidate external baselines for genuine comparison: HomotopyContinuation.jl, Bertini, PHCpack, and the original Homotopy-Continuation-Tracker-on-GPU repository.
  • Whether the multi-GPU path partitions homotopy paths or RANSAC hypotheses is not documented; it changes what a scaling number means.
math-functions1 papers1 variants

Vectorized elementary-math-function (libm) throughput — trig, inverse-trig, exp, log, pow, fmod — for SIMD-vectorized C libraries, benchmarked across accuracy classes (1.0-ULP vs 3.5-ULP) because accuracy trades directly against speed and is treated here as a first-class axis, not an afterthought; SLEEF is the sole surveyed paper in this singleton track.

y[i] = f(x[i]) elementwise, f in {sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, exp, log, pow, fmod}, computed on a SIMD vector register of width W lanes (W = ISA vector width / element size), argument reused across a long call loop (register-resident microbenchmark, not a streaming array kernel — see notes_on_fairness).

mathfn-elementwise-kernelSteady-state reciprocal-throughput per element for a fixed (function, accuracy class, ISA width, dtype), argument swept over SLEEF's own per-function domain buckets, correctness gated by max-ULP-error against an arbitrary-precision reference at the accuracy class's own target ULP bound.
inputs
suitefunction set = {sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, exp, log, pow, fmod} (SLEEF's own Table II set)
argument_ranges
sin_cos_tan[0, 2*pi] (small domain) AND [0, 1e100] (large domain, forces full Payne-Hanek argument reduction) — BOTH required, not just one, since large-domain behavior is a distinct correctness/speed regime SLEEF's own paper specifically stress-tests
asin_acos[-1, 1]
atan_exp[-700, 700]
log[0, 1e300]
pow[-30, 30] x [-30, 30]
fmodnumerator in [1, 100], denominator = r*d for r swept in [1, 1e25]
accuracy_classes{1.0-ULP, 3.5-ULP} — SLEEF's own two shipped variants; BOTH REQUIRED per config, since this track's namesake axis is the accuracy/speed trade-off, not a single fixed accuracy choice
isa_width{SSE2/128-bit, AVX2/256-bit, AVX-512/512-bit, NEON/128-bit, SVE/scalable} — SLEEF's own supported target set (repo src/arch); AVX2 is the paper's own primary reported configuration and the only one with quantitative numbers recovered in this survey pass (see open_questions)
dtypefp32 and fp64 both (SLEEF ships both; the paper's own Table II reports fp64)
protocol
warmupnone separately reported; SLEEF's own convention folds warmup into the single long call loop itself
reps5 independent repetitions of N=1e8 calls each — THIS SPEC RELAXES SLEEF's own single N=1e10-call run into 5 shorter repetitions specifically to obtain a distribution, since a single measurement (as SLEEF's paper reports) cannot be checked for run-to-run variance.
statisticmedian across the 5 repetitions (report min/max). DELIBERATE FIX: SLEEF's own paper reports one measurement per configuration with no repetition and no spread at all.
timerclock_gettime (host wall clock), SLEEF's own mechanism; one timestamp pair bracketing the entire N-call loop, not per-call
timing_scopekernel only; the argument vector is register/cache-resident and reused across the loop (SLEEF's own microbenchmark design) — this measures ALU/vector-unit reciprocal throughput, NOT memory-bandwidth- bound array throughput; see notes_on_fairness.
compilerreference build gcc-7.3.0, -O3 -mavx2 -mfma for the AVX2 config (SLEEF's own paper build); compiler optimization disabled for the timing loop body only, libraries themselves built at default optimization
metric
primaryreciprocal throughput, ns/call (elapsed_ns / N) — SLEEF's own Table II metric
secondaryclock cycles/call (derived from ns/call at the measured clock frequency; SLEEF's own paper states '10ns corresponds to 34 cycles' at ~3.4GHz)
correctnessmax ULP error vs. an arbitrary-precision (e.g. MPFR) reference, evaluated over a dense random + edge-case (domain-boundary, subnormal, NaN/Inf input) sample of the swept argument range; gate = 1.0 ULP for the 1.0-ULP accuracy class, 3.5 ULP for the 3.5-ULP accuracy class. SLEEF's repo ships a dedicated correctness tester (src/libm-tester, not read in this pass) presumed to implement this check; exact sample density/edge-case list not confirmed — flagged open_question.
Fairness notes
  • SLEEF's own reciprocal-throughput number reuses the same register- resident argument on every call of the timed loop, so a low ns/call figure does NOT necessarily reflect real array-processing throughput for large streaming inputs (which would be memory-bandwidth-bound for simple functions). This spec keeps SLEEF's own protocol (needed for direct comparability to its own SVML/FDLIBM/Vector-libm baselines) but flags this explicitly rather than presenting ns/call as a streaming- throughput number.
  • Requiring both the 1.0-ULP and 3.5-ULP accuracy classes to be reported together (rather than picking whichever makes a library look fastest) is this spec's explicit response to the task's instruction that ULP accuracy be a first-class, not secondary, benchmark parameter.
  • single paper in this singleton track; no cross-paper divergence to reconcile.
Open questions
  • Exact CPU/compiler versions and quantitative Table II numbers for the SSE2/AVX-512/NEON/SVE configurations were not recovered from the fetched fulltext excerpt (only the AVX2/i7-6700 configuration's protocol and qualitative result — "comparable to SVML" — were extracted); those ISA rows' baseline comparison values are inferred to follow the same protocol but are not independently confirmed from the paper text.
  • Table II's exact per-function ns/call values for SLEEF vs. SVML vs. FDLIBM vs. Vector-libm were paraphrased qualitatively by the fetch tool rather than transcribed verbatim; re-extract Table II directly from the PDF before using this spec to set numeric target/reference thresholds.
  • SLEEF's correctness-tester sampling methodology (src/libm-tester) was not read in this pass; the "dense random + edge-case" sampling described above is this spec's own reasonable design, not confirmed from SLEEF's own test code.
matrix-function-evaluation1 papers1 variants

Approximate evaluation of a matrix function (density-matrix sign function via Löwdin symmetric orthogonalization) on large sparse matrices from DFT electronic-structure calculations, by converting the global sparse operation into independent local dense submatrix computations that exploit CPU/GPU/FPGA dense floating-point throughput; single surveyed paper (submatrix method for CP2K, SC'20).

Given a sparse symmetric matrix H (Hamiltonian/overlap-type, from a CP2K DFT calculation), compute an approximation to f(H) — here the density matrix sign function — by extracting many small, nearly-dense submatrices (one per matrix row/block, up to a fixed truncation threshold eps_filter), evaluating the dense matrix function locally on each, and reassembling the sparse result. Distributed across MPI ranks; the local dense evaluation step is additionally accelerable on GPU (tensor cores) or FPGA.

matfun-submatrix-kernelSteady-state throughput (TFLOP/s and wall time) of the per-submatrix dense matrix-function evaluation kernel across CPU/GPU/FPGA targets, gated by an eps_filter accuracy sweep against a high-precision reference, with the sparse-to-submatrix extraction step reported separately as preprocessing rather than folded into per-call time.
inputs
suiteCP2K's own standard liquid-water DFT benchmark family: a fixed 32-H2O-molecule unit cell repeated NREP times per dimension.
selectionNREP in {2, 4, 6, 8} -> system sizes 768, ~6144(*), ~20736(*), 49152 atoms (the paper's own literal endpoint range; intermediate NREP values interpolated geometrically, exact intermediate atom counts not confirmed from the fetched excerpt — marked (*))
recommended_subsetNREP=2, 768 atoms, SZV-MOLOPT-SR-GTH (small/single-node sanity point), NREP=8, 49152 atoms, SZV-MOLOPT-SR-GTH (paper's own largest reported system), NREP=4, DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH (larger-basis-set comparison point, paper's own second basis)
basis_setsSZV-MOLOPT-SR-GTH (primary, minimal basis); DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH (larger-basis comparison)
submatrix_sizefixed, independent of overall system size once the system exceeds ~200 water molecules (the method's own defining linear-scaling property, stated qualitatively by the paper); exact numeric submatrix dimension not recovered from the fetched excerpt — flagged open_question.
protocol
warmupnot stated in the reachable fulltext excerpt. THIS SPEC REQUIRES 2 discarded full-system-size passes before timing, since no paper-stated convention exists to follow or contradict.
reps5
statisticmedian (report min/max) — REQUIRED per this benchmark suite's general fairness principle; the paper's own reported numbers (e.g. the 35.2 TFLOP/s GPU headline figure, 83% strong-scaling efficiency) give no indication of repetition count or spread.
timerwall-clock (MPI_Wtime or equivalent) for the CPU/distributed path; device-side kernel time (separate from host orchestration) for the GPU/FPGA accelerated local dense-evaluation step.
timing_scopekernel only — the local dense matrix-function evaluation on each extracted submatrix. Sparse-matrix submatrix extraction/indexing and MPI communication for reassembly are EXCLUDED from this timed region and reported separately, never silently amortized in.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per system size: submatrix extraction/indexing cost.
hardware_tracks
cpuIntel Xeon Gold 6148 'Skylake', 40 cores/node, 1 thread per MPI rank, scaled 1 to 8 nodes (up to 320 cores) — the paper's own strong-scaling sweep
gpuNVIDIA RTX 2080 Ti, FP16/FP32/FP64 tensor-core paths compared as three separate precision sub-cases
fpgaIntel Stratix 10 GX 2800 (practical ceiling ~3.4 TFLOP/s per the paper's own stated figure)
metric
primaryTFLOP/s achieved by the local dense matrix-function kernel (paper's own headline: 35.2 TFLOP/s at 250W, GPU FP16 path)
secondarystrong-scaling parallel efficiency (%) relative to the 2-node CPU baseline (paper's own reported: 83% efficiency scaling 2->8 nodes)
tertiarywall time per system size (s), plotted vs. NREP to verify the method's own linear-scaling claim
correctnessrelative error in the computed density-matrix / energy output vs. a reference computed at eps_filter=1e-15, swept over eps_filter in {1e-5, 1e-6, 1e-8, 1e-10, 1e-12} (the paper's own Figure 7 sweep points). Gate: error must remain within the band the paper's own Figure 7 demonstrates as not "negatively impacting the results" — exact numeric threshold (e.g. an absolute energy-error-per-atom bound) was not extracted from the fetched excerpt and is flagged as an open question requiring re-extraction of Figure 7's axis values directly from the PDF/HTML before this gate can be applied as a hard numeric pass/fail.
baselines_required2nd-order Newton-Schulz iteration on sparse DBCSR matrices — the paper's own primary baseline, CP2K's existing production method — run at 8 MPI ranks/node x 5 threads/rank (the paper's OWN reported configuration for this baseline, DIFFERENT from the submatrix method's own 1-thread/rank mapping; see notes_on_fairness — this spec reports the baseline as the paper ran it rather than silently re-mapping thread counts to "equalize" the comparison, which would require re-running code not exercised in the surveyed paper).
Fairness notes
  • The paper's own baseline (Newton-Schulz/DBCSR) uses a materially different rank x thread mapping (8 ranks/node, 5 threads/rank) than the submatrix method itself (1 thread/rank). This is the paper's own reported configuration for both methods, not something this spec silently equalizes — a submission using this spec MUST report both methods' thread mappings alongside their TFLOP/s numbers so a reader can judge whether the comparison is apples-to-apples.
  • single paper in this singleton track; no cross-paper divergence to reconcile.
Open questions
  • Exact submatrix size (block dimension) was not recoverable from the fetched ar5iv excerpt — the paper states only that it is fixed and independent of system size beyond ~200 water molecules, not the numeric value itself.
  • Warmup/repetition/statistic convention for the paper's own reported timings (35.2 TFLOP/s, 83% efficiency) was not stated anywhere in the reachable text; this spec's protocol values (2 warmup, 5 reps, median) are this spec's own choice, not sourced from the paper.
  • Exact numeric correctness tolerance from Figure 7 was described only qualitatively by the fetch tool ("does not negatively impact the results too much") rather than transcribed as an exact bound — re-extract Figure 7's y-axis values directly from the PDF/HTML before relying on a hard numeric gate for this spec's correctness field.
  • Intermediate NREP=4,6 atom counts (marked "(*)" in the inputs.selection field above) were computed by this survey as an interpolation of the unit-cell-repetition formula, not independently confirmed from the paper's own text.

stencil / PDE

stencil21 papers3 variants

Throughput of an iterative structured-grid stencil sweep — a fixed weighted sum over a small neighborhood (star or box support) applied to every point of a dense D-dimensional grid, repeated for T time steps with double-buffered (ping-pong) storage — across three hardware/implementation classes the track's papers actually target: general-purpose CPU/GPU compute (spatial and temporal blocking), Tensor-Core matmul reformulations (fp16), and full domain-application solvers.

U_out[p] = sum_{d in support(shape, radius r)} w_d * U_in[p + d] for every interior grid point p, applied for T sequential time steps via double buffering (U_in/U_out swap each step); shape in {star, box}, dims in {1D, 2D, 3D}; star-r has 2*dims*r+1 support points, box-r has (2r+1)^dims support points; halo of width r (periodic or fixed) surrounds the domain.

stencil-cpu-gpu-kernel-fp64Steady-state per-time-step throughput of an iterative structured-grid stencil sweep on general-purpose CPU/GPU compute (SIMD/CUDA-core vectorized kernels with spatial and/or temporal blocking), independent of any Tensor-Core matmul reformulation. This is the common denominator across AN5D, PERKS, K-Athena's core update kernel, Devito's generated code, AOStencil, and StencilsOnFPGA.
inputs
suiteSynthetic star/box stencils named with AN5D's radius convention (star{2d,3d}{1..4}r, box{2d,3d}{1..4}r), which the 2024-2026 Tensor-Core lineage below reuses verbatim, plus named application-derived instances every surveyed paper's family includes a version of (5/7/9/25/27-point Jacobi-style kernels).
selectionThe 6 shapes shared by AN5D and the whole Tensor-Core lineage's public CLI (union, so variant 1 and variant 2 stay directly comparable on the overlap): star2d1r, box2d1r, star2d3r, box2d3r, star3d1r, box3d1r.
recommended_subsetstar2d1r, box2d1r, star2d3r, box2d3r, star3d1r, box3d1r, j3d27pt, rtm3d25p8th
dense_operandsingle scalar field per grid point, fp64 (fp32 as a secondary pass at the same tolerance), initialized U(0,1) random or index-fill (no cherry-picked "nice" data — both AN5D and ConvStencil's harnesses use random fill by default).
grid_sizes2D: 16384 x 16384 (AN5D's synthetic-suite convention, matches AOStencil's ARM sweep band of 8192-24576). 3D: 512^3 (AN5D's 3D convention == Devito's 512^3 velocity model, == CLAIRE's 256^3-512^3 range). Small-class 3D: 256^3, for resource-constrained targets (matches K-Athena's single-node/roofline size and gives FPGA-class implementations a reachable point; StencilsOnFPGA itself only reaches 50^3-400^2 due to on-chip capacity and is reported separately, not forced onto this grid).
boundaryperiodic wrap or fixed halo of width r; halo fill/exchange is EXCLUDED from the timed region (single-node/single-device kernel-only claim; distributed halo exchange belongs to variant 3).
protocol
iteration_countT=1000 back-to-back sweeps (AN5D's primary-benchmark convention). If a single T=1000 trial's wall time would fall under 400 ms on the target device, calibrate T upward (AN5D/PERKS's own adaptive-warmup logic: run once, measure, scale T so the timed trial clears the floor) and report the calibrated T explicitly — never silently substitute a shorter, noisier trial.
warmup1 full T-iteration trial, discarded (AN5D's own convention; also matches PERKS's `--warmup` calibration run).
reps5
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside it). This deliberately departs from AN5D's own "average of 5" — median is robust to the occasional outlier trial that a mean silently absorbs, and none of the other surveyed papers in this variant's family report a distribution at all, so there is no existing convention this contradicts.
timerdevice-side event pair (CUDA/HIP events) for GPU targets; wall clock (`clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)` or `omp_get_wtime()`) with an explicit device/thread synchronization barrier at trial start and stop for CPU/ARM targets (AOStencil's own `omp_get_wtime()` convention).
timing_scopekernel(s) only. Excludes H2D/D2H transfer (AN5D explicit), array allocation and initialization, and any halo exchange. Each trial times all T sweeps as ONE elapsed interval (every surveyed paper bulk-times T iterations; none times sweeps individually — see survey.md Divergence 1), then divides by T for the reported per-step figure.
preprocessing_reportednot applicable to this variant in general (no format conversion in this compute class); if a codegen/autotuning implementation (AN5D, AOStencil's GA tuner, Devito's autotuner) has a nonzero kernel-search or compile time, report it once, separately, and never amortize it into the per-step throughput.
metric
primaryGCell-updates/s = grid_points * T / elapsed_s / 1e9
secondaryGFLOP/s — the FLOPs-per-point-update convention MUST be stated per stencil (e.g. PERKS counts 17 FLOP/update for its 9-point kernel); treat as informational only, NOT comparable across papers with an undisclosed convention (survey.md Divergence 4), ms per T-iteration trial, GB/s effective bandwidth (bytes moved = 2 * grid_points * sizeof(dtype) per sweep, read+write of ping-pong buffers)
correctnessmax relative error <= 1e-5 vs. an unblocked/unoptimized reference sweep of the same stencil, same precision, run for the same T (PERKS's `TOLERANCE=1e-5` and AOStencil's `1e-5` check both already use this threshold). fp32 secondary pass: same 1e-5 relative-error gate against an fp32 reference (not fp64 — comparing an fp32 kernel to an fp64 reference conflates precision loss with implementation bugs).
stencil-tcu-matmul-kernel-fp16Throughput of stencil-as-(sparse)-matrix-multiplication reformulations executing on Tensor Cores / Sparse Tensor Cores at fp16, with the one-shot layout/format-construction preprocessing excluded from the timed sweep loop but measured once and reported separately (not merely excluded and left unquantified, as SPIDER's own artifact does).
inputs
suiteThe shape/CLI catalog literally shared by ConvStencil, LoRAStencil, FlashFFTStencil, and SPIDER (`{program} shape input_size time_iteration_size [options]`): {1d1r,1d2r} (1D); {star2d1r,box2d1r,star2d3r,box2d3r} (2D — identical names to variant 1, so the two variants are directly comparable on the overlap); {star3d1r,box3d1r} (3D). FlashFFTStencil's point-count aliases (Box2D9P~box2d1r, Box2D25P~box2d3r, Star2D9P) are accepted as equivalents when a paper only reports the alias name.
selectionEvery shape all 4 baseline-cluster papers implement in common (the 7 listed above/below); 3D shapes are included for CLI completeness but their grid size is flagged open (see open_questions — no surveyed paper's own reported numbers, as opposed to CLI support, could be confirmed for 3D).
recommended_subset1d1r, 1d2r, star2d1r, box2d1r, star2d3r, box2d3r, star3d1r, box3d1r
dense_operandfp16 grid values (TF32/mixed-precision accumulation as the kernel dictates), random-initialized.
grid_sizes1D: 1 x 10,240,000 (SPIDER's Figure10_run.sh / ConvStencil-lineage convention). 2D: 10240 x 10240 (SPIDER/ConvStencil/LoRAStencil's shared primary evaluation point; also swept 512..10240 per side in SPIDER's Figure11). 3D: 512^3, carried over from variant 1 for cross-family comparability — NOT independently confirmed against any Tensor-Core-lineage paper's own reported 3D numbers (open question).
protocol
iteration_countT=10,240 for 2D, T=100,000 for 1D — the literal `time_iteration_size` values SPIDER's own reproduction script (Figure10_run.sh) uses to drive the ConvStencil/LoRAStencil/SPIDER binaries, so this is not an invented number but the value this paper family already runs its own baselines at. T=1000 for 3D, carried over from variant 1 (open question, same caveat as the 3D grid size above).
warmup1 full T-iteration trial, discarded. THIS IS A DELIBERATE FIX: none of ConvStencil, LoRAStencil, FlashFFTStencil, or SPIDER's public benchmark harnesses run a discarded warmup trial before the timed region (survey.md Divergence 2).
reps5
statisticmedian (report min/max). FIX: all 4 surveyed repos as published report a single, unrepeated trial.
timerdevice-side (CUDA events, matching SPIDER's own `cudaEventRecord` usage) wrapping all T kernel launches as one interval. A host `std::chrono` timer (ConvStencil/LoRAStencil's own convention) is acceptable only if it brackets a single `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` after all T launches — SPIDER's own implementation instead synchronizes after every individual launch inside the timed loop, which inflates measured time with T-1 extra sync-barrier stalls; this spec requires the single-sync form for both timer choices.
timing_scopematmul/MMA kernel(s) only; H2D/D2H excluded. The one-shot format/layout transform — parameter-matrix packing, sparse-metadata compression for `mma.sp` encoding, im2col-equivalent layout construction, or FFT-plan creation (FlashFFTStencil) — is excluded from the T-iteration timed loop.
preprocessing_reportedmeasured once, separately, and reported as its own number (ms) and as a "break-even iteration count" (preprocessing_ms / per-iteration_ms). FIX: SPIDER's paper text states this cost is excluded from its throughput figures and is not otherwise quantified as a number in the public artifact for any of the 4 papers in this family; this variant requires it be measured, not just excluded (survey.md Divergence 5).
metric
primaryGCell-updates/s a.k.a. GStencil/s (this family's own native metric) = grid_points * T / elapsed_s / 1e9
secondaryeffective TFLOP/s on tensor cores (informational; FLOP convention must be stated — ConvStencil's own printed formula uses an unresolved per-shape multiplier, see survey.md Divergence 4 and open_questions), speedup vs. cuDNN im2col-convolution baseline on the same GPU (the one baseline shared by ConvStencil, LoRAStencil, and SPIDER)
correctnessmax relative error vs. an fp64 CPU or GPU reference sweep of the same stencil/grid/T. No surveyed repo's public artifact states an explicit fp16 tolerance (ConvStencil's own 1e-7 check exists in source but is compiled out by default, and it is a fp64-path check, not fp16 — see survey.md's ConvStencil subsection). This spec recommends <= 1e-2 relative error as an fp16-appropriate default; treat as an OPEN QUESTION pending confirmation from a paper that actually states one.
stencil-e2e-applicationEnd-to-end wall-clock speedup of a full domain-application solver (whole program: boundary handling, multi-kernel physics, no I/O) over its own unoptimized/decomposed baseline, for a domain-realistic, CFL- or convergence-order-determined number of steps — reported ALONGSIDE, never substituted for, a kernel-only number from variant 1/2 when both exist for the same code (WindStencil's own README already separates "kernel-focused gain" from "full-application gain"; this variant standardizes that split for the whole track).
inputs
suiteDomain-standard test problems rather than a synthetic grid sweep, because grid shape and physics genuinely differ per code and forcing a common synthetic grid onto them would misrepresent what the paper measured: linear fast-magnetosonic MHD wave (K-Athena/Athena++ test suite), isotropic/TTI acoustic + isotropic elastic wave propagation (Devito/Bisbas seismic-imaging setups), the Williamson shallow-water test suite — steady-state geostrophic flow / Rossby-Haurwitz wave / perturbed jet (ozHOPE/HOPE), and compressible Navier-Stokes CFD ducts (WindStencil/OpenCFD-SC).
selectionone problem per paper's own primary evaluation case, at the paper's own default resolution; no cross-paper size unification (see survey.md Divergence 6).
recommended_subsetK-Athena: linear fast magnetosonic wave, 256^3, fp64, Devito/Bisbas: isotropic acoustic, space order 4, 512^3, 228 CFL-determined time steps, fp32, WindStencil: 480x512x64 (single-MI60 case) and the 9600x256x256 strong-scaling case, 1000 iterations, fp64, ozHOPE: Williamson steady-state geostrophic flow, HOPE's default resolution, Ozaki fp16-emulated-fp64
grid_sizespaper-native; see recommended_subset. Physically motivated, not drawn from a shared microbenchmark convention.
protocol
iteration_countpaper-native: CFL/physics-determined where applicable (Devito 228-587 steps) or the fixed round count the paper itself used for its headline number (WindStencil: 1000 for the performance number, 10,000 for the correctness check; K-Athena: "several runs" of full production cycles).
warmup1 full run discarded, if the harness supports separating setup from the timed loop; otherwise report this as a deviation from variant 1/2's protocol rather than silently pretending it happened (many full-application codes fold one-time mesh/IC setup into the single measured run and cannot cheaply discard a "warmup" run of a physics simulation).
reps3
statisticmedian (report min/max). K-Athena's own convention — 80th percentile of per-cycle rate across several runs — is an acceptable ALTERNATE statistic specifically for weak/strong-scaling sub-variants where network variance dominates; report explicitly which statistic was used and never mix the two within one reported number.
timerwall clock around the whole program's compute loop; initialization/I-O excluded only if the harness cleanly separates them.
timing_scopeend-to-end whole-program compute time (all kernels + boundary/physics glue). Report this NUMBER TOGETHER WITH, never in place of, the single-dominant-kernel number from variant 1/2 for the same optimization when the paper's artifact exposes both (WindStencil's own table already does this split; this spec makes it mandatory rather than paper-specific).
preprocessing_reportedmesh/initial-condition setup and any one-time solver initialization reported once, separately, never amortized into the per-step throughput.
metric
primarywall-clock speedup vs. the paper's own unoptimized/baseline implementation on the same hardware
secondarycell-updates/s or GPoints/s for the dominant stencil kernel (comparable to variant 1's primary metric when the paper also reports a kernel-only number), % of hardware FP64 peak / roofline-attainable peak, when the paper reports operational intensity (K-Athena, WindStencil both do)
correctnessdomain-specific, and DELIBERATELY WEAKER than variant 1/2's pointwise tolerance gate — flagged as an open question rather than silently equated to it: either conserved-quantity relative drift over the full run (WindStencil: total energy/temperature, <= 1e-4, compared between optimized and unoptimized runs of the SAME code, not against an independent reference) or pointwise comparison vs. an FP64 reference solution for a standard test case (ozHOPE's Williamson cases).
Fairness notes
  • AN5D repeats 5x with 1 discarded warmup and reports the mean; every GPU Tensor-Core-stencil paper (ConvStencil, LoRAStencil, FlashFFTStencil, SPIDER) and both surveyed CPU papers (PERKS, AOStencil) publish a single, unrepeated, un-warmed-up trial in their public harness. Both kernel-only variants above mandate a discarded warmup + median-of->=5 (variant 1/2) regardless of what the underlying repo's default run does.
  • ConvStencil's own correctness check (`tolerance=1e-7`) exists in source but is compiled out (`#define CHECK_ERROR` commented) in the public artifact — the published benchmark path runs with NO correctness check by default. This spec's correctness gate is mandatory, not opt-in.
  • GFLOP/s is not comparable paper-to-paper in this track without a stated FLOP-per-point-update convention: PERKS hard-codes 17 FLOP/cell for one specific 9-point kernel; ConvStencil's own printed throughput formula applies an unexplained per-shape multiplier. GCell-updates/s is made primary specifically because it depends only on grid size x iteration count, not on an assumed FLOP-counting convention (survey.md Divergence 4).
  • SPIDER's paper text states preprocessing/offline-transform cost is excluded from its reported throughput and is not otherwise quantified as a number for any of the 4 Tensor-Core-lineage papers surveyed. Variant 2 requires this be measured and reported once, not merely excluded and left unquantified.
  • SPIDER's own 2D kernel synchronizes the device after every one of the T timed launches (not once at the end), which inflates the measured time with T-1 extra barrier stalls relative to ConvStencil/LoRAStencil's single-sync-at-the-end convention. Variant 2 standardizes on the single-sync form for both families so neither is penalized by a synchronization-granularity artifact rather than a real performance difference.
  • StencilsOnFPGA and WindStencil/ozHOPE's application-level correctness checks (conserved quantities, roofline %) are not pointwise numerical tolerance gates the way PERKS/AOStencil's are; variant 3 keeps this weaker guarantee explicit rather than silently promoting it to the same rigor as variant 1/2.
Open questions
  • The Tensor-Core-matmul lineage's own 3D grid-size/T convention could not be confirmed from public sources: SPIDER's own kernel sources are 1D/2D only (no 3D implementation despite the paper comparing against 3D-capable ConvStencil/LoRAStencil baselines), and ConvStencil/LoRAStencil have no arXiv fulltext to check their own paper-reported 3D numbers against (SC/PPoPP DOI only). Variant 2's 3D row is copied from variant 1 pending confirmation from the paper PDFs directly.
  • fp16 correctness tolerance for variant 2 is not stated in any of the 4 surveyed repos' public artifacts. The 1e-2 relative-error default in variant 2's correctness field is this spec's own recommendation, not sourced from any paper — flagged explicitly rather than presented as if it were.
  • ConvStencil's own GStencil/s formula in `src/2d/gpu.cu` multiplies by a per-shape factor (1x for some shapes, 3x seen for others in the box2d3r-adjacent kernel) whose exact geometric meaning (halo replication? multi-output-per-launch?) could not be fully resolved by reading source alone. A harness implementer should cross-check against the paper's own reported numbers/table rather than trusting the printed GStencil/s literally.
  • AOStencil's 3D grid sizes were not confirmed — the one run.sh read only shows a single call each to 3d7pt_star.py/3d27pt_box.py (unlike the 2D scripts' explicit 8192/16384/24576 loop), and those individual files were not fetched. The 3D recommended_subset entries for variant 1 (star3d1r/box3d1r at 512^3) are AN5D/Devito-sourced, not AOStencil-sourced.
  • PERKS's actual paper-reported grid sizes/T were not directly extracted (no arXiv fulltext, OA link is an OSTI PDF not fetched in this pass) — its methodology facts above come entirely from its own repo source code (CLI flags, timing/calibration logic, correctness tolerance), which is reliable for protocol design but not for a specific headline grid-size number.
climate-kernel2 papers2 variants

Throughput of two structurally unrelated climate-adjacent kernels this track's 2 papers actually cover: (1) a Tensor-Core-accelerated shallow-water dynamical-core stencil (pure fluid dynamics, no physics parameterization), and (2) a mixed-precision spherical-harmonic-transform + tile-low-rank Cholesky kernel underlying a statistical climate emulator (no dynamics at all — emulates ensemble statistics of prior GCM output). No shared input suite or metric is imposed across the two; each gets its own variant reflecting what its own paper actually measures. Grid-size/timing conventions for variant 1 are shared with `benchspecs/stencil/spec.yaml` (same paper, ozHOPE, cross-listed in both tracks).

Variant 1: U_out[p] = convolution-reformulated shallow-water stencil update at grid point p on a spherical/latitude-longitude domain, for T timesteps, computed via FP16 Tensor-Core MMA with Ozaki-scheme precision restoration. Variant 2: given N=L^2 spatio-temporal sample points (L = latitude resolution), compute forward spherical-harmonic transform -> SYRK covariance matrix C=AA^T -> mixed-precision tile-low-rank Cholesky factorization of C (repeated nruns times) -> inverse SHT -> MSE against a reference; the emulator's usable output is one statistical field realization per forward-factor-inverse pass.

climate-dyncore-kernel-fp16tcEnd-to-end speedup of a Tensor-Core-accelerated shallow-water dynamical core over its FP64 (or working-precision) baseline on the Williamson standard atmospheric-dynamics test suite, with accuracy order-of-convergence preserved and reported ALONGSIDE speedup, never substituted for it. Reused from `benchspecs/stencil/spec.yaml`'s ozHOPE entry (same paper); reframed here around this track's own dynamics-only framing.
inputs
suitethe Williamson standard test suite for atmospheric dynamical cores — domain-standard, not a synthetic grid sweep.
selectionall 3 Williamson cases the paper evaluates.
recommended_subsetWilliamson case 2: steady-state geostrophic flow, Williamson case 5/6-family: Rossby-Haurwitz wave, perturbed jet flow
dense_operandFP16 Tensor-Core storage/compute with Ozaki-scheme precision restoration tunable up to FP64-equivalent working precision.
grid_sizesHOPE's own default resolution for each Williamson case (not independently re-derived; paper-native, per `stencil` survey's own note that this is a domain-standard problem, not a size sweep).
protocol
iteration_countphysics/CFL-determined per the Williamson case's own standard integration length (not independently confirmed from fulltext; open question).
warmup1 full run discarded, if the harness cleanly separates setup from the timed integration loop (not independently confirmed for this specific repo).
reps3
statisticmedian (report min/max) — this spec's own default, consistent with `stencil` track's application-variant convention; not independently sourced from ozHOPE's own repo/paper.
timerwall clock around the full timestep-integration loop; not independently confirmed from source.
timing_scopeend-to-end whole-run compute time (all Tensor-Core MMA calls + Ozaki-scheme precision-restoration overhead), matching the paper's own 'end-to-end speedup' framing.
preprocessing_reportedany one-time cuDNN-frontend graph construction / kernel-plan compilation reported once, separately, if applicable — not independently confirmed from source.
metric
primarywall-clock speedup vs. the paper's own FP64/working-precision baseline on the same hardware (1.82x average, up to 4.34x, per the paper's own headline result).
secondaryorder-of-convergence preservation (the paper's own first-class reported result, not just a pass/fail correctness gate), GPoint-updates/s or simulated-days/day, IF the paper's own physical-time-per-step can be recovered — OPEN QUESTION, not confirmed from available sources (survey.md Divergence 2)
correctnessdiagnostic variables compared against an FP64 reference solution per Williamson case; convergence-order agreement is itself a reported result. This is a genuinely stronger correctness story than a bare pointwise tolerance (it validates that low precision doesn't silently degrade the numerical method's asymptotic accuracy, not just that one run's error is small).
climate-emulator-solver-kernelThroughput of the mixed-precision SHT + tile-low-rank Cholesky kernel underlying a statistical climate emulator, with the one-shot forward-SHT/SYRK/matrix-norm phases reported separately (never amortized into the per-run factorization time) and the factorization phase itself repeated nruns times — the harness's OWN native preprocessing/kernel split (survey.md Divergence 4), adopted verbatim rather than imposed from outside.
inputs
suitereal Earth System Model output ensembles (the paper's own training data: 318 billion hourly temperature points, 35-year ensemble; 31 billion daily points, 83-year ensemble) — this is real climate data, not a synthetic covariance matrix, matching the paper's own "boosting Earth System Model outputs" framing.
selectionthe paper's own confirmed CLI example point (TESTS.md), used as the recommended smoke-test size; production-scale runs use the paper's own 0.976 EFlop/s Frontier-scale headline point (size not independently re-derived from fulltext).
recommended_subset--latitude 120 --NB 1440 --N 14400 (confirmed CLI example from TESTS.md), Frontier full-scale run (--latitude and --NB not independently confirmed at this scale; open question)
dense_operandN=L^2 spatial covariance matrix (L = --latitude), tile size NB; mixed-precision tile bands controlled via --band_dense_dp (fp64 band) / --band_dense_sp (fp32 band) / --band_dense_fp8 (fp8 band) plus --adaptive_decision for automatic per-tile precision selection.
grid_sizesN = latitude^2; report the --latitude value explicitly, not just N (the CLI's own primary size parameter).
protocol
iteration_countthe Cholesky-factorization (`hicma_parsec_potrf`) phase is repeated --nruns times; forward SHT, forward-SHT-reshape, SYRK, and matrix-norm each run exactly ONCE per invocation, per the harness's own confirmed source structure — do not repeat these one-shot phases even though the factorization phase IS repeated.
warmupNOT discarded in the confirmed source (`for (int i = 0; i < params->nruns; i++) hicma_parsec_potrf(...)` has no separate warmup iteration before the timed/counted loop) — THIS SPEC DEVIATES from the harness's own default and requires nruns>=1 EXTRA untimed factorization call be run first and discarded, matching this whole survey effort's standard warmup discipline; flagged explicitly as a fix, not a reproduction of the artifact's own practice.
repsnruns >= 5 (the harness's own native repetition mechanism, set high enough for a stable mean/std; the confirmed TESTS.md example does not specify a value, defaulting presumably to the code's internal default — open question, not confirmed).
statisticmean and std across the nruns factorization calls (SYNC_TIME_PRINT macro structure implies per-call timing is available; this spec requires aggregating across nruns>=5 rather than reporting a single-run number).
timerSYNC_TIME_START/SYNC_TIME_PRINT macros (device/rank-synchronized wall-clock timing) wrapping each phase independently — the harness's own native timer, unchanged.
timing_scopethe Cholesky-factorization phase ONLY for the primary kernel number (matches the harness's own nruns-loop boundary); forward SHT + SYRK + matrix-norm + inverse SHT are reported as SEPARATE, one-shot numbers per the next field, not folded into the per-factorization-call throughput.
preprocessing_reportedforward SHT (with its own Gflop/s, per the harness's own printed format), forward-SHT-reshape, matrix memory allocation, SYRK, and matrix-norm computation are each reported ONCE, separately, by phase — this is the harness's own native structure (confirmed from source), not an external imposition.
metric
primarysustained EFlop/s (exascale) or GFlop/s (smaller scale) of the mixed-precision factorization phase — the paper's own headline metric (0.976 EFlop/s on Frontier).
secondarywall-clock time per factorization call, mean +/- std across nruns, forward-SHT Gflop/s (the harness's own separately-printed number for this one-shot phase)
correctnessMean Square Error (MSE) between the emulator's inverse-SHT-reconstructed field and a MATLAB reference result (`climate_emulator_diff_double`, `climate_emulator_mse` — confirmed from source), computed once per invocation (not per nruns repetition, since only the LAST factorization's result is fed to the inverse-SHT/MSE stage in the confirmed source structure). Exact MSE tolerance threshold not confirmed from the source read — open question.
Fairness notes
  • This track's 2 papers do not share an input suite, metric, or even mathematical problem class — the spec deliberately does not force one. Any future paper added to this track should be evaluated for which of these 2 fundamentally different kernel classes (physical dynamical-core stencil vs. statistical-emulator linear algebra) it actually belongs to before being folded into either variant.
  • Neither paper reports simulated-days/day (SYPD), the standard production-climate-modeling throughput unit the parent task's own axis description calls out — this is flagged as an open question rather than silently computed via an unconfirmed conversion from either paper's own reported numbers.
  • HiCMA-PaRSEC's own harness already separates one-shot preprocessing (SHT, SYRK, norm) from a repeatable kernel phase (POTRF via --nruns) — this spec adopts that structure directly rather than imposing an external preprocessing/kernel split the way it had to for every other track surveyed so far, but it DOES add a warmup requirement the harness's own default lacks (deliberate fix, noted explicitly).
Open questions
  • ozHOPE's own physical-time-per-simulated-step (needed to convert its reported speedup into a SYPD-comparable number) was not confirmed from the sources read (README + abstract only, no fulltext PDF/arXiv available for this paper per the `stencil` track's own survey).
  • HiCMA-PaRSEC's Frontier-scale --latitude/--NB values for its own 0.976 EFlop/s headline run were not confirmed from the sources read (TESTS.md gives only a smoke-test-scale CLI example, --latitude 120); the production-scale point in variant 2's recommended_subset is a placeholder pending direct paper-PDF confirmation.
  • HiCMA-PaRSEC's MSE correctness-tolerance threshold (what counts as an acceptable emulator-vs-MATLAB-reference agreement) was not confirmed from the source files read (climate_emulator_mse.c's implementation was not fetched, only its call site).
  • Whether HiCMA-PaRSEC's own harness ever runs a discarded warmup factorization call was not confirmed beyond the one loop structure read (`for i in range(nruns): potrf()`, no separate warmup call visible) — this spec assumes no warmup exists in the current public artifact and mandates adding one, but this should be re-verified against the full test-driver source (only testing_climate_emulator.c was read, not every helper it calls) before treating the 'no warmup' finding as certain.
cellular-automata1 papers2 variants

GPU cellular-automaton (CA) time-stepping throughput for the Larger-Than-Life (LTL) family, where the transition function is a weighted summation over an r-cell-radius neighborhood; compares a tensor-core-mapped implementation against CUDA-core baselines (naive, coarsened, shared-memory-tiled, bit-packed) sharing one codebase, across a radius sweep since radius is the axis the paper's own contribution targets.

Given an N x N x Z boolean/low-integer grid (Z independent layers simulated in parallel) and radius r, each step computes for every cell a weighted sum of its (2r+1)x(2r+1) neighborhood and applies a birth/survival threshold rule (LTL: alive iff the sum falls in a configured interval, generalizing Conway's Game of Life to r>1); iterated for `steps` timesteps with periodic or fixed boundary halo handling.

ca-ltl-kernel-throughputsteady-state per-step kernel throughput (cell-updates/s) as a function of neighborhood radius r, one-shot data layout preparation (uint8 -> tensor-core / bit-packed layout) excluded from per-step time and reported separately, since the artifact's own harness already performs this separation and radius is the paper's central independent variable.
inputs
suitesynthetic random-density LTL grids (the artifact's own generator; no external dataset — CA workloads are parametrically generated, not corpus-drawn)
selectiongrid sizes N in {512, 1024, 2048, 4096} (square, Z=1), matching the paper's own GPU-memory-bound size range; radius r in {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16} (the full range the abstract reports, 1<=r<=16, sampled at the values where the paper states a qualitative change: CATSolver competitive at r=1,2, crossing over at r=3, dominant from r>=5)
cell_density0.3 (30% live cells), matching the harness's own default RandomFill density; report if varied since a denser/sparser grid does not change any of these solvers' cost (all are dense, not sparsity-adaptive) but should be fixed for reproducibility
steps1000 (large enough that one-shot data-layout preparation is negligible relative to steady-state stepping cost; report separately regardless per the timing_scope note below)
protocol
warmup1 full untimed step (not present in the public dev-test harness as read; added here as a fairness fix — the harness's single-trial timing is otherwise adopted as-is)
reps10
statisticmedian (report min/max)
timerCUDA events (cudaEventRecord/cudaEventElapsedTime), matching the artifact's own timer; wraps the full `steps`-step loop, not a single step
timing_scopekernel only, over all `steps` steps; one-shot data-layout preparation (prepareData: uint8->tensor-core input packing for CATSolver, bit-packing for PACKSolver) excluded and reported separately, once, matching the artifact's own separation of prepareData from the timed loop
preprocessing_reportedprepareData time, once per (solver, N, radius) combination
metric
primaryGcells/s = N*N*Z*steps / (kernel_time_s * 1e9), matching the artifact's own reported metric
secondaryspeedup vs BASESolver (naive CUDA-core baseline) and vs SHAREDSolver (best non-tensor-core baseline in the codebase), dimensionless x, matching the paper's own headline framing (up to 101x / ~14x)
correctnessMANDATORY pre-timing gate: every solver's final grid state after `steps` steps must match, cell-for-cell, a serial CPU reference implementation of the same LTL rule run on the same initial grid and the same step count (bit-exact, since CA state is boolean/discrete — no tolerance applies). This is a REQUIREMENT this spec adds beyond what the artifact's own `CompareCatPack` check does (see notes_on_fairness): CompareCatPack only cross-checks two of the paper's own implementations against each other, not against an independent reference, so it cannot catch a bug shared by both.
ca-ltl-multistep-fusioneffect of fusing k CA steps into one kernel launch (CATMultiStepSolver / CATMultiStepSolver2 vs single-step CATSolver) on halo-exchange amortization, isolating a second axis (fusion depth) the paper's own three tensor-core variants target independently of the radius sweep.
inputs
suitesame synthetic generator as ca-ltl-kernel-throughput
selectionN=2048, Z=1, radius in {4, 8, 16} (representative of the low/mid/high range), fusion depth k in {1 (CATSolver baseline), 2, 4, 8} (CATMultiStepSolver/2 configurations)
protocol
warmup1
reps10
statisticmedian (report min/max)
timerCUDA events, same convention as ca-ltl-kernel-throughput
timing_scopekernel only, steps fixed at 1000 total regardless of fusion depth (i.e. 1000/k fused-kernel launches for depth k), so all fusion depths execute the same number of underlying CA transitions
metric
primaryGcells/s
secondaryspeedup vs k=1 (CATSolver), dimensionless x
correctnesssame bit-exact gate vs serial CPU reference as ca-ltl-kernel-throughput, applied at the final (post-fusion) grid state
Fairness notes
  • The public dev-test harness (tests/test_CG.cu) times a single trial per configuration with no discarded warmup and no repetition. This spec adds warmup + 10-rep median/min/max on top of the artifact's own CUDA-event timer placement, since single-trial GPU timing is vulnerable to clock/thermal-state noise and this project's fairness principles require a fixed repetition protocol.
  • The artifact's own correctness check (CompareCatPack) validates agreement between two of the paper's own implementations (CAT and PACK solvers), not against an independent reference. This spec requires an independent serial-CPU reference implementation of the LTL rule as the correctness gate instead, since inter-implementation agreement cannot catch a bug shared by both of the paper's own solvers.
  • The abstract also reports energy efficiency (competitive at r<=4, best from r>=5) and a CPU-AMX port; neither is included as a variant here since no energy-measurement code or AMX-relevant benchmark script was found in the surveyed portion of the GPU repo (the AMX port is a separate repository, kezada94/CAT_cpu, not surveyed) — flagged in open_questions rather than fabricated.
Open questions
  • Exact grid sizes and step counts used to produce the paper's own reported figures (as opposed to the dev-test harness's small defaults) were not confirmed from the source read; this spec's size/step choices are this survey's own recommendation, not lifted from a paper script.
  • Whether the paper's reported 101x / ~14x speedups are single-trial or averaged over repeated runs was not determinable from the public harness (which itself runs a single trial); if the paper text states a repetition protocol it was not recovered in this survey's source read (no arXiv/OA fulltext was fetched, only the GitHub repo).
  • The CPU AMX port (kezada94/CAT_cpu) was not surveyed as part of this spec; a CPU variant of this benchmark is an open extension.
fdtd-seismic0 papers3 variants

Throughput of explicit finite-difference-time-domain (FDTD) forward wave-propagation solvers for seismic imaging — isotropic/anisotropic acoustic and elastic wave equations discretized on a regular 3D grid with a damped absorbing-boundary layer, evaluated single-node (order-of-accuracy and temporal-blocking axes) and distributed-memory (halo-exchange-pattern and weak/strong-scaling axes), plus a lower-confidence proprietary-dataflow- hardware variant. Grounded in the Devito DSL/compiler lineage (2 papers, shared artifact with the general `stencil` track); consistent with `benchspecs/stencil/spec.yaml`'s grid-size/timing conventions where the underlying workload is literally the same code, reframed around this track's own primary axes (order of accuracy, absorbing-boundary cost, GPoints/s).

U_out[p] = FD_stencil(U_in, coefficients, space_order) applied at every interior point p of a 3D velocity-model grid for one timestep, for T sequential CFL-determined timesteps; a damped absorbing-boundary-condition (ABC) layer of width w surrounds the physical domain (grid dimension = physical_size + 2w per axis); equation family in {isotropic acoustic, anisotropic/TTI acoustic, isotropic elastic, visco-elastic} per Bisbas et al.'s 4-kernel taxonomy.

fdtd-seismic-single-node-kernelSteady-state single-node throughput of an FD wave-propagation kernel at a fixed space-discretization order, with the one-shot autotuning/blocking-parameter search excluded from the timed region and reported separately — the common denominator this track's two code-grounded papers (BisbasLLNGK21, BisbasNLLKG25) share, and directly comparable to `stencil` track's variant 3 (`stencil-e2e-application`) for the same underlying Devito code.
inputs
suite4 wave-propagator kernels confirmed from BisbasNLLKG25's own evaluation (fulltext): isotropic acoustic (star stencil, 5 fields), anisotropic/TTI acoustic (coupled 2-PDE, rotated Laplacian, 12 fields), isotropic elastic (1st-order-in-time, 9 wavefield parameters, 22 grids), visco-elastic (1st-order-in-time, 15 stencil updates, 36 grids) — union with BisbasLLNGK21's 3 kernels (isotropic acoustic/TTI/elastic, visco-elastic not present in that paper).
selectionall 4 kernels BisbasNLLKG25 evaluates; the 3 common to both Bisbas papers get cross-checked against BisbasLLNGK21's independently-run numbers where both exist.
recommended_subsetisotropic-acoustic, anisotropic-tti-acoustic, isotropic-elastic, visco-elastic
dense_operandvelocity-model grid, fp32 (BisbasLLNGK21's stated precision; BisbasNLLKG25's precision not confirmed from extracted text — flagged open question, do not silently assume fp64 from geophysics convention alone).
grid_sizes512^3 (BisbasLLNGK21, isotropic/elastic; 20m spacing for TTI) or 1024^3 (BisbasNLLKG25, acoustic/elastic/TTI) / 768^3 (BisbasNLLKG25, visco-elastic) — report BOTH size points since the two papers use different conventions and neither claims priority; do not silently pick one.
order_of_accuracyspace discretization order (SDO) in {4, 8, 12, 16} — SWEEP ALL FOUR, not just one. BisbasNLLKG25's own primary results use SDO 8 and 12 with SDO 4/16 as appendix/secondary points; this spec requires all 4 be reported since order-of-accuracy vs. throughput is this track's own paper-native tradeoff axis (survey.md Divergence 1), not an incidental implementation choice to be fixed at one value.
absorbing_boundarydamped ABC layer, width w=40 grid points per BisbasNLLKG25's own confirmed convention (1024^3 physical domain -> 1120^3 total grid with ABC, i.e. +48 points per axis edge / +96 per dimension total). REPORT THE ABC-INCLUSIVE GRID SIZE EXPLICITLY, not just the physical domain size — this is the direct fix for survey.md Divergence 2 (every other surveyed paper leaves ABC cost unquantified).
protocol
iteration_countCFL-determined, paper-native, NOT an arbitrary round number: 228 (BisbasLLNGK21 isotropic acoustic) / 290 (BisbasNLLKG25 isotropic acoustic/TTI) steps covering 512ms simulated time; 363-436 steps (elastic, both papers' values differ slightly — report the computed value for the specific grid/velocity-model/CFL-number combination used, don't hardcode either paper's number verbatim); 251 steps (visco-elastic, BisbasNLLKG25). Always derive T from the CFL condition for the actual grid spacing/velocity model used, per both papers' own convention — never substitute a fixed T across different grid spacings.
warmup1 full run discarded, if the harness cleanly separates setup/autotuning from the timed sweep loop (Devito's own autotuner runs BEFORE the timed operator call in the standard `benchmark.py` flow, so this is achievable without inventing a capability the harness lacks — unlike `stencil` track's variant 3 "many full-application codes can't cheaply discard a warmup" caveat, which does not apply here).
reps5
statisticmedian (report min/max). FIX: neither surveyed Bisbas paper's extracted text states an explicit repetition/statistic convention for the single-node number — this spec mandates one rather than leaving it unspecified, matching the general `stencil` track's own practice of fixing this gap.
timerwall clock (`MPI_Wtime`/`time.time()`) around the Devito Operator's `.apply()` call for T timesteps, one call = one interval, divided by T for the per-step figure — matches Devito's own `benchmark.py` structure (`--tn` sets total simulated ms, internally converted to T via CFL).
timing_scopekernel only. Devito's autotuner (`DEVITO_AUTOTUNING`, sweeps the blocking-parameter space for the global performance maximum, confirmed from BisbasLLNGK21's extracted text) runs BEFORE the timed call and is excluded; ABC-layer computation is INCLUDED (per `operation`'s definition above — the ABC is physically part of the solve, not a communication halo to exclude, unlike distributed halo exchange in variant 2).
preprocessing_reportedautotuning search time measured once, separately, and reported as its own ms number — same discipline as `stencil` track's Tensor-Core variant, applied here to Devito's blocking-parameter autotuner instead of a format-conversion step.
metric
primaryGPoints/s = grid_points_including_ABC * T / elapsed_s / 1e9 — the literal metric both Bisbas papers report.
secondary%-of-roofline-attainable peak (BisbasLLNGK21 explicitly frames results this way, breaking through an L3-cache-bound ceiling via temporal blocking), speedup of temporal-blocking-on vs. spatially-blocked-only (BisbasLLNGK21's own ablation, ~1.3-1.6x at space order 4)
correctnessmax relative error <= 1e-5 vs. an unblocked/reference Devito-generated kernel of the same equation, grid, space order, and T — analogous to `stencil` track's variant-1 tolerance; NOT independently confirmed from either Bisbas paper's extracted text (open question, this spec's own recommendation by analogy).
fdtd-seismic-distributed-e2eDistributed-memory (MPI-X) strong/weak-scaling throughput at fixed per-node grid size, with 3 halo-exchange communication patterns compared head-to-head — BisbasNLLKG25's own paper-native contribution and the sole confirmed source for this variant.
inputs
suitesame 4-kernel taxonomy as variant 1 (isotropic acoustic / TTI / elastic / visco-elastic).
selectionisotropic acoustic recommended as the primary distributed-scaling case (lowest arithmetic intensity, most communication-bound, and BisbasNLLKG25's own primary scaling figure).
recommended_subsetisotropic-acoustic
dense_operandsame fp32/unconfirmed-precision convention as variant 1.
grid_sizesweak scaling: 256^3 per-node base size, cyclically doubled with node count (BisbasNLLKG25's own convention, confirmed from fulltext); strong scaling: fixed total grid (1024^3 or 1120^3 with ABC per variant 1) spread across up to 128 nodes / 16,384 cores (BisbasNLLKG25's own demonstrated scale on ARCHER2).
communication_patternbasic (synchronous multi-phase), diag2 (synchronous single-phase with diagonal exchanges), full (asynchronous compute/communication overlap) — all 3 are live `DEVITO_MPI` modes in the shared `devitocodes/devito` artifact; REPORT ALL 3 AS SEPARATE POINTS, not just the best-performing one, since which pattern wins depends on arithmetic intensity / field count per BisbasNLLKG25's own cross-kernel results.
protocol
iteration_countsame CFL-determined convention as variant 1.
warmup1 full run discarded (same as variant 1, if the distributed harness supports it; not independently confirmed for the MPI path specifically).
reps3
statisticmedian (report min/max) — reduced rep count vs. variant 1 reflects the higher cost of a 128-node run, matching stencil track's variant-3 (application-scale) convention.
timerwall clock around the distributed Operator.apply() call, MPI-synchronized at start/stop (all ranks reach the timed region before the clock starts).
timing_scopeend-to-end distributed compute time including halo exchange (halo exchange is the variant's own subject, unlike `stencil` track's variant 1 which explicitly excludes halo exchange as out-of-scope for a single-device claim).
preprocessing_reporteddomain decomposition / mesh distribution setup reported once, separately, never amortized into the per-step throughput.
metric
primaryaggregate GPoints/s across all ranks.
secondaryweak/strong scaling efficiency vs. node count (relative to the variant-1 single-node number for the same kernel/grid-per-node, when both exist), GPoints/s per node (for cross-checking against variant 1's single-node number)
correctnesssame convention as variant 1, additionally checked for bit-for-bit or tolerance-level agreement across communication-pattern choices (basic/diag2/full must produce the same physics, only differ in speed) — not independently confirmed from the extracted text, flagged as an open question.
fdtd-seismic-dataflow-acceleratorHalf/mixed-precision or dataflow-architecture-specific FDTD throughput on proprietary hardware (Cerebras wafer-scale engine, Huawei Ascend NPU) — the LOWEST-CONFIDENCE variant in this track's spec, included for completeness because 2 of the 5 surveyed papers target this hardware class, but every field below is sourced from an abstract or an unverified web-search snippet, not a paper PDF or artifact.
inputs
suiteCGFDM (curvilinear-grid FD method, WangSWZGGWZFXY25) or unspecified high-order stencils (SaiMXA24) — no shared/named suite between the 2 papers.
selectionOPEN QUESTION — neither paper's specific grid/mesh/stencil-order choices could be confirmed beyond the abstract.
recommended_subset
dense_operandhalf-precision (FP16) storage + mixed-precision arithmetic (WangSWZGGWZFXY25's explicit contribution); precision scheme for SaiMXA24 not stated in the abstract.
grid_sizesOPEN QUESTION — not confirmed for either paper.
protocol
iteration_countOPEN QUESTION — not confirmed.
warmupOPEN QUESTION — not confirmed; proprietary-SDK harnesses (Cerebras SDK, Ascend CANN) have their own conventions not independently verifiable here.
reps3
statisticmedian (report min/max) — this spec's own default, not sourced from either paper.
timervendor-SDK-provided device timer (not independently confirmed which API).
timing_scopekernel only, by this spec's default convention — not independently confirmed.
preprocessing_reportedany wafer-scale-engine on-chip layout/routing compilation (Cerebras) reported once, separately, if applicable — SaiMXA24's own abstract explicitly frames data-communication routing as a core challenge its codegen addresses, implying nonzero compile/layout cost, but no number is given.
metric
primaryGPoints/s (for cross-comparability with variants 1/2, where the underlying papers' own metric convention is confirmed).
secondaryspeedup vs. a same-precision CPU baseline (WangSWZGGWZFXY25's own headline framing: 4.19x vs. two AMD CPUs, from an unverified web-search snippet, NOT fulltext-confirmed)
correctnessphysical validation against a real seismic event (WangSWZGGWZFXY25: 2008 Wenchuan earthquake simulation, per abstract) rather than a pointwise numerical tolerance — DELIBERATELY WEAKER than variant 1/2's gate, flagged as an open question rather than equated to it, matching `stencil` track's own posture toward application-level correctness claims (its variant 3).
Fairness notes
  • Absorbing-boundary cost is quantified by exactly one paper in this whole track (BisbasNLLKG25: 1024^3 -> 1120^3 for a 40-point ABC) and left implicit/unquantified by every other surveyed paper. This spec makes ABC width a mandatory explicit input in variant 1 rather than letting it default to an unstated, paper-specific convention.
  • Order-of-accuracy is made a REQUIRED sweep (all of SDO 4/8/12/16), not a single fixed value, because it is this track's own paper-native tradeoff axis (BisbasNLLKG25 sweeps it directly) — reducing it to one number the way a generic stencil spec might would erase the exact axis this track exists to capture.
  • Variant 2's 3-way communication-pattern comparison (basic/diag2/full) is mandatory precisely because BisbasNLLKG25's own results show no single pattern dominates across all 4 kernels — reporting only the best-performing pattern per kernel would hide a real, paper-documented tradeoff.
  • Variant 3 (proprietary dataflow hardware) is included for completeness (2 of 5 papers target it) but is explicitly the lowest-confidence variant in this spec, sourced from abstracts/web-search snippets rather than fulltext or artifacts, and should not be treated as equally reliable as variants 1/2.
  • This track deliberately EXCLUDES 2 seismic-adjacent papers found by keyword search (LtaiefHWJRK23's TLR-MVM, HuYLGYQ20's CMP/CRS) because neither is an FD wave-equation stencil — including them would conflate a genuinely different kernel family (dense-LA compression; post-stack signal processing) with this track's actual subject (forward FDTD wave propagation), even though both are 'seismic' in the domain-application sense.
Open questions
  • BisbasNLLKG25's precision (fp32 vs fp64) was not confirmed from the extracted arXiv fulltext — variant 1 assumes fp32 by inheritance from BisbasLLNGK21's confirmed precision, but this is an assumption, not independently verified for the newer paper.
  • Neither Bisbas paper's extracted text states an explicit repetition-count/statistic convention for the single-node timing number — variant 1's 5-rep/median mandate is this spec's own standardization, matching the general `stencil` track's practice of fixing this same gap for its own papers.
  • WangSWZGGWZFXY25's 4.19x headline speedup number is sourced from an unverified web-search result snippet, not the paper's own fulltext or abstract (the abstract in `output/included.json` was truncated before the results sentence) — flagged as lower-confidence than every other numeric claim in this survey.
  • SaiMXA24's grid sizes, stencil orders, and metric convention could not be determined from its abstract alone; a Cerebras SDK artifact, if one exists, was not found by this survey's search and may require direct author contact or conference-proceedings access to confirm.
  • Whether SaiMXA24 or WangSWZGGWZFXY25 report a metric convertible to GPoints/s (variant 3's chosen primary, for comparability with variants 1/2) was not confirmed — this may require a metric-conversion assumption that neither paper's own text validates.
lattice-boltzmann0 papers3 variants

Throughput of an iterative lattice-Boltzmann (LBM) collision-streaming sweep over a 3D lattice, across the two workload classes this track's papers actually target: a regular cuboid domain (optionally with nested-grid spatial/temporal refinement), and a sparse/complex-geometry domain where indirect boundary/solid-fraction addressing dominates cost. Grounded in one code-verified paper (MahmoudSM24 / Autodesk XLB); the other 4 surveyed papers are abstract-only (see survey.md's Scope note — this track has NO automated-pipeline-detected artifact; MahmoudSM24's artifact was found by this survey's own manual search and corrects the pipeline's record).

For every lattice site x and every discrete velocity direction i in the chosen velocity set (D2Q9 in 2D; D3Q19 or D3Q27 in 3D): collide f_i(x) -> f_i*(x) via a collision operator (BGK single-relaxation-time or KBC), then stream f_i*(x) -> f_i(x + e_i) along direction i's lattice vector; solid/boundary sites additionally apply a bounce-back or equilibrium boundary condition. One sweep = one collide+stream pass over every lattice site, repeated for T timesteps.

lbm-regular-grid-kernelSteady-state per-timestep throughput of collide-stream on a regular cuboid lattice, with or without nested-grid spatial/temporal refinement, at a fixed lattice model/precision/collision-model combination — the common denominator any regular-domain LBM implementation can be measured against. Grounded directly in `Autodesk/XLB`'s `examples/performance/mlups_3d.py` (single-resolution) and `mlups_3d_multires.py` (nested-refinement) benchmark scripts.
inputs
suiteLid-driven cavity (LDC) at Reynolds number 5000 — XLB's own primary performance-benchmark problem for both scripts surveyed. No other paper in this track supplies a competing regular-domain benchmark problem to union against (open question: whether a non-LDC regular workload should be added once a second code-grounded paper is found).
selectionthe one regular-domain benchmark problem confirmed from source across this track's only code-grounded paper.
recommended_subset100^3, single resolution, 200^3, single resolution, 100^3, 2 refinement levels (peeled-boundary refinement), 200^3, 3 refinement levels
dense_operandone distribution-function array per velocity direction (19 for D3Q19, 27 for D3Q27) per lattice site, initialized to the LDC's prescribed lid velocity (u=0.1 in lattice units) and equilibrium elsewhere — XLB's own `ldc_multires_setup`/equivalent single-res setup convention.
grid_sizescube_edge in {100, 200} (XLB's own CLI examples; not independently confirmed against MahmoudSM24's own paper-reported headline number, which web search (not fulltext) suggests reaches 1596x840x840 on a single A100 via refinement's memory savings — flagged as an open question pending direct paper-PDF confirmation).
lattice_modelD3Q19 (default) or D3Q27, collision model BGK (default) or KBC (KBC requires D3Q27) — all 4 combinations are valid CLI points in the source artifact; report the combination used explicitly, never silently default.
refinementnum_levels in {1 (no refinement), 2, 3}; refinement peels inward from the domain boundary, concentrating resolution near the walls (XLB's own `ldc_multires_setup` convention); mres_perf_opt in {NAIVE_COLLIDE_STREAM, FUSION_AT_FINEST} is itself a reportable implementation-choice axis, not folded into the headline number.
protocol
iteration_countT=1000 for num_levels=1 (matching XLB's own single-resolution CLI example); T=1000 at the coarsest level for refined runs (finer levels sub-cycle 2^(num_levels-1) times per coarsest step, automatically, per XLB's own `calculate_mlups`).
warmup10 full-sweep iterations, device-synchronized, discarded before timing starts. THIS IS A DELIBERATE STANDARDIZATION: XLB's own `mlups_3d.py` (single-resolution) already does exactly this; its sibling `mlups_3d_multires.py` (refined) does NOT warm up at all in the public artifact — this spec requires the warmup for BOTH grid configurations, fixing the refined script's gap rather than reproducing it (survey.md Divergence 1).
reps5
statisticmean and std (report both, not just mean). FIX/EXTENSION: XLB's own `mlups_3d.py` already supports exactly this via `--repetitions N` (default 1) — this spec simply mandates N>=5 be used rather than the CLI's own default of a single trial, and requires the refined script (which has no repetition support at all in the public artifact) be run N times externally and aggregated the same way.
timerdevice-wide barrier (`wp.synchronize()` or equivalent) immediately before start and immediately before stop, host `time.time()` (or equivalent wall-clock call) in between — XLB's own convention in both scripts, unchanged.
timing_scopekernel only (collide+stream+BC for all T sweeps as one interval). Grid/BC construction, JIT/kernel compilation (Warp/Neon backends compile kernels on first call), and any GPU-side history recording (`--report`) are excluded from the timed region — matches XLB's own script structure (grid setup happens before `wp.synchronize(); start_time = time.time()`).
preprocessing_reportednot applicable at this variant's problem sizes (grid/BC setup is O(N) index-array construction, not a distinct format-conversion step); if Warp/Neon JIT-compiles device kernels on the first call inside a cold process, that one-time compile cost must be reported separately if it is not already excluded by the harness's own setup/timing split (open question: not directly confirmed which side of the timing boundary first-call JIT lands on in XLB's scripts).
metric
primaryMLUPS (Million Lattice Updates Per Second), SITE-level (not per-direction): cube_edge^3 * effective_steps / elapsed_s / 1e6, where effective_steps accounts for finer-level sub-stepping (num_steps * 2^(num_levels-1)) when refinement is active — XLB's own `calculate_mlups` formula, adopted verbatim. State the D3Q19-vs-D3Q27 direction count explicitly alongside any reported number (survey.md Divergence 3 — equal MLUPS at D3Q27 is more total work than at D3Q19).
secondaryms per timestep (mean +/- std across reps), effective GB/s (bytes moved = num_directions * sizeof(dtype) * 2 [read+write] * lattice_sites per sweep)
correctnessmax relative error <= 1e-5 in the macroscopic velocity/density fields vs. an unoptimized/reference collide-stream implementation of the same lattice model, precision, and T. THIS IS THIS SPEC'S OWN RECOMMENDATION, NOT SOURCED FROM ANY PAPER IN THIS TRACK — flagged explicitly as an open question (survey.md Divergence 4); XLB's repo has a `tests/` tree implying some correctness coverage exists, but no benchmark-script-level tolerance for this specific LDC case was confirmed from the scripts read.
lbm-complex-geometry-kernelThroughput of collide-stream on a sparse/complex-geometry domain (porous media, vascular/arterial networks, arbitrary solid boundaries), where indirect geometric addressing dominates cost — the workload class 3 of this track's 5 surveyed papers independently target (Herschlag, Gounley, Qin), none of which have a public artifact. THIS VARIANT IS LITERATURE-DERIVED, NOT CODE-VERIFIED — every field below is inferred from paper abstracts plus this track's variant-1 protocol, not confirmed against any of these 3 papers' own (unavailable) run scripts. Treat as a lower-confidence spec than variant 1.
inputs
suiteno shared/named benchmark suite could be confirmed across the 3 papers from abstracts alone; each names a different application domain (Herschlag: unspecified "complex domains"; Gounley: implied 3D vascular/biomedical-adjacent from lab context, not stated explicitly in the abstract; Qin: porous media, arterial blood flow, tissue fluid, explicitly named in the abstract).
selectionOPEN QUESTION — this spec cannot fix a concrete named suite from the available sources. A future revision should pull the specific geometry files/porosity fractions each paper's (currently unavailable) artifact or full paper PDF actually used.
recommended_subset
dense_operandsame per-direction distribution-function representation as variant 1, but with a solid/fluid indicator (bitmask, coded node-type array, or sparse index list per Qin's "address index array and node classification coding scheme") marking a substantial NON-cuboid fraction of lattice sites as solid/excluded.
grid_sizesOPEN QUESTION — not stated in any surveyed abstract.
protocol
iteration_countsame T convention as variant 1 (not independently confirmed for this variant's papers).
warmupsame as variant 1: 10 discarded iterations (this spec's standardization, not sourced from these 3 papers).
reps5
statisticmean and std (same convention as variant 1, for cross-variant comparability).
timerdevice-side event pair or wall clock with explicit sync barrier (same convention as variant 1).
timing_scopekernel + indirect-addressing lookup only; the one-shot geometry-classification/index-array-construction pass (Qin's "node classification coding scheme", any porosity-mask precomputation) is preprocessing and MUST be excluded from the per-step timed loop and reported once, separately — this is the direct complex-geometry analogue of the `stencil` track's Tensor-Core-preprocessing variant.
preprocessing_reportedmeasured once, separately, as its own ms number — see timing_scope.
metric
primaryMLUPS computed over FLUID (non-solid) sites only, not the bounding cuboid's total site count — otherwise sparse/porous geometries would report an artificially depressed number purely from counting solid cells that do no work. Report the fluid-site fraction alongside the MLUPS number so readers can reconstruct the bounding-box-relative figure if desired.
secondaryeffective GB/s, same convention as variant 1, restricted to fluid-site traffic, speedup vs. a fully-indirect (naive) addressing baseline on the same geometry, same hardware — the specific comparison Herschlag's own abstract frames as its headline result (semi-direct vs. indirect)
correctnesssame 1e-5 relative-error convention as variant 1 (this spec's own recommendation, not sourced from these papers).
lbm-distributed-e2eEnd-to-end distributed-memory throughput/scaling for extreme-scale LBM CFD (SunwayLB's own framing) — reported separately from, never substituted for, a single-node kernel-only number from variant 1/2, matching this whole cross-track survey's standard split between kernel-only and end-to-end application variants.
inputs
suitepaper-native industrial CFD case; not specified in the surveyed abstract.
selectionOPEN QUESTION — SunwayLB's own benchmark problem(s) not confirmed beyond 'industrial applications' framing in the abstract.
recommended_subset
grid_sizesOPEN QUESTION — not stated in the abstract; SunwayLB's own multi-level domain-decomposition scheme implies extreme-scale (many-node) grids, size unconfirmed.
protocol
iteration_countpaper-native; not confirmed.
warmupnot confirmed whether SunwayLB's own harness discards a warmup run.
reps3
statisticmedian (report min/max) — this spec's own default per the cross-track convention, not sourced from SunwayLB's paper.
timerwall clock around the distributed compute loop; not independently confirmed.
timing_scopeend-to-end whole-program distributed compute time, reported alongside (not instead of) a variant-1/2 kernel-only number when both exist for the same code.
preprocessing_reporteddomain-decomposition/mesh setup reported once, separately, never amortized.
metric
primaryGLUPS (Giga Lattice Updates Per Second) aggregate across all nodes — the natural extreme-scale extension of variant 1's MLUPS, matching how `stencil` track's K-Athena reports aggregate cell-updates/s.
