correctnessdomain-specific; not confirmed from the abstract. Flagged as an open question, deliberately not equated to variant 1/2's pointwise tolerance (same posture as `stencil` track's variant 3).
Fairness notes
  • This track has ZERO papers with a Phase-1-pipeline-detected public artifact. One (MahmoudSM24/XLB) was found by this survey's own manual search and corrects that record; the other 4 remain genuinely artifact-less as far as this survey could determine. Any spec built here is necessarily lower-confidence than `stencil`'s, and this is stated up front rather than papered over with confident-sounding but unsourced numbers.
  • XLB's own two benchmark scripts disagree with each other on warmup rigor (mlups_3d.py: 10-iteration discarded warmup + N-repetition mean/std; mlups_3d_multires.py: single trial, no warmup). This spec mandates the more rigorous protocol for BOTH grid configurations rather than letting the refined-grid variant inherit the less rigorous script's practice.
  • Complex-geometry LBM (variant 2) is independently identified as a real, recurring sub-problem by 3 separate papers (Herschlag, Gounley, Qin) from 2 different research groups, which is why it earns its own variant despite zero of the 3 having a confirmed artifact — the convergent literature signal is strong even though the code-verification signal is absent.
  • MLUPS is made site-level (not per-direction) primary specifically so a D3Q19 and a D3Q27 kernel's numbers are NOT silently treated as equivalent 'work done' — this is the direct analogue of the `stencil` track's GCell-updates/s-vs-undisclosed-FLOP-convention fix (survey.md Divergence 3).
Open questions
  • MahmoudSM24's own paper-reported headline grid size/hardware point (web search suggests 1596x840x840 on a single A100) could not be verified against the paper PDF directly (escholarship PDF was not text-extractable by this survey's tooling) — variant 1's grid_sizes field uses XLB's own CLI example sizes (100^3/200^3) instead, flagged as smaller than the paper's actual headline demonstration.
  • None of Herschlag, Gounley, Liu (SunwayLB), or Qin's OA/abstract sources yielded concrete grid sizes, precision, hardware, or MLUPS numbers — variant 2 and variant 3 are structurally underspecified relative to variant 1 and should be revisited once a paper PDF (not just abstract) from one of these 4 can be obtained and text-extracted.
  • Whether Warp/Neon backend JIT/kernel-compilation cost falls inside or outside XLB's own timed region in `mlups_3d.py`/`mlups_3d_multires.py` was not conclusively determined by reading the benchmark scripts alone (grid/BC setup precedes the timer start, but first-kernel-launch JIT compile inside the timed loop's first iteration was not ruled out) — flagged rather than asserted either way.
  • No correctness tolerance specific to this track's own papers could be sourced; the 1e-5 relative-error default in variants 1/2 is this spec's own recommendation by analogy to the `stencil` track's AN5D/PERKS convention, not derived from any lattice-Boltzmann paper itself.

spectral

fft10 papers4 variants

Throughput of the (Fast) Fourier Transform — forward and inverse, complex-to-complex (C2C) and real-to-complex/complex-to-real (R2C/C2R), 1D/2D/3D, batched — across the four usage patterns this track's own papers actually benchmark: a bare batched-kernel microbenchmark (TurboFFT, TurboFNO, cuFalcon), an FFT embedded inside a larger scientific pipeline on a dense regular grid (FFCz, CLAIRE, cuHPX's ring-FFT), a distributed multi-node/multi-GPU transform whose all-to-all (or device-direct) communication dominates at scale (FLUPS, CLAIRE), and the one-shot plan-creation / kernel-codegen cost every one of those targets pays before its first transform and which none of them consistently reports as its own number (this track's analogue of "preprocessing").

Y = FFT_dims(X, direction), X a dense array of shape [batch, N_1, ..., N_d] (d in {1,2,3}), direction in {forward, inverse}; C2C keeps X,Y complex of the same shape, R2C/C2R halve/double the last transformed dimension per the standard Hermitian-symmetry packing. N_i may be a power of two (the majority convention in this track's own papers) or mixed-radix (FlashFFTStencil's PFA-decomposed 56/64/128, cuHPX's ellmax=3*nside-1). "Plan creation" denotes whatever one-shot setup a given implementation requires before its first transform of a given (shape, precision, direction) configuration — a runtime plan object (cufftPlan*/fftw_plan_dft*), a build-time kernel-codegen+compile step (TurboFFT/TurboFNO), or a precomputed Green's-function+communication pattern (FLUPS) — see survey.md Divergence 3.

fft-1d-batched-kernelSteady-state batched 1D FFT kernel throughput, power-of-two AND mixed-radix lengths, both fp32 and fp64, with plan creation / kernel codegen excluded from the timed region but measured once and reported separately (never silently amortized in). This is the common denominator across TurboFFT, TurboFNO, and cuFalcon's internal FFT use — the three papers in this track that treat FFT as (or reduce to) a bare batched-kernel call rather than a step inside a larger pipeline.
inputs
suitePower-of-two 1D C2C lengths spanning TurboFFT's own full sweep (N = 2^9 .. 2^25), PLUS three mixed-radix lengths drawn from other papers in this track so the suite is not power-of-two-only, per the task instructions' explicit ask: 56 (FlashFFTStencil's PFA tile size, = 2^3 * 7), 3071 (cuHPX's ellmax = 3*nside-1 at nside=1024, prime-adjacent), 10000 (a 5-smooth control point, = 2^4 * 5^4, of the kind FFTW/cuFFT both handle efficiently via mixed-radix decomposition but naive radix-2-only implementations cannot).
selectionUnion of every N value literally read out of a surveyed paper's own code/config in this track (TurboFFT's power-of-two sweep bounds, TurboFNO's N in {64,128}, FlashFFTStencil's 56/64/128, cuHPX's 3*nside-1, cuFalcon's Falcon_N in {512,1024}), plus the one 5-smooth control point added for mixed-radix coverage since no surveyed paper's own suite contains a "generic" mixed-radix length.
recommended_subset512, 1024, 4096, 56, 65536, 1048576, 3071, 4194304, 10000, 16777216, 33554432
batchTWO required sweep modes, both reported, matching TurboFFT's own `--if_bench 1` vs `--if_bench 2` distinction (survey.md's TurboFFT subsection): (a) size-scaling — fix N, sweep batch in {1, 8, 64, 512, 4096, 32768}; (b) fixed-total-work batch/size tradeoff — fix N*batch = 2^25 (TurboFFT's own constant), sweep N across the power-of-two suite above and set batch = 2^25 / N accordingly. Mode (b) is the one that actually stresses the "many small transforms" (crypto/NTT-adjacent) vs. "few huge transforms" (scientific-HPC) regimes on equal total FLOP footing, and is included specifically because it is the more informative of the two, not merely the cheaper one to run.
dense_operandcomplex interleaved input, BOTH fp32 and fp64 REQUIRED (not primary/secondary — TurboFFT and FFCz are the two papers in this track that benchmark both symmetrically on the same workload, and this spec follows that convention rather than TurboFNO's fp32-only practice), initialized U(-1,1) random (matching TurboFFT/FlashFFTStencil's own random-fill convention, not cherry-picked "nice" data like an impulse or a low-frequency sinusoid that would be atypically compressible/predictable).
layoutBOTH in-place and out-of-place reported as separate numbers. This is an explicit ADD by this spec: no paper surveyed in this track states which layout its own reported numbers use, yet the choice materially changes achievable memory bandwidth (in-place halves the traffic for a pure-FFT kernel but forces extra synchronization/scratch-space handling for multi-pass radix decompositions like TurboFFT's own multi-kernel-launch design) — collapsing this to one unstated choice would silently hide a real, paper-relevant performance axis.
protocol
warmup2 full launch-sequence passes, discarded. Strengthens TurboFFT's own convention (1 undiscarded-but-excluded warmup pass) by a small margin; does not change TurboFFT's own methodology in any way that would make its numbers non-reproducible under this spec.
reps20
statisticmedian (report min and max alongside it). THIS IS A DELIBERATE FIX: TurboFFT reports the mean of ntest=10 reps and TurboFNO reports the mean of "tens of runs" — neither reports a spread, and cuFalcon reports a single untimed-loop measurement with no repetition at all (survey.md Divergence 1). Median-of-20 with min/max is chosen specifically because none of this track's own surveyed papers already reports a distribution, so there is no existing convention this contradicts, and a mean over few reps is sensitive to the occasional outlier launch that a median absorbs.
timerdevice-side event pair (CUDA/HIP events), with exactly ONE synchronization call after all `reps` timed launches complete, not one sync per individual kernel launch inside the loop. THIS IS A DELIBERATE FIX: TurboFFT's own reference implementation calls `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` after EVERY individual radix-stage kernel launch inside its timed `ntest` loop (survey.md Divergence 2), which adds `kernel_launch_times * ntest` sync-barrier stalls rather than `ntest` — internally consistent for TurboFFT's own TurboFFT-vs-cuFFT comparison (both timed the same way) but not comparable to a differently-synchronized harness without correcting for it. This spec requires the single-sync-at-the-end form uniformly.
timing_scopetransform kernel(s) only; H2D/D2H excluded. Whatever one-shot setup an implementation needs before its first transform of a given (N, precision, direction, layout) configuration — a runtime plan object OR a build-time codegen+compile step (survey.md Divergence 3) — is EXCLUDED from this variant's timed region and instead measured by the dedicated `fft-plan-creation` variant below.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per (N, precision, direction, layout) configuration, via the `fft-plan-creation` variant; never amortized into this variant's per-call number.
metric
primaryGFLOP/s = 5 * N * log2(N) * batch / elapsed_s (the standard radix-2 Cooley-Tukey FLOP-count convention, literally TurboFFT's own formula) for power-of-two N. For the three mixed-radix N values in the suite, this convention does not cleanly apply (mixed-radix FFT algorithms have a different, decomposition-dependent operation count) — report ms only for those points and do not force a GFLOP/s number onto them (do not silently reuse the power-of-two formula, which would misrepresent mixed-radix efficiency).
secondaryms per transform (median, min, max), GB/s effective bandwidth = 2 * N * batch * sizeof(dtype) / elapsed_s (TurboFFT's own convention; halved for the in-place layout sub-case)
correctnessmax relative error <= 1e-4 vs. cuFFT (or FFTW, CPU target) at the SAME precision, for fp32 (TurboFFT's own tolerance, `utils::compareData`). For fp64: max relative error <= 1e-10 against the same reference at fp64 — THIS IS THIS SPEC'S OWN RECOMMENDATION, not sourced from any surveyed paper (TurboFFT applies its 1e-4 tolerance uniformly to both its fp32 and fp64 paths, which is unnecessarily loose for fp64 and would not catch a real fp64-path regression); flagged as an open question pending confirmation from a paper that states an fp64-specific tolerance.
fft-ndgrid-e2eEnd-to-end round-trip (forward + inverse) FFT throughput on a dense 2D/3D regular grid, with ONE-SHOT plan creation amortized over k round trips (k reported explicitly) — representative of how FFT actually appears in this track's application-embedded papers (FFCz's compression-correction pass, CLAIRE's registration-solver preconditioner, cuHPX's ring-FFT-plus-Legendre-transform, FLUPS's Poisson solve) rather than as a bare kernel call.
inputs
suiteEvery named grid size literally reported by a surveyed paper in this track (not a synthetic size invented for this spec): 256^3 (CLAIRE's single-GPU headline size), 512^3 (FFCz's own README usage example), 1024x768x768 (CLAIRE's real, non-cubic CLARITY microscopy dataset), 2048^3 (CLAIRE's largest weak-scaling point, ~25 billion unknowns), plus two 2D sizes since cuHPX's ring-FFT and 2D-FNO variants operate on 2D grids: 4096^2, 8192^2.
selectionUnion of every grid size explicitly named in a surveyed paper's README/abstract text for this variant's usage class (FFCz, CLAIRE); the two 2D sizes are this spec's own addition (open question below) since no surveyed paper states a headline 2D grid size — they are included so the 2D axis is not silently dropped rather than being sourced from a specific paper's own reported number.
recommended_subset256^3, fp64 (CLAIRE single-GPU headline case), 512^3, fp32 AND fp64 (FFCz's own dual-precision example workload), 1024x768x768, fp32 (CLAIRE CLARITY dataset — non-cubic, tests mixed-radix dimension handling since 768 = 2^8*3), 2048^3, fp32 (CLAIRE largest weak-scaling point; single-node/GPU subset of this size for the e2e variant, full-scale only under fft-distributed-alltoall), 4096^2, fp32 AND fp64 (2D control point; open question — not paper-sourced), 8192^2, fp32 (2D control point; open question — not paper-sourced)
dense_operandreal-valued input, real-to-complex (R2C) forward + complex-to-real (C2R) inverse round trip (the natural pairing for real scientific grid data — cosmology density fields, combustion scalar fields, diffraction images per FFCz's own motivating domains). fp32 and fp64 BOTH required per grid size where listed above, following FFCz's own dual-precision CLI design (the only paper in this track's e2e-usage class to test both explicitly).
layoutout-of-place by default (the safer, more common library default); in-place reported as a secondary number when the target implementation supports it for R2C/C2R (note: R2C/C2R in-place requires padding the real array to the complex array's size, per FFTW/cuFFT convention — this padding is NOT counted as a separate "format conversion" cost, it is part of the transform's own memory layout).
protocol
plan_creationperformed ONCE per (grid size, precision, direction) configuration, amortized over k=20 forward+inverse round trips for this variant's steady-state number. k=20 is THIS SPEC'S OWN CHOICE — no surveyed paper states a numeric amortization count, though FLUPS's own README explicitly frames its precomputed Green's-function and communication pattern as reusable "many times... at low cost," which this variant's design generalizes into a concrete, reportable number (survey.md's FLUPS subsection).
warmup2 full round-trip passes after plan creation, discarded.
reps20
statisticmedian (report min and max).
timerdevice-side events (GPU targets) or wall-clock with an explicit synchronization barrier at trial start and stop (CPU targets, e.g. FLUPS's own FFTW-backed CPU path) — matching whichever mechanism is native to the target, same convention as this track's `fft-1d-batched-kernel` variant.
timing_scopeforward+inverse transform only, per round trip; H2D/D2H excluded for GPU targets. Plan creation is excluded here and reported once, separately, by the dedicated `fft-plan-creation` variant.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per (grid size, precision, direction) configuration, via `fft-plan-creation`; never amortized silently into this variant's per-round-trip number (the amortization THIS variant itself performs, over k=20, is reported as its own labeled number, distinct from the zero-amortization plan-creation-only measurement).
metric
primaryms per round trip (forward+inverse), median. Chosen as primary instead of GFLOP/s because the GFLOP/s convention is genuinely ambiguous across mixed 2D/3D/non-cubic grid shapes in this suite (the 1024x768x768 case in particular has no single agreed "N*log2(N)" convention once the dimensions differ) — see survey.md Divergence 4's precision-coverage note for the parallel issue in variant 1.
secondaryGFLOP/s = 5 * N_total * log2(N_total) / elapsed_s, N_total = product of grid dims, reported ONLY when every grid dimension is individually power-of-two-decomposable (i.e. NOT for the 1024x768x768 case); N/A otherwise, never silently approximated, effective GB/s = 2 * N_total * sizeof(dtype) / elapsed_s
correctnessround-trip relative error ||x - iFFT(FFT(x))|| / ||x|| in the L2 norm, <= 1e-5 for fp32 and <= 1e-12 for fp64 — generalizing cuHPX's own round-trip-error methodology (the only paper in this track's e2e-usage class with an explicitly stated, well-specified correctness metric for a full forward+inverse pipeline; survey.md's cuHPX subsection) to plain R2C/C2R grids. The fp32/fp64 tolerance SPLIT itself is this spec's own addition (cuHPX's own text does not state separate fp32 vs. fp64 numbers) — flagged as an open question.
fft-distributed-alltoallDistributed multi-node/multi-GPU FFT weak-scaling throughput, with local transform compute time and inter-rank communication (all-to-all, non-blocking, or device-direct) time reported as TWO SEPARATE numbers rather than one conflated total — representative of FLUPS (CPU+MPI) and CLAIRE (multi-GPU+MPI), the only two papers in this track that report genuinely distributed FFT numbers.
inputs
suite3D grid, per-rank problem size fixed at FLUPS's own README-stated performance sweet spot (~128^3 unknowns per core) for the weak- scaling sweep, so total problem size grows proportionally with rank count. Rank/GPU counts are the literal points each paper's own text reports, kept as two separate platform sub-cases rather than unified onto one axis (survey.md Divergence 6): CPU/MPI counts {1, 8, 64, 512, 4096, 49152} (FLUPS's own reported max); GPU counts {1, 8, 64, 256} (CLAIRE's own reported max — 256 V100 GPUs across 64 nodes).
selectionFLUPS's and CLAIRE's own literally-reported scale points (49,152 cores; 256 GPUs / 64 nodes), with intermediate points added as a geometric sweep so the weak-scaling curve has more than two data points; no cherry-picking of a single "best" scale point.
recommended_subsetCPU/MPI: 1, 8, 64, 512, 4096, 49152 ranks, ~128^3 unknowns/rank, fp64 (FLUPS-style), GPU: 1, 8, 64, 256 GPUs, 256^3 unknowns/GPU (CLAIRE's own per-GPU headline size), fp32 or fp64 (open question — CLAIRE's precision not confirmed, see survey.md)
dense_operandreal-valued unbounded/semi-unbounded/periodic Poisson right-hand side (FLUPS's own solved problem type) for the CPU/MPI sub-case; real-valued registration/Poisson-preconditioner field (CLAIRE's own solved problem type) for the GPU sub-case. Both are the actual physically-motivated workload each paper solves, not a synthetic FFT-only microbenchmark — this variant intentionally keeps the solver-level framing since neither paper's own reported distributed numbers isolate a bare distributed-FFT-only microbenchmark from their full solve (open question).
protocol
communication_patternTHREE distinct sub-cases, reported separately and never averaged together (survey.md Divergence 6): (1) CPU/MPI all-to-all (`MPI_Alltoall`/`MPI_Alltoallv`, FLUPS's own "default robust option"); (2) CPU/MPI non-blocking point-to-point (FLUPS's own compile-time alternative, persistent-request or `MPI_Datatype`-based); (3) GPU device-direct communication (GPU-aware MPI / NCCL-style transport, CLAIRE's own described but not further specified mechanism — flagged open question on the exact primitive).
plan_creationFFTW/cuFFT planner effort, Green's-function precomputation (CPU sub-case), and communication-pattern construction ALL performed once per (rank count, per-rank size, precision) configuration and reported separately (FLUPS's own convention, generalized track-wide); amortized over k=10 solves for this variant's steady-state number (k lower than variant 2's k=20 because distributed runs at 49,152 cores are substantially more expensive to repeat).
warmup1 full solve, discarded. Matches the reduced-repetition convention this track borrows from the stencil track's own `stencil-e2e-application` variant for physically/computationally expensive distributed runs, since neither FLUPS nor CLAIRE's own reachable text states a warmup convention for their large-scale numbers at all.
reps3
statisticmedian (report min and max). THIS IS A DELIBERATE FIX: neither FLUPS's nor CLAIRE's reachable text states any repetition or statistic convention for their own large-scale distributed numbers (survey.md's FLUPS and CLAIRE subsections both flag this as unrecoverable/unstated).
timer`MPI_Wtime()` with a barrier immediately before start/stop (CPU sub-case); CUDA-event-wrapped-in-host-timer with an explicit cross-rank barrier (GPU sub-case) — matching each platform's own natural mechanism.
timing_scopelocal FFT compute time and communication time (all-to-all / non-blocking / device-direct, per the sub-case) reported as TWO SEPARATE numbers, plus their sum as total solve time. THIS SPLIT IS AN EXPLICIT ADD by this spec: neither FLUPS's nor CLAIRE's reachable text confirms this decomposition is already performed by default in their own reported headline numbers, even though FLUPS's `PROF` build flag and `h3lpr`-based profiler suggest the underlying instrumentation to do so already exists in FLUPS's own codebase.
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per configuration, via `fft-plan-creation`; never amortized silently into this variant's per-solve number beyond the explicit k=10 amortization stated above.
metric
primarytime-to-solution (ms), median, plotted vs. rank/GPU count (weak-scaling curve)
secondaryparallel efficiency (%) relative to the single-rank/single-GPU baseline of the same per-rank problem size, communication time as % of total solve time (isolates the all-to-all bottleneck this track's distributed-FFT papers are explicitly concerned with)
correctnessrelative error vs. an analytic solution (FLUPS's own convention for its unbounded/semi-unbounded/periodic Poisson test cases) <= 1e-6, OR — when no analytic reference exists for the chosen workload (e.g. CLAIRE's registration solve) — the round-trip error convention from `fft-ndgrid-e2e` applied to the FFT sub-step in isolation. FLUPS's own correctness regime is substantially more thorough than this single number (a 16,000-case nightly regression suite across boundary conditions x Green's-function kernels x data layouts, per survey.md); this spec's single tolerance is the minimum bar for a benchmark run, not a replacement for that regression suite.
fft-plan-creationIsolated, one-shot plan-creation / kernel-codegen / Green's-function- and-communication-pattern-setup cost, measured ALONE and reported once per configuration — never silently amortized into any other variant's per-call number. This is this track's realization of the "preprocessing" axis every other kernel track in this benchmark suite separates out, generalized to cover BOTH a classical runtime plan object (cuFFT `cufftPlan*`, FFTW `fftw_plan_dft*`) AND a build-time kernel-codegen+compile step (TurboFFT/TurboFNO's own architecture, which has NO runtime plan call at all — survey.md Divergence 3).
inputs
suiteThe same (N, precision, direction, layout) configurations as `fft-1d-batched-kernel` (1D) and the same (grid size, precision, direction) configurations as `fft-ndgrid-e2e` (2D/3D) — this variant does not introduce a new input suite, it adds a preprocessing-only measurement pass over the other two variants' own suites.
recommended_subsetsame as fft-1d-batched-kernel.recommended_subset and fft-ndgrid-e2e.recommended_subset
protocol
what_is_measuredFor runtime-plan targets (cuFFT, FFTW, FLUPS's Green's-function + communication-pattern construction): wall-clock time of the plan-creation call(s) themselves, isolated from any transform execution. For build-time-codegen targets (TurboFFT/TurboFNO-style templated kernels): wall-clock time of the offline Python codegen step PLUS the nvcc/hipcc compilation time for the specific (N, precision, GPU architecture) configuration under test — reported as a one-time BUILD cost, explicitly outside any online/runtime latency budget (it is not re-paid on every process launch the way a cuFFT plan-creation call is).
planner_effort_levelsfor FFTW-backed targets specifically, report at EACH of `FFTW_ESTIMATE` / `FFTW_MEASURE` / `FFTW_PATIENT` (FLUPS's own exposed compile-time flag, per survey.md) rather than collapsing to one number — THIS IS AN EXPLICIT STRENGTHENING by this spec: FLUPS's README exposes the flag but its own reported performance numbers do not state which level was used, and planner effort trades directly against per-call transform speed (a higher planner effort produces a faster per-call kernel at a higher one-time plan-creation cost), so reporting only one level would hide that tradeoff entirely.
reps5
statisticmedian.
amortization_reportingreport the derived break-even iteration count = plan_creation_ms / steady_state_per_call_ms (the corresponding number from `fft-1d-batched-kernel` or `fft-ndgrid-e2e` at the same configuration) — i.e. "how many transforms before the one-shot setup cost pays for itself." This directly operationalizes FLUPS's own stated design philosophy (solve "many times... at low cost using precomputed Green's function and communication patterns") as a concrete, comparable number rather than a qualitative claim.
metric
primaryplan-creation / codegen+compile time (ms), median
secondarybreak-even iteration count (see amortization_reporting above)
correctnessnot applicable — this variant produces no numerical transform output; the correctness gate for the transform itself lives in `fft-1d-batched-kernel` / `fft-ndgrid-e2e` / `fft-distributed-alltoall`.
Fairness notes
  • TurboFFT reports the mean of ntest=10 reps and TurboFNO reports the mean of "tens of runs," with no spread reported by either; cuFalcon reports a single, unrepeated measurement. All three code-level-verified papers in this track skip the median-with-min/max convention this spec requires uniformly across all four variants (survey.md Divergence 1).
  • TurboFFT's own reference timing harness synchronizes the device after EVERY individual kernel launch inside its timed rep loop, not once at the end — this inflates measured time with extra sync-barrier stalls in a way that is internally consistent for TurboFFT's own TurboFFT-vs-cuFFT comparison but not comparable to a differently-synchronized harness without correction. This spec requires single-sync-at-the-end timing uniformly (survey.md Divergence 2).
  • "Plan creation" means something architecturally different in every surveyed codebase (runtime plan object vs. build-time codegen vs. precomputed Green's-function+comm-pattern) and NONE of TurboFFT, TurboFNO, or cuFalcon's own reported numbers include their respective one-shot setup cost anywhere at all — it is simply absent from their published throughput figures, not merely reported separately. The dedicated `fft-plan-creation` variant fixes this by requiring the cost be measured and reported for every configuration, not merely excluded and left unquantified (survey.md Divergence 3).
  • TurboFNO benchmarks fp32 only; FLUPS's precision is not stated in any reachable source. TurboFFT and FFCz are the only two papers in this track that explicitly benchmark both fp32 and fp64 on the identical workload — this spec follows their (stricter) convention rather than TurboFNO's fp32-only practice, requiring both precisions wherever a variant's inputs section lists them (survey.md Divergence 4).
  • No surveyed paper in this track states whether its own reported numbers use in-place or out-of-place layout. Since this materially changes achievable memory bandwidth, this spec requires both be reported as separate numbers rather than leaving the choice unstated the way every surveyed paper's own text does.
  • FlashFFTStencil validates its STENCIL output against a direct spatial-domain convolution reference, not its internal FFT's numerical output against a reference FFT — its own correctness check is one level removed from FFT accuracy. This spec's correctness gates in `fft-1d-batched-kernel` and `fft-ndgrid-e2e` are genuine FFT-vs-FFT (or FFT-round-trip) numerical checks, not proxied through a downstream application's output (survey.md Divergence 7).
Open questions
  • CLAIRE's precision, exact timing protocol (warmup/reps/statistic/timer), and the exact distributed-communication primitive used for its FFT ("device direct communication" — all-to-all, all-to-allv, or custom) could not be recovered from reachable text: both `arxiv.org/pdf/2008.12820` and its ar5iv mirror returned raw PDF binary in this environment (no `pdftoppm`/poppler-utils available to render pages), and the plain abstract page has no methodology section. The `fft-distributed-alltoall` variant's GPU sub-case precision and communication-primitive specificity are flagged accordingly.
  • FLUPS's precision (single vs. double) is inferred as FFTW-double (the library's likely implicit default) but not confirmed from any reachable text — flagged in the `fft-distributed-alltoall` variant's CPU sub-case.
  • TurboFNO's exact timer mechanism (CUDA events vs. host wall clock) was not independently confirmed from the reachable arXiv text beyond "averaged over tens of runs"; this spec assumes it follows its own TurboFFT submodule's CUDA-event convention but this is inference, not a directly sourced fact.
  • No surveyed paper's own reported numbers state a numeric plan-creation amortization count (the `k` in "amortized over k round trips/solves"). The k=20 (`fft-ndgrid-e2e`) and k=10 (`fft-distributed-alltoall`) values in this spec are this spec's own choices, motivated by but not directly sourced from FLUPS's qualitative "solve many times at low cost" framing.
  • The two 2D grid sizes in `fft-ndgrid-e2e` (4096^2, 8192^2) are this spec's own addition — no surveyed paper in this track's e2e-usage class states a headline 2D grid size; they are included so the 2D axis is not silently dropped from the suite.
  • FFCz's own timing protocol, baselines, and metric could not be determined — only its README was read this pass; its CPU/GPU source directories were not opened. Its dual spatial+frequency correctness-gate DESIGN is reflected in this spec's framing but its specific numeric tolerances are not incorporated (no numbers were found to incorporate).
  • cuFalcon's correctness-verification tolerance/comparison logic is referenced in its README but was not located in the read portion of its `main.cu` — its small-N/high-batch regime informs `fft-1d-batched-kernel`'s N={512,1024} recommended_subset entries, but no correctness number from cuFalcon itself was available to cite.
  • The `cuTensor`/`cuTensor-tubal` shared repo's `t-fft` primitive exposes a based/streamed/batched 3-way execution-mode axis that this spec does NOT explicitly incorporate as a fifth variant (to stay within the 1-4-variant guidance) — its "batched" mode (a distinct code path using a batched-plan API, not merely a larger batch-size parameter) is conceptually folded into `fft-1d-batched-kernel`'s batch axis, but this is an approximation, not a literal representation of that paper's own three-way distinction.
ntt1 papers2 variants

Number-Theoretic Transform (forward NTT / inverse INTT) over Z_q[x]/(x^N+1) as used inside RNS-CKKS fully homomorphic encryption — this track's single paper (Cheddar) never times bare NTT/INTT in isolation, only as a component slice inside fused elementary-CKKS-op kernels (HMult/HRot/HAdd/Rescale) or whole-FHE-workload runs (bts/HELR/ ResNet/Sort). This spec defines both the isolated microkernel the instructions require (degree, modulus bit-width, batch, correctness vs a reference NTT) and an embedded variant that matches what the paper actually reports, so the two are never conflated.

Forward: A_hat[i] = sum_{j=0}^{N-1} A[j] * omega^{ij} mod q, for each RNS limb q_i independently (q_i prime, q_i = 1 mod 2N so a primitive 2N-th root of unity omega exists mod q_i); Inverse (INTT) is the scaled conjugate transform, INTT(NTT(A)) = A mod q_i exactly. N is a power of two (this track's paper uses only N=2^16). A polynomial is represented in RNS as L limbs, each an independent length-N vector mod its own q_i; "batch" = number of limbs L processed together (Cheddar fuses all L limbs' NTTs into one kernel launch) and, orthogonally, number of independent ciphertexts/polynomials submitted together (not swept by this track's paper — see survey.md Divergence 3).

ntt-kernel-isolatedSteady-state throughput of a STANDALONE forward+inverse NTT pair (INTT(NTT(x)) round trip, or NTT-only if reporting one direction), decoupled from BConv/automorphism/elementwise ops it is normally fused with in this track's own artifact. This variant does not exist as a ready-to-run benchmark in Cheddar's repo as read; it requires either disabling kernel fusion in Cheddar or invoking a library's raw per-limb NTT device function directly. Included because the instructions require this axis and because Cheddar's own Fig. 3b shows the NTT component is a substantial, separately-optimized (EOT: 1.16x) fraction of a fused kernel's time — isolating it is a reasonable ask, not an invented one.
inputs
polynomial_degreeN in {2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^17}; N=2^16 is the only value evaluated by this track's paper (Cheddar's sole parameter set, `bootparam_40.json`: log_degree=16) and MUST be included; smaller/ larger N are this spec's own addition to give the requested degree axis, since the source paper sweeps only modulus and limb count at fixed N.
modulus_bit_widthb in {30, 31, 32} (Cheddar's SMR primes, q_i in [0, 2^31)) and b in {62, 64} (this track's baseline libraries' native double-word RNS primes — Liberate.FHE/HEonGPU/Phantom, all cited as Table 7 comparators). Both classes MUST be run at the same polynomial degree N so throughput-per-bit-of-modulus is comparable.
batch_limbsL (number of RNS limbs run in one launch) in {12, 24, 48}; L=48 (dnum=4, alpha=12) is Cheddar's default parameter set and L=24 is its reduced comparison point (Table 7); when comparing against a 64-bit baseline at nominal limb count L_64, halve L_64 to L_64/2 before comparing throughput at matched total modulus bit-width — this is Cheddar's OWN normalization ("we halved the number of limbs and alpha for fair comparison"), reproduced here explicitly rather than left implicit.
batch_ciphertexts1 (single polynomial/ciphertext per launch, matching every measurement in the source paper); a multi-ciphertext batch sweep is NOT covered by this track's paper and is flagged as an open question, not fabricated.
datauniform random coefficients in [0, q_i) per limb
protocol
warmup5 (Cheddar's own `unittest/BasicTest.cpp` warm_up constant)
repsrun the isolated NTT/INTT call >=30 times after warmup and report the distribution; Cheddar's own harness only times ONE post-warmup call per test-binary invocation (see survey.md), so this spec requires MORE repetitions per invocation than the source artifact does, to actually get the median/min/max the paper claims to report without relying on an unconfirmed external repeat-the-binary harness
statisticmedian (report min/max)
timerdevice-side (CUDA events); the source artifact instead uses std::chrono::high_resolution_clock bracketed by explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize() calls immediately before/after — equivalent in practice on a single stream, and reproduced here as an acceptable alternative timer
timing_scopeNTT/INTT kernel(s) only; twiddle-factor generation is IN scope if generated on-the-fly (Cheddar's EOT design explicitly avoids a separate precomputed-table load, i.e. there is no analogous 'plan creation' step to exclude); if an implementation instead precomputes/loads a twiddle table, that load is reported separately, once, analogous to preprocessing
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: any one-time root-of-unity / twiddle-table precomputation for the (N, q_i) configuration
metric
primaryGNTT-elements/s (N*L / time) and Melem/s per limb
secondaryus per (N,L) call
correctnessEXACT modular equality, not an epsilon tolerance: for every limb i, INTT_i(NTT_i(x)) == x (mod q_i) bit-for-bit, AND NTT_i(x) matches a reference NTT computed via an independent method (schoolbook O(N^2) DFT mod q_i, or a big-integer/double-double floating-point DFT rounded to the nearest residue) for at least one N per bit-width class. This deliberately does NOT reuse Cheddar's own message-level tolerance (max_error_ = 1e-3 in `Testbed.h`), which is a CKKS-approximation gate for the FULL encrypt/op/decrypt/decode pipeline and could mask a small but real NTT bug inside the FHE noise budget — see survey.md Divergence 2.
ntt-embedded-fhe-opSteady-state throughput of an elementary CKKS ciphertext op (HMult, HRot, HAdd, or Rescale) that internally issues one or more NTT/INTT calls as part of a fused INTT->BConv->NTT sequence — this is what Cheddar's own Table 7 actually measures, reproduced here as the track's real "kernel-only" number, with the NTT/BConv/other-component time breakdown reported alongside (not hidden) per Cheddar's own Fig. 3b practice.
inputs
ring_dimensionN = 2^16 (the only value in this track's paper)
modulus_systemCheddar 32-bit SMR (q_i in [0, 2^31)) at L in {24, 48} limbs, alpha in {6, 12}; baseline 64-bit RNS libraries (Liberate.FHE, HEonGPU, Phantom) at the same L (their native limb count halved per Cheddar's own normalization, see ntt-kernel-isolated.inputs.batch_limbs)
operationsHMult, HRot, HAdd, Rescale
hardwareRTX 4090 (Table 7's card); V100 / A100 40GB / A100 80GB / H100 / RTX 5090 optionally, for the scaling story in Table 4/5/6
protocol
warmup5
reps>=30 post-warmup calls per configuration (source artifact times exactly 1 post-warmup call per binary invocation and reports a cross-invocation 'median' whose repeat count N is not recoverable from the reachable files — see survey.md open_questions; this spec requires an explicit, disclosed rep count instead)
statisticmedian (report min/max) — matches the paper's own stated statistic (Table 7 reports median execution times), just with a disclosed rep count
timerdevice-side events (CUDA events) or host std::chrono + explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize() bracketing (source artifact's own method, `__ProfileStart`/`__ProfileEnd` macros in `unittest/Testbed.h`)
timing_scopethe op kernel sequence only (INTT->BConv->NTT + elementwise/automorphism as applicable); key/evaluation-key generation and initial encryption are one-shot setup, excluded from per-call time
component_breakdown_requiredreport the NTT-only, BConv-only, Automorphism-only, Elementwise-only, and Memcpy/etc-only fractions of the total (Cheddar's own Fig. 3b practice for HRot) — required disclosure, not optional, since this is the only place an NTT-only number can be recovered for a fused-kernel implementation
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: evaluation-key generation time (needed for HMult/HRot specifically)

secondaryus per op call (matches Table 7's own unit)
correctnessmessage-level: decrypt+decode the op's output and compare to an unencrypted reference computation of the same op on the same input values; max abs error < 1e-3 per complex slot (Cheddar's own `max_error_` constant in `Testbed.h`) — appropriate HERE because this variant measures the full approximate-FHE op, not a bare NTT.
Fairness notes
  • No paper in this 1-paper track times bare NTT/INTT; ntt-kernel-isolated is this spec's own construction (not extracted from any track paper's reported number) built from what IS confirmed — Cheddar's parameter set (N, limb counts, modulus bit-width) and its Fig. 3b NTT-specific optimization ablation — plus the instructions' required axes. Anyone submitting to this variant should expect to write a small standalone harness, not find one pre-built in the cheddar-fhe repo.
  • ntt-kernel-isolated's correctness gate (exact modular equality) is deliberately STRICTER than the source paper's own end-to-end message tolerance (1e-3), because NTT/INTT over a prime field is exact arithmetic and an epsilon gate at that layer would hide real bugs inside the FHE noise budget — this is a fairness fix, not a reproduction of the paper's practice (see survey.md Divergence 2).
  • The 32-bit-vs-64-bit modulus comparison in ntt-embedded-fhe-op keeps Cheddar's own normalization (halve the 64-bit baseline's limb count) rather than inventing a different one, since that is the actual basis for the paper's headline speedup claims and changing it would make this spec's numbers incomparable to the paper's.
Open questions
  • The external harness that produces Table 7's 'median execution time' from BasicTest.cpp's single-post-warmup-call-per-invocation design (repeat count, whether the whole test binary is relaunched per sample) is not in the files read this pass (only unittest/Testbed.h and BasicTest.cpp were read; a possible driver script outside unittest/ was not located) — ntt-embedded-fhe-op's rep count is this spec's own choice (>=30), not copied from Cheddar's own (unrecovered) practice.
  • Fig. 3b's exact per-category (NTT vs BConv vs Automorphism vs Elementwise vs Memcpy) numeric breakdown for the four optimization stages (Base/+LR/+OT/+EOT) was only partially recoverable as OCR'd axis/bar numbers from the extracted PDF text (values '200 203 184 175 / 136 72 71 70 / 212 212 204 196' without a confirmed row-to-category mapping) — the QUALITATIVE claims (EOT gives NTT a 1.16x speedup, LR gives BConv a 1.89x speedup) are used in this spec and survey.md, but no absolute NTT-only microsecond number from Fig. 3b is asserted as fact.
  • Whether Cheddar's on-the-fly twiddle generation (EOT) changes the correctness-relevant behavior of ntt-kernel-isolated's 'twiddle-table precomputation, if any' protocol field for implementations that DO use a precomputed table (e.g. the compared baseline libraries) was not confirmed from their READMEs (not read this pass, out of the ~4-minute budget for a singleton track) — flagged rather than assumed zero-cost.
  • No track paper addresses a genuinely mixed-radix or non-power-of-two N for NTT (unlike the FFT track, which does cover mixed-radix cases via FlashFFTStencil) — this spec's polynomial_degree axis is power-of-two only, matching the one paper actually surveyed, and this is a real coverage gap rather than an oversight.

tensor

tensor-network5 papers3 variants

Classical-HPC simulation of quantum circuits, covering two structurally distinct simulation paradigms found in this track's literature: gate-by-gate state-vector/density-matrix propagation (SliQSim, HyQuas, SV-Sim, DM-Sim), where there is no contraction path to search, and genuine tensor-network contraction of a random-quantum-circuit (RQC) tensor network via slicing + contraction-path search (SWQsim). A third variant isolates SliQSim's fundamentally different claim -- exact-arithmetic scalability frontier under a fixed time/memory budget, not steady-state throughput. This track's rqc-tensor-network-contraction variant is deliberately kept consistent (same protocol, same flop-counting convention, same permutation-always-included rule) with the sibling tensor-contraction track's quantum-circuit-contraction-kernel-fp32-mixed variant, which uses the same source paper (SWQsim) as evidence.

General form: given an n-qubit quantum circuit (a sequence of 1- and 2-qubit unitary gates, or, for the density-matrix case, a corresponding sequence of gate-conjugation superoperators), compute either (a) the full final state -- a 2^n-entry state vector or a 2^n x 2^n density matrix -- by applying each gate/superoperator to the current state in circuit order (state-vector/density-matrix paradigm), or (b) a specific amplitude or batch of amplitudes by contracting the tensor network obtained from the circuit's gate graph along a chosen contraction order, optionally with memory-reducing slicing of a subset of the network's edges (tensor-network paradigm). Index permutation required to align tensor operands for a contraction step is always included in the timed step for the tensor-network paradigm (never amortized out), per this track's one point of agreement with the sibling tensor-contraction track.

state-vector-density-matrix-gate-kernel-fp64steady-state per-gate/per-circuit latency and throughput of gate-by-gate state-vector or density-matrix propagation on a standard NISQ-era circuit benchmark suite, single-node and distributed, fp64 by default
inputs
suiteQASMBench (Li & Krishnamoorthy, the SV-Sim/DM-Sim authors' own prior benchmark-suite paper), supplemented with HyQuas's own named circuit-family generator set where QASMBench does not already cover a family (QAOA, hidden-shift, quantum-volume, basis-change)
selectionunion of QASMBench circuits named across SV-Sim's and DM-Sim's own evaluations (11-23 qubits) plus HyQuas's own 7 circuit families (basis_change, bv, hidden_shift, qaoa, qft, quantum_volume, supremacy) at 24-30 qubits; density-matrix runs use the SAME circuits at HALF the state-vector-equivalent qubit count (an n-qubit density-matrix run is computationally equivalent to a 2n-qubit state-vector run, per DM-Sim's own stated equivalence -- report both the density-matrix qubit count AND its state-vector-equivalent count explicitly, never one without the other)
recommended_subsetseca_n11, sat_n11, cc_n12, multiply_n13, bv_n14 (SV-Sim medium set), qf21_n15, qft_n15, multiplier_n15 (SV-Sim medium set, deepest), dnn_n16, bigadder_n18, square_root_n18, qft_n20 (SV-Sim large set), cat_state_n22, ghz_state_n23 (SV-Sim large set, widest), basis_change_28, qaoa_28, supremacy_28, quantum_volume_28 (HyQuas default 28-qubit set), adder_n9 / adder_n18 density-matrix (DM-Sim named routine, both qubit counts), VQE-UCCSD H2, 10 qubits / ~86 gates (SV-Sim chemistry case study)
dense_operandn/a -- the state vector / density matrix and the gate unitary matrices are the operands; fp64 (complex double) by default, matching all 4 papers in this sub-family's own stated precision
protocol
formatgiven circuit as OpenQASM/QASMBench source, gate-set parsing and circuit-to-native-IR translation timed once and reported separately (never re-timed per repetition)
warmup5
reps10
statisticmedian (report min/max) -- SV-Sim's own protocol is mean-of-10 with no stated warmup, DM-Sim's is mean-of-5 with no stated warmup; this spec keeps SV-Sim's higher rep count, adds an explicit warmup, and switches mean to median per the project's track-wide fairness rule
timerdevice-side events (CUDA/HIP events) for GPU; std::chrono/system clock for CPU, matching both SV-Sim's and DM-Sim's own stated choice
timing_scopefull-circuit gate-application sequence only (all gates fused into one kernel launch where the target system supports it, per SV-Sim/DM-Sim's own MG-BSP/functional-pointer designs -- report separately if a system instead launches one kernel per gate, since that is itself a measurable design difference, not something to normalize away); one- time circuit-parsing/IR-translation cost reported separately, once
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: OpenQASM parsing + native-IR translation/compilation time; for HyQuas specifically, its evaluator- preprocess method-selection database build (built once, reused across all circuits) reported separately as well
metric
primaryGFLOP/s using the paradigm's own known per-gate operation- count formula (state-vector: 8 double-precision flops per 1-qubit- gate application per amplitude pair, i.e. one 2x2 complex matrix-vector multiply; density-matrix: 12x8^n total DP ops for the full gate-conjugation multiply per DM-Sim's own Section III-A derivation) -- NOT from hardware performance counters
secondaryms/gate and total circuit latency (ms); speedup vs. Qiskit/ Cirq/Q# default simulators on the same machine, per SV-Sim's own baseline practice
correctnessexact bitwise match (up to floating-point associativity) vs. a reference sequential single-gate-at-a-time evaluation of the same circuit in fp64, OR max relative error < 1e-10 in any measured amplitude/probability if a different summation order is used -- none of the 4 source papers in this sub-family state an explicit tolerance; this spec adds one rather than leaving correctness unchecked before timing
rqc-tensor-network-contraction-fp32-mixedsustained throughput and time-to-solution for extreme-scale, structurally imbalanced tensor-network contraction of a random-quantum- circuit (RQC), single- and mixed-precision, contraction-order/slicing search reported separately from execution -- this spec's variant is kept consistent with the sibling tensor-contraction track's quantum-circuit-contraction-kernel-fp32-mixed variant (same source paper, same protocol) since both tracks' literature converges on the identical evidence (SWQsim)
inputs
suitenamed, fixed, published random-quantum-circuit tensor networks -- not a selectable suite in the usual sense, given the extreme cost of each data point
selection10x10x(1+40+1)-qubit circuit (2D lattice, PEPS-sliced contraction path, near-uniform rank~5-6/dim-32 pairwise contractions -- the source paper's own headline target) and the 53-qubit/20-cycle Google Sycamore circuit (CoTenGra-searched contraction path, imbalanced rank-30-vs-rank-4/dim-2 pairwise contractions); a 20x20x(1+16+1) circuit is available as a scaling-only supplementary case (not a headline accuracy/throughput target in the source paper)
recommended_subset10x10x(1+40+1) RQC, PEPS-sliced contraction path, Sycamore 53-qubit x 20-cycle, CoTenGra-searched contraction path, 20x20x(1+16+1) RQC, scaling-only supplementary case
dense_operandn/a -- tensor-network amplitude tensors are the operands; fp32 and mixed fp32/fp16 (adaptive per-tensor scaling) -- fp64 is explicitly never used for this variant (memory-bandwidth- bound design choice, per the source paper's own roofline analysis)
protocol
formatgiven tensor network + a pre-computed slicing/contraction path (path search itself reported separately, once, per the preprocessing rule below)
warmup0
reps25
statisticmedian (report min/max) -- the source paper itself reports mean of only 3 runs; this spec raises the repetition count for any reproduction at feasible (non-full-machine) scale, while noting that full-machine-scale reproductions (tens of millions of cores) may only be able to afford the source paper's own 3-run practice, which should be disclosed explicitly if used; warmup is 0 because a run at this scale is itself the measurement -- there is no steady state to warm into for a single extreme-scale contraction
timerwall-clock (MPI_Wtime or equivalent) at the full-application granularity, since the kernel is distributed across the whole machine
timing_scopefull contraction execution only (permutation ALWAYS fused into the timed step, per this track's and the sibling tensor-contraction track's point of universal agreement); contraction-path/slicing- scheme search reported separately, once. NOTE: the source paper's own accessible text does not give an explicit wall-clock number for how long its CoTenGra path search itself took to run (it reports only the resulting complexity and the execution time-to-solution) -- a reproduction under this spec MUST report the search wall-clock explicitly, closing a gap the source paper itself leaves open
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: contraction-path search (CoTenGra hyper-optimized search) and slicing-scheme selection, INCLUDING the search's own wall-clock time (see timing_scope note)
metric
primarysustained PFLOP/s or EFLOP/s, using the CONSERVATIVE counted- instruction flop method (not the hardware perf-counter method, which the source paper's own analysis shows reads 10-20% high due to temporary-operation generation -- state which method was used)
secondaryachieved memory-bandwidth utilization (% of peak); wall- clock time-to-solution for the full sampling task (source paper's own headline: 304s for a 2^21-correlated-amplitude Sycamore-equivalent bunch); percent of theoretical peak efficiency achieved (source paper's own headline: ~80%/75% fp32/mixed for the balanced 10x10x(1+40+1) circuit vs. only ~4%/1.7% for the imbalanced Sycamore circuit -- both numbers MUST be reported together, since reporting only the higher one would misrepresent the method's actual behavior on imbalanced tensor-network shapes)
correctnessNOT a fixed elementwise tolerance (meaningless for stochastically- sampled quantum amplitudes). Instead: (1) computed-amplitude probability distribution must match the theoretical Porter-Thomas distribution (Kolmogorov-Smirnov or equivalent goodness-of-fit); (2) mixed-precision relative error vs. an fp32 reference run must converge below 1% once >=300 aggregated contraction-path blocks are summed, with <2% of individual mixed-precision paths discarded for under/overflow (both criteria taken directly from the source paper's own validation method, Section 6.2 and Fig. 10/11)
exact-arithmetic-scalability-frontiermaximum qubit count reachable under EXACT (zero-precision-loss) arithmetic within a fixed wall-clock and memory budget, across structurally distinct circuit families -- a fundamentally different claim from steady-state throughput (variant 1) or sustained FLOP/s (variant 2): this variant measures HOW FAR a method scales before failing, not how fast it runs per gate
inputs
suite4 named circuit families from the source paper's own evaluation: (a) randomly generated circuits from a fixed 10-gate universal-gate-set library, (b) RevLib reversible-circuit benchmarks (classical-function circuits converted to quantum via H-gate insertion for superposition), (c) algorithmic circuits (entanglement/ Bell-state preparation, Bernstein-Vazirani), (d) Google's published random-quantum-supremacy circuits (from the public GRCS repository)
selectionrandom circuits: qubit sizes {40, 80, 120, 160, 200, 300, 400, 500}, gate:qubit ratio fixed at 3:1, 10 circuit instances per size; RevLib: all 14+ named benchmarks (130-923 qubits), both as-given and modified with H-gate insertion; algorithmic: entanglement and Bernstein-Vazirani circuits at {80, 90, 100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000} qubits; Google-supremacy: 16-90 qubits at reduced depth 5 (from the published depth-10 circuits), 10 instances per qubit count, from the `inst/rectangular/cz_v2` directory of the public GRCS repository
recommended_subsetrandom-circuit-40q through random-circuit-500q (8 sizes, 10 instances each), RevLib callif_32_439 (130 qubits, smallest) and apex2_289 (289 qubits) -- both original and H-gate-modified, entanglement-10000q, bv-10000q (largest algorithmic-circuit cases), google-supremacy-42q through google-supremacy-90q (10 instances each, depth-5-reduced)
dense_operandn/a -- circuit gates only; exact algebraic-integer arithmetic under a Clifford+T-superset universal gate set (X, Y, Z, H, S, T, Rx(pi/2), Ry(pi/2), CNOT, CZ, Toffoli, Fredkin), zero floating-point precision loss by construction
protocol
formatn/a -- circuit given as OpenQASM/RevLib-format source, no sparse-format or matrix-format conversion involved
warmup0
reps1
statisticsingle run per instance (repetition is not meaningful for this variant's claim: the metric is completion-within-budget, not steady-state speed -- report the count of successes/TO/MO/error/ segfault out of the N instances per qubit-size bucket, plus the mean wall-clock time averaged ONLY over the successful instances, explicitly disclosing that this average excludes failed instances rather than treating them as censored/infinite, per the source paper's own practice)
timerwall-clock (process-level, e.g. time or std::chrono at the whole-simulation granularity)
timing_scopefull simulation (state construction through final-amplitude/ probability computation) under a hard TIME-OUT of 7200 seconds and a hard MEMORY-OUT of 2GB per instance, both applied identically across every method compared (source paper's own limits, adopted verbatim since the claim being tested -- scalability frontier under a fixed budget -- is meaningless without a fixed, stated budget)
preprocessing_reportedn/a -- no separate preprocessing step exists for this workload; state construction is part of the timed simulation itself
metric
primarycount of successful instances (out of 10) per qubit-size bucket, per circuit family, under the fixed TO/MO budget -- the primary reportable number for this variant, NOT a speed metric
secondarymean wall-clock time (s) over successful instances only (explicitly disclosed as excluding TO/MO/error/segfault cases); peak memory usage (MB), reported for ALL instances including failed ones where measurable (source paper reports this for its Google-supremacy set)
correctnessNOT a numerical tolerance -- the claim under test IS exactness. A run counts as correct only if all reported state probabilities sum to exactly 1 (within the algebraic representation's own exact-arithmetic guarantee, i.e. no floating-point summation at all until the final user-facing probability readout) and no `error`/segfault condition is raised. Any run that requires an approximate/floating-point fallback does not qualify for this variant and should instead be reported under the state-vector-density-matrix-gate-kernel-fp64 variant, whose correctness clause DOES use a numerical tolerance.
Fairness notes
  • This track's 5 papers split cleanly into two simulation paradigms (gate-by-gate propagation: SliQSim/HyQuas/SV-Sim/DM-Sim; genuine tensor- network contraction: SWQsim only), so the 'contraction-order search time vs. execution time' axis this spec was asked to investigate is simply not applicable to 4 of the 5 papers -- forcing it onto them would misrepresent what those systems actually do. This spec keeps the paradigms in separate variants rather than inventing a fictitious contraction-path-search step for methods that have none.
  • SliQSim's claim (exact-arithmetic scalability frontier) is not commensurable with a throughput number at all -- reporting its GFLOP/s would be meaningless since the entire point of the method is that it trades speed for zero-precision-loss reach. This spec gives it its own variant with its own metric (completion count under a fixed budget) rather than shoehorning a throughput figure onto a paper that never reports one.
  • SWQsim's own accessible text reports contraction-path complexity and execution time-to-solution but never an explicit CoTenGra search wall-clock number -- this spec requires that number be measured and reported for any reproduction, closing a genuine gap in the one fully- accessible tensor-network-contraction paper in this track.
  • SWQsim explicitly demonstrates that hardware flop counters read 10-20% higher than an instruction-level count due to temporary operations, and deliberately chooses the lower, conservative number -- this spec adopts the same conservative-counting principle and requires every throughput number in the rqc-tensor-network-contraction variant to state its flop-counting method explicitly, matching the sibling tensor-contraction track's identical rule for the same source paper.
  • SWQsim's own efficiency figures show a stark ~80% vs ~4% split between its balanced (10x10x(1+40+1)) and imbalanced (Sycamore) circuits -- this spec requires both numbers be reported together for any claim about this method's efficiency, since a paper (or a reproduction) reporting only the 80% figure would misrepresent the method's actual behavior on realistic, imbalanced tensor-network shapes.
  • SliQSim's own reported average runtimes are computed only over successful (non-TO/MO/error/segfault) instances -- a survivorship-biased statistic. This spec keeps that practice (there is no principled alternative for a method that sometimes fails to complete at all) but REQUIRES it be disclosed explicitly alongside the success/failure counts, never presented as a plain average without that context.
  • None of the 5 papers state a warmup-iteration count for any of their timing protocols. This spec adds one for the two throughput-oriented variants and explicitly sets it to 0 (with justification) for the exact-arithmetic-scalability-frontier variant, where a 'warmup' has no coherent meaning for a method whose entire point is a one-shot exact-arithmetic scalability test.
Open questions
  • HyQuas's own ICS'21 paper PDF (dl.acm.org) could not be fetched by any means tried (direct fetch, proxy text-extraction service); no arXiv preprint exists. Its entry in this spec (folded into the state-vector-density-matrix-gate-kernel-fp64 variant) is built entirely from artifact-repo scripts and the paper's public abstract -- its exact timing protocol (warmup/reps/statistic), specific named baseline systems, and correctness-tolerance definition could not be independently verified and should be treated as the lowest-confidence entry in this spec.
  • Whether HyQuas's per-circuit-segment OShareMem/TransMM method-selection decision (informed by its evaluator-preprocess time-predictor database) is reported separately from execution time in the source paper could not be confirmed from the accessible repo material; this spec's preprocessing reporting for that specific decision is this spec's own addition, not verified against the paper's actual practice.
  • SWQsim's exact wall-clock cost for the CoTenGra contraction-path search step (as opposed to the resulting path's complexity, which IS reported) was not stated anywhere in the accessible fulltext including the appendix; this spec requires it be measured for any reproduction but cannot state what the source paper's own number was.
  • No paper in this track's accessible material states an explicit qubit- count-vs-memory-ceiling table beyond SWQsim's own detailed derivation; SV-Sim's and HyQuas's implicit O(2^n)/O(4^n) ceilings were inferred from each paper's own framing rather than a directly-stated numeric bound, and should be treated as this spec's own extrapolation rather than a verified paper claim.
mttkrp4 papers3 variants

Matricized-Tensor-Times-Khatri-Rao-Product, the dominant kernel in CP-ALS tensor decomposition (and, via S3TTMc/S3TTMcTC, the closely related symmetric Tensor-Times-Matrix-chain kernel used in Tucker/HOOI/HOQRI). Given an N-mode sparse tensor X and N-1 dense factor matrices, compute the mode-n unfolding of X contracted against the Khatri-Rao product of the other factor matrices.

M = X_(n) * (A^(N) ⊙ ... ⊙ A^(n+1) ⊙ A^(n-1) ⊙ ... ⊙ A^(1)) where X is an N-mode sparse tensor (given in some sparse format), A^(i) are dense I_i x R factor matrices, ⊙ is the Khatri-Rao (column-wise Kronecker) product, and M is the dense I_n x R result. In practice M is computed directly from the nonzeros of X (no explicit Khatri-Rao materialization).

Fairness notes
  • BLCO reports all N modes and shows up to 12x variation across modes for the same tensor under mode-specific formats; WACO reports mode-0 only. The general-kernel variant resolves this by mandating all-mode reporting; a mode-0-only number (as in WACO) is explicitly insufficient evidence for a track-wide MTTKRP performance claim.
  • WACO's fp32 precision is a real, stated divergence from the other three papers' fp64: the spec makes fp64 the default and calls for fp32 to be reported as a clearly-labeled secondary result, not silently compared against fp64 numbers from other systems.
  • SySTeC and SymProp both exclude output/data rearrangement (transposition, non-canonical-triangle replication) from timed kernel cost; BLCO reports format-construction cost separately with an explicit amortization count. The spec requires ALL preprocessing costs (format construction, autotuning search, output rearrangement) to be reported explicitly, never silently mixed into per-iteration numbers, following BLCO's practice rather than SySTeC/SymProp's silent exclusion.
  • WACO's headline numbers use the fastest of the top-10 SuperSchedules the tuner's own cost model selected, evaluated on real hardware -- a mild best-of-N practice. The e2e variant instead specifies reporting the #1-ranked schedule the tuner actually picked, to avoid rewarding systems for over-searching at evaluation time.
  • No paper in this track states an explicit correctness tolerance for MTTKRP; the spec adds one (1e-6 relative error in fp64, matching common practice for GFLOPS papers surveyed in the sibling tracks of this project) rather than leaving correctness unchecked before timing counts.
Open questions
  • None of the 4 papers give a full, precise formula for what counts as a 'flop' in MTTKRP (e.g., whether the final scale-and-accumulate per nonzero is counted as 2R or R flops). The spec's 2*R*nnz formula is the common convention in the sparse-tensor literature but was not verified against each paper's own internal flop counter.
  • BLCO's correctness-validation method for MTTKRP (tolerance, reference implementation) is not described in the fetched paper text; likely exists in the artifact but was not directly inspected.
  • SymProp targets S3TTMc/S3TTMcTC (Tucker-decomposition TTM-chain), which is closely related to but not literally MTTKRP; its recommended_subset entries above use the paper's own Tucker rank values, which may not be the ideal rank range if a reader wants a pure symmetric-MTTKRP (CP-ALS-style) comparison instead of Tucker/HOOI.
  • WACO's exact MTTKRP synthetic-tensor generation procedure (dimensions, density distribution) is only described by reference to a third paper (SpTFS); the generator was not independently reproduced for this survey.
tensor-contraction4 papers4 variants

General tensor-contraction / einsum evaluation, covering four structurally distinct contraction-shape families found in this track's literature: dense multi-operand contraction trees (TCCG + tensor-network applications), small batched irregular fused contractions (knowledge- graph embedding score functions), Kronecker-structured contraction chains, and extreme-scale imbalanced tensor-network contraction (quantum-circuit simulation). No single suite spans all four shape families, so this spec defines one variant per family rather than forcing an artificial common denominator.

General form: given tensors {T_1, ..., T_k} and an einsum expression string over multi-indices, compute the output tensor via a sequence of binary contractions (a contraction tree/path), each binary step being C[free_C] = sum_{contracted} A[idx_A] * B[idx_B], with any necessary index permutation performed as part of the same timed step (never amortized out -- see notes_on_fairness).

preprocessing_reportedseparately: autotuning/kernel-parameter search time (FastKron's own autotuner takes <2 minutes per problem shape, searching up to 10,000 tile-size configurations in parallel) -- reported once, never amortized into per-call GFLOP/s
metric
primaryachieved TFLOP/s using the algorithm-level complexity O(M*P*sum_{i=1..N} Q^{N-i}*P^i) as the flop count
secondaryspeedup vs. shuffle-algorithm and FTMMT-algorithm baselines; percent of GPU peak FLOPS achieved
correctnessmax relative error vs. explicit-Kronecker-matrix-then- matmul reference in fp64 < 1e-5 (fp32 kernel) / < 1e-10 (fp64 kernel)
quantum-circuit-contraction-kernel-fp32-mixedsustained throughput and time-to-solution for extreme-scale, structurally imbalanced tensor-network contraction (random-quantum- circuit simulation), single- and mixed-precision, permutation fully fused into the timed kernel by design
inputs
suitenamed random-quantum-circuit tensor networks
selection10x10x(1+40+1)-qubit circuit (PEPS-sliced, near-uniform rank~5-6/ dim-32 pairwise contractions) and the 53-qubit/20-cycle Google Sycamore circuit (CoTenGra-searched path, imbalanced rank-30-vs- rank-4/dim-2 pairwise contractions) -- both circuits are fixed, published, and independently reproducible targets, not a selectable "suite" in the usual sense given the extreme cost of each data point
recommended_subset10x10x(1+40+1) RQC, PEPS-sliced contraction path, Sycamore 53-qubit x 20-cycle, CoTenGra-searched contraction path
dense_operandn/a -- tensor-network amplitude tensors are the operands; fp32 and mixed fp32/fp16 (adaptive per-tensor scaling) -- fp64 is explicitly never used for this shape family (memory- bandwidth-bound design choice, unlike every other variant in this track)
protocol
formatgiven tensor network + a pre-computed slicing/contraction path (path search itself reported separately, once, per the preprocessing rule below)
warmup10
reps25
statisticmedian (report min/max) -- SWQsim itself reports mean of only 3 runs; this spec raises the repetition count for any reproduction at feasible (non-full-machine) scale, while noting that full-machine-scale reproductions (tens of millions of cores) may only be able to afford SWQsim's own 3-run practice, which should be disclosed explicitly if used
timerwall-clock (MPI_Wtime or equivalent) at the full-application granularity, since the kernel is distributed across the whole machine
timing_scopefull contraction (permutation ALWAYS fused in, per this track's one point of universal agreement); one-time contraction-path/ slicing-scheme search reported separately
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once: contraction-path search (CoTenGra hyper-optimized search) and slicing-scheme selection
metric
primarysustained PFLOP/s or EFLOP/s, using the CONSERVATIVE counted-instruction flop method (not the hardware perf-counter method, which SWQsim's own paper shows reads 10-20% high due to temporary-operation generation -- state which method was used)
secondaryachieved memory-bandwidth utilization (% of peak); wall-clock time-to-solution for the full sampling task
correctnessNOT a fixed elementwise tolerance (meaningless for stochastically- sampled quantum amplitudes). Instead: (1) computed-amplitude probability distribution must match the theoretical Porter-Thomas distribution (Kolmogorov-Smirnov or equivalent goodness-of-fit); (2) mixed-precision relative error vs. an fp32 reference run must converge below 1% once >=300 aggregated contraction-path blocks are summed, with <2% of individual mixed-precision paths discarded for under/overflow
Fairness notes
  • Permutation/transpose is the one point of universal agreement across all 4 papers in this track: never strip it out of a timed kernel or amortize it separately, even for baselines whose transpose cost is large (FastKron's own Table 1 shows the shuffle-algorithm baseline spending up to 80% of its time on transpose -- that 80% stays in the reported number for that baseline).
  • Einsum Trees' own benchmark driver uses a single warmup call and a single timed call with no repetition statistic at all; this spec fixes warmup=10/reps=50 (or reps=100 for the Kron-Matmul variant, matching FastKron's own already-adequate protocol) and mandates median+min/max reporting instead.
  • SWQsim explicitly demonstrates that hardware flop counters read 10-20% higher than an instruction-level count due to temporary operations, and deliberately chooses the lower, conservative number. This spec adopts that same conservative-counting principle for the quantum-circuit variant and asks every variant to state its flop- counting method explicitly, since Einsum Trees and cuKE do not.
  • fp64 is NOT assumed available or default in this track the way it is in the MTTKRP track: SWQsim never uses it, cuKE and Einsum Trees' reported figures are fp32-only. Only the Kron-Matmul variant reports both fp32 and fp64 as co-primary, following FastKron's own practice; the other three variants are fp32 by default with fp64 an optional secondary result only where the underlying system implements it.
Open questions
  • No paper in this track gives a single unified flop-counting formula usable across score functions/contraction shapes; the kge-batched variant's metric section flags this explicitly rather than papering over it with a single generic formula that would misrepresent TransE (vector-only) vs. TransR/RESCAL (matrix-operand) cost.
  • Einsum Trees' internal `num_ops()` counter definition was not directly inspected (only its call site in bench_expression.cpp was visible); whether it matches the 2*flops-per-multiply-add convention used elsewhere in this spec was not independently verified.
  • None of the 4 papers' accessible text states an explicit numeric correctness tolerance (SWQsim's statistical/convergence checks are the partial exception); the tolerances given above for the other 3 variants are this spec's own additions, not verified against any paper's actual validation code.
  • The ACM-paywalled Einsum Trees paper itself (only the poster and GitHub repo were accessible) may contain evaluation details -- exact TCCG case count, exact permutation-cost breakdown numbers -- not captured in this survey; a reader with ACM Digital Library access should cross-check against the full paper.
sparse-tensor-contraction3 papers3 variants

Contraction of sparse tensors/matrices under an einsum-style index-contraction specification, covering three structurally distinct sub-problems found in this track's literature: sparse(A)-times-dense(B) GPU kernels expressed as indirect einsums over fixed-length sparse formats (Insum), true sparse-tensor x sparse- tensor contraction (SpGETT) over FROSTT N-mode tensors (parTC), and fused multi-kernel composite sparse-tensor-algebra expression chains built by loop-nest restructuring (SparseLNR). No single input suite or reference kernel spans all three, so this spec defines one variant per sub-problem rather than forcing an artificial common denominator, following the same resolution used by the sibling tensor-contraction track for its four shape families.

General form: given sparse tensor(s)/matrice(s) {A, B, ...} and an einsum-style index-contraction expression, compute the output tensor C by contracting the specified shared indices, where at least one operand is sparse (stored in a compressed format that skips explicit zeros) and the output may itself be dense (sparse-times-dense case) or sparse (sparse-times-sparse case, with a data-dependent, not-known-a-priori output nonzero count). Format conversion and/or any index-permutation required to align operand layouts is scoped explicitly per variant below (never silently amortized into per-call time unless stated).

sparse-dense-indirect-einsum-gpu-kernel-fp32-fp16steady-state kernel throughput of GPU sparse(-structured or -unstructured) times dense einsum kernels expressed via fixed-length sparse formats (GroupCOO/BlockGroupCOO) and executed as fully-fused gather-matmul-scatter Triton/Tensor-Core kernels, format conversion and compile/autotune time reported separately

dense_operanddense operand shapes as given per application (N=128 for unstructured SpMM; batch=10000 for equivariant tensor product); fp32 primary, fp16 (Tensor-Core path) reported as a labeled secondary result, since Tensor Cores are the headline optimization target of this variant's source paper

metric
primaryGFLOP/s using the flop count of the UNFUSED composite expression (sum of each constituent kernel's own standard flop formula, e.g. 2*nnz*N for the SpMM sub-step, 2*R*nnz for the MTTKRP sub-step), since fusion changes memory traffic but not the number of useful arithmetic operations performed
secondaryspeedup vs. TACO-Original (single perfectly-nested loop) and TACO-Separate (temporaries between sub-kernels); thread-count scaling (1 to 64 cores)
