correctnessMANDATORY pre-timing gate, exact-geometry-required (the paper's own stated technical challenge is recovering full precision despite RT hardware's limited native precision support -- 'close enough' is explicitly NOT the bar here): every rt-mode and lbvh-mode result set (intersection points for LSI, polygon assignment for PIP) must match the grid-mode result set (RayJoin's own designated reference, matching its own -check convention) EXACTLY for PIP polygon assignment (discrete, must be bit-identical) and within double-precision-equivalent tolerance (<1e-9 relative, in the original coordinate units) for LSI intersection-point coordinates. External baseline (cuSpatial) results are compared the same way, pinned to cuSpatial >=24.06 specifically because the artifact's own README documents a memory/correctness-relevant bug in 23.12 that was fixed upstream in 24.06 (rapidsai/cuspatial#1381) -- comparing against the unfixed version would not be a fair correctness baseline.
Fairness notes
  • RayJoin's own README already demonstrates good baseline hygiene: it identifies and documents a specific cuSpatial version (23.12) with a memory-allocation bug that would otherwise force an unfair workaround (batched processing, inflating cuSpatial's apparent cost via extra I/O/index-construction overhead), and re-benchmarks against the fixed version (24.06). This spec pins the baseline version explicitly for the same reason, rather than silently accepting whatever cuSpatial version happens to be installed.
  • This track's brief explicitly calls out 'index build vs. query' as a required axis; RayJoin's own README does not clearly state whether its reported query_exec times include BVH build, so this spec makes the separation mandatory rather than assuming it is already done, since RT-hardware BVH build is one of the paper's own two stated bottlenecks and folding it silently into query time would hide exactly the tradeoff under study.
  • grid mode is used as BOTH a performance baseline AND the correctness reference (via RayJoin's own -check convention) -- this spec preserves that dual role since it is the artifact's own design, but notes explicitly that this means grid's own correctness is assumed, not independently re-verified against a fully external ground truth (e.g. a CPU double-precision computational-geometry library) in this spec; see open_questions.
Open questions
  • Whether query_exec's reported query time includes or excludes RT-mode BVH construction was not stated in the fetched README at the CLI-flag level; this spec's mandatory build/query separation is therefore a REQUIREMENT this spec imposes, not a confirmed description of the artifact's current default behavior -- a re-measurement pass should confirm which the raw timer currently captures.
  • grid mode is RayJoin's own correctness reference (via -check); whether grid mode itself has been validated against a fully independent ground truth (e.g. GEOS/CGAL double-precision computational geometry) was not confirmed from the fetched sources -- if grid mode has its own subtle bugs, using it as the sole correctness reference would not catch them.
  • The exact xsect_factor values used in the paper's own reported evaluation (as opposed to the README's example invocation, 0.1-0.5) were not confirmed from the fetched text.

N-body / MD

md-force1 papers4 variants

Per-timestep short-range (and, for MLIP/ReaxFF, learned/reactive) pairwise force and potential-energy evaluation in classical molecular dynamics, including the neighbor/cell-list construction that feeds it.

Given atom positions X[N,3], box/PBC, a cutoff r_c and a potential (LJ / EAM / Tersoff+ILP / ReaxFF+QEq / MLIP neural potential), compute per-atom forces F[N,3] and total potential energy E for one MD step; periodically (every k_nb steps) rebuild the neighbor/cell list used to restrict the O(N) pairwise search to r < r_c + skin.

md-force-classical-kernel-f64steady-state force-kernel throughput for classical empirical potentials on the de facto standard LAMMPS input suite; neighbor-list build reported separately (see md-force-neighbor-list-build), not amortized into this number.
inputs
suiteLAMMPS bench/ standard inputs (github.com/lammps/lammps/tree/stable/bench)
selectionall three of LAMMPS's canonical single-potential benchmarks, chosen because NONE of the surveyed papers used a shared suite themselves (see Divergences) — this is the closest thing to a de facto standard in the wider MD-HPC community and is what the spec imposes to make cross-implementation comparison possible at all.
recommended_subsetin.lj — LJ melt, reduced units, rho*=0.8442, r_c=2.5 sigma, 32,000 atoms (4 replicas -> 2,048,000 for the 'large' point), in.eam — EAM Cu (Cu_u3.eam potential), 32,000 atoms (and 4x/32x replicated sizes for weak scaling), in.rhodo — rhodopsin protein in solvated lipid bilayer, 32,000 atoms, CHARMM force field + PPPM long-range electrostatics (the one input in this variant needing a k-space solve, mirroring the Ewald/PME papers in the survey)
size_classes
small32,000 atoms (single-node/single-GPU point, comparable to LMFF's case_5016 and TensorMD's Intel-node points)
medium256,000 atoms (8x replicate)
large2,048,000 atoms (64x replicate; weak-scaling anchor, atoms/process held fixed above this point)
protocol
buildpotential parameters + initial neighbor list built once, not timed
warmup10
reps100
statisticmedian; report min and max alongside
timerwall-clock around the force+energy call only (std::chrono / LAMMPS internal MPI timer 'Pair' phase)
timing_scopeforce + energy evaluation only; neighbor-list rebuild, I/O, and thermo output excluded and reported under md-force-neighbor-list-build instead. This deliberately breaks with Jia et al. 2020's "loop time incl. I/O" convention (their own choice was flagged as unusually generous in the survey) and follows LMFF's GPTL-style phase separation instead.
preprocessing_reportedpotential-table setup / initial cell-list build reported once, separately
metric
primaryatom-steps/s = N_atoms * (1 / median_step_time)
secondarytimesteps/s (for direct comparison to LMFF and the Cerebras WSE paper), ms/step
correctness(a) forces within 1e-5 relative L2 error vs. a reference double-precision LAMMPS build on the same input (structural correctness of the ported kernel); (b) NVE energy-drift < 1e-4 (relative, per-atom) over a 10,000-step run at the benchmark's timestep — the classic MD correctness check that, per the survey's open_questions, none of the 6 surveyed papers actually reports quantitatively, so this tolerance is taken from standard LAMMPS/MD practice rather than from the pool.
md-force-mlip-kernel-f64steady-state force-kernel throughput for machine-learned interatomic potentials (DeePMD-kit / TensorMD-style), which are 100-1000x more compute-intensive per atom-step than the classical potentials above and so must not be pooled with them (see Divergences).
inputs
suitebulk single-element crystals at 3 sizes, mirroring the DeePMD/TensorMD papers' own systems
selectioncopper (fcc, EAM-lattice-equivalent geometry) and tungsten (bcc) — the two elements actually reported in the surveyed MLIP papers — each at 3 sizes; water (SPC/E-equivalent box) as an additional case because both DeePMD papers report it and it is the one input with a 6 A rather than 8 A cutoff, testing the harness's cutoff-generality.
recommended_subsetCu bulk crystal, 12,288 / 128,000 / 540,000 atoms (0.54M point matches LiLGLLLYWTJ24's Fugaku Cu system), W bulk crystal, 6,912 / 55,296 / 552,960 atoms (matches TensorMD's Intel-node points + a 10x extrapolation), H2O box, 12,288 / 124,416 / 558,000 atoms (0.56M point matches LiLGLLLYWTJ24's water system; 12,288-atom point matches Jia et al. 2020's single-GPU validation case)
dense_operandtrained DeePMD-kit se_e2_a descriptor, embedding net [25,50,100] + fitting net [240,240,240], fp64 weights for the baseline variant
protocol
buildnetwork weight load + descriptor-table setup once, not timed
warmup10
reps50
statisticmedian; report min and max
timerwall-clock around the force+energy call (device-side events if GPU)
timing_scopeforce + energy evaluation only, same neighbor-list exclusion as the classical variant
preprocessing_reportednetwork load reported once, separately
metric
primaryatom-steps/s
secondarys/step/atom (TensorMD's own convention, for direct comparability), PFLOPS (Jia et al.'s convention; report the FLOP-counting formula used, since MLIP FLOP counts are not self-evident)
correctnessforce RMSE < 1e-4 eV/A and energy error < 1e-5 eV/atom vs. an un-optimized direct network evaluation on the same weights (matches TensorMD's "static accuracy" check); additionally, for any reduced-precision run, report energy/force error vs. the fp64 run of THIS variant using the DeePMD papers' own error metrics (eV/atom, eV/A) so precision-vs-speed tradeoffs are visible rather than folded into a single headline number (the failure mode flagged for the Cerebras WSE and Fugaku-DeePMD papers in Divergences).
md-force-neighbor-list-buildisolated neighbor/cell-list construction throughput, reported separately because it is the axis every "rebuild every k steps" design choice in the survey trades against, and because it was 2 of the surveyed papers' actual optimization target (LMFF's SWLMFF cell list, the ReaxFF Sunway neighbor-list redesign) yet none of them isolate its cost from the force kernel in a reusable way.
inputs
suitesame atom configurations as md-force-classical-kernel-f64's 3 size classes (32K/256K/2.048M atoms), LJ-melt density
selectionreuse in.lj geometry so this variant's atom-steps/s is directly divisible against the classical-kernel variant's, giving the neighbor-fraction-of-total-time split the survey found only LMFF reports (via GPTL)
protocol
warmup10
reps100
statisticmedian; report min and max
timerwall-clock around the list-build call only
timing_scopecell-bin + Verlet-list construction only, given a skin distance; excludes force evaluation entirely
rebuild_frequency_reportedreport throughput at skin={1.0, 2.0} Angstrom (the two values found in the survey: TensorMD's 1 A / every-5-steps and the DeePMD papers' 2 A / every-50-steps) so the amortized-into-force-kernel cost can be reconstructed for either convention: amortized_ns_per_atomstep = build_time_per_atom / rebuild_interval.
metric
primaryatom-builds/s = N_atoms / median_build_time
secondaryfraction of total per-step time (build_time / (build_time/k_nb + force_time)) at k_nb in {5, 50}, the two rebuild frequencies found in the survey
correctnesslist completeness: every true neighbor pair within r_c must appear in the built list (zero false negatives), verified against an O(N^2) reference on a <=10,000-atom subset
md-force-e2e-weak-scalingend-to-end, multi-node weak-scaling throughput including amortized neighbor-list rebuild — the "Gordon-Bell-class" claim every SC paper in the survey actually reports, made comparable by fixing the metric to atom-steps/s (not ns/day, whose per-paper timestep-size confound is documented in Divergences) and requiring the timestep and rebuild interval to be stated alongside it.
inputs
suitethe classical- or MLIP-kernel variant's medium/large size classes, replicated to hold atoms/process fixed as node count scales (LMFF's own '-var SX n' convention)
selectionatoms/process fixed at 2,000-20,000 (spans LMFF's 2.7M-atoms/process weak-scaling point down through the smaller per-process sizes used by the DeePMD Fugaku paper, ~0.93-0.97 atoms/core, i.e. close to 1 atom/core -- report both ends since the pool disagrees by 3+ orders of magnitude on this ratio); node counts {1, 8, 64, full-allocation}.
protocol
warmupone full k_nb-step neighbor-rebuild cycle (i.e. >= k_nb steps), not counted
reps200 measured steps, following LMFF's convention, split into 4x50-step windows each reported separately (not just averaged) so run-to-run variance at scale is visible
statisticmedian of the 4 windows per experiment, averaged over >=5 repeated experiments (LMFF's own recommended practice)
timerLAMMPS-style phase timer or equivalent, reporting pair/neighbor/comm/output split
timing_scopefull step loop INCLUDING amortized neighbor-list rebuild and inter-process communication; I/O and thermo-output timing reported separately from compute (unlike Jia et al. 2020, which folded I/O into the headline number).
preprocessing_reportedone-time domain decomposition + initial neighbor-list build reported separately, once
metric
primaryatom-steps/s
secondaryns/day (report alongside, but ONLY together with the timestep size used, per the Divergences confound), parallel efficiency vs. the single-node point of the same size class
correctnesssame NVE energy-drift / force-RMSE gate as the corresponding kernel-only variant, evaluated at the largest feasible node count actually run
Fairness notes
  • No surveyed paper shares a common input suite; the classical-potential and neighbor-list-build variants therefore impose the LAMMPS bench/ suite (in.lj/in.eam/in.rhodo) as the closest available de facto standard, rather than adopting any one paper's bespoke system.
  • ns/day is disallowed as the SOLE metric because it silently absorbs the per-system physical timestep (0.5fs water vs 1.0fs Cu vs 2fs EAM-Ta in the surveyed papers) -- atom-steps/s is required in every variant, ns/day only permitted alongside a stated timestep.
  • Classical empirical potentials (LJ/EAM/Tersoff/ReaxFF) and MLIP neural potentials (DeePMD/TensorMD) are split into separate variants: pooling them would let a Tersoff kernel's atom-steps/s be misread against a DeePMD kernel's, when the compute intensity differs by 100-1000x (LMFF/Cerebras-WSE vs. Jia-et-al./TensorMD in the survey).
  • Neighbor-list build time is a first-class, separately reported variant instead of being silently amortized: LMFF is the only surveyed paper that reports this split at all (via GPTL); Jia et al. explicitly fold it (and I/O) into the headline loop time, which this spec's md-force-classical/mlip-kernel variants deliberately do NOT do.
  • Cross-precision, cross-hardware 'speedup' claims (Cerebras WSE fp32-vs-Frontier fp64; Fugaku DeePMD's 31.7x which also changes atoms/core by >8x) are explicitly out of scope for what this spec calls a valid benchmark result -- a reported number must hold precision and problem size fixed while varying only the implementation, per the correctness/error-reporting requirements in each kernel-only variant.
  • Repetition/statistic practice in the pool ranges from LMFF's rigorous >=5-experiment average to TensorMD/Cerebras-WSE's single-run point numbers; this spec fixes warmup+reps+median/min/max reporting for every variant rather than following any one paper's (looser) practice.
Open questions
  • Exact cutoff radii for LMFF's Tersoff/ILP potentials and the Cerebras WSE paper's Cu/W/Ta EAM potentials were not recoverable from the accessible sources; LAMMPS bench/ defaults are used as a fallback where a paper's own value is unstated.
  • No paper in the surveyed pool reports a quantitative NVE energy-drift tolerance; the value used in this spec (1e-4 relative, 10,000 steps) is taken from general LAMMPS/MD practice, not from the track's own literature.
  • OCTANE (ICS'26 Best Paper, conf/ics/ToutouniCTH26, 'Breaking the Neighbor-List Bottleneck in GPU Molecular Dynamics') is exactly on-topic for md-force-neighbor-list-build but its methodology could not be recovered (ACM DL/IEEE 403, no arXiv preprint found as of this survey).
  • journals/tpds/GaoDZZSZSZGXFLY20 (ReaxFF billion-atom Sunway): only the scale/metric claim (1.36B atoms, 4.26M cores, 0.015 ns/day) was recoverable; warmup/reps/timer/precision/correctness protocol unknown (paywalled, no preprint).
  • journals/tpds/ChenASGDSYCGYL26 (LJ+Tersoff on ARM Kunpeng) is the pool's one paper using textbook LJ/Tersoff potentials rather than a bespoke production system -- exactly the standard-benchmark data point this spec needed most -- but its IEEE Xplore fulltext is paywalled and only abstract-level detail was recovered, so it was not included as a fully-surveyed source.
  • ReaxFF's QEq charge-equilibration solve (an iterative CG coupled into every force-kernel call) is architecturally different enough from the other classical potentials that it may deserve its own variant rather than being folded into md-force-classical-kernel-f64; deferred until a ReaxFF paper's full methodology is recovered.
nbody1 papers1 variants

Fixed-radius pairwise-proximity/collision detection for dense spherical-particle systems on GPU ray-tracing hardware (BVH build + RT-core broad/narrow-phase query + integration), measured as interactions/s jointly with an exactness gate, since this track's sole available paper has no tunable accuracy/approximation knob and no energy-conservation notion the way a classical Barnes-Hut/FMM tree-code would (see survey.md Divergences #1-2 for why those two axes from the parent task template do not apply here and are recorded as N/A rather than fabricated).

collisions[t] = DCD(particles[N] (position, velocity, radius_i), domain (unit cube), substep dt); per substep: rebuild RT bounding-volume hierarchy (BVH) over current particle positions, launch an RT ray-generation kernel that queries the BVH for candidate sphere-sphere pairs (broad phase) and resolves true intersections (narrow phase) in one hardware pass, then integrate position/velocity from resolved collision responses. Exact/exhaustive within the query radius -- not an approximation controlled by a tunable order/resolution parameter.

dcd-kernel-particle-scalingsteady-state per-substep throughput of RT-hardware-accelerated fixed-radius collision detection across a particle-count sweep, with BVH-build / detect / integrate reported as three separate phases (matching the paper's own decomposition) rather than blended into one number
inputs
suiteuniformly-packed random spherical-particle systems in a unit cube domain (BOX_WIDTH=1.0), same generator/format as the paper's own datasets/*.txt
selectionn in {10,000; 100,000; 1,000,000}; 100,000 is the paper's own default and the only instance directly confirmed from the repo (datasets/100k_particles.txt); 10,000 and 1,000,000 are this spec's own additions for a scalability curve the paper itself does not report, disclosed as such rather than presented as paper-verified
recommended_subset10k_particles (uniform radius, generated at the same packing density as the paper's 100k set), 100k_particles.txt (paper's shipped default dataset, confirmed from repo), 1M_particles (uniform radius, generated, same packing density)
dense_operandN/A (no dense operand; particle position/velocity/radius arrays only)
accuracy_parameterNOT APPLICABLE. The parent task template requires an accuracy parameter as an explicit spec axis since it normally trades against speed (multipole order, mesh resolution, etc.). Mochi's RT-BVH traversal is exact/exhaustive -- every true sphere-sphere intersection within the query radius is found on every substep; there is no order/resolution knob to sweep. This is recorded here as an explicit N/A per survey.md Divergences #1, not silently dropped or faked with an invented parameter. The one paper in this corpus that DOES have a genuine multipole-order accuracy parameter (RT-BarnesHut, PPoPP 2025) has no public artifact and could not anchor this spec (survey.md, Related-but-excluded).
non_uniform_radiisupported by the paper (heterogeneous particle sizes); the recommended_subset above is uniform-radius for a controlled particle-count baseline, non-uniform-radius instances are an optional reportable extension
protocol
substep_definitionone substep = BVH rebuild + one RT broad/narrow-phase collision query-and-resolve pass + one position/velocity integration step (paper's own 3-phase decomposition, confirmed from hostCode.cu)
frames200
iterations_per_frame400
total_substeps80,000 (200 x 400), matching the paper's own default run configuration
warmupfirst 1 frame (400 substeps) discarded -- a benchmark-spec addition; the paper's own public harness runs single-trial with no discarded warmup and no repetition, flagged in notes_on_fairness
repsremaining 199 frames (79,600 substeps) measured as the reportable window
statisticmedian per-substep phase time across the measured window, report min/max -- deviates from the paper's own single-run sum-and-print-once convention, see notes_on_fairness
timerstd::chrono::steady_clock (paper's own choice), one accumulator per phase (build/detect/update), summed and also reported per-phase
timing_scope3 phases only: BVH build, RT collision query+narrow-phase resolve, integration; optional PNG rendering path explicitly excluded (the paper's own harness already separates render I/O from the 3 timed phases, confirmed from hostCode.cu -- this spec inherits that separation rather than introducing it)
preprocessing_reportedno separate one-shot preprocessing phase exists for this algorithm -- the BVH is rebuilt every substep by construction (unlike a static-scene RT application), so 'build' is already a per-substep cost, not an amortizable one-time cost; flagged as a structural property of the algorithm, not a spec choice
metric
primaryinteractions/s = (candidate pairs tested during broad-phase BVH traversal, summed over all substeps in the measured window) / detect_phase_time_seconds -- a DERIVED metric, since the paper's own artifact reports only per-phase ms and a raw collision count, not a normalized throughput figure (survey.md Divergences #3)
secondarysubstep_time_ms (build+detect+update, median/min/max), each phase's ms standalone, resolved-collisions/s (via the COUNT_COLLISIONS build flag)
correctnessSUBSTITUTE for the parent task's energy-conservation gate: DCD has no potential-energy term to conserve, and no conservation-law check exists in the paper's public artifact (survey.md Divergences #2). In its place: enable -DCOUNT_COLLISIONS=1 and, on a reduced instance (n<=2,000, single substep), independently compute the exact O(n^2) brute-force sphere-sphere intersection set; the RT-BVH path's resolved collision set MUST match the brute-force set exactly -- this is a correctness bug check, not a quality/speed tradeoff, since the algorithm claims exactness. At full scale (n>=100k), where an exhaustive per-substep check is too costly to run every submission, only the aggregate collision COUNT (via COUNT_COLLISIONS) is checked against the small-scale-verified implementation's count on a matched-density subsample, for gross-error detection only.
Fairness notes
  • The paper's own public harness runs a single trial with no discarded warmup and no repetition (survey.md, Timing protocol) -- this spec adds a 1-frame warmup discard and reports median/min/max over the remaining 199 frames instead of the paper's own single sum-and-print-once total, since a single untimed trial cannot distinguish steady-state throughput from one-time GPU/driver warmup effects (BVH allocator warmup, JIT of the OptiX pipeline, etc.).
  • The particle-count sweep (10k/100k/1M) is this spec's own addition, not a reproduction of a paper table -- the paper evaluates only n=100,000. This is disclosed explicitly rather than presented as paper-verified so a submitter knows which numbers are anchored to the source and which are this spec's extrapolation.
  • No accuracy-parameter axis is included, in deliberate contrast to the parent task's default template, because inventing one for an exact algorithm would misrepresent the paper's actual design; see accuracy_parameter field above and survey.md Divergences #1.
Open questions
  • Whether Mochi's throughput or phase-time breakdown changes qualitatively at n=1,000,000 (e.g. BVH rebuild cost superlinear in n, RT-core occupancy saturation) is unconfirmed -- the paper itself only reports n=100,000, so this spec's high end of the particle-count sweep is unvalidated extrapolation, not a reproduced result.
  • The Taichi CPU/GPU baseline shipped in the repo's taichi/ directory was noted (survey.md) but not read in detail; whether it implements the identical DCD algorithm (making it a fair same-algorithm ablation, analogous to graphB+'s CUDA-vs-OpenMP split in the signed-graph-balancing track) or a structurally different method was not confirmed, so it is not included as a required baseline in this compact spec.
  • No genuinely classical (multipole/tree-code, energy-conservation- checked) N-body paper with a public artifact exists in this corpus (RT-BarnesHut has none); if one becomes available, it should get its own variant with the accuracy_parameter and energy-conservation axes the parent task template originally asked for, rather than retrofitting them onto Mochi.

mesh / AMR

amr-kernel1 papers2 variants

Wavelet-error-driven octree adaptive-mesh-refinement (AMR) time-evolution of the BSSN formulation of the Einstein field equations (binary-black-hole merger, gravitational-wave generation), benchmarked with the paper's own regrid-cost-vs-solve-cost profiling decomposition (remsh_igt vs. rhs/evolve) rather than a synthetic uniform-grid correctness reference, since this track's sole paper's own repo has no such bundled reference script (survey.md Divergences #3).

for each of NT RK4 sub-timesteps: (1) Regrid -- re-evaluate the wavelet refinement criterion on the current solution and refine/coarsen octants where the estimated wavelet coefficient crosses BSSN_WAVELET_TOL (with BSSN_DENDRO_AMR_FAC coarsening hysteresis), performed every BSSN_REMESH_TEST_FREQ steps, not every step; (2) Unzip -- convert the distributed octree (compressed-graph) representation to zero-padded ghosted patches ("octant-to-patch"), optionally overlapped with the corresponding MPI ghost-exchange; (3) RHS -- evaluate the 6th-order finite-difference BSSN right-hand side on every patch; (4) Zip -- convert patches back to the octree representation ("patch-to-octant"); repeat (2)-(4) 4x per RK4 sub-step. Periodically (BSSN_GW_EXTRACT_FREQ), extract psi4 gravitational-wave modes at 6 fixed observer radii.

bssn-amr-single-node-phase-breakdownsteady-state per-timestep cost broken into regrid vs. solve vs. data- layout-conversion phases, matching the paper's own profiling-field decomposition exactly (survey.md: remsh_igt / unzip+comm / rhs / zip), at a fixed, reduced problem size runnable on a single GPU or CPU node -- NOT the full production q=1 config (which targets a full supercomputer allocation), since a single-node kernel-level variant needs a problem size within reach of one node
inputs
suitebinary-black-hole-merger initial data via the Two-Puncture solver (tpid), same generator as the paper's own q1/q2/q4 configs
selectionmass ratio q=1 (paper's own default config, BSSN_GR/pars/q1.par.json, confirmed from repo), reduced to BSSN_MAXDEPTH=12 (matching the paper's own weak-scaling config q1_ws.par.json, the shallowest of the paper's 3 confirmed refinement depths -- chosen here specifically because it is the one config confirmed runnable on a small rank count) rather than the production BSSN_MAXDEPTH=15 config, which the paper itself only runs at full allocation scale
recommended_subsetq1 (mass ratio 1, paper's primary configuration), q2 (mass ratio 2, paper's secondary configuration, optional), q4 (mass ratio 4, paper's tertiary configuration, optional)
dense_operandN/A -- structured per-octant finite-difference stencil state (24 BSSN evolution variables + 6 constraint-monitor variables per grid point), not a dense matrix operand
refinement_levelsBSSN_MAXDEPTH=12, BSSN_MINDEPTH=3 (paper's own weak-scaling config, confirmed from q1_ws.par.json); wavelet tolerance BSSN_WAVELET_TOL=1e-5 with spatially-varying tolerance function (R0=20, R1=220), confirmed from q1.par.json
discretization6th-order (BSSN_ELE_ORDER=6) finite differences, RK4 time integration, CFL=0.25, Kreiss-Oliger dissipation sigma=0.4 -- all confirmed from q1.par.json
protocol
timesteps_measuredstep_ets as reported by the solver's own profiling output (paper's own field name, confirmed from ReadMe.md); recommend >=100 RK4 steps for a stable min/mean/max-across-ranks estimate
regrid_frequencyevery 10 steps for the reduced/weak-scaling-style config (BSSN_REMESH_TEST_FREQ=10, confirmed from q1_ws.par.json) -- NOTE this differs from the production q1.par.json's BSSN_REMESH_TEST_FREQ=30; using the more-frequent-regrid weak-scaling-style value here specifically so the regrid-cost phase is well-represented in a short measured window, flagged as this spec's deliberate choice
warmupfirst regrid cycle (10 steps) discarded from the measured average -- this spec's own addition; the paper's profiling harness (per ReadMe.md) reports min/mean/max over the full `step_ets` profiled window with no described discard, not explicitly a warmup-excluded protocol

timing_scope4 phases exactly as the paper's own profiling output reports them: remsh_igt (regrid), unzip_async and unzip (data-layout conversion, with communication cost inferred as comm = unzip_async_max - unzip_max), rhs (BSSN right-hand-side solve), zip_async (reverse conversion); evolve (= sum of the above across all step_ets steps) reported as the aggregate. GW (psi4) extraction excluded from the per-step timed region since it runs at a coarser BSSN_GW_EXTRACT_FREQ cadence, not every step.
preprocessing_reportedTwo-Puncture initial-data solve (tpid executable) and the initial grid-refinement convergence pass reported separately, once, before the measured evolution window begins -- matches the paper's own 2-stage workflow (run tpid first, then launch the BSSN solver), confirmed from ReadMe.md
metric
primarycell-updates/s = dof_uz (grid points after padding, paper's own reported field) x 24 (BSSN evolution variables) / rhs_max time -- a DERIVED metric, since the paper's own artifact reports phase wall-times and a single headline GFlops/s figure, not a normalized cell-updates/s throughput (survey.md Divergences #1)

correctnessNOT sourced from the paper's own bundled artifact (survey.md Divergences #3: no uniform-grid-reference or GPU-vs-CPU numerical- agreement script was found in the repo's scripts/ directory, which contains only visualization/post-processing utilities). This spec's own recommendation, flagged as such: run the SAME q1 config on both the CPU (bssnSolverCtx) and GPU (bssnSolverCUDA) executables (both confirmed present and separately buildable from the same source tree, ReadMe.md) at matched BSSN_MAXDEPTH/wavelet tolerance, and require the Hamiltonian and momentum constraint-violation norms (C_HAM, C_MOM0-2 -- confirmed as reported/extractable evolution-constraint variables from q1.par.json's variable-index comment block) to agree between the two executables to within a small relative tolerance (recommend 1e-3 relative) at each GW-extraction checkpoint. This is a CPU-vs-GPU cross-implementation agreement gate, not a comparison to an independent uniform-grid reference (which the paper's own artifact does not provide the tooling for).
bssn-amr-scaling-regrid-vs-solvestrong- and weak-scaling behavior with the regrid-cost fraction (remsh_igt / evolve) reported explicitly as a function of scale, since this track's paper's central claim is GPU acceleration AT SCALE (up to 8 A100s strong scaling, up to 229,376 x86 cores weak scaling per the abstract), not single-node throughput alone -- included as a second variant specifically so the scaling claim is independently checkable, matching this project's pattern of a kernel-only + a scaling/e2e variant per track

Fairness notes
  • The paper's fulltext (Methodology/Evaluation section) was unreachable (no arXiv id, only paywalled ACM/IEEE links found) -- the headline numbers cited above (800 GFlops/s, 6x, 2.5x, 8 A100s, 229,376 cores) come from the paper's abstract only, while the phase-decomposition and parameter-file details come from a direct repo read. This split is flagged consistently: metric/protocol STRUCTURE is source-verified, the paper's own reported NUMBERS are abstract-only.
  • No correctness/validation script was found bundled in the artifact repo; this spec substitutes a CPU-vs-GPU cross-implementation agreement check using the solver's own constraint-violation monitors (C_HAM, C_MOM0-2), which IS something the repo's parameter format supports (these are named, indexed output variables), even though no ready-made script runs the comparison automatically.
  • Variant 1 deliberately uses the weaker-refinement q1_ws.par.json (BSSN_MAXDEPTH=12) rather than the physically-production-quality q1.par.json (BSSN_MAXDEPTH=15), because the latter is only meaningful at the paper's own full-allocation scale; this spec is explicit that variant 1's numbers are NOT the paper's own physically-accurate production configuration, to avoid readers mistaking a scaling-study-grade run for the paper's scientific-quality result.
Open questions
  • Exact evaluation-section prose (workload sizes actually plotted in each figure, exact node/GPU counts per data point, exact statistic reported per data point) is unresolved -- the paper's fulltext was unreachable from any open source found.
  • Exact timer instrumentation (MPI_Wtime, std::chrono, or a custom profiling macro) behind the reported phase times is not stated in the README text read.
  • Whether the abstract's "229,376 x86 cores" weak-scaling endpoint used the same q1_ws.par.json configuration this spec anchors on, or a different (larger-BSSN_MAXDEPTH) production-grade config, is unconfirmed.
  • No bundled correctness/reference-comparison tooling was found in the repo; whether the authors validated GPU-vs-CPU numerical agreement internally (and simply did not ship the comparison script) is unknown.
particle-in-cell0 papers2 variants

Explicit electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) cycle (push -> deposit -> field-solve -> interpolate) on a 3D structured grid, benchmarked as particles-processed/s with a per-timestep phase split (interpolation+push / deposition / redistribution) matching this track's sole paper's own decomposition, gated by a per-step charge/energy/ momentum conservation check (see survey.md for why this track's one paper's own diagnostic already matches the parent task's suggested correctness axis almost exactly). This track's paper's own artifact repo is inaccessible (survey.md scope note); the spec is grounded in arXiv fulltext only, flagged throughout wherever repo-level confirmation (exact timer, warmup length) was not obtainable.

for each of NT timesteps: (1) Field Interpolation -- interpolate E/B fields from the Yee-staggered grid to each particle's position, reformulated as an MPU-friendly outer-product (3rd-order B-spline shape factors); (2) Push -- advance particle velocity/position via the Boris pusher; (3) Deposition -- scatter each particle's current contribution back to the Yee grid (direct-current deposition); (4) Field solve -- update E/B on the grid (Yee FDTD update, grid-only, not part of the particle-phase timing bucket); (5) Redistribute -- migrate particles that crossed cell/rank boundaries to their new owning rank/cell, asynchronously overlapped with (3).

pic-particle-phase-ppc-sweepsteady-state particle-phase throughput (particles processed/s) across a particles-per-cell (PPC) sweep, with the paper's own 3-way phase split (interpolation+push / deposit / redistribute) reported separately rather than blended into one number; field-solve (grid-only Yee update) excluded from this variant since it carries no per-particle cost and is not part of what this track's paper contributes on
inputs
suite2 named 3D scenarios from the paper (no broader public benchmark suite exists for this exact contribution -- see survey.md Divergences #1; this is this track's biggest single-paper fairness caveat, inherited rather than papered over)

recommended_subsetuniform-plasma-256x128x128 (paper default scenario), laser-ion-192x192x256 (paper's real-world application scenario, ~7.5x7.5x15um domain)
dense_operandN/A -- no dense matrix operand; per-particle state arrays (position, velocity, weight) plus the Yee-staggered E/B/J grid fields
accuracy_parameterparticles-per-cell (PPC), swept in {1, 4, 16, 64, 128, 256, 512} (paper's own sweep range is PPC in [1,512]; this subset is this spec's own choice of representative points within that range, flagged since the paper's exact tested points were not resolved from the extracted text); thermal velocity varied jointly with PPC in the paper to control particle-migration intensity -- this spec additionally recommends reporting at both a "low-migration" and "high-turbulence" thermal-velocity setting per PPC point, matching the paper's own weak-scaling stress-test framing (survey.md)
protocol
timesteps_measured100
warmup"an initial warm-up phase" per the paper's own text -- EXACT warmup timestep count not stated in the extracted arXiv fulltext and could not be cross-checked against source (artifact inaccessible, survey.md scope note). This spec's own choice, flagged as unconfirmed: warm up for 10 timesteps (10% of the measured window) before starting the 100-timestep measured region.

Field-solve (Yee grid update) explicitly excluded -- grid-only cost, not part of TParticle by the paper's own construction.

SEPARATELY, for the laser-ion scenario specifically, the paper's own MSE=3.198 / MAE=0.8401 (~0.84% relative error) vs. a WarpX reference trajectory is reported as an additional, paper-verified correctness data point, though the exact reference quantity (fields? positions?) is unconfirmed from the extracted text.

Fairness notes
  • This track's paper's public artifact repo is inaccessible (survey.md scope note) -- every protocol detail this spec could not verify against source code (exact warmup length, exact timer instrument, exact PPC sweep points, exact per-node problem size for weak scaling) is flagged individually above rather than presented as paper-verified. A submitter implementing this spec against a real PIC code should treat those fields as this spec's own reasonable defaults, not reproductions.
  • The paper reports mean of 3 trials; this spec substitutes median+min/max per this project's standing fairness principle. Since only 3 trials are specified (paper's own choice), min/max reporting is especially informative here (median of 3 is just the middle value, so min/max carries most of the variance information with only 3 samples).
  • Only 2 named scenarios exist in the source (no larger suite to draw a "standard" subset from, unlike e.g. SuiteSparse-based sparse-kernel tracks in this project) -- both are used, in full, rather than a cherry-picked subset.
Open questions
  • Exact warm-up timestep count before the 100-timestep measured window (paper says only "an initial warm-up phase") -- unresolved from arXiv fulltext; would need artifact access (currently unavailable) or direct author contact to confirm.
  • Exact timer instrument(s) behind TParticle/PPS/CPP -- whether all three share one wall-clock measurement or CPP specifically comes from a separate hardware cycle counter, is not disambiguated in the extracted text.
  • Meaning of the G0-G7 interpolation-kernel variant labels in the paper's Table 3 ablation (likely a tiling/blocking-factor sweep for the MPU outer-product formulation, based on context, but not confirmed).
  • Exact reference quantity behind the laser-ion MSE/MAE correctness numbers (field values vs. particle positions/trajectories) is not stated in the extracted text.
  • Whether/how the physically-ordered particle layout's initial construction cost is isolated from the 100-timestep measured region in the paper's own harness (no repo access to confirm; this spec's preprocessing_reported field is this spec's own assumption).

solvers

cg-krylov7 papers4 variants

Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (and closely related nested/mixed- precision Krylov variants) for sparse symmetric positive-definite linear systems A x = b; measured as four distinct claims this track's own artifacts already draw different lines around — a fixed-iteration unpreconditioned kernel-throughput variant (PERKS's own research question), an end-to-end to-convergence ILU(0)-preconditioned variant with mandatory separate preconditioner-setup reporting (generalizing SPCG's own good practice), a synthetic HPCG-style 3D-stencil-generator + AMG-preconditioned distributed/weak-scaling variant (BootCMatchGX, Graphene, and CLAIRE all use a generator instead of a downloaded matrix), and a reduced-precision cascade variant (F3R, Mille-feuille) that requires an independent fp64-accuracy gate rather than trusting the low-precision recurrence's own residual.

solve A x = b (A sparse, real, symmetric positive-definite, N x N) via (preconditioned) Conjugate Gradient. One PCG iteration = 1 SpMV (q = A*p) + optional preconditioner apply (z = M^-1*r) + 2 dot-product reductions + 3 AXPY-family vector updates (p = z + beta*p; x = x + alpha*p; r = r - alpha*q).

cg-kernel-fixed-itersteady-state per-iteration cost of the UNPRECONDITIONED CG kernel (SpMV + 2 dots + 3 axpys), fixed iteration count, preconditioner excluded entirely — isolates the CG kernel itself from any preconditioner-specific behavior, matching PERKS's explicit research question (persistent-kernel throughput for iterative memory-bound solvers). Fixes two things found in this track's own artifacts: (1) PERKS's own single CUDA-event bracket spanning ALL iterations (divided by iteration count afterward) is replaced with genuine per-iteration timestamps, and (2) the iteration count used in any derived per-iteration number must be read back from the actual loop counter, not a hardcoded literal — the exact bug found in Mille-feuille's public artifact (loop always runs a hardcoded 10000 iterations regardless of the `maxiter` argument, and the reported time is divided by a literal 100, not the true iteration count or a variable).
inputs
suiteSuiteSparse Matrix Collection
selectionreal, symmetric positive-definite (or numerically-SPD-verified) matrices; nnz in [1e4, 4e8]; square. Matches SPCG's own ILU-preconditioned-SPD selection intent and F3R's "symmetric" list; explicitly excludes F3R's own "general" nonsymmetric/BiCGSTAB list (out of scope for a CG-specific track — see open_questions for a possible future BiCGSTAB track).
recommended_subsetbcsstk17, bcsstk18, bcsstk25, bcsstk36, ct20stif, nasasrb, olafu, gyro, cfd1, thermal1, crystm03, nd3k, cant, apache1, apache2, audikw_1, Bump_2911, ecology2, Emilia_923, G3_circuit, ldoor, Queen_4147, Serena, thermal2, tmt_sym
vector_operandb: dense, U(-1,1), fixed seed=42; x0 = 0 (matches the zero initial-guess convention used by SPCG, Mille-feuille, and BootCMatchGX).
protocol
formatCSR (given). If the technique requires a different internal layout (e.g. Mille-feuille's tiled sparse format), the one-time conversion is performed once before timing, measured, and reported separately (see preprocessing_reported) — never folded into the per-iteration number.
warmup5 full iterations (untimed) before the timed block
repsk=50 CG iterations per trial, 20 trials (1000 individual per-iteration timestamps total)
statisticmedian per-iteration time (report min/max/stdev alongside)
timerONE timestamp pair PER ITERATION (not a single bracket spanning all k iterations, which is what PERKS's own public artifact does): GPU = CUDA/HIP event pair per iteration; CPU = std::chrono or omp_get_wtime per iteration; IPU = Poplar profiler region marker per iteration (reported as its own platform-labeled row, not pooled with CUDA/CPU numbers — see notes_on_fairness).
timing_scopekernel only: SpMV + 2 dot-product reductions + 3 AXPY-family updates per iteration, NO preconditioner apply. H2D/D2H excluded (operands device-resident before timing starts).
preprocessing_reportedformat conversion (if any), separately, once — never silently excluded (this is what Mille-feuille's own artifact does correctly for its tile format, via a `time_format` gettimeofday bracket) and never silently included in the per-iteration number.
precisionfp64 (primary); fp32 (secondary) — matches PERKS's own --fp32 flag and SPCG's fp32-only default
metric
primaryms/iteration (median across all per-iteration timestamps)
secondaryGFLOP/s using the per-iteration flop count 2*nnz (SpMV) + 10*N (2 dot products @ 2N flops + 3 AXPYs @ 2N flops each ≈ 10N vector-op flops), NOT PERKS's own hand-rolled memory-traffic-only GB/s formula (kept as an optional tertiary metric alongside, since bandwidth-boundedness is PERKS's own stated design assumption).
correctnessresidual must be monitored EVERY iteration even though it is not used for termination (fixes Mille-feuille's practice of shipping a commented-out residual check) — reject the run if the tracked residual is non-finite or non-decreasing over a 10-iteration trailing window at any point. After k iterations, independently recompute r = b - A*x directly (not via the recurrence) and compare against the recurrence-tracked residual: relative difference < 1e-6 (fp64) / 1e-3 (fp32) — catches recurrence-vs-true-residual drift silently.
cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergenceend-to-end time-to-solution for ILU(0)-preconditioned CG run to a relative-residual convergence gate, with preconditioner analysis+factorization ALWAYS measured and reported separately from the PCG loop — generalizes SPCG's own artifact discipline (which gets this right in the one file surveyed) into a mandatory requirement for every submission, since no other surveyed paper in this track implements this exact ILU(0)+CG configuration to compare against directly.
inputs

selectionsame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter
recommended_subsetsame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter
vector_operandsame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter
protocol
formatCSR (given); ILU(0) analysis+factorization computed once per run, timed, and reported separately — never silently folded into the per-iteration or total-solve number.
warmupnone (a to-convergence solve is inherently single-use; see reps)
reps5 independent runs (fresh factorization each run, to capture any nondeterminism in parallel ILU factorization ordering on GPU)
statisticmedian total time-to-solution (report min/max)
timerone bracket for factorization/analysis (separate), one for the PCG loop (separate) — CUDA events (GPU) or std::chrono/MPI_Wtime (CPU/distributed) — PLUS per-iteration timestamps within the loop (matching SPCG's own per-iteration CSV granularity) so a residual-vs-time curve can be reported, not just a final number.
timing_scopefactorization+analysis (reported separately, once per run) + PCG loop to convergence (this variant's headline number). H2D of the original matrix included once in the factorization-phase timing; D2H of the final solution excluded.
preprocessing_reportedILU(0) setup time (ms, standalone, once per run) — mandatory in every submission, not merely "if measured" (SPCG's own artifact happens to do this; this spec makes it a requirement rather than a lucky default).
precisionfp32 (primary — matches SPCG, the only surveyed paper that implements and times this exact ILU(0)+CG configuration); fp64 (secondary — matches BootCMatchGX's preconditioned-CG convention, generalized from AMG/AFSAI/l1Jacobi to ILU(0) for this variant).
metric
primarytime-to-solution (ms), median across 5 runs, factorization+solve
secondaryiterations-to-converge (median); ILU(0) setup time (ms, standalone); PCG-loop-only time (ms); GFLOP/s = iterations * (2*nnz + 10*N + 2*nnz [triangular-solve preconditioner apply, lower+upper]) / pcg_loop_time.
correctnessRELATIVE residual ||r_k|| / ||r_0|| < rtol, rtol = 1e-6 (BootCMatchGX's own convention) — deliberately NOT SPCG's own absolute threshold (tol=1e-12 on the squared, unnormalized residual dot(r,r)), which is not scale-invariant across matrices/right-hand-sides of different norm (see notes_on_fairness). max_iter = 2000 cap; a run that hits the cap without meeting rtol is reported as non-converged, not silently truncated into a "time" number.
cg-hpcg-generator-amgto-convergence throughput on synthetic HPCG-style 3D-stencil SPD systems (generated in-memory, not downloaded), AMG-preconditioned, reported as weak- and strong-scaling curves — targets the distributed/multi-node usage pattern that a fixed downloaded matrix cannot represent, and which THREE independently-surveyed papers on three different platforms actually use (BootCMatchGX's `--laplacian-3d SIZE --laplacian-3d-generator 7p|27p` on multi-GPU MPI, F3R's locally-generated `hpcg_<nx>_<ny>_<nz>.mtx`, and Graphene's `-p/--poisson nx,ny,nz` on IPU) — confirming this is a real methodological split in the track's own literature, not a spec-author invention.
inputs
suitesynthetic 3D Laplacian / Poisson stencil generator (not SuiteSparse)
selectionboth 7-point and 27-point stencil variants (BootCMatchGX ships both; they differ in nnz/row and therefore in arithmetic intensity); local subdomain sizes and rank counts chosen to cover both a strong-scaling series (fixed global problem, increasing rank count) and a weak-scaling series (fixed per-rank local problem, growing global problem with rank count).
recommended_subsetweak scaling: local subdomain 50^3 per rank (matches BootCMatchGX's own regressionTest config lap3d_27p_50x50x50_{1x1x1,2x1x1,2x2x2}) and 128^3 per rank, at rank counts {1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}; strong scaling: fixed global 256^3 grid at the same rank-count series.
vector_operandb = A * ones(N) (standard Poisson-generator convention); x0 = 0
protocol
formatgiven directly in the solver's native distributed CSR by the generator itself — no format-conversion phase applies here (this variant explicitly sidesteps the format-conversion discipline used in the other three variants, since there is no "given" matrix to convert from).
warmupnone (each (grid size, rank count) point is inherently a single scaling-study run)
reps3 independent runs per (grid size, rank count) point
statisticmedian wall time (report min/max — important at high rank counts as a scaling-noise indicator)
timerMPI_Wtime (distributed CPU/GPU) or platform-native equivalent (Poplar profiler region for IPU — reported as its OWN platform-labeled row, explicitly NOT pooled with MPI_Wtime/CUDA- event numbers from other platforms, since the instrumentation mechanisms are not equivalent). One bracket for AMG bootstrap/hierarchy setup (reported separately, once per run) plus one for the PCG-with-AMG-preconditioner loop.
timing_scopeAMG setup timed and reported separately, never folded into per-iteration time. Solve loop timed to convergence. Halo-exchange/communication cost is NOT separated out as its own line item in this variant (unlike the one-shot format-conversion discipline elsewhere) because it is inherent to the distributed SpMV/AMG-apply kernel itself at every iteration, not a one-time preprocessing cost.
preprocessing_reportedAMG hierarchy setup time (ms, standalone) + grid-generation time (ms, standalone) — both are one-time per-run costs distinct from the iterative solve.
precisionfp64 (primary, matches BootCMatchGX and CLAIRE's presumed convention). Graphene's software-emulated fp64 / `twofloat` double-word arithmetic (required since the IPU lacks native fp64) is reported as its OWN separately-labeled precision row, never silently pooled with true hardware-fp64 numbers from GPU/CPU runs, since the cost models are not comparable (see notes_on_fairness).
metric
primarytime-to-solution (ms) vs. rank count — weak- and strong-scaling curves
secondaryparallel efficiency (%) = T(1 rank) / T(N ranks) at fixed per-rank work (weak scaling); AMG setup time (ms, standalone); iterations-to-converge.
correctnesssame relative-residual gate as cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence (rtol = 1e-6, max_iter = 2000), applied to the AMG-preconditioned loop.
cg-mixed-precision-cascadeto-convergence solve using a reduced-precision cascade (fp64 outer / fp32-or-fp16 inner), reporting speedup vs. a matched fp64-only baseline WITHOUT silently trading away final accuracy — targets F3R's nested FGMRES/Richardson fp16-inner design and Mille-feuille's tile-grained on-chip dynamic precision conversion, the two papers in this track that build reduced-precision Krylov solvers as their central contribution.
inputs
suitesame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter, restricted to the symmetric/SPD recommended_subset (F3R's own symmetric list already overlaps heavily with it)
selectionsame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter
recommended_subsetsame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter
vector_operandsame as cg-kernel-fixed-iter
protocol
formatgiven as CSR at fp64; technique-specific reduced-precision copies (tile-grained fp32 companions, or fp16 inner-solver arrays) constructed once, timed, and reported separately — same discipline as every other variant.
warmupnone beyond cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence's
reps5 independent full to-convergence runs (matches F3R's own `<average>` repeated-full-solve pattern), report median
statisticmedian total time-to-solution (report min/max)
timersame as cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence, PLUS a mandatory breakdown of time spent at EACH precision level (fp64 outer iterations vs. fp32/fp16 inner iterations) — required because neither F3R's plain CSV output nor Mille-feuille's (broken) loop currently surfaces this breakdown cleanly.
timing_scopeto-convergence, full solve, same H2D/D2H discipline as cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence
preprocessing_reportedreduced-precision copy construction, standalone, once per run
precisionfp64 outer/reference; fp32 AND fp16 inner-solve configurations BOTH run and reported as SEPARATE rows (matches F3R's actual 3-way sweep: cg64/cg32/cg16 etc.) — never averaged together into one number.
metric
primaryspeedup = T(fp64-only baseline, this same matrix run through cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence's unpreconditioned-CG-equivalent config) / T(mixed-precision cascade)
secondaryfraction of total iterations spent at each precision level; final relative accuracy vs. the fp64 reference solution.
correctnessTWO mandatory gates, not one: (a) the OUTER fp64-tracked relative residual must still satisfy < 1e-6 (same as cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence) — the inner reduced-precision iterations are never allowed to relax the outer convergence criterion just because they are cheaper; AND (b) the final solution x is compared against an INDEPENDENTLY-computed fp64-only reference solve, relative error < 1e-8. Gate (b) is the explicit fix for the failure mode Mille-feuille's own artifact exhibits: a post-hoc correctness check computed AFTER the (mis-terminated) loop that never actually gates whether the reported time counts.
Fairness notes
  • cg-kernel-fixed-iter requires genuine per-iteration timestamps and a true iteration-counter readback, fixing two independent issues found by reading this track's own artifacts: PERKS's single CUDA-event bracket spanning all `max_iter` iterations (divided by iteration count only after the fact, which can hide per-iteration variance or GPU-clock-ramp effects during the run) and Mille-feuille's hardcoded `while (iterations < 10000)` loop that ignores its own `maxiter=10` argument, combined with a reported time divided by a literal `100` rather than the true iteration count — an artifact bug that would silently misreport per-iteration cost by roughly 100x if taken at face value.
  • cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence and cg-hpcg-generator-amg both mandate that preconditioner-setup time (ILU(0) factorization, or AMG hierarchy bootstrap) be measured and reported separately in EVERY submission. SPCG's own artifact already does this correctly via distinct CUDA-event brackets for "Preconditioning Time" vs. "PCG Time" — this spec generalizes that into a requirement rather than treating it as one paper's lucky default (contrast Mille-feuille and PERKS, both unpreconditioned, where the question does not even arise in their own artifacts).
  • cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence and cg-hpcg-generator-amg both use a RELATIVE residual normalized by the initial residual norm (BootCMatchGX's convention: `l2_norm < rtol * delta0`), not SPCG's own absolute/unnormalized threshold (`r1 > tol*tol` with `tol=1e-12` and no normalization by the initial residual). An absolute threshold is not comparable across matrices or right-hand-sides of different scale; this spec fixes one relative-tolerance convention across every to-convergence variant instead of adopting either paper's own choice as-is.
  • cg-mixed-precision-cascade requires BOTH an outer fp64 relative- residual gate AND an independent fp64-reference-solution accuracy check, specifically because reduced-precision Krylov recurrences can report a residual that "looks converged" via the low-precision recurrence while the true error is larger. Mille-feuille's own public artifact only checks correctness AFTER its (already mis-terminated) loop finishes, via a CPU-recomputed `l2_norm`, and that check never actually gates whether the loop's reported time is accepted — this spec makes an equivalent check load-bearing rather than informational.
  • cg-hpcg-generator-amg reports IPU (Poplar-profiler) numbers as their own explicitly platform-labeled row rather than pooling them with CUDA-event/MPI_Wtime numbers from GPU/CPU platforms, and similarly keeps Graphene's software-emulated-fp64/`twofloat` numbers in a separate row from true hardware-fp64 numbers — both instrumentation mechanism and underlying precision implementation differ enough that pooling them would be an apples-to-oranges comparison, not a fairness fix per se but a labeling requirement to prevent one.
Open questions
  • CLAIRE's PCG solve is nested inside a much larger nonlinear Gauss- Newton image-registration optimization, with an inner-preconditioner tolerance (1e-3 for NIREP, 1e-2 for CLARITY datasets) chosen for the OUTER optimization's convergence behavior rather than the CG kernel's own standalone accuracy. Both WebFetch attempts at the arXiv fulltext (PDF and ar5iv HTML) truncated before reaching the paper's Section 4 (Numerical Experiments), so its exact timing protocol, precision, and baseline comparisons could not be confirmed. It cannot be cleanly reduced to any of the four variants above without stripping away the surrounding registration pipeline; whether a fifth "PCG-as-a-nested-component" variant is worth adding is left open, contingent on obtaining the full paper text.
  • BootCMatchGX's exact AMG-setup-vs-solve-time output field (the specific CSV/log column the `-M`/`-P`/`-p` profiling flags actually produce) was inferred from the existence of those CLI flags and the `BEGIN_PROF`/`END_PROF` macro infrastructure, not confirmed by reading the profiling-output-writing code itself. cg-hpcg-generator-amg's "AMG setup time reported separately" requirement should be checked against a real run's output before being treated as load-bearing.
  • Graphene's JSON solver-configuration schema (default relative tolerance / max-iteration values, and whether they differ per solver type — PBiCGStab vs. Mixed-Precision Iterative Refinement vs. Gauss- Seidel) was not fetched (would require reading `Configuration::fromJSON` plus a sample config file, not pursued within the survey's time budget). cg-hpcg-generator-amg's IPU row currently assumes BootCMatchGX's rtol=1e-6/itnlim=2000 defaults by analogy; this is unconfirmed for Graphene specifically.
  • Extended precision (Graphene's software-emulated fp64 and `twofloat` double-word arithmetic) runs in the OPPOSITE direction from this spec's precision-cascade variant (which is scoped to reduced precision, fp32/fp16, matching F3R and Mille-feuille — the two papers where concrete, comparable reduced-precision numbers actually exist). Whether extended precision deserves its own fifth variant, or is better left as a platform-specific footnote on the fp64 rows of the other variants, is unresolved.
  • PERKS's and Mille-feuille's actual paper-reported matrix suites (as opposed to the single smoke-test matrix each public artifact ships — `add20.mtx` for Mille-feuille, a synthetic tridiagonal matrix or an unspecified user-supplied `--mtx` for PERKS) could not be recovered from the public artifacts within the survey's time budget. Every variant's `recommended_subset` above is therefore drawn only from SPCG's (code-confirmed, 114-matrix) and F3R's (code-confirmed, 15-matrix symmetric) lists, and has not been independently cross-checked against PERKS's or Mille-feuille's own paper tables.
multigrid5 papers4 variants

Algebraic/geometric multigrid as a preconditioner or standalone solver for Ax=b, measured with the setup phase (hierarchy construction: coarsening + interpolation + Galerkin SpGEMM triple product) and the solve phase (V-cycle smoothing + SpMV) reported as fully separate numbers — the split every surveyed solver paper's own code enforces internally, even when its headline speedup blends them. GPU/algebraic-AMG variants and a CPU/ geometric-MG variant are kept separate because they have structurally different hierarchies (SpGEMM-coarsened matrix hierarchy vs. a geometrically-refined structured grid with no comparable "setup phase").

solve A[N,N](sparse, s.p.d.) x[N] = b[N] via (P)CG with an AMG/MG V-cycle preconditioner; A_k+1 = R_k A_k P_k for the algebraic-setup variants

mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64steady-state GPU AMG SETUP-phase throughput (coarsening + interpolation + Galerkin triple-product SpGEMM chain that builds the grid hierarchy), reported ENTIRELY separately from solve-phase time — the axis this track's own instructions call out as the classic AMG split, and one that AmgT's and BootCMatchGX's own code/plots both already keep separate internally (AmgT's `t_start/t_stop` bracket around `HYPRE_BoomerAMGSetup` alone; BootCMatchGX's `tsetup` reported apart from `tsolve`). This variant exists so a paper cannot advertise a blended "total speedup" number that hides a setup-time regression behind a solve-time win, or vice versa.
inputs
suitetwo explicitly separate, non-interchangeable input classes (see Divergences in survey.md — no surveyed paper mixes them, and results on one are not comparable to results on the other): (a) "poisson-3d": a synthetic 3D Poisson problem, -div(K grad u)=f on [0,1]^3, homogeneous Dirichlet BC, K=1, discretized by the standard 7-point finite-difference stencil (BootCMatchGX's exact generator, the closest match in this track to an "AMG2023-style Poisson" generator); (b) "suitesparse-real": real algebraic matrices from the SuiteSparse Matrix Collection.
selection(a) poisson-3d: cubic grids nd in {64, 128, 192, 300}, i.e. up to 300^3 ~= 27e6 dofs (BootCMatchGX's own strong-scaling size), RHS f=1, unitary right-hand side. (b) suitesparse-real: real, square, s.p.d.-or-near-s.p.d. matrices with 2e4 <= nnz <= 5e7, matching the order-of-magnitude range AmgT's own 16-matrix set spans (229,947-46,522,475 nnz); no cherry-picking beyond that range filter.
recommended_subsetpoisson-3d: [64^3, 128^3, 192^3, 300^3] (192^3 matches MGopt-APP's HPCG grid size for CPU/GPU cross-reference; 300^3 matches BootCMatchGX's strong-scaling size exactly). suitesparse-real (AmgT's own 16-matrix curated list, Table II): [spmsrtls, thermal1, Pres_Poisson, Chevron2, venkat25, bcsstk39, mc2depi, stomach, parabolic_fem, cant, TSOPF_RS_b300_c3, af_shell4, msdoor, CoupCons3D, nd24k, ldoor].
rhs_operandb: all-ones vector (matches AmgT's test driver) for suitesparse-real; b=f=1 (unitary RHS) for poisson-3d (matches BootCMatchGX).
protocol
hierarchy_configV-cycle only for this variant (see mg-cpu-geometric-symgs for the F-cycle case and open_questions for W-cycle, which no surveyed paper benchmarks). Coarsening: PMIS (AmgT's exact choice) or maximum-weight-matching pairwise aggregation (BootCMatchGX's exact choice) — report which was used, do not silently pick one. Max levels: 7 (AmgT) or until coarsest size <= 40*nd with max 40 levels (BootCMatchGX) — implementation-specific, report the actual level count reached per input. Strong threshold 0.25 (AmgT) as the default if the implementation exposes this knob.
formatmatrix given as CSR (or COO->CSR); any internal reformatting the setup phase itself performs (e.g. AmgT's CSR<->mBSR conversion, invoked 2*levels-1 times) stays INSIDE this variant's timed setup window, since it is part of what 'setup' means for that implementation — it is NOT amortized or excluded the way spmv/spgemm-track format conversion is, because here it genuinely only happens once per solve, not once-then-reused-across-many-calls.
warmup3
reps10
statisticgeometric mean (MGopt-APP's own stated protocol — the only surveyed paper with an explicit statistic); report min/max and the run-to-run coefficient of variation alongside (MGopt-APP reports <5% variance and this is the bar every other surveyed paper failed to state at all)
timerdevice-side wall-clock bracket around ONLY the hierarchy-construction call (e.g. HYPRE_BoomerAMGSetup, or the equivalent aggregation+SpGEMM chain), matching AmgT's own t_start/t_stop code exactly
timing_scopesetup kernel only; H2D of the input matrix excluded (matrix assumed device-resident before setup starts, or its H2D cost reported once, separately, under preprocessing_reported)
preprocessing_reportedH2D transfer of the input matrix/RHS: separately, once. Any host-side matrix generation (poisson-3d stencil assembly) or Matrix-Market parsing (suitesparse-real): separately, once; neither counts toward setup_time.
precisionfp64 (both input classes; matches all 3 solver papers' baseline — none of them runs setup itself in reduced precision, only the solve-phase SpMV/smoother steps use mixed precision in AmgT)
metric
primarysetup_time (ms), geometric mean of 10 reps
secondaryoperator complexity OPC = sum_k nnz(A_k)/nnz(A_0) (BootCMatchGX's exact metric — required so a faster-but-worse hierarchy is visible, not just a smaller number)
correctnesshierarchy is well-formed: coarsest-level matrix size > 0 and <= configured max coarse size; every A_k+1 = R_k A_k P_k Galerkin product checked against a reference (host CPU, fp64) triple-sparse-product for a small held-out grid (64^3 poisson-3d or one small suitesparse-real matrix) with max relative nnz-pattern and value mismatch < 1e-10
mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-itersteady-state GPU AMG SOLVE-phase throughput for a FIXED, disconnected- from-convergence iteration count — the protocol AmgT's own driver code actually implements (`HYPRE_BoomerAMGSetMaxIter(precond, 50)` combined with `HYPRE_BoomerAMGSetTol(precond, 1e-20)`, which can never trigger early exit). This variant exists specifically to give every implementation the SAME fixed amount of work (comparable per-iteration throughput, no implementation can "win" by converging in fewer iterations that happen to do less real work) — paired with mg-gpu-e2e-pcg below, which is the honest convergence-gated counterpart this variant alone cannot provide.
inputs
suitesame two classes as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64 (poisson-3d, suitesparse-real)

rhs_operandsame as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64
protocol
hierarchy_configV-cycle, fixed 50 iterations (AmgT's exact number), pre/post smoothing sweeps = 3/3 (AmgT) or 4/4 (BootCMatchGX) — report which configuration; coarsest-level solve = a fixed number of smoother sweeps (BootCMatchGX: 20 l1-Jacobi sweeps; AmgT: direct or iterative, implementation-dependent), NOT a sparse-triangular direct solve (both surveyed GPU papers deliberately avoid this for GPU-friendliness — see BootCMatchGX's explicit discussion of why direct coarsest-level solves are avoided on GPU).
formathierarchy from mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64 is reused (given, not rebuilt); if the implementation's solve phase requires its own internal reformatting per iteration (e.g. AmgT's CSR<->mBSR round trips inside the V-cycle), that stays inside the timed solve window
warmup3
reps10
statisticgeometric mean, min/max/coefficient-of-variation reported (same protocol as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64)
timerdevice-side wall-clock bracket around ONLY the solve call (e.g. HYPRE_BoomerAMGSolve), matching AmgT's t1/t2 code exactly
timing_scopesolve kernel only, hierarchy already resident on device; H2D/D2H of x/b vectors excluded from the timed window (assumed device-resident)
preprocessing_reportedN/A for this variant (setup already excluded by construction; see mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64 for that number)
precisiontwo required sub-variants, both against the SAME fixed 50-iteration protocol: (i) fp64 throughout (baseline); (ii) AmgT's exact level-dependent mixed-precision cascade — fp64 at the finest grid level, fp32 at the second-finest level, fp16 (or fp64 fallback if the target GPU/instruction set has no usable fp16 tensor-core path for this operation) at all remaining coarser levels. Report both; do not report only the faster one.
metric
primarysolve_time (ms) for the fixed 50-iteration V-cycle, geometric mean of 10 reps
secondaryfinal relative residual norm ||b-Ax||_2/||b||_2 reached after the 50 fixed iterations (NOT gated as pass/fail for this variant, since the point is fixed-work throughput regardless of convergence quality — but MUST be reported so a reader can see whether 50 iterations actually reached a usable answer for that input, closing the gap AmgT's own paper leaves open by never disclosing this number itself)
correctnessthe final x from the 50-iteration run must be finite (no NaN/Inf) and the reported residual norm above must be computed from an independently-recomputed b-Ax (not reused from the solver's internal bookkeeping), fp64, regardless of the run's own precision — this catches a mixed-precision implementation silently corrupting the answer while still reporting fast, since a fast-but-wrong 50th iteration is not a valid result even under a fixed-iteration protocol.
mg-gpu-e2e-pcgend-to-end, CONVERGENCE-GATED preconditioned-CG solve: one-shot AMG setup + PCG iterations to a real stopping tolerance — BootCMatchGX's exact protocol (relative residual < 1e-6 in the l2 norm, capped at 1000 iterations), the honest counterpart to mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-iter's fixed-work number. This is the claim practitioners actually care about ("how long until I have a usable answer"), and the one AmgT's own fixed-iteration/tol=1e-20 protocol structurally cannot answer.
inputs
suitesame two classes as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64
selectionsame as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64, restricted to matrices/grids where the problem is s.p.d. (a PCG requirement both surveyed convergence-gated papers rely on)

rhs_operandsame as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64

formatsame as mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-iter
warmup3
reps10
statisticgeometric mean of wall time; report the PCG iteration count as its own reported quantity (not averaged away — report min/median/max iteration count across the 10 reps, since a fixed problem+solver should converge in a near-constant iteration count and material variance across reps is itself a red flag worth surfacing)
timerdevice-side wall-clock bracket around setup+solve combined (total time to solution) AND the solve-only portion reported separately, so both 'time to answer including hierarchy build' and 'PCG solve time given a hierarchy' are available

preprocessing_reportedsame as mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64
