correctnessrelative residual ||b-Ax||_2/||b||_2 < 1e-6 (BootCMatchGX's exact tolerance) REQUIRED to reach within the iteration cap (max 1000 iterations, BootCMatchGX's exact cap) for the run to count as a valid result at all — unlike mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-iter, failing to converge within the cap is a hard FAIL for this variant, not just a reported number, since the entire claim being measured here is "time to a real answer."
mg-cpu-geometric-symgsend-to-end CPU multi-core geometric-multigrid throughput (HPCG-style): no separate algebraic setup phase exists for this problem class (the grid hierarchy is defined directly by geometric refinement, factor of 8 per level, not by SpGEMM coarsening from a matrix) — MGopt-APP's exact evaluation shape, kept as its own variant rather than forced into the GPU setup/solve split above, since that split does not apply to a geometrically-generated hierarchy.
inputs
suiteHPCG v3.1's own synthetic 3D 27-point-stencil-flavored problem generator (structured grid, no external matrix file)
selectioncubic local grids per MPI rank; standard HPCG problem-size convention (grid dimensions must be multiples of 8 to support the 4-level V-cycle's factor-of-8-per-level coarsening)
recommended_subset[64^3, 104^3, 144^3, 192^3] per MPI rank (192^3 is MGopt-APP's exact evaluated size); optionally a real-application-embedded validation problem (YHAMG solving Poisson via 7-point or 27-point stencil, or CitcomCU's finite-element earth-simulation grid) reported separately, not blended into the synthetic-grid numbers
rhs_operandHPCG reference RHS convention (b constructed so the exact solution x is known, for correctness checking)
protocol
hierarchy_configV-cycle, 4 levels (HPCG standard), SYMGS as pre-/post-smoother (1 sweep each, HPCG default) and as the bottom/coarsest-level solver; F-cycle reported as a secondary configuration ONLY if the implementation under test is applied to CitcomCU or an equivalent F-cycle-capable application (do not force F-cycle onto the synthetic HPCG grid, which MGopt-APP itself only ever runs as V-cycle)
formatN/A — no sparse-matrix input format; grid and stencil operator generated in-memory by the HPCG reference generator
warmup0
reps10
statisticgeometric mean; report cross-run variance explicitly (MGopt-APP's own bar: must be < 5%, stated in the report, not just computed silently)
timerwall-clock (e.g. MPI_Wtime or std::chrono::steady_clock) around the full timed HPCG run, matching MGopt-APP's own 'end-to-end benchmark performance' scope exactly
timing_scopewhole benchmark run (there is no separable setup phase for this problem class, per the claim above); MPI/OpenMP process and thread counts must be reported alongside the result (MGopt-APP: 8 MPI x 7 OpenMP on ARM, 4 MPI x 7 OpenMP on x86 to match 28 physical cores) since GFLOPS without a reported core/rank count is not comparable across machines
preprocessing_reportedN/A (grid generation cost is part of the timed run in HPCG convention, matching MGopt-APP's own practice, since it is a fixed, small, one-time cost relative to the iterative solve that follows)
precisionfp64 (HPCG reference convention; no paper in this track's CPU-solver methodology explores mixed precision on this problem class)
metric
primaryGFLOPS (HPCG's own reference FLOP-counting convention: fixed FLOP count per SYMGS+SpMV+dot+axpy call in the reference algorithm, independent of the optimized implementation's actual instruction count)
secondaryparallel efficiency T_1/(N*T_N) for multi-node runs, N = node/rank count (MGopt-APP's own metric for its 256-node scaling result)
correctnessHPCG's own built-in reference-residual check: computed x must satisfy the reference implementation's convergence/correctness gate (HPCG spec: relative residual reduction by a fixed factor within the standard iteration count) — reject any run that alters this numerical behavior even if it alters loop structure/memory layout, since MGopt-APP's own stated design goal is "preserves SYMGS semantics without changing the computation outcome," and a spec permitting numerically-different-but-faster SYMGS would undercut the entire point of that constraint.
Fairness notes
  • AmgT's own benchmark driver sets `HYPRE_BoomerAMGSetTol(precond, 1e-20)` — a tolerance so tight it can never trigger — specifically so every timed solve always executes exactly 50 iterations regardless of actual convergence, and the paper never reports the final residual reached. This spec does not just adopt that protocol: mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-iter keeps the fixed-work comparison (useful for isolating per-iteration kernel throughput) but requires the final residual be reported anyway, and mg-gpu-e2e-pcg adds the convergence-gated counterpart AmgT's own paper never provides, so a reader can tell whether "50 iterations" was ever enough to reach a real answer for a given input.
  • No two of the three genuine solver papers (AmgT, BootCMatchGX, MGopt-APP) share a baseline library, an input suite, or even a problem-generation philosophy (real matrices vs. synthetic Poisson vs. HPCG's own generator) — see survey.md's Divergences. Rather than forcing all three into one variant and hiding this incompatibility, the spec keeps poisson-3d and suitesparse-real as explicitly separate, labeled input classes within the GPU variants, and keeps the CPU/geometric-MG variant entirely separate from the GPU/algebraic-AMG variants, since their setup/solve semantics genuinely differ (see claim text above).
  • Only MGopt-APP's paper states an explicit timing protocol (10 reps, geometric mean, <5% variance stated in prose) among the 3 solver papers; AmgT's own code shows a single, unrepeated `gettimeofday` bracket per phase, and BootCMatchGX's paper gives no repetition/ statistic language at all. This spec fixes MGopt-APP's protocol (reps=10, geometric mean, explicit variance report) as the uniform requirement across every GPU and CPU variant, rather than the single-shot measurement AmgT's own artifact actually performs.
  • BootCMatchGX's comparison against Nvidia AmgX is a rare example of a genuinely fair baseline-matching effort in this track: the authors modified AmgX's own `PCG_AGGREGATION_JACOBI.json` config specifically to produce a hierarchy with comparable operator complexity to their own BCMG solver, rather than comparing against AmgX's arbitrary defaults. This spec generalizes that discipline: every variant above requires operator complexity (or an equivalent hierarchy-quality metric) be reported alongside timing, specifically so config-mismatched comparisons (a "fast" solver that got there by building a cheaper, lower-quality hierarchy) are visible rather than laundered into a bare speedup number.
  • MGARD and GPTuneCrowd are excluded from the 4 variants above even though both are in this track's paper set — see open_questions. Folding MGARD's non-iterative data-refactoring throughput or GPTuneCrowd's black-box-tuning-of-Hypre-as-one-of-five-applications into a "multigrid solver kernel" spec would blend three incompatible claims (solve a linear system fastest vs. compress data fastest vs. tune parameters best) under one metric, which is exactly the kind of apples-to-oranges comparison this track's fairness principles are meant to prevent.
Open questions
  • W-cycle is asserted as "equally applicable" by MGopt-APP but never actually benchmarked by any of the 3 solver papers (all three report V-cycle only; MGopt-APP additionally reports F-cycle for one real application, CitcomCU, but not on its synthetic HPCG grid). A W-cycle variant was considered but not added — no surveyed paper provides even one concrete number to calibrate expected iteration-count/convergence- rate tradeoffs against, so adding the variant now would mean inventing a protocol with no literature anchor at all, unlike every other variant above which traces to a specific paper's actual practice.
  • MGARD's data-refactoring throughput (GB/s/TB/s against theoretical peak memory bandwidth, no setup/solve split, no convergence criterion, no Ax=b ever solved) does not fit any of the 4 variants above and was deliberately left out rather than forced in. If this track's scope is later widened to include "multigrid mathematics applied to non-solver problems," MGARD's own evaluation methodology (§IV-A in survey.md item 4) is a ready-made template for a `mg-data-refactoring-throughput` variant: synthetic Gray-Scott-simulation grids, GB/s vs. hardware peak, weak-scaling up to 1024 nodes — but this is a decision for whoever owns the track's scope, not implicit in the 5-paper survey alone.
  • GPTuneCrowd's Hypre/BoomerAMG sensitivity-analysis result (agg_num_levels and smooth_type are the most-influential of 12 tuning parameters, per Sobol S1/ST scores on a 100^3 Poisson grid) is a genuinely useful signal for anyone building an autotuning harness ON TOP of the mg-gpu-* variants above (e.g. "which of BootCMatchGX's/AmgT's exposed knobs are worth a search budget"), but GPTuneCrowd itself benchmarks tuning QUALITY (tuned runtime after N function evaluations), not kernel throughput — a fundamentally different measurement axis this spec does not attempt to fold in. Left as a candidate cross-reference for a future autotuner-focused track (see benchspecs/autotuner-multi-kernel/) rather than a multigrid-track variant.
  • AmgT's exact fp16 substitution behavior when the target GPU/HYPRE build lacks a usable tensor-core fp16 path for the coarse-level SpGEMM/SpMV (the paper states it "did not utilize FP16 precision" in its own mixed-precision run and set the coarser levels to fp64 instead of the fp32/fp16 cascade described elsewhere in the same paper) means the exact per-GPU precision cascade actually run is inconsistent even within AmgT's own paper (H100/A100 runs vs. the MI210 run use different fallbacks). mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-iter's precision sub-variant (ii) requires reporting WHICH actual per-level precision assignment was used, rather than assuming "AmgT's mixed-precision cascade" is one fixed, unambiguous configuration across all hardware.
  • Neither BootCMatchGX's nor MGopt-APP's paper discloses a warmup-run count (BootCMatchGX: none discussed at all; MGopt-APP: "we run each test case 10 times," ambiguous on whether the first of the 10 is a cold run included in the geometric mean or excluded as warmup). This spec's warmup=3 for the GPU variants is not traceable to any single surveyed paper's stated practice (none states a warmup count at all) and should be treated as a spec-author default pending a code-level check of whichever reference implementation is actually used to run this benchmark, not as a value extracted from the literature.
preconditioner5 papers4 variants

Measures preconditioner cost along three axes that the track's own papers keep separate but a benchmark must report together where an outer solver exists: one-shot setup (factorization / hierarchy construction / DAG scheduling), per-application or per-iteration apply cost, and, for variants that exercise an outer Krylov solver, the number of iterations the preconditioner buys or costs versus a reference.

Setup: build M (an approximate inverse of A, or a multigrid hierarchy, or a scheduled DAG) once from sparse A. Apply: z = M*r, either as a standalone kernel proxy (matrix-power A^d*x for polynomial preconditioners; forward/ backward triangular solve for ILU(0)/IC(0)) or nested inside a Krylov solve (PCG/BiCGStab) that is run to a residual-based convergence criterion.

mpk-kernel-cpu-f64steady-state per-application throughput of the matrix-power kernel A^d*x that underlies polynomial preconditioners, one-shot block- partitioning setup excluded and reported separately; no outer solver exercised (this is a kernel-only proxy, not a solve-to-convergence).

Fairness notes
  • DBMPK's own artifact never checks correctness (computes both baseline and DBMPK outputs, never diffs them); mpk-kernel-cpu-f64 adds a hard gate.
  • SPCG and BootCMatchGX both time a single solve-to-convergence with no warmup and no repeated runs; both full-solve variants add explicit warmup plus N reps plus median/min/max, since GPU clock throttling or first-touch page faults on a single run would otherwise silently pollute the reported number.
  • SPCG's own convergence tolerance (1e-12, absolute, on fp32 arithmetic) is tighter than fp32's practical residual floor; precond-solve-single-gpu-f32 replaces it with a relative 1e-8 criterion so iteration counts reflect the preconditioner, not an unreachable tolerance.
  • Neither DBMPK nor HDagg ships a fixed matrix list in its artifact (DBMPK takes one path via -in; HDagg globs a local directory); both kernel-only variants fix an explicit, named list built from matrices independently verified elsewhere in this track's artifacts (Graphene's and SPCG's own named SuiteSparse instances), rather than leaving the suite to whatever the user happens to have on disk.
  • HDagg's own correctness check (testing()) only logs a warning on mismatch, never fails; ilu-apply-kernel-cpu-f64 makes it a hard gate before timing counts.
  • The setup-vs-apply-vs-iteration-count-together rule is scoped to the two full-solve variants (precond-solve-single-gpu-f32, amg-precond-solve-multigpu-f64): the two kernel-only variants (mpk-kernel-cpu-f64, ilu-apply-kernel-cpu-f64) have no outer solver and hence no iteration count to report. Collapsing all four variants onto one iteration-count column would be meaningless for two of them, so the spec keeps setup-vs-apply reporting mandatory everywhere but iteration-count mandatory only where an outer Krylov loop exists.
Open questions
  • DBMPK's and HDagg's own paper-reported matrix suites could not be recovered (PPoPP 2026 DL page paywalled, no arXiv id for either; IPDPS 2022 PDF at cs.toronto.edu could not be text-extracted with the tools available). The recommended_subset lists above are the spec's own construction, not verbatim from either paper.
  • BootCMatchGX's floating-point precision (the vtype typedef used throughout BCMGX/src/datastruct/CSR.h) was not located in the header files read; fp64 is assumed by AMG/CG convention but unconfirmed.
  • Graphene (IPDPS 2025, Graphcore IPU) is excluded from all four variants: its architecture has no native fp64 and a fundamentally different tile-memory execution model incompatible with a shared CPU/GPU timing harness. Its artifact is still useful evidence for this spec's iteration-count-as-first-class-metric principle (its solver configs print inner/outer iteration counts and residuals by default) and for the precision axis (fp32 base plus twofloat32/ float64 extended precision as its actual research contribution). A future IPU-specific variant would need its own harness built around Poplar's profiler, whose own warmup/repeat/statistic policy is opaque from the repo.
  • SPCG's SC 2025 paper text (setup vs iteration-count breakdown beyond what the abstract states) is paywalled (ACM DL) and has no arXiv id; the precond-solve-single-gpu-f32 variant's exact size range for the 113-matrix suite is inferred from matrix names, not stated bounds.
mixed-precision-solver4 papers4 variants

Solvers (dense LU, nested sparse Krylov, tile-based Cholesky) that trade numerical precision (fp8/fp16/fp32) for throughput and rely on a precision-recovery mechanism — fp64 iterative refinement, an independent fp64 residual re-check, an outer statistical-accuracy metric, or a one-shot adaptive per-tile precision choice — to reach an accuracy target this spec treats as a FIRST-CLASS, load-bearing requirement: a mixed-precision run that is fast but does not reach fp64-equivalent accuracy (or an explicitly-defined statistical/application accuracy bar) reports no valid speedup number, full stop. Four variants, one per surveyed paper's own precision-recovery strategy, since (per survey.md's Divergences) none of the four strategies reduces to any other.

solve a linear system or covariance-parameter estimation problem using a reduced-precision computational core (fp16/fp32 factorization or fp16 inner Krylov iterations or fp8/fp16/fp32/fp64 adaptive tile precision), paired with an accuracy-recovery step (fp64 IR / independent residual recompute / outer MLE optimization / one-shot precision selection) and, where the paper's own codebase supports it, a same-codebase pure-fp64 sibling binary run on the identical input as the baseline.

mp-dense-lu-ir-hplaidense LU factorization (fp32 panel decomposition + fp16 tensor-core GEMM) followed by fp64 iterative refinement to the OFFICIAL HPL-AI accuracy criterion (hplerror < 16, the same constant HPL-AI submissions use), capped at 50 refinement iterations — targets OpenMxP's exact HPL-AI benchmark design. This spec adds one mandatory fix: a run whose IR loop exhausts 50 iterations without reaching hplerror < 16 MUST be reported as a hard FAIL, not silently printed alongside converged runs — OpenMxP's own main.cpp currently prints the loop's {-1,-1} non-convergence sentinel unconditionally (residual=-1, hpl-harness=-1) with no check before the headline TFlop/s line, indistinguishable in the console output from a legitimately converged run.
inputs
suitesynthetic dense matrix, generated in-place (not downloaded) by the implementation's own generator (OpenMxP: matgen.hpp / Higham test-matrix generator in highammgen.hpp — matches HPL-AI convention of self-generating its own test matrix rather than reading one).
selectionsquare dense N x N; N chosen per scale point to approach available device memory at each rank/GPU count (weak-scaling convention). Spec-fixed defaults below, since OpenMxP's own README gives tuning guidance (best block size, best local-N) but no fixed benchmark size list — the paper's own headline numbers are full-Summit/Frontier- scale runs whose exact N was not recoverable from the repo (see open_questions).
recommended_subsettile size B=2560 (OpenMxP's own stated best); local-per-rank N (LN)=125440 (OpenMxP's own stated best), global N = P*LN at scaling points P (GPU count) in {1, 8, 64, 512}; a smaller smoke-test point N=40960 (P=1) for quick validation runs.
dense_operandright-hand side b generated jointly with A by the same Higham/HPL random generator (matches OpenMxP's matgen/Matgen<double> pairing used for both the low-precision factorization input and the fp64 residual-recompute reference).
protocol
formatN/A — matrix generated in-device/in-place, no file format or conversion step exists in this variant.
warmup1 reduced-flop-count calibration run (matches OpenMxP's own -w/ --warmup flag: runs with maxit=1 for the IR loop and subtracts a skip-flop correction from the reported flop count for that run; excluded from the timed/reported measurement).
reps1 per scale point (matches OpenMxP's own single-run-per-invocation design; this is a spec-flagged weakness, not an endorsement — see notes_on_fairness. At scale points where resource cost permits, 3 reps with median/min/max is recommended, but a single full-system run is accepted as inherent to HPL-AI-class submissions).
statisticsingle measurement at full scale (spec-flagged, see above); median of >=3 at any scale point below full-system size.
timerMPI_Wtime() bracket around factorization+IR combined (matches OpenMxP's start_time/stop_time), PLUS a separate MPI_Wtime bracket around the IR phase alone (matches OpenMxP's own "IR Time" line) — both reported.
timing_scopefactorization (fp32 panel + fp16 GEMM) + fp64 IR, combined AND IR-only reported separately; matrix generation happens BEFORE the timed region starts in OpenMxP's own code (confirmed: pmatgen calls precede Timer::beg(TOTAL)/start_time) and is correctly excluded.
preprocessing_reportedN/A — matrix generation is untimed setup by construction in this variant (no conversion/preprocessing step separate from generation).
precisionfixed cascade, not swappable sub-variants: fp32 factorization panel + fp16 tensor-core GEMM (OpenMxP's FHIGH=float / FLOW=__half), fp64 iterative refinement for accuracy recovery (matches OpenMxP's own fixed design — the paper does not sweep alternative precision assignments the way F3R does).
metric
primaryTFlop/s per GPU (hplflops = 2/3*N^3 + 3/2*N^2, divided by rank/GPU count and wall time)
secondaryIR iteration count to reach hplerror<16 (cap 50), reported as a distribution across scale points
tertiaryresidual and hpl-harness value at convergence (or FAIL, per correctness below)
correctnessHARD gate, mandatory: hpl_harness < 16 AND IR iteration count <= 50 required for a run to report a valid TFlop/s number. The harness MUST explicitly check for OpenMxP's own {-1,-1} non-convergence sentinel (er.residual == -1) and refuse to report a throughput number for that run — spec-added fix for OpenMxP's own main.cpp gap described in the claim above.
baselinepure double-precision HPL / the HPL-AI-defined "double-precision- equivalent accuracy" criterion itself IS the correctness bar (not a separately-timed same-binary fp64 LU run — OpenMxP's own repo does not build a pure-fp64 comparison binary). Speedup vs classical HPL is reported as a cross-benchmark ratio against published HPL Rmax numbers on the same system, matching the paper's own Table/Figure approach — flagged as a weaker baseline-pairing than mp-krylov-nested-cascade- sparse's same-script comparison below (see notes_on_fairness).
mp-krylov-nested-cascade-sparsenested FGMRES/Richardson Krylov cascade (fp64 outer / fp32 mid / fp16 inner) with TWO independent residual channels tracked per run (recurrence-tracked "implicit" + independently recomputed "explicit"), run back-to-back against a SAME-SCRIPT, SAME-MATRIX pure-precision baseline family (cg64/cg32/cg16, gm64/gm32/gm16) — targets F3R's exact design and its own reproduction script's paired-comparison structure, the strongest same-codebase fp64-baseline pairing found in this track.

baselinesame-binary-family pure-precision solvers (cg64/cg32/cg16 for the symmetric list, bicg64/32/16 for the general list; gm64/32/16 GMRES as a second baseline family) — F3R's own suite-cpu.py runs these on the identical matrix in the identical script invocation, the paper's own comparison.
mp-tile-cholesky-mle-geostatmixed single/double-precision tile Cholesky factorization, called once per likelihood evaluation inside an outer NLopt (derivative-free) maximum-likelihood optimization loop — targets ExaGeoStat's exact MLE design. "Convergence" here is the OUTER OPTIMIZER's convergence (function-evaluation budget), not a Krylov/refinement iteration count; "accuracy" is STATISTICAL prediction quality (mean-square prediction error against held-out observations, or parameter-recovery error against known synthetic ground truth), not a floating-point residual — the mixed-precision (sdmle) run's accuracy must not degrade materially relative to the SAME-CODEBASE pure-double (dmle) run on the identical dataset/seed for the speedup to be legitimate.
inputs
suite(a) synthetic Gaussian random fields (Matern covariance family) with KNOWN ground-truth theta parameters (ExaGeoStat's own synthetic_dmle_test.c / synthetic_sdmle_test.c, via the MLE_zvg generator) — primary, accuracy-controlled variant; (b) real observational datasets (ExaGeoStat's own real_csv_dmle_test.c / real_csv_sdmle_test.c, e.g. wind-speed data) — secondary, real-world variant, reported separately from (a).
selectionN and dts (dense tile size) not recoverable from the driver source alone (open question; the paper's own SC22 12x-speedup headline configuration was not confirmed). Spec-fixed defaults below.
recommended_subsetsynthetic: N in {20000, 40000, 80000} locations, univariate Matern stationary kernel (`kernel_fun=univariate_matern_stationary`, num_params=3 — ExaGeoStat's own default kernel per the driver code), dts swept per the paper's own tuning guidance (implementation- dependent, report the actual value used).
dense_operandsynthetic case: generated jointly with known initial_theta by MLE_zvg (fixed seed for reproducibility, seed value not confirmed — open question); real case: CSV observation + location files per ExaGeoStat's own real_csv_*_test.c input format.
protocol
formatN/A — dense covariance matrix generated in-place from a locations file/array, not read from a sparse-matrix file; no format-conversion step in this variant.
warmupnone observed in the driver (spec-added: 1 discarded MLE run before the timed run, for a fair comparison to the other 3 variants' warmup discipline)
reps3 (spec-added; ExaGeoStat's own driver runs a single nlopt_optimize call per invocation with no repetition observed)
statisticmedian, report min/max (spec-added)
timerTWO separate brackets, matching ExaGeoStat's own START_TIMING/ STOP_TIMING macro pairs: (a) total_exec_time, spanning the entire nlopt_optimize call (the full MLE fit — this variant's headline number); (b) pred_time, spanning ONLY the held-out prediction phase, reported separately (matches ExaGeoStat's own "fit" vs "predict" split, the closest analogue in this track to a setup-vs-solve split).
timing_scopefull MLE optimization (fit) and prediction, reported as 2 separate numbers, never blended into one
preprocessing_reportedN/A for this driver (data reading / location-array setup happens before START_TIMING(data.total_exec_time); not separately measured in the source read)
precisionpure double (`dmle` binary, data.precision path not using EXAGEOSTAT_sdmle_Call) as the REQUIRED baseline vs mixed single/ double (`sdmle` binary, data.precision=2) as the treatment — BOTH run on the identical synthetic dataset/seed (or identical real CSV input) for a valid paired comparison; spec-required, since ExaGeoStat's own repo builds both as separate binaries from the same codebase but the driver scripts do not automate running them paired.
metric
primaryspeedup = total_exec_time(dmle) / total_exec_time(sdmle), same dataset/seed
secondaryNLopt function-evaluation count to convergence (outer "iteration" count, capped at data.opt_max_iters) for both dmle and sdmle, reported side by side (a mixed-precision run needing materially more outer evaluations to converge is not a clean win, same iteration-count-as-first-class principle as this track's sibling cg-krylov/multigrid/preconditioner specs)
tertiaryprediction error (MSPE) delta = prediction_error(sdmle) - prediction_error(dmle), and, for the synthetic case, ||estimated theta - ground truth theta|| relative error delta between the two precisions
correctnessspec-added HARD gate (ExaGeoStat's own driver computes but never gates on this): for synthetic data, sdmle's theta-recovery relative error must be within 10% of dmle's own theta-recovery error; for real data, sdmle's prediction MSPE must be within 5% of dmle's MSPE on the identical held-out set. A run failing either bound reports no valid speedup number.
baselinepure double-precision MLE (`dmle`), same codebase, same dataset/seed (ExaGeoStat's own paired binaries, not automated as a pair by the driver scripts — see precision above).
mp-tile-cholesky-onestep-climate-emulatorone-shot (no iterative refinement, no outer optimization loop) mixed-precision tile factorization pipeline: forward spherical- harmonic transform (SHT) -> SYRK -> Cholesky factorization (adaptive per-tile precision among double/single/half/fp8, chosen ONCE before factorization, never corrected afterward) -> inverse SHT — targets hicma-x's exact climate-emulator design, the fourth and structurally most different precision-recovery strategy in this track (accuracy measured as an application-domain RMSE against a reference field, not a floating-point residual and not a statistical prediction metric).
inputs
suiteERA5-style climate reanalysis data (hicma-x's own testing_climate_emulator, `--mesh_file` input; download link given in TESTS.md), gridded by `--latitude L` (N = L*L).
selectionlatitude values covering TESTS.md's own worked example plus a larger scale point approaching the paper's claimed near-EFlop/s Frontier configuration (exact paper-reported N not recoverable from the repo — open question).
recommended_subsetlatitude in {120, 480, 1440} (N = 14400, 230400, 2073600); 120 matches TESTS.md's own worked example exactly
dense_operandreanalysis climate field read from the mesh_file input (real data, not synthetic)
protocol
formatN/A — dense covariance-like matrix built from SHT output, not read from a sparse-matrix file
warmupnone stated in the source read (spec-added: 1 discarded full pipeline run)
reps--nruns wraps ONLY the Cholesky-factorization phase in hicma-x's own code (hicma_parsec_potrf loop in performCholeskyFactorization); SHT/ SYRK/inverse-SHT/MSE are each single-shot in the artifact. Spec REQUIRES reps>=3 for EVERY phase, not just factorization — strengthens the artifact's own partial-repetition practice.
statisticmedian per phase, report min/max (spec-added; hicma-x's own SYNC_TIME_PRINT prints a single value per phase per run)
timerSYNC_TIME_START()/SYNC_TIME_PRINT() macro pairs around EACH phase separately (matches hicma-x's own code exactly: forward SHT, forward-reshape, SYRK, matrix-norm, factorization, inverse SHT, MSE) — the finest-grained per-phase split of any paper surveyed across this track and its cg-krylov/multigrid/preconditioner siblings.
timing_scopeevery phase reported separately, plus a total; no phase is silently folded into another
preprocessing_reportedmesh/data reading (climate_emulator_reading_data), timed separately (gb.time_init), excluded from every downstream phase's number
precisionadaptive per-tile cascade among double/single/half/fp8 (--adaptive_decision, tuned via --band_dense_dp/--band_dense_sp/ --band_dense_fp8), chosen ONCE at setup from the matrix's error-bound structure — no runtime refinement pass exists in this variant. The spec REQUIRES reporting the actual precision assigned per band/tile-region (not just "mixed precision was used"), since the decision algorithm itself was not independently verified (see open_questions) and a submission's specific band assignment is otherwise unreproducible.
metric
primarytime-to-solution (ms) per phase (SHT-forward, SYRK, factorization, SHT-inverse) plus total
secondaryGflop/s for the SHT-forward and factorization phases (hicma-x's own gb->flops_forward-based metric)
tertiarynormalized RMSE (hicma-x's own climate_emulator_mse metric) vs the reference/observed climate field, per time-slot and aggregated
correctnessspec-added HARD gate (hicma-x's own code computes but never gates on this — climate_emulator_mse.jdf prints the RMSE unconditionally at verbose>1 with no threshold comparison anywhere in the reviewed source): normalized RMSE vs the reference field must be < 1e-2 (spec-author default, since no paper-stated threshold exists — see open_questions) for the run's timing number to count as valid.
baselinea pure fp64, single-precision-level run of the SAME pipeline (all bands forced to double, i.e. --band_dense_sp=0 --band_dense_fp8=0) on the identical mesh/latitude — not automated as an explicit A/B pair by hicma-x's own test driver; spec-required for a valid speedup claim.
Fairness notes
  • OpenMxP's own main.cpp prints the iterative-refinement loop's {-1,-1} non-convergence sentinel (residual=-1, hpl-harness=-1) unconditionally alongside legitimate converged results, with no check before the headline TFlop/s line — mp-dense-lu-ir-hplai's correctness gate makes this check mandatory. This is the same class of silent-non-convergence reporting bug this project's cg-krylov survey found in Mille-feuille's public artifact (loop runs regardless of its own termination argument).
  • This track's 4 papers use FOUR incompatible notions of "accuracy": floating-point residual harness (OpenMxP), dual implicit/explicit residual channels (F3R), statistical prediction quality (ExaGeoStat), and application-domain field RMSE (hicma-x). The spec deliberately does not force one universal "residual < eps" rule across all 4 variants, since a linear-algebra residual and a geostatistics prediction error are not the same kind of quantity and forcing them into one metric would hide exactly the information a reader needs to judge the claim.
  • F3R's own suite-cpu.py is the only artifact in this track whose reproduction script runs the mixed-precision treatment (f3r16/f3r32) and a same-binary-family pure-precision baseline (cg64/gm64) back-to- back on the IDENTICAL matrix in the SAME script invocation — the cleanest same-codebase baseline pairing surveyed. The other 3 papers' drivers require this spec to mandate the paired run explicitly, since their own scripts do not automate it (OpenMxP has no fp64 LU sibling binary in-repo at all; ExaGeoStat's dmle/sdmle and hicma-x's all-double- band configuration exist but are not scripted as an automatic pair).
  • Both ExaGeoStat's prediction-error/MLOE-MMOM values and hicma-x's MSE value are computed by their own drivers and then only WRITTEN to a file or PRINTED under a verbosity flag — neither driver gates on its own accuracy number anywhere in the source read. Both this track's mp-tile-cholesky-mle-geostat and mp-tile-cholesky-onestep-climate- emulator variants turn these into hard, mandatory gates.
  • F3R (SuzukiI25) is also surveyed in benchspecs/cg-krylov/spec.yaml's cg-mixed-precision-cascade variant (SPD/CG-specific framing of the same artifact). This track's mp-krylov-nested-cascade-sparse variant is complementary, not duplicative: it documents the same-binary-family paired baseline (T3C_SYM/T3C_GEN in sc25/suite-cpu.py) discovered by reading that specific reproduction script, which the cg-krylov survey's own evidence line for this paper does not mention.
Open questions
  • OpenMxP's exact paper-reported problem sizes N at full Summit/Frontier scale (the SC22 headline numbers themselves) were not recoverable from the public repo; README gives tuning guidance (best B, best local-N), not a fixed benchmark size list. mp-dense-lu-ir-hplai's recommended_subset is constructed from that tuning guidance, not verbatim from the paper's own reported configuration.
  • hicma-x's per-tile adaptive-precision decision algorithm (--adaptive_decision) was located only by CLI flag name (TESTS.md); the source implementing the actual decision criterion (which tile gets which of double/single/half/fp8) was not read within this survey's budget. mp-tile-cholesky-onestep-climate-emulator's requirement to report the actual per-band precision assignment is a workaround for not being able to independently verify the decision logic itself.
  • ExaGeoStat's paper-reported N and dts values for the SC22 "Reshaping Geostatistical Modeling" 12x-Fugaku-speedup headline number were not recovered (no arXiv id, ACM DL paywalled, no OA fulltext link in the track input JSON). mp-tile-cholesky-mle-geostat's recommended_subset is the spec's own construction, not verbatim from the paper.
  • F3R's exact M2/M3/M4/W/Precond/ACC CSV column semantics (visible as literal CLI arguments in sc25/suite-cpu.py's `add = [...]` lists but not decoded from the senk library source within this survey's time budget) are used descriptively only in mp-krylov-nested-cascade-sparse; the spec does not assert a precise per-column meaning for any of them.
  • Whether F3R's own senk library hard-fails a run when ImplRes and ExplRes diverge beyond tolerance, or merely logs both columns without asserting agreement, was not confirmed — the driver script only captures binary stdout into a CSV; the underlying pass/fail logic (if any) lives in the senk library's own headers, not reviewed here. mp-krylov-nested-cascade- sparse's correctness gate (relative agreement bound) is therefore a spec-author addition, not a confirmed existing behavior.
  • hicma-x's normalized-RMSE correctness threshold (1e-2) in mp-tile-cholesky-onestep-climate-emulator is a spec-author default: no paper-stated accuracy threshold was found in the source read (the metric is diagnostic/logged-only in the artifact, per notes_on_fairness above), so this value should be treated as a starting point pending validation against a real run's actual RMSE distribution.

compression

lossy-compression20 papers3 variants

Measure error-bounded lossy compression/decompression of scientific floating-point data on SDRBench-standard fields: compression ratio and throughput (GB/s) at fixed error bounds, plus a rate-distortion (PSNR-vs-bitrate) curve that lets error-bound-target (SZ-family) and rate-target (ZFP/SPERR-family) compressors be plotted on one axis.

compress: C = Compress(D, eb) where D is an n-dimensional fp32/fp64 array and eb is an error-bound spec (mode in {abs, rel}, value in R+); decompress: D' = Decompress(C); correctness requires max_i |D_i - D'_i| <= eb (abs mode) or <= eb * (max(D) - min(D)) (rel mode) for every element, not just on average.

lossy-comp-kernel-cpu-eboundsteady-state CPU compress/decompress throughput and ratio at a fixed error bound; I/O and any one-shot autotuning search excluded and reported separately. The common denominator across the SZ-family papers (PFPL, QoZ, FAZ, TAC/TAC+, and as an SZ3-baseline reference for SPERR).
inputs
suiteSDRBench (https://sdrbench.github.io)
selectionnamed fields from the 6+ SDRBench applications most cited across the surveyed papers (FZ-GPU's 6-dataset table + PFPL/SPERR's explicit SDRBench pointer); fixed list below, both fp32 and fp64 variants where the dataset provides them.
recommended_subsetHACC/xx (cosmology, 1D, 280,953,867 elements, fp32, log-transform before compression), HACC/vx (cosmology, 1D, 280,953,867 elements, fp32, log-transform before compression), CESM-ATM/CLDICE (climate, 2D 1800x3600, fp32), CESM-ATM/RELHUM (climate, 2D 1800x3600, fp32), NYX/baryon_density (cosmology, 3D 512^3, fp32/fp64), NYX/dark_matter_density (cosmology, 3D 512^3, fp32/fp64), NYX/temperature (cosmology, 3D 512^3, fp32/fp64), Hurricane-ISABEL/CLDICE (weather, 3D 100x500x500, fp32), Hurricane-ISABEL/QRAIN (weather, 3D 100x500x500, fp32), Hurricane-ISABEL/Uf,Vf,Wf (weather, 3D 100x500x500, fp32, velocity components), QMCPACK/einspline (quantum MC, 3D 69x69x115, fp32/fp64), Miranda/density (hydrodynamics, 3D 256x384x384, fp32), Miranda/viscosity (hydrodynamics, 3D 256x384x384, fp32), S3D/combustion field (3D 500^3, fp32), EXAALT (molecular dynamics, 1D 2,869,440 elements, fp64), SCALE-LETKF (climate DA, 3D 98x1200x1200, fp32)
layoutrow-major (C order); dimensions as listed, dim_x fastest-varying per SZ/cuSZp convention
protocol
error_bound
modesabs, rel
primaryrel (fraction of value range max(D)-min(D))
values1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4
noterel is the SZ-family/FZ-GPU/cuSZp community default; abs is also swept once per dataset at eb = rel_value * (max(D)-min(D)) for rel in {1e-2,1e-3,1e-4} so both axes are comparable, since TAC and cuSZp report abs-mode numbers directly (TAC used raw abs values 1E8/1E9/1E10 tuned to its own density field's dynamic range, which is not portable across datasets, so we normalize abs bounds through the dataset's own value range instead).
warmup3
reps9
statisticmedian (report min/max alongside)
timerwall-clock (std::chrono / equivalent) wrapping only the compress() / decompress() call on data already resident in memory
timing_scopekernel only; disk I/O, format parsing, and any autotuning parameter search excluded
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per dataset x error-bound point (covers AMR-style level-unification preprocessing and FAZ-style autotuning search, both observed as one-shot costs in the surveyed papers)
metric
primarycompression ratio (original_bytes / compressed_bytes)
secondarythroughput GB/s, both directions (original_bytes / compress_time, original_bytes / decompress_time) -- numerator is ALWAYS original (uncompressed) byte count, confirmed community convention (cross-checked from lsCOMP's worked example)
correctness100% of reconstructed elements satisfy |D_i - D'_i| <= eb (zero pointwise violations, not a statistical/average tolerance -- this is the compressor's core guarantee, not an approximation)
lossy-comp-gpu-dual-scopeGPU kernel throughput reported at TWO explicit scopes so the two incompatible community meanings of "end-to-end" (FZ-GPU/TAC's incl.-PCIe-transfer sense vs. cuSZp's fused-single-kernel-only sense) are never conflated: (a) device-resident kernel-only throughput, and (b) full pipeline throughput including H2D input transfer and D2H compressed/decompressed output transfer.
inputs
suiteSDRBench (same recommended_subset as lossy-comp-kernel-cpu-ebound)
dense_operandn/a (not a GEMM-style kernel); data resident on device as flat fp32/fp64 buffer, dims passed via -d flag per cuSZp/lsCOMP CLI convention
protocol
error_bound
modesabs, rel
values1e-2, 1e-3, 1e-4
warmup3
reps20
statisticmedian (report min/max)
timerdevice-side events (CUDA events), matching cuSZp's TimingGPU pattern
timing_scope_akernel-only: timer starts/stops around the compress()/decompress() device-pointer-to-device-pointer call, H2D/D2H excluded (this is what cuSZp/cuSZp2/cuSZp3 call 'end-to-end' -- one fused kernel, no PCIe)
timing_scope_bfull-pipeline: timer starts before H2D copy of input, stops after D2H copy of decompressed output lands on host (this is what FZ-GPU's 'overall throughput' and TAC's 'total time' mean)
preprocessing_reportedn/a for regular-grid SDRBench inputs at this variant; format is a flat array, no conversion step
metric
primarycompression ratio (original_bytes / compressed_bytes)
secondarythroughput GB/s at scope (a) and scope (b) reported as two separate numbers, never averaged together
correctness100% of reconstructed elements satisfy |D_i - D'_i| <= eb, verified after D2H copy-back (not on-device only, to catch transfer corruption)
lossy-comp-rate-distortionrate-distortion curve (PSNR in dB vs. bits-per-value) comparing rate-target compressors (ZFP, SPERR) against error-bound-target compressors (SZ-family, cuSZp, FZ-GPU) on one shared axis -- resolves the track's core divergence that these two compressor families expose opposite control knobs (SPERR/ZFP take bpp as input and report resulting PSNR; SZ-family take error bound as input and report resulting bpp+PSNR).
inputs
suiteSDRBench (same recommended_subset as lossy-comp-kernel-cpu-ebound, 3D fields only -- SPERR's compressor_3d requires volumetric input)
selectionNYX/baryon_density, Hurricane-ISABEL/CLDICE, Miranda/density, S3D combustion field, QMCPACK/einspline (5 of the 16 above, chosen because all 4 surveyed families -- SZ3/QoZ, cuSZp, FZ-GPU, SPERR -- publish numbers on at least one of them)
protocol
sweep_axisfor rate-target compressors (ZFP, SPERR): sweep target bitrate bpp in {0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4} bits/value, taken directly from SPERR's own evaluate_compress.sh sweep list, record resulting PSNR
sweep_axis_altfor error-bound-target compressors (SZ3, QoZ, FAZ, cuSZp, FZ-GPU): sweep rel error bound in {3e-1, 1e-1, 3e-2, 1e-2, 3e-3, 1e-3, 3e-4, 1e-4, 3e-5, 1e-5} (log-spaced to cover the same ~0.1-4 bpp range these compressors typically land in), record resulting (bpp, PSNR) pair
warmup3
reps5
statisticmedian
timerwall-clock CPU or device-side GPU events per the compressor's native platform
timing_scopekernel only, same as lossy-comp-kernel-cpu-ebound; RD variant's primary deliverable is the curve, not throughput, but timing is still recorded per point for the record
metric
primaryPSNR (dB) at each achieved bitrate (bits-per-value = 8 * compressed_bytes / n_elements)
secondarycompression ratio at each point, throughput at each point (for context, not the headline)
correctnessfor error-bound-target compressors: 100% pointwise |D_i-D'_i| <= eb still enforced at every swept eb, exactly as in lossy-comp-kernel-cpu-ebound; for rate-target compressors (no error-bound contract at fixed bpp): PSNR itself IS the reported quality metric, no separate pass/fail gate
Fairness notes
  • "End-to-end" is a false-friend term in this literature: FZ-GPU/TAC use it to mean incl. PCIe transfer, cuSZp/cuSZp2/cuSZp3 use it to mean "one fused kernel, no multi-pass pipeline" (explicitly PCIe-EXCLUDED). The spec never reuses the bare term; lossy-comp-gpu-dual-scope names both scopes explicitly and reports them as two separate numbers so no paper's claim can be silently compared against the wrong scope.
  • TAC (HPDC'22) merges AMR-level-unification preprocessing into its reported throughput; its own successor TAC+ (TPDS'24) separates it out. The CPU kernel-only variant follows TAC+'s (the more rigorous, more recent) convention: preprocessing reported separately, never silently amortized into the per-run kernel number.
  • FAZ's one-shot autotuning search (predictor/encoder combination search per block) is architecturally the same kind of one-shot cost as format conversion in other tracks' kernel-only-vs-e2e split: reported once, separately, never amortized into steady-state throughput without saying so.
  • The rate-distortion variant's error-bound sweep for SZ-family compressors is a spec design choice (log-spaced eb list), not something directly lifted from any single paper, because no surveyed SZ-family paper publishes a literal bpp-target sweep -- they all sweep error bound and only incidentally report the resulting bpp. This is flagged as engineered-for-fairness rather than literature-derived.
  • Correctness is a hard 100%-pointwise gate, not a statistical tolerance (unlike, e.g., an SpMM-style "<1e-4 relative error" spec) -- because the entire product claim of every SZ/ZFP-family compressor in this track is a guaranteed pointwise error bound, and a spec that only checked average error would let a compressor that silently violates the bound on a minority of elements pass.
  • lsCOMP (uint16/uint32 light-source data, quantization-bin + pooling lossy knobs instead of abs/rel error bound) and the TAC/TAC+ AMR family (hierarchical multi-level grids, not flat arrays) are both genuinely out of scope for the 3 variants above -- forcing them onto the abs/rel SDRBench axis would misrepresent what they actually measure. See open_questions.
Open questions
  • QoZ (SC'22), FAZ (ICS'23), and VGC/cuSZp3 (SC'25) paper PDFs are ACM-DL/computer.org paywalled and were not machine-readable via WebFetch (redirects to dl.acm.org returned 403). Their exact named dataset lists, disclosed repetition counts, and hardware are therefore NOT independently confirmed here -- only README + abstract-level claims were used. If a verified copy becomes available, the recommended_subset and protocol numbers above should be cross-checked against it.
  • No AMR-specific benchmark variant is defined despite 2 dedicated papers (TAC, TAC+) and partial relevance in IPComp/CEAZ, because there is no SDRBench-equivalent standardized AMR corpus found during this survey (TAC and TAC+ each use their own private Nyx/WarpX/IAMR dumps, not a shared public benchmark set). Flagged as a follow-up track extension, not solved here.
  • lsCOMP's integer quantization-bin + pooling lossy mode has no closed-form error-bound equivalent to compare against the rest of the track's abs/rel convention; excluded from all 3 variants rather than force-fit.
  • Repetition/warmup counts are a synthesis (PFPL's disclosed 9 reps + lsCOMP's disclosed 3 warmup iters), not a literature-wide consensus -- most surveyed papers disclose neither number. This is the single protocol parameter in this spec with the weakest evidentiary backing.
  • SPERR's third quality-control mode (point-wise error, PWE) is functionally identical to the SZ-family's abs-error-bound mode and could arguably be folded into lossy-comp-kernel-cpu-ebound rather than only appearing in the RD variant; left in the RD variant only for this first cut since that is where the surveyed evidence (evaluate_compress.sh) was found.
lossless-compression7 papers3 variants

Measure bit-exact lossless compression/decompression of byte and multi-byte integer streams across three distinct data domains this track's papers actually target -- generic byte-stream/text/genomic corpora, HPC/scientific multi-byte integer data (mostly SZ/cuSZ quantization-code streams and sensor/detector data), and structured LLM-weight-tensor operands feeding a downstream GEMM kernel -- reporting compression ratio and compress/decompress throughput (GB/s) jointly, never one alone, gated by a hard bit-exact roundtrip check.

compress: C = Compress(D) where D is a byte or multi-byte-integer stream (or, for variant 3, a structured 2D weight tensor); decompress: D' = Decompress(C); correctness requires D' == D bit-for-bit for every byte, not a statistical or average tolerance -- unlike the lossy-compression track, there is no error bound to trade off against ratio/throughput.

lossless-comp-cpu-byte-decodesteady-state, multi-core CPU decompression throughput of standard gzip/DEFLATE-format byte streams, scaled across a fixed 3-corpus suite spanning generic text, genomic, and near-incompressible control data. The corpus's own compression ratio is treated as a FIXED, once-measured property of a reference encoder run -- never re-measured per decompressor tool -- because the one paper defining this sub-domain (Rapidgzip) is decompression-only and has no compression path of its own to time.
inputs
suiteSilesia corpus + 1 genomic (FASTQ) corpus + 1 synthetic near-incompressible control corpus, all gzip/DEFLATE-encoded -- the exact 3-corpus set Rapidgzip's own HPDC'23 evaluation uses.
selectionthe literal corpus set disclosed in Rapidgzip's fulltext evaluation section, scaled by concatenating multiple gzip tarballs/files to reach each target core-count's workload size (2-256x per Rapidgzip's own scaling method).
recommended_subsetSilesia corpus (12 standard files: dickens, mozilla, mr, nci, ooffice, osdb, reymont, samba, sao, webster, x-ray, xml), gzip -9, ratio ~3.1, concatenated 2-256x, FASTQ genomic reads, SRA accession SRR22403185, gzip -9, ratio ~3.74, base64-encoded random-content control (near-incompressible; isolates raw byte-shuffling throughput from match-finding payoff), gzip -9, ratio ~1.315
reference_encodergzip -9, single fixed level, applied ONCE per corpus to produce the input files under test -- compression ratio is reported as a corpus property, not re-measured per decompressor tool under test.
protocol
cpu_coressweep {1, 16, 32, 64, 128} threads (trimmed subset of Rapidgzip's own {1,16,48,64,96,128,256} sweep to typical HPC-node core counts)
warmup1 (discarded)
reps30 (within Rapidgzip's own disclosed 20-100-repeat range)
statisticmean +/- 1 standard deviation (Rapidgzip's own disclosed convention, the most statistically explicit protocol found in this track -- adopted as-is)
timerwall-clock, process pinned via taskset
timing_scopedecompression only; input resident in tmpfs (/dev/shm), output sunk to /dev/null -- I/O deliberately routed around the measurement, not subtracted after the fact
preprocessing_reportedn/a -- input is the standard gzip container as-produced, no format conversion step
metric
primarydecompression throughput GB/s = original (decompressed) bytes / decompression time
secondaryspeedup vs. single-threaded GNU gzip baseline; corpus compression ratio (fixed per corpus, see reference_encoder -- reported once, not per decompressor tool)
correctness100% byte-exact match between decompressed output and the original uncompressed corpus (memcmp-equivalent over the full file) -- imposed by this spec since Rapidgzip's own disclosed evaluation methodology text does not report an explicit round-trip verification step.
lossless-comp-gpu-multibyte-dual-scopeGPU compress/decompress kernel throughput on multi-byte scientific and sensor integer data -- mostly SZ/cuSZ intermediate quantization-code streams plus native detector data -- reported at TWO explicit scopes (kernel-only vs. full-pipeline-incl-H2D/D2H) so the two incompatible "end-to-end" meanings already identified in the lossy-compression track (GPULZ's coarse CLI wall-clock default vs. the Huffman-decoder paper's kernel-only convention) are never silently conflated. Block/ chunk/window parameters are explicitly disclosed and swept, not fixed, since GPULZ's own Table 2 shows throughput varying by >2x across its block-size grid alone.

preprocessing_reportedthe upstream cuSZ quantization step that produces the *-quant inputs is a ONE-SHOT preprocessing cost, external to and reported separately from this variant's compress/decompress kernel timing -- this variant benchmarks the LOSSLESS back-end stage only (GPULZ's and the Huffman-decoder's own shared framing), not the upstream lossy quantizer.

correctness100% byte-exact roundtrip (bit-for-bit, memcmp-equivalent over every byte), hard gate -- matches MANS's (std::memcmp, hard-aborts on mismatch) and the Huffman-decoder paper's (CUHDUtil::equals, prints "mismatch" on failure) own strongest disclosed practice, extended track-wide to GPULZ and lsCOMP's lossless mode where their own public artifacts print a correctness proxy (compression ratio; a one-off "Max abs diff: 0") but stop short of a hard-coded pass/fail assertion wired into the benchmark loop itself.
lossless-comp-structured-operand-fusedfused decompress+downstream-compute (decompress-GEMM) kernel throughput for lossless-compressed LLM weight tensors vs. a dense uncompressed baseline kernel, gated by a standalone bit-exact weight-roundtrip check that is STRICTLY STRONGER than the correctness verification found in the one source paper's (ZipServ) own public artifact, which checks only downstream GEMM-output similarity and never the decompressed weight tensor itself.
inputs

warmup10 (spec-imposed; STRICTLY STRONGER than ZipServ's own WARM_UP_ITERATION=0 hardcoded in test_mm.cu/test_decompress.cu)
reps50 (spec-imposed; STRICTLY STRONGER than ZipServ's own BENCHMARK_ITERATION=1)

secondarycompression ratio of the weight tensor (bytes_original / bytes_compressed); end-to-end inference throughput vs. a dense vLLM baseline, reported as a SEPARATE system-level number, never substituted for the kernel-level primary metric
correctnessTWO-TIER gate, both required to pass before any timing counts -- stronger than ZipServ's own disclosed verification: (1) bit-exact weight roundtrip: Decompress(Compress(W)) == W byte-for-byte for every weight tensor, checked BEFORE any GEMM is timed (this check is ABSENT from ZipServ's own public verify_compression.py, which only compares downstream GEMM output); (2) fused-kernel GEMM output within the standard bf16-Tensor-Core rounding tolerance of a cuBLAS bf16 reference (cosine similarity > 0.999, ZipServ's own disclosed threshold, reused here). Tier (2) is necessarily a tolerance rather than bit-exactness because bf16 Tensor Core matmul is not itself bit-reproducible -- it validates the FUSED KERNEL's arithmetic, not the compression's losslessness, which tier (1) alone establishes and which this spec adds on top of what ZipServ's own artifact checks.
Fairness notes
  • hZCCL (SC'24) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from all 3 variants above, even though it appears in this track's input list. Its own compressor is an error-bounded LOSSY homomorphic codec (correctness verified via PSNR/NRMSE/max-error against a swept relative error bound {1e-1..1e-4}, not bit-exactness) -- its contribution is "accelerate a collective communication primitive by computing directly on compressed data," architecturally adjacent to but not itself lossless compression. Forcing it onto this track's bit-exact axis would misrepresent what it actually guarantees, exactly the same reasoning the lossy-compression track's survey used to scope out lsCOMP's own integer-quantization lossy mode and the TAC/TAC+ AMR family from ITS core variants.
  • ZipServ markets itself as LOSSLESS weight compression, but its own public verify_compression.py never compares the decompressed weight tensor against the original byte-for-byte -- it only checks that a downstream GEMM's output is numerically close (cosine similarity > 0.999) to a bf16 cuBLAS reference, a check that is inherently tolerant of bf16 rounding and could not detect a decompression bug that happens to still produce a numerically-similar matmul result. Variant 3 above adds the missing bit-exact weight-roundtrip check as tier (1) of its correctness gate specifically to close this gap, rather than accepting ZipServ's own (weaker) self-verification as sufficient.
  • MANS's own benchmark harness reports BEST-of-N throughput (`std::max` across all post-warmup iterations) rather than mean or median, despite exposing clean `--warmup`/`--runs` CLI flags that make a fairer statistic trivial to compute from the same data. Variant 2 above explicitly overrides this with median-of-10, per benchspec_instructions.md's guidance to fix a literature-common flaw ("only reporting best-of-N") rather than diplomatically inherit it.
  • GPULZ's own README-printed "e2e throughput" is a coarse host-side process-wall-clock number (the README itself recommends `nsys` for "more accurate timing for the compression kernel"), while the Huffman-decoder paper's own benchmark code cleanly separates H2D/decode/D2H into 3 independent timed blocks. Variant 2's dual-scope structure (mirroring the lossy-compression track's own gpu-dual-scope variant) resolves this by naming both scopes explicitly rather than letting either paper's "e2e"/"end-to-end" label stand unqualified.
  • hZCCL's standalone-compressor test driver (testfloat_homocompress_fastmode1_arg.c) hardcodes `#define ITERATIONS 1` -- a literal single-shot `gettimeofday` measurement, no warmup, no repetition -- the single weakest timing protocol discipline found across both the lossy-compression and lossless-compression track surveys conducted so far. This is a second, independent reason (beyond its lossy correctness contract) that hZCCL's numbers as published are not directly comparable to this spec's fixed protocol.
  • Rapidgzip has no compression path of its own to benchmark (it is a decompressor for pre-existing gzip files). Variant 1 does not force a compression-throughput number onto it; instead the corpus's compression ratio is fixed once via a stated reference encoder (gzip -9) and decompression throughput stands alone as the headline metric for this sub-domain, with the joint-ratio-and-throughput principle satisfied at the corpus level rather than the per-tool level.
Open questions
  • No arXiv/OA fulltext exists for 6 of the 7 track papers (only Rapidgzip has an arXiv id in the track input). ZipServ, MANS, hZCCL, GPULZ's equation-level detail, and the Huffman-decoder paper's exact timing were all recovered from repo READMEs + raw benchmark source code rather than the paper PDFs themselves (GPULZ's own PDF WAS recovered, repo-hosted, via direct download + `pypdf` text extraction, since neither the arXiv abstract page nor ar5iv's HTML conversion returned usable content for it). If verified paper PDFs for ZipServ, MANS, hZCCL, and the Huffman-decoder paper become available, the exact repetition/warmup/ hardware numbers above should be cross-checked against the papers' own stated methodology, not just their code defaults.
  • ZipServ's benchmark GPU is not pinned to a single model in its own README (3 supported GPUs listed as a minimum-compute-capability requirement: A100, A6000, RTX 4090); the abstract's "2.21x over cuBLAS" figure's exact hardware is therefore unconfirmed from the sources read here.
  • Variant 2's `recommended_subset` list is a union across 4 different papers' own dataset choices, none of which uses the exact same 8-item list; unlike the lossy-compression track's SDRBench convergence, there is no single standardized corpus this track's scientific-multibyte-data papers share wholesale -- the union-with-provenance approach here is a spec design choice, flagged as such rather than presented as a literature-wide consensus suite.
  • MANS's exact named real-world dataset list beyond its shipped `testdata/exafel` sample could not be pinned down further without the paywalled SC'25 paper PDF; its contribution to variant 2's `recommended_subset` (EXAFEL) is the one dataset independently confirmed from the repo itself, not the README's broader unnamed "quantization-based datasets" claim.
  • No independent round-trip verification could be confirmed for GPULZ beyond its algorithmic argument (LZSS is dictionary-based and inherently lossless by construction) -- no printed diff-check was found in its Experimental Setup or Evaluation sections, unlike MANS and the Huffman-decoder paper which both hard-gate on exact equality inside their own harnesses.
  • Whether ZipServ's `run.sh` (ncu-hardware-counter, single kernel launch) or a Rapidgzip/Huffman-decoder-style repeated-wall-clock-average is the "right" substitute for repetition on a system this fine-grained (a single fused GEMM kernel launch, microseconds-scale) is left as an open methodological question -- variant 3 above picks the repeated CUDA-event-average approach for consistency with variant 2 and the lossy-compression track's own GPU variant, but a hardware-counter-based single-launch measurement (ZipServ's own `run.sh` approach) is a legitimate alternative not fully explored here.
content-defined-chunking1 papers1 variants

SIMD-vectorized content-defined chunking (CDC) for data deduplication: scan a byte stream and emit content-determined chunk boundaries (so identical content re-aligns to identical chunks regardless of insertions/deletions elsewhere in the stream), measured as throughput JOINTLY with achieved average chunk size and deduplication space savings on a real dataset -- never throughput alone, since a degenerate boundary rule (e.g. always chunk at a fixed offset) trivially maximizes throughput while destroying dedup ratio.

Given a byte stream of length N and target average chunk size C_avg (with configured min/max bounds C_min, C_max): scan the stream once, left to right, and at each candidate position evaluate a content-dependent boundary predicate (rolling hash threshold for Rabin/Gear/FastCDC-family algorithms; local-extremum/skip-based rule for AE/MAXP/RAM/SeqCDC-family algorithms) to decide whether to cut a chunk boundary there. SeqCDC's specific contribution: a lightweight (non-hash) boundary-detection rule plus content-defined SKIPPING (jumping ahead by a content-dependent stride instead of evaluating every byte position), vectorized via SSE/AVX/NEON/AltiVec to evaluate multiple candidate positions per SIMD lane-width.

cdc-throughput-dedupratio-jointsteady-state single-thread chunking throughput on a real (non-synthetic) dataset, reported JOINTLY with achieved average chunk size and resulting deduplication space savings %, across the SIMD-acceleration axis (unaccelerated vs. best-available vector ISA for the host CPU) and the chunk-size-target axis -- matches SeqCDC's own claimed "10x over unaccelerated / 1.2-1.35x over vector-accelerated alternatives" comparison set (the other 10 algorithms in the same DedupBench harness).
inputs
suitethe DEB (Deduplication Evaluation Benchmark) dataset -- real VM disk images spanning multiple application stacks, the paper's own canonical evaluation set (shared across VectorCDC/FAST'25, SeqCDC/Middleware'24, and this TPDS'26 paper); a synthetic random_dataset control (0% achievable dedup by construction) is required as a throughput-only sanity check, NEVER reported as a dedup-ratio result.
selectionall DEB images still available (per the repo's own README, some Bitnami image URLs retired since Sept 2024) -- minimum 6 of the original 11 named stacks

candidate_algorithmsSeqCDC (this paper's contribution) vs. the other 10 in the same harness (AE-Max, AE-Min, CRC-32, FastCDC, Fixed-size, Gear, MAXP, Rabin, RAM, TTTD), each at its best-available SIMD tier for the test CPU (AE/MAXP/RAM/SeqCDC support SIMD per the repo's own compatibility table; CRC-32/FastCDC/Fixed-size/Gear/Rabin/TTTD are unaccelerated-only in the current release)

timerwall-clock around the full dataset-directory chunking pass (DedupBench's own dedup.exe timing convention, std::chrono at the process level)
timing_scopechunking + fingerprinting/hashing fused, matching DedupBench's own single-pass dedup.exe design (chunking-only isolation is not exposed by the released harness -- see open_questions); report the fused number as the primary metric and flag explicitly that it is NOT chunking-only.
threadingsingle-threaded (DedupBench's dedup.exe is not stated to be multi-threaded in the fetched README) -- report explicitly if a multi-threaded configuration is used, since that would not be comparable to the paper's own presumably-single-threaded numbers
preprocessing_reportednot applicable (CDC has no separable one-shot preprocessing stage distinct from the scan itself)
metric
primarythroughput, MB/s (bytes of input scanned per second)
secondaryachieved average chunk size (bytes, vs. the configured target -- CDC algorithms only approximate the target due to content-dependence); deduplication space savings % (via measure-dedup.exe on the SAME chunked output, run as the required companion measurement, never omitted)
correctnessMANDATORY joint gate, not a numerical tolerance (CDC boundary- finding is deterministic, not approximate): (1) determinism check -- re-running the SAME algorithm on the SAME input twice must produce byte-identical chunk boundaries; (2) content-defined-ness check -- inserting or deleting a small byte range at one point in the stream must leave chunk boundaries FAR from that point unchanged (the defining CDC property that distinguishes it from fixed-size chunking; verified by comparing boundary sets before/ after a synthetic single-byte insertion at a known offset, at least 90% of boundaries beyond 2x the target chunk size from the insertion point must be unchanged); (3) reported dedup space savings % must be computed via measure-dedup.exe on the SAME chunked output used for the throughput number, never a different run.
Fairness notes
  • The paper's abstract already frames its own contribution as a throughput-vs-dedup-ratio tradeoff ('10x throughput... while MINIMALLY AFFECTING deduplication space savings'), so this track's joint-reporting requirement is not an external correction but a direct formalization of the paper's own framing -- made mandatory here because DedupBench's separate measure-dedup.exe tool makes it easy to report ONLY the throughput half in a future re-measurement if not required.
  • DedupBench's dedup.exe appears to fuse chunking and hashing/fingerprinting cost into one throughput number (not stated as separable in the fetched README); this spec is explicit that the reported number is FUSED, not chunking-only, to prevent a future reader from assuming it isolates the paper's own specific contribution (the boundary-detection + skipping algorithm) from the (unrelated, off-the-shelf) hashing stage.
  • A random_dataset control is required specifically because throughput-only benchmarking on synthetic data trivially favors any algorithm that scans faster regardless of boundary quality -- pairing it with the mandatory dedup-ratio gate on REAL data (DEB) prevents a report from citing only the synthetic-data throughput number as if it characterized real-world dedup performance.
Open questions
  • Whether DedupBench's dedup.exe reports a chunking-only throughput number separately from the fused chunking+hashing number (via some config.txt option not surfaced in the top-level README) was not determined -- if such an option exists, isolating chunking-only cost would be a strictly better match to the paper's own stated contribution than the fused number used here.
  • The paper's own reported throughput/space-savings numbers are specific to the TPDS'26 journal extension (which adds ARM/IBM SIMD support on top of the FAST'25/Middleware'24 x86-only prior work); which of the DEB images and chunk-size targets were used in THIS paper's specific evaluation table (as opposed to the shared harness's general capability) was not confirmed from the fetched README alone.
  • No stated warmup/repeat/statistic convention was found for dedup.exe's own throughput reporting; the protocol here (1 discarded warmup, 5 reps, median) is this spec's own construction, not extracted from the artifact.
erasure-coding1 papers1 variants

CPU XOR-based Reed-Solomon erasure coding (encode: compute m parity blocks from k data blocks via GF(2) XOR-schedules compiled and optimized as straight-line programs; decode: reconstruct erased blocks from surviving data+parity), measured separately for encode, decode at maximum tolerable erasure count, and degraded-read at partial erasure, across (k,m) configurations and the paper's own three-tier optimization ablation (Nooptim / Fusion / FusionSchedule).

Given k data blocks D_1..D_k (each BLOCK_SIZE bytes), compute m parity blocks P_1..P_m such that any k of the (k+m) total blocks suffice to reconstruct all k original data blocks, using ONLY XOR operations (no Galois-field multiplication) — i.e. each P_j and each reconstructed D_i is a fixed XOR-subset of the surviving blocks, with that XOR schedule compiled as a straight-line program (SLP) and optimized via grammar compression (fewer XOR ops), deforestation (fewer memory accesses), and pebble-game scheduling (fewer cache misses) before execution.

ec-xor-encode-decode-kernelsteady-state single-thread CPU throughput for encode and decode (at maximum-tolerable erasure count, i.e. exactly m blocks erased) separately, at each of the paper's own three optimization tiers, across a spread of (k,m) configurations -- SLP compilation/ optimization is a one-shot cost EXCLUDED from the per-run timed loop (matching the artifact's own code structure, which already separates estimate_compile from the timed run::run_program loop).
inputs

selection(k,m) pairs actually exercised in the artifact's README examples, plus RS(6,3) and RS(12,4) to bracket typical distributed-storage EC configurations (matching common systems like HDFS-EC/Ceph defaults, e.g. RS(6,3))

data_size~10 MB total (matching the artifact's own reported example, data size = 10158080 bytes) AND a larger 1 GB point to check whether throughput is stable across the working-set/cache-fitting boundary
optimization_levelsNooptim, Fusion, FusionSchedule (the artifact's own --optimize-level values) -- all THREE required per (k,m) point, not only the fully-optimized FusionSchedule headline number, so each technique's individual contribution stays visible
degraded_read_sub_caseREQUIRED additional sub-case: decode with erasure count < m (e.g. 1 block erased out of RS(10,4)'s tolerable 4) -- a degraded-read is the common case in real storage systems (single node/disk failure), while the artifact's own default example erases the MAXIMUM tolerable count; reporting only the max- erasure case would overstate decode cost for the far more common single-failure scenario, since decode SLP size/cost is a function of exactly which and how many blocks are erased.
protocol
warmup1 discarded iteration -- DEVIATION from the artifact's own convention, which times all 1000 iterations undiscarded from a cold state; added since the first XOR-schedule execution touches cold cache lines the SLP-compiled program was scheduled against, biasing iteration 1 high relative to steady state.
reps1000
statisticmedian (report min/max) -- DEVIATION from the artifact's own avg+sd reporting (xorslp_ec's README shows 'Encode: avg = 7188.13 MB/s, sd = 405.67'); switched to median+min/max per this project's general timing-protocol convention, since a plain mean over 1000 undiscarded reps is more sensitive to rare scheduling-noise outliers than a median.
timerhost-side, std::time::Instant per iteration (the artifact's own timer choice, retained since XOR-SLP execution is a pure-CPU, no-device-sync workload where Instant is already the right-granularity timer)
timing_scopekernel only: run::run_program (the compiled XOR schedule) execution; SLP compilation/optimization (grammar compression, deforestation, pebble-game scheduling) excluded, matching the artifact's own code structure
threadingsingle-threaded (the artifact's benchmarked path is single-core; report explicitly if a multi-threaded/SIMD-batched variant is measured instead, since BLOCK_SIZE_PER_ITER already implies some data-parallel lane width within a single core)
preprocessing_reportedseparately, once per (k, m, erased_indices, optimization_level) combination: SLP compilation + optimization wall time (estimate_compile), since a higher optimization tier trades more compile-time cost for less per-run cost and both numbers are needed to judge the tradeoff for a given amortization count
metric
primarythroughput, MB/s (total data-block bytes processed per second: encode = sum of D_i bytes; decode = sum of RECONSTRUCTED D_i bytes, not counting surviving blocks read)
secondaryXOR instruction count and memory-transfer count per block (the artifact's own --stat-enc/--stat-dec/--all-stat output), reported as the mechanistic explanation for any throughput delta between optimization tiers
correctnessMANDATORY pre-timing gate, exact bit-reconstruction required (XOR- based EC over GF(2) is lossless/exact by construction, no numerical tolerance applies): for every decode configuration, the reconstructed D_i blocks must be BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original data blocks before encoding. This is not stated as an automated check in the fetched artifact's benchmark-invocation examples (--enc-dec/--stat-enc/--stat-dec show no visible pass/fail output); this spec makes it mandatory and requires it be checked in the SAME run as the timed measurement, for every (k,m,erased_indices, optimization_level) combination, not just once for a default configuration.
Fairness notes
  • The artifact's own reported metric is avg+sd over 1000 undiscarded iterations; this spec switches to median+min/max with 1 discarded warmup iteration, the same class of fix applied throughout this project's other specs (see benchspecs/attention-kernel's notes on PAT/MEATTEN/ByteTransformer) for run-to-run variance robustness -- this is an explicit, noted DEVIATION from the paper's own literal reported numbers, not a claim those numbers are wrong.
  • The artifact's own default example erases exactly m blocks (the maximum tolerable erasure count) for its decode benchmark; this spec adds a degraded_read_sub_case at a SMALLER erasure count specifically because production distributed-storage systems overwhelmingly experience single-block failures, not simultaneous max-tolerable-count failures, and XOR-SLP decode cost is a function of which/how-many blocks are erased -- reporting only the max-erasure case would not characterize the common operating point.
  • The paper's own three-tier optimization ablation (Nooptim/Fusion/FusionSchedule) is preserved as a REQUIRED axis (not collapsed to only the best tier) specifically because this is the paper's actual scientific contribution (isolating each program-optimization technique's individual effect) -- collapsing to a single headline number would erase the paper's own most informative result.
Open questions
  • The Intel ISA-L baseline comparison (~6.7 GB/s per the abstract) is documented via a SEPARATE procedure (HOWTO_BENCHMARK_ISAL.md) not fetched in this survey -- ISA-L's own timing protocol (warmup/reps/statistic) is unconfirmed and may differ from xorslp_ec's own 1000-iteration convention, which would make a direct number-to-number comparison between the two tools' README-reported throughputs potentially apples-to-oranges without re-running both under this spec's unified protocol.
  • BLOCK_SIZE_PER_ITER (the SIMD-lane/block granularity constant controlling how XOR operations are vectorized within run::run_program) was not inspected -- whether the reported throughput already reflects AVX2/AVX-512-width XOR batching, or is scalar, is unconfirmed from the fetched source, and materially affects whether the 8.92 GB/s headline number is a fair single-core comparison point against ISA-L (which is itself SIMD-accelerated).
  • No automated correctness check was found in the fetched benchmark-invocation examples; whether one exists elsewhere in the crate (e.g. a `cargo test` suite distinct from the `xorslp_ec` CLI binary) was not checked.

ML kernels

gnn-aggregation11 papers4 variants

Sparse-times-dense-matrix neighbor aggregation as used in GNN message passing (C = A_sparse @ X_dense, optionally symmetrically normalized by degree), measured at three DIFFERENT scopes the surveyed literature conflates under one "SpMM"/"aggregation" label — isolated kernel, single-layer forward with real feature dims, and full training epoch — plus an explicit preprocessing-amortization split, since several artifacts' headline numbers move visibly (EPPGCN: 1.48-5.65x kernel-only vs 1.03-1.37x end-to-end) depending on which scope and preprocessing treatment is chosen.

Forward: H'[V,F] = A_hat[V,V](sparse, given CSR) @ H[V,F](dense row-major), where A_hat is either the raw binary/weighted adjacency or its symmetric degree-normalization D^-1/2 A D^-1/2 (both appear as first-class targets in the surveyed papers, e.g. CBM benchmarks all three of A@X, A@D^-1/2@X, D^-1/2@A@D^-1/2@X separately). Backward (where in scope): grad_H[V,F] = A_hat^T @ grad_H'[V,F] (same operation shape, transposed sparse operand).

gnn-agg-kernel-f32steady-state isolated-kernel throughput of one aggregation call, given CSR (no format conversion timed), synthetic dense features swept over N — the common denominator of GE-SpMM, MaxK-GNN's kernel benchmark, TLPGNN, and CBM's benchmark_matmul.py. THIS variant intentionally does NOT include any Python/framework dispatch overhead, backward pass, or other GCN layers (unlike TC-GNN/QGTC/EPPGCN's epoch numbers below).
